### Page 102 (lower) — Sūkta 22, Rik 13

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> म॒ही द्यौः पृ॑थि॒वी च॑ न इ॒मं य॒ज्ञं मि॑मिक्षतां ।
> पि॒पृ॒तां नो॒ भरी॑मभिः ॥१३॥
>
> *mahī́ dyáuḥ pṛthivī́ ca na imáṃ yajñáṃ mimikṣatāṃ |*
> *pipṛtā́ṃ no bhárīmabhiḥ ||13||*

*(Bars under म (मही), थि, इ (इमं) and य (यज्ञं); strokes over पृ, च and the first मि. Line 2: bars under पि, पृ and नो; a stroke over री.)*

### Page 103 — Rik 13: Pada, bhāṣya

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> मही । द्यौः । पृथिवी । च । नः । इमं । यज्ञं । मिमिक्षतां ॥
> पिपृतां । नः । भरीमऽभिः ॥१३॥
>
> *mahī | dyauḥ | pṛthivī | ca | naḥ | imaṃ | yajñaṃ | mimikṣatāṃ ||*
> *pipṛtāṃ | naḥ | bharīma 'bhiḥ ||13||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(The Āśvalāyana numbers are printed ८-१०, २-९, २-१६, ३-१०, ६-५. The bhāṣya prints the root of* pipṛtām *as पॄ with* hrasva iti eke*, and the sūtra number पा० ७-४-७७.)*

> द्वितीये छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति द्यावापृथिव्यनिविद्धानीयस्तृचः । द्वितीयस्याग्निं व इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नो युवाना पितरा पुनः । आ० ८-१० । इति ॥ आग्रयणेष्टौ मही द्यौरित्येषा द्यावापृथिव्यैककपालस्यानुवाक्या । आग्रयणं व्रीहिश्यामाकेति खण्डे सूत्रितं । ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमाया मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नः । आ० २-९ । इति ॥ अग्निमन्थनेऽप्येषा विनियुक्ता । प्रातर्वैश्वदेव्यामिति खण्डे सूत्रितं । अभि त्वा देव सवितर्मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नः । आ० २-१६ । इति ॥ विष्यन्दमानं सांनाय्यमनयैवाहवनीयदेशे निनयेत् । विध्यपराध इति खण्डे तथैव सूत्रितं । विष्यन्दमानं मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इत्यन्तःपरिधिदेशे निनयेयुः । आ० ३-१० । इति ॥ आश्विनशस्त्रेऽप्येषा । संस्थिते ष्वाश्विनायेति खण्डे सूत्रितं । मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नस्ते हि द्यावापृथिवी विश्वशंभुवा । आ० ६-५ । इति ॥
>
> *dvitīye chandome vaiśvadevaśastre mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivyanividdhānīyastṛcaḥ | dvitīyasyāgniṃ va iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca no yuvānā pitarā punaḥ | ā0 8-10 | iti || āgrayaṇeṣṭau mahī dyaurityeṣā dyāvāpṛthivyaikakapālasyānuvākyā | āgrayaṇaṃ vrīhiśyāmāketi khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyā mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ | ā0 2-9 | iti || agnimanthane 'pyeṣā viniyuktā | prātarvaiśvadevyāmiti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | abhi tvā deva savitarmahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ | ā0 2-16 | iti || viṣyandamānaṃ sāṃnāyyamanayaivāhavanīyadeśe ninayet | vidhyaparādha iti khaṇḍe tathaiva sūtritaṃ | viṣyandamānaṃ mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na ityantaḥparidhideśe ninayeyuḥ | ā0 3-10 | iti || āśvinaśastre 'pyeṣā | saṃsthite ṣvāśvināyeti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naste hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśaṃbhuvā | ā0 6-5 | iti ||*

**Translation (application):** "In the second *chandoma* day, at the *vaiśvadeva-śastra*, the tṛca to Heaven-and-Earth, *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ*, the one to be put in the place of the *nivid*; it is laid down in the section *dvitīyasyāgniṃ vaḥ*: '*mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ*, *yuvānā pitarā punaḥ*' (Āśv. 8-10). In the *āgrayaṇa-iṣṭi*, *mahī dyauḥ* is the *anuvākyā* of the one-potsherd cake to Heaven-and-Earth; it is laid down in the section *āgrayaṇaṃ vrīhiśyāmāka*: '*ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ*, *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ*' (Āśv. 2-9). It is used also at the churning of fire; it is laid down in the section *prātarvaiśvadevyām*: '*abhi tvā deva savitaḥ*, *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ*' (Āśv. 2-16). With this same ṛk one should pour the *sāṃnāyya* that is trickling away on to the place of the *āhavanīya*: so it is laid down in the section *vidhyaparādha*: 'the trickling one, with *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ*, they should pour within the enclosing sticks' (Āśv. 3-10). It is used also at the *āśvina-śastra*; it is laid down in the section *saṃsthite ṣv āśvināya*: '*mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ*, *te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuvā*' (Āśv. 6-5)."

> मही महती द्यौर्द्युलोकदेवता पृथिवी भूमिदेवता च नोऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञं मिमिक्षतां । स्वकीयसारभूतेन रसेन मिमिक्षतां । सेक्तुमिच्छतां । तथा भरीमभिर्भरणैः पोषणैर्नोऽस्मान्पिपृतां । उभे देव्यौ पूरयतां ॥ मही । महच्छब्दादुगितश्चेति ङीप् । अच्छब्दलोपश्छान्दसः । बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानमिति ङीप उदात्तत्वं । द्यौः । दिव्शब्दः प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । गोतो णित् । पा० ७-१-९० । इति ततः परस्य सोर्णिद्वद्भावाद्वृद्धिरपि स्थानिवद्भावेनोदात्ता । पृथिवी । प्रथ प्रख्याने । प्रथेः षिवन्संप्रसारणं च । उ० १-१५० । इति षिवन्प्रत्ययः । षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च । पा० ४-१-४१ । इति ङीष् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मिमिक्षतां । मिह सेचने । सनि द्विर्भावहलादिशेषौ । ढत्वकत्वषत्वानि । पिपृतां । पॄ पालनपूरणयोः । ह्रस्व इत्येके । शपः श्लुः । अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च । पा० ७-४-७७ । इत्यभ्यासस्याकारस्येकारः । तिङः प्रत्ययस्वरः । भरीमभिः । डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोः । हुसृधृक्षिभृभ्य ईमनिनिति ईमन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥
>
> *mahī mahatī dyaurdyulokadevatā pṛthivī bhūmidevatā ca no 'smadīyamimaṃ yajñaṃ mimikṣatāṃ | svakīyasārabhūtena rasena mimikṣatāṃ | sektumicchatāṃ | tathā bharīmabhirbharaṇaiḥ poṣaṇairno 'smānpipṛtāṃ | ubhe devyau pūrayatāṃ || mahī | mahacchabdādugitaśceti ṅīp | acchabdalopaśchāndasaḥ | bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānamiti ṅīpa udāttatvaṃ | dyauḥ | divśabdaḥ prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | goto ṇit | pā0 7-1-90 | iti tataḥ parasya sorṇidvadbhāvādvṛddhirapi sthānivadbhāvenodāttā | pṛthivī | pratha prakhyāne | pratheḥ ṣivansaṃprasāraṇaṃ ca | u0 1-150 | iti ṣivanpratyayaḥ | ṣidgaurādibhyaśca | pā0 4-1-41 | iti ṅīṣ | pratyayasvaraḥ | mimikṣatāṃ | miha secane | sani dvirbhāvahalādiśeṣau | ḍhatvakatvaṣatvāni | pipṛtāṃ | pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ | hrasva ityeke | śapaḥ śluḥ | artipipartyośca | pā0 7-4-77 | ityabhyāsasyākārasyekāraḥ | tiṅaḥ pratyayasvaraḥ | bharīmabhiḥ | ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ | husṛdhṛkṣibhṛbhya īmaniniti īman | nittvādādyudāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "May *mahī*, great, *dyauḥ*, the deity of the heavenly world, and *pṛthivī*, the deity of the earth, *mimikṣatām*, wish to sprinkle, *imaṃ yajñam*, this our sacrifice, with their own essential juice. Likewise may they *pipṛtām*, fill, *naḥ*, us, *bharīmabhiḥ*, with supports, nourishments: may both goddesses fill us." (Grammatical tail: *mahī*, *ṅīp* after *mahat* by *ugitaś ca*, the dropping of *at* Vedic, the *ṅīp* udātta by *bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam*; *dyauḥ*, *div* final udātta by the stem accent; by *goto ṇit* (Pā. 7-1-90) the *su* after it is like *ṇit*, and the *vṛddhi* too is udātta by *sthānivadbhāva*; *pṛthivī*, *pratha prakhyāne*, the suffix *ṣivan* by *pratheḥ ṣivan saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca* (U. 1-150), *ṅīṣ* by *ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca* (Pā. 4-1-41), the suffix accent; *mimikṣatām*, *miha secane*, with *san* reduplication and *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*, then *ḍh*, *k* and *ṣ*; *pipṛtām*, *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ* (some say short), *ślu* for *śap*, *i* for the *a* of the reduplication by *artipipartyoś ca* (Pā. 7-4-77), the accent of the *tiṅ* suffix; *bharīmabhiḥ*, *ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*, *īman* by *husṛdhṛkṣibhṛbhya īman*, initial udātta as *nit*.)

### Page 104 — Rik 13: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**मही (mahī)** — great | **द्यौः (dyauḥ)** — the deity of the heavenly world | **पृथिवी च (pṛthivī ca)** — together with the deity of the earth | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **इमं यज्ञं (imaṃ yajñaṃ)** — this sacrifice | **मिमिक्षतां (mimikṣatāṃ)** — may they be ready to make it full of juice | **भरीमभिः (bharīmabhiḥ)** — with nourishing works | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **पिपृतां (pipṛtāṃ)** — may they make full.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

May the deities of the world of the gods and of the earth make our sacrifice full of juice, and nourish us with nourishing things.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> May the great Heaven and Earth sprinkle (with sweetness) this our Sacrifice ; may they fill us with nourishments.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

This ṛk has many applications. At the time of reciting the *vaiśvadeva-śastra* mantras, on the second *chandoma*, this ṛk *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ* is used as the mantra for the recitation of a mantra with Heaven-and-Earth as deity. In the section *dvitīyasyāgniṃ vaḥ* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra there is the sūtra *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) *yuvānā pitarā punaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-20-4) (Ā. 8-10).

In the *āgrayaṇa-iṣṭi*, this ṛk *mahī dyauḥ* is used as the *puronuvākyā* ṛk for the offering of the one-potsherd cake with Heaven-and-Earth as deity. In the section *āgrayaṇaṃ vrīhiśyāmāka* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra this matter is explained in the sūtra *ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-52-14 [?]) *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) (Ā. 2-9).

At the time of churning the fire too this ṛk is applied. In the section *prātarvaiśvadevyām* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra there is the sūtra *abhi tvā deva savitaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3) *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) (Ā. 2-16).

When pouring the *puroḍāśa* called *sāṃnāyya* to the place of the *āhavanīya*, this mantra is recited. In the section *vidhyaparādha* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra there is the sūtra *viṣyandamānaṃ mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) *ity antaḥparidhideśe ninayeyuḥ* (Ā. 3-10).

### Page 105 — Rik 13: Special Topics (continued)

In the recitation of the *āśvina-śastra* mantras too, its application is explained in the section *saṃsthite ṣv āśvināya* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra by the sūtra *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) *te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuvā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-160-1) (Ā. 6-5).

Apart from such *śrauta* rites, this mantra is used also in domestic rites and on occasions of prayer to the earth.

**द्यौः, पृथिवी (dyauḥ, pṛthivī)** — heaven and earth. Though there are many mantras that praise together (as a pair, *saṃstavika*) the two deities Heaven-and-Earth who preside over heaven and earth, there are also some mantras that praise them using the separate words *dyauḥ* and *pṛthivī*:

> उप श्वासय पृथिवीमुत द्यां पुरुत्रा ते मनुतां विष्ठितं जगत् ॥ (ऋ० सं० ६-४७-२९)
> मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्यां । (ऋ० सं० ३-५९-१)
> विश्वकर्मन्हविषा वावृधानः स्वयं यजस्व पृथिवीमुत द्यां ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-८१-६)
>
> *upa śvāsaya pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ purutrā te manutāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat || (ṛ0 saṃ0 6-47-29)*
> *mitro janānyātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ | (ṛ0 saṃ0 3-59-1)*
> *viśvakarmanhaviṣā vāvṛdhānaḥ svayaṃ yajasva pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-81-6)*

*(Glosses of these quotations are not given in the source.)* There are twenty-four words, *rodasī*, *purandhrī* [as printed: *svadhe purandhī*] and the rest, that indicate the meaning of the word *dyāvāpṛthivī* (Ni. 3-30 [?], as read). In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, with *dyauḥ pitaḥ pṛthivi mātaḥ*, heaven is addressed as father and the earth as mother. In the Ṛgveda the world (the universe) is generally counted in three main divisions (worlds): heaven, mid-air and earth. Heaven too has three divisions: *nāka* (the highest, best place in heaven), *viṣṭap* (the middle region) and *pṛṣṭha* (the lower part). Though there are no particular divisions in the mid-air, words like *vyoman*, *rocana* (the shining region) and *antarikṣa* indicate a difference in meaning. The word *pṛthivī* too is called by names such as *pṛthivī* (the wide region), *mahī* (the great region), *iḷā* (this world), *vasumatī* (rich in wealth). In the Ṛgveda the word *dyāvāpṛthivī* is generally used thinking of the presiding deities of heaven and earth.

> द्यौः पितः पृथिवि मातः ।
>
> *dyauḥ pitaḥ pṛthivi mātaḥ |*

**यज्ञं मिमिक्षतां (yajñaṃ mimikṣatāṃ)** — *svakīyasārabhūtena rasena sektum icchatām |* The intention is: may the deities Heaven-and-Earth, who preside over heaven and earth, favour this sacrifice so that it is well accomplished with the best things in heaven and on earth.

### Page 106 — Rik 13: Special Topics (end), grammar

**पिपृतां नो भरीमभिः (pipṛtāṃ no bharīmabhiḥ)** — *bharaṇasamarthair annai rasaiś ca ||* May they make our sacrifice complete with nourishing articles of food and with drinks such as soma juice.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**मही (mahī)** — the word *mahat*, being treated like one ending in *śatṛ* by *vartamāne pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca* (U. Sū. 2-[?]), is *ugit*. By *ugitaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-6), *ṅyāpprātipadikāt* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-12 [?], as read), the word *prātipadikāt* is the heading. *Ugitaḥ* qualifies *prātipadikāt*; so by *yena vidhis tadantasya* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72) a qualifier denotes what ends in it, and 'ending in it' is obtained. Though, this being a rule of suffixes, by *samāsapratyayavidhau pratiṣedhaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72 Vā. 4444 [?]) — in rules of compounds and of suffixes, the obtaining of 'ending in it' is to be prohibited — the prohibition would apply, yet by *ugidvarṇagrahaṇavarjam* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72 Vā. 4445 [?]) — except where an *ugit* or a letter is mentioned, the prohibition of 'ending in it' is to be stated in rules of compounds and suffixes — since here there is the mention of an *ugit*, *ugitaḥ*, the prohibition does not come. Or: the heading *anupasarjanāt* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-14) makes known that in the section on feminine suffixes there is the rule of 'ending in it'; so 'ending in it' is obtained. *Striyām* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-3) is the heading. From *ṛnnebhyo ṅīp* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-5) *ṅīp* is carried on. So the sense of the sūtra: after a nominal stem ending in an *ugit*, *ṅīp* comes in the feminine. *Ugit* is of two kinds: 1. a nominal stem; 2. a suffix. By the qualification of residing only in a nominal stem, wherever a nominal stem is mentioned, there is the prohibition *vyapadeśivadbhāvo 'prātipadikena* (Paribhā. 33); so *vyapadeśivadbhāva* cannot come there. Here, since the *u*-marked suffix is in both the stem and the suffix, *vyapadeśivadbhāva* comes here. So *mahat* is a stem ending in an *ugit*. When *ṅīp* follows it: *mahat* + *ī*; as a Vedic matter the word *at* is dropped. *Viśiṣṭa apadeśaḥ, vyapadeśaḥ* means the main usage. *Vyapadeśinā tulyam, vyapadeśivat*: for something unaccompanied, the usage 'ending in it' does not come in the main sense; yet, in the way an operation comes where there is the main usage, in the same way the operation comes: this is the meaning of *vyapadeśivadbhāva*. Here *mahat* is *ugit* by extension; yet, since it is not at the end of another, the main usage 'ending in an *ugit*' cannot come. In *atimahat* there is the main usage 'ending in an *ugit*'. Here, as the operation comes where there is the main usage, so here the operation comes: this results from *vyapadeśivadbhāva*. So

### Page 107 — Rik 13: grammar (continued)

there is no hindrance here to *ṅīp* coming. *Ṅīp* is *pit*; so by *anudāttau suppitau* it would be unaccented. Yet by *bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam*, read at *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173) — the *nadī*-named suffix and the vowel-initial case-endings *śas* and the rest after the words *bṛhat* and *mahat* are also udātta — it is udātta. By *yū stryākhyau nadī* (Pā. Sū. 1-4-3): on the view that it names letters, the sense of the sūtra is that the letters *ī* and *ū* that convey the specific sense of being always feminine get the name *nadī*; on the view that it names what ends in them, words ending in *ī* and *ū* that convey the specific sense of being always feminine get the name *nadī*. Here, on the view that it names letters, *ṅīp* has the name *nadī*. Though the udātta would be established by the extension of being treated like *śatṛ*, we have explained before that the *vārttika* was begun to obtain the restriction that the udātta is excluded for a suffix after words other than *bṛhat* and *mahat*.

**द्यौः (dyauḥ)** — this word can be derived in two ways. 1. The root *dyuta dīptau*; after it, by the word *bahula* in *uṇādayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-1), the Uṇādi suffix *ḍo* comes. By the force of the suffix being made *ḍit*, even without the name *bha*, the *ṭi* of the root, *ut*, is dropped: it became *dyo*. After this, the nominative singular suffix *su*. *Goto ṇit* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-90) means that the suffixes named *sarvanāmasthāna* after the word *go* — that is, the five suffixes *su*, *au*, *jas*, *am*, *auṭ* — are like *ṇit*. Here the author of the *vārttika*, in *otaḥ ṇid iti vācyam* (Pā. Sū. Vā. 7-1-90-1), says the sūtra *goto ṇit* should be made *oto ṇit*; that is, the word *gotaḥ* should be taken away and the word *otaḥ* put in its place. Accordingly it results that the *sarvanāmasthāna* suffixes after a word ending in *o* are like *ṇit*, that is, like those marked *ṇ*. So the *su* after the word *dyo* ending in *o* becomes like *ṇit*; by *aco 'ñṇiti* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115) — when suffixes marked *ñ* or *ṇ* follow, a stem ending in a vowel takes *vṛddhi* — *vṛddhi*, *au* for *o*, and with *ru* and *visarga* for *su* it becomes *dyauḥ*. On this view the *o* is udātta by the suffix accent; the *au* coming in its place is also udātta by likeness of place. 2. *Div* is a nominal stem ending in *v*; it is udātta by *phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ*. After it the suffix *su*; by *diva aut* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-84) — when the suffix *su* follows, the substitute *au* for the final letter of the nominal stem *div* — the substitute *au* for the *v* of *div*: *di* + *au* + *s*; by *iko yaṇ aci* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-77) *y* for the *i*: *dyau s*, the *au* having come in place of *v*. By *sthānivad ādeśaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-56), with *sthānivadbhāva*, it is as if *v* were there. So one may doubt that by *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-68) the *su* should be dropped;

### Page 108 — Rik 13: grammar (continued)

but in *sthānivad ādeśo 'nalvidhau* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-56), *analvidhau* means that *sthānivadbhāva* does not come in a rule about letters; so when making the rule about letters *halṅyābbhyaḥ*, *sthānivadbhāva* does not come. So the *su* is not dropped. With *ru* and *visarga* it becomes *dyauḥ*. On this view the *i* in *div* is udātta; the *au* coming in place of the *v*, by *asvarakāṇām asvarakā ādeśāḥ*, is unaccented; by *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) — an unaccented vowel after a *yaṇ* standing in place of an udātta or svarita becomes svarita — the *au* after the *y* standing in place of the udātta *i* becomes svarita: this is the situation. In the present Veda commentary, where it says *div śabdaḥ prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ*, it would be right to read *dyo śabdaḥ bāhulakāt auṇādikaḍopratyayāntaḥ, pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ*. It is not unknown to scholars that the present reading has arisen through the carelessness of scribes and proof-readers.

> दिव्शब्दः प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः ।
> द्योशब्दः बाहुलकात् औणादिकडोप्रत्ययान्तः प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः ।
>
> *divśabdaḥ prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ |*
> *dyośabdaḥ bāhulakāt auṇādikaḍopratyayāntaḥ pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ |*

**पृथिवी (pṛthivī)** — the root *pratha prakhyāne*; by *pratheḥ ṣivan saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca* (U. Sū. 1-144 [?], as read), the suffix *ṣivan* comes after the root *prath*, and the root takes *saṃprasāraṇa*: so when the suffix *ṣivan* comes, *saṃprasāraṇa* and *ṛ* for the *r*: *pṛth* + *iv* = *pṛthiv*; the suffix is *ṣit*. By *ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-41) — after words marked *ṣ* and words read in the *gaurādi* class, *ṅīṣ* in the feminine — *ṅīṣ* comes. Though here the suffix is *ṣit*, and the word *pṛthiv* is not *ṣit*, yet by the maxim *avayave 'caritārthaṃ liṅgaṃ samudāyopakārakaṃ bhavati*, since the *ṣ*-marking in the suffix has no other purpose, that *ṣ*-marking qualifies the whole; *pṛthivī* is final udātta by the suffix accent.

> अवयवेऽचरितार्थं लिङ्गं समुदायोपकारकं भवति ।
>
> *avayave 'caritārthaṃ liṅgaṃ samudāyopakārakaṃ bhavati |*

**मिमिक्षताम् (mimikṣatām)** — the root *miha secane*. By *dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-7) the suffix *san*; by *sanyaṅoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-9) reduplication: *mih mih* + *sa*; by *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-60) the *h* of the first *mih* is dropped. *Loṭ*, third person *tas*; by *loṭo laṅvat* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) treated like *laṅ*; by *tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) the substitute *tām*. Since the root *mih* is in the *aniṭ-kārikā*, *vasatir dahadihaduho nah mih ruh lih vahis tathā* (Pā. Sū. Pā. Mā. 7-2-10-6 [?], as read), the augment *iṭ* is barred by *ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-10). *Mimih* + *sa* + *tām*: now by *ho ḍhaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-31) *ḍh* for *h*; for this *ḍh*, by *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* (Pā. Sū. 8-8-41 [?], as read) the substitute *t* [sic; for *k*]; for the *s* after it, by *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-59)

### Page 109 — Rik 13: grammar (end)

*ṣ*: it becomes *mimikṣatām*. By *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) it is wholly unaccented.

**पिपृताम् (pipṛtām)** — the root *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*; some hold that *pṛ* ends in a short vowel. *Loṭ*, third person *tas*, the substitute *tām* as before, *śap*; by *juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-75) *ślu* (dropping); by *ślau* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-10) reduplication; on the view that *ślu* has come, by *artipipartyoś ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-77) — *ṛ gatau*, *pṝ*, *pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ* — *i* comes as the final substitute for their reduplication: so for the *ṛ* of the first *pṛ*, *i*; by *uraṇ raparaḥ* it comes followed by *r*. By *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* the *r* is removed: it becomes *pipṛtām*. In the Bhāṣya it is described as: first, by *ur at* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-66), when a suffix follows, *a* comes for the *ṛ* of the reduplication; then *i* for the *a* by *artipipartyoś ca*. In fact, since the rule laying down *i* is an exception to *ur at*, it is right to say that *i* comes first. Here, since the root *pṛ* ending in a short vowel is taken, the *u* for the *ṛ* of the second *pṛ* by *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-102) does not come. Since there is the prohibition *kṅiti ca* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-5), *guṇa* does not come. Since this is at the beginning of the *pāda*, by the prohibition *apādādau*, the total lack of accent by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* does not come. So by the suffix accent *tām* is udātta.

**भरीमभिः (bharīmabhiḥ)** — the root *ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*. By *husṛdhṛkṣibhṛbhya īman* (Daśa. Pā. 6 [as printed]) — after the roots *hu dānādanayoḥ*, *styai*[*ñ*] *ācchādane* [as printed], *ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*, *dhṛñ avasthāne*, *svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ*, *sṛ gatau*, the suffix *īman* comes — when *īman* comes: *bhṛ* + *īman*, *guṇa*; the suffix is *nit*, so by the *nit* accent *bharīmabhiḥ* is initially udātta. ॥13॥

### Page 109 (lower) — Sūkta 22, Rik 14

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> त॒योरिद्घृ॒तव॒त्पयो॒ विप्रा॑ रिहन्ति धी॒तिभिः॑ । [accent ?]
> ग॒न्ध॒र्व॑स्य ध्रु॒वे प॒दे ॥१४॥
>
> *tayór id ghṛtávat páyo víprā rihanti dhītíbhiḥ |* [accent ?]
> *gandharvasya dhruvé padé ||14||*

*(Bars under त or यो of तयोः (the bar stands between them [accent ?]), घृ, व (वत्), यो (पयो) and धी; strokes over प्रा and भिः. Line 2: bars under ग, ध (न्ध), ध्रु and प; a stroke over र्व.)*

### Page 110 — Rik 14: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तयोः । इत् । घृतऽवत् । पयः । विप्राः । रिहन्ति । धीतिऽभिः ॥
> गन्धर्वस्य । ध्रुवे । पदे ॥१४॥
>
> *tayoḥ | it | ghṛta 'vat | payaḥ | viprāḥ | rihanti | dhīti 'bhiḥ ||*
> *gandharvasya | dhruve | pade ||14||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> गन्धर्वस्य ध्रुवं पदमन्तरिक्षं । तथा च तापनीयशाखायां समाम्नायते । यक्षगन्धर्वाप्सरोगणसेवितमन्तरिक्षं । नृ० ता० १-२ । इति । तेनान्तरिक्षेणोपलक्षित आकाशे वर्तमानयोस्तयोरिद्द्यावापृथिव्योरेव संबन्धि पयो जलं घृतवद्घृतसदृशं विप्रा मेधाविनः प्राणिनो धीतिभिः कर्मभी रिहन्ति । लिहन्ति । यद्वा । घृतवद्घृतं सारं तेनोपेतं रिहन्ति । लिहेर्व्यत्ययेन रेफः । गन्धर्वस्य । धृञ् धारणे । गवि गन् धृञो व इति वप्रत्ययः । तत्संनियोगेन गोशब्दस्य च गन्नादेशः ॥
>
> *gandharvasya dhruvaṃ padamantarikṣaṃ | tathā ca tāpanīyaśākhāyāṃ samāmnāyate | yakṣagandharvāpsarogaṇasevitamantarikṣaṃ | nṛ0 tā0 1-2 | iti | tenāntarikṣeṇopalakṣita ākāśe vartamānayostayoriddyāvāpṛthivyoreva saṃbandhi payo jalaṃ ghṛtavadghṛtasadṛśaṃ viprā medhāvinaḥ prāṇino dhītibhiḥ karmabhī rihanti | lihanti | yadvā | ghṛtavadghṛtaṃ sāraṃ tenopetaṃ rihanti | lihervyatyayena rephaḥ | gandharvasya | dhṛñ dhāraṇe | gavi gan dhṛño va iti vapratyayaḥ | tatsaṃniyogena gośabdasya ca gannādeśaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "The firm place of the Gandharva is the mid-air; so it is recorded in the Tāpanīya branch: 'the mid-air, frequented by the hosts of Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Apsarases' (Nṛ. Tā. 1-2). The *viprāḥ*, wise living beings, *rihanti*, lick, *dhītibhiḥ*, by their rites, the *payaḥ*, water, *ghṛtavat*, like ghee, belonging *tayoḥ it*, to those two alone — Heaven and Earth — that are in the sky marked by that mid-air. Or: *ghṛtavat* — *ghṛta* is the essence; they lick [the water] furnished with it." (Grammatical tail: the *r* of *lih* by *vyatyaya*; *gandharvasya*, *dhṛñ dhāraṇe*, the suffix *va* by *gavi gan dhṛño vaḥ*, and along with it the substitute *gan* for the word *go*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**गन्धर्वस्य (gandharvasya)** — of the Gandharvas | **ध्रुवे (dhruve)** — eternal | **पदे (pade)** — in the place, the mid-air (sky) (being there) | **तयोः इत् (tayoḥ it)** — belonging to just those two (Heaven and Earth) | **पयः (payaḥ)** — the water | **घृतवत् (ghṛtavat)** — like ghee | **विप्राः (viprāḥ)** — the wise | **धीतिभिः (dhītibhiḥ)** — by good rites | **रिहन्ति (rihanti)** — taste.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The wise, as the fruit of their good deeds, taste like ghee the water belonging to the heavenly world and the earth, which is in the sky.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The wise men sitting in the eternal home of the Gandharvas taste, through their pious acts the essence of all good things of both heaven and earth as the ghee is the essence of milk.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The meaning of this ṛk fits properly if some words are supplied: in milk the essence is ghee; likewise in heaven and earth there are many things that are the essence. The main intention is that intelligent people, by the performance of sacrifice and the like, reach the eternal world of the Gandharvas (the world of mid-air), the best place, and there enjoy the finest essential things of heaven and earth.

### Page 111 — Rik 14: Special Topics (end), grammar

**घृतवत् पयः (ghṛtavat payaḥ)** — like ghee, the essence in milk; or, since *payaḥ* also means water, it may be said to mean the essential things such as soma juice.

**धीतिभिः (dhītibhiḥ)** — *karmabhiḥ |* by the performance of good rites such as sacrifice.

**गन्धर्वस्य ध्रुवे पदे (gandharvasya dhruve pade)** — the commentator has quoted the sentence of the Tāpanīya branch, *yakṣagandharvāpsarogaṇasevitam antarikṣam* (Nṛ. Tā. 1-2), to say that the chief place of the Gandharvas is the mid-air. Or it may also be said to mean: in the best place (world) frequented by the Gandharva folk. The main intention is that, by good conduct such as sacrifice, they reach the best place, the world of the Gandharvas and the like, and there enjoy the finest things, the essence of heaven and the earthly world.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**रिहन्ति (rihanti)** — *liha āsvādane*; *r* for the *l* by *vyatyaya*; *laṭ*, third person plural *jhi*; by *jho 'ntaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-3) the substitute *ant* for *jh*; by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) *śap* is dropped (*luk*): it becomes *rihanti*.

**गन्धर्वस्य (gandharvasya)** — by *gavi gan dhṛño vaḥ*, when the word *go* is *upapada*, after the root *dhṛñ dhāraṇe*, the suffix *va*, and the substitute *gan* for the word *go*: so with the suffix *va* and the substitute *gan* laid down along with it, *gan* + *dhṛ* + *va*; *guṇa* comes followed by *r*: it becomes *gandharva*. The sūtra *gavi gan…* is not in the Uṇādi [list]. ॥14॥

*(A bar under स्यो, a stroke over पृ, bars under क्ष and नि, a stroke over श (निवेशनी). Line 2: strokes over च्छा, र्म and थः; bars under नः and स.)*

### Page 112 — Rik 15: Pada, bhāṣya

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> स्योना । पृथिवि । भव । अनृक्षरा । निऽवेशनी ॥
> यच्छ । नः । शर्म । सऽप्रथः ॥१५॥
>
> *syonā | pṛthivi | bhava | anṛkṣarā | ni 'veśanī ||*
> *yaccha | naḥ | śarma | sa 'prathaḥ ||15||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० ८-१४, आ० गृ० २-३-६, नि० ९-३२, उ० ३-९, पा० ६-३-७४, पा० २-२-२८, पा० ६-३-८२; उ० ३-७५ is read with doubt [?]. Read टेश्च यो इत्यादेशः [?]. The bhāṣya ends with ॥६॥, the close of the sixth varga.)*

> स्योना पृथिवीत्येषा महानाम्नीव्रते भूमिस्पर्शने विनियुक्ता । एतद्विदं ब्रह्मचारिणमिति खण्डे सूत्रितं । स्योना पृथिवि भवेति समाप्य । आ० ८-१४ । इति ॥ स्मार्ते हेमन्तप्रत्यवरोहणेऽप्येषा जप्या । मार्गशीर्ष्यां प्रत्यवरोहणमिति खण्डे सूत्रितं । तस्मिन्नुपविश्य स्योना पृथिवि भवेति जपित्वा । आ० गृ० २-३-६ । इति ॥
>
> *syonā pṛthivītyeṣā mahānāmnīvrate bhūmisparśane viniyuktā | etadvidaṃ brahmacāriṇamiti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | syonā pṛthivi bhaveti samāpya | ā0 8-14 | iti || smārte hemantapratyavarohaṇe 'pyeṣā japyā | mārgaśīrṣyāṃ pratyavarohaṇamiti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | tasminnupaviśya syonā pṛthivi bhaveti japitvā | ā0 gṛ0 2-3-6 | iti ||*

**Translation (application):** "This ṛk *syonā pṛthivi* is used in the *mahānāmnī* vow, at the touching of the ground; it is laid down in the section *etadvidaṃ brahmacāriṇam*: 'having finished with *syonā pṛthivi bhava*' (Āśv. 8-14). In the *smārta* rite of the winter *pratyavarohaṇa* too this is to be muttered; it is laid down in the section *mārgaśīrṣyāṃ pratyavarohaṇam*: 'having sat down on it and muttered *syonā pṛthivi bhava*' (Āśv. Gṛ. 2-3-6)."

> हे पृथिवि स्योनत्वादिगुणयुक्ता भव । स्योनशब्दो विस्तीर्णवाची । तथा च वाजसनेयब्राह्मणे स्योनशब्दोपेतं कंचिन्मन्त्रमुदाहृत्य व्याख्यातं । इन्द्रस्योरुमाविश स्योनः स्योनमिति विस्तीर्णो विस्तीर्णमित्येव तदाहेति । यद्वा । स्योनशब्दः सुखवाची । तथा च यास्कवाक्यमुदाहरिष्यते । अनृक्षरा कण्टकरहिता निवेशनी निवासस्थानभूता सप्रथो विस्तारयुक्तं शर्म शरणं नोऽस्मभ्यं यच्छ । हे पृथिवि देहि । तामेतामृचमुदाहृत्य यास्क एवं व्याचष्टे । सुखा नः पृथिवि भवानृक्षरा निवेशन्यृक्षरः कण्टक ऋच्छतेः कण्टकः कन्तपो वा कृन्ततेर्वा कण्टतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मण उद्गततमो भवति यच्छ नः शर्म शरणं सर्वतः पृथु । नि० ९-३२ । इति ॥ स्योना । षिवु तन्तुसंताने । सिवेष्टेर्यू च । उ० ३-९ । इति नप्रत्ययः । टेश्च यो इत्यादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । स्योना पृथिवीत्यनयोर्भवेत्याख्यातेनैवान्वयो न परस्परं । अतोऽसामर्थ्यान्नैव पराङ्गवद्भावाभावादोकारस्य नामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । अनृक्षरा । ऋषी गतौ । गच्छत्यन्तरित्यृक्षरः कण्टकः । तन्यृषिभ्यां क्सरन् । उ० ३-७५ । षढोः कः सीति कत्वं । आदेशप्रत्यययोरिति षत्वं । नञा बहुव्रीहिः । तस्मान्नुडचि । पा० ६-३-७४ । इति नुडागमः । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । निविशन्त्यस्यामिति निवेशनी । करणाधिकरणयोश्चेति ल्युट् । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । यच्छ । दाण् दाने । पाघ्रेत्यादिना यच्छादेशः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घः । सप्रथः । प्रथ प्रख्याने । असुन् । प्रथसा सह वर्तत इति तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे । पा० २-२-२८ । इति समासः । वोपसर्जनस्य । पा० ६-३-८२ । इति सभावः । कृत्स्वरः ॥६॥
>
> *he pṛthivi syonatvādiguṇayuktā bhava | syonaśabdo vistīrṇavācī | tathā ca vājasaneyabrāhmaṇe syonaśabdopetaṃ kaṃcinmantramudāhṛtya vyākhyātaṃ | indrasyorumāviśa syonaḥ syonamiti vistīrṇo vistīrṇamityeva tadāheti | yadvā | syonaśabdaḥ sukhavācī | tathā ca yāskavākyamudāhariṣyate | anṛkṣarā kaṇṭakarahitā niveśanī nivāsasthānabhūtā sapratho vistārayuktaṃ śarma śaraṇaṃ no 'smabhyaṃ yaccha | he pṛthivi dehi | tāmetāmṛcamudāhṛtya yāska evaṃ vyācaṣṭe | sukhā naḥ pṛthivi bhavānṛkṣarā niveśanyṛkṣaraḥ kaṇṭaka ṛcchateḥ kaṇṭakaḥ kantapo vā kṛntatervā kaṇṭatervā syādgatikarmaṇa udgatatamo bhavati yaccha naḥ śarma śaraṇaṃ sarvataḥ pṛthu | ni0 9-32 | iti || syonā | ṣivu tantusaṃtāne | siveṣṭeryū ca | u0 3-9 | iti napratyayaḥ | ṭeśca yo ityādeśaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | syonā pṛthivītyanayorbhavetyākhyātenaivānvayo na parasparaṃ | ato 'sāmarthyānnaiva parāṅgavadbhāvābhāvādokārasya nāmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | anṛkṣarā | ṛṣī gatau | gacchatyantarityṛkṣaraḥ kaṇṭakaḥ | tanyṛṣibhyāṃ ksaran | u0 3-75 | ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ sīti katvaṃ | ādeśapratyayayoriti ṣatvaṃ | nañā bahuvrīhiḥ | tasmānnuḍaci | pā0 6-3-74 | iti nuḍāgamaḥ | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | niviśantyasyāmiti niveśanī | karaṇādhikaraṇayośceti lyuṭ | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvaṃ | yaccha | dāṇ dāne | pāghretyādinā yacchādeśaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghaḥ | saprathaḥ | pratha prakhyāne | asun | prathasā saha vartata iti tena saheti tulyayoge | pā0 2-2-28 | iti samāsaḥ | vopasarjanasya | pā0 6-3-82 | iti sabhāvaḥ | kṛtsvaraḥ ||6||*

**Translation:** "O Earth, *bhava*, be possessed of the qualities of *syona*-ness and the rest. The word *syona* means 'wide': so in the Vājasaneya-brāhmaṇa, citing a mantra with the word *syona*, it is explained: '*indrasyorum āviśa syonaḥ syonam* — it says "wide, wide" only.' Or the word *syona* means 'happiness', as Yāska's statement will be cited. *Anṛkṣarā*, free from thorns, *niveśanī*, being a place of dwelling, *yaccha*, give, *naḥ*, us, *śarma*, shelter, *saprathaḥ*, furnished with breadth: O Earth, give. Citing this ṛk Yāska explains it thus: '*Be happy (sukhā) for us, O Earth, thornless, a dwelling place. Ṛkṣara is a thorn, from ṛcchati; kaṇṭaka is from kantapa, or from kṛntati, or it may be from kaṇṭati, meaning to go: it stands most up. Give us shelter, wide on all sides*' (Ni. 9-32)." (Grammatical tail: *syonā*, *ṣivu tantusaṃtāne*, the suffix *na* by *siveṣ ṭer yū ca* (U. 3-9), with the substitute for the *ṭi* [as read]; the suffix accent; *syonā* and *pṛthivi* are each construed only with the verb *bhava*, not with each other; so, for lack of mutual connection there is no treating as part of the following, and the *o* does not take the vocative initial udātta; *anṛkṣarā*, *ṛṣī gatau*, 'it goes within': *ṛkṣara*, a thorn; *ksaran* by *tanyṛṣibhyāṃ ksaran* (U. 3-75 [?]); *k* by *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si*, *ṣ* by *ādeśapratyayayoḥ*; a bahuvrīhi with *nañ*; the augment *nuṭ* by *tasmān nuḍ aci* (Pā. 6-3-74); the last member final udātta by *nañsubhyām*; *niveśanī*, 'they enter into her', *lyuṭ* by *karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca*, the syllable before the suffix udātta by *liti*; *yaccha*, *dāṇ dāne*, the substitute *yaccha* by *pāghrā…*, lengthening by *dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ*; *saprathaḥ*, *pratha prakhyāne*, *asun*; 'that which is with breadth', compounded by *tena saheti tulyayoge* (Pā. 2-2-28), *sa* by *vopasarjanasya* (Pā. 6-3-82); the *kṛt* accent.)

### Page 113 — Rik 15: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**पृथिवि (pṛthivi)** — O Earth (you) | **स्योना (syonā)** — wide, or bringing happiness | **भव (bhava)** — be | **नः (naḥ)** — for us | **अनृक्षरा (anṛkṣarā)** — free from thorns | **निवेशनी (niveśanī)** — as a dwelling place | **सप्रथः (saprathaḥ)** — wide | **शर्म (śarma)** — shelter | **यच्छ (yaccha)** — give.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O goddess Earth, being always wide and free from thorns, a dwelling place, give us a wide shelter.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Earth, give us extensive abode free from thorns; give us great happiness.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The application of this ṛk is in both *śrauta* and *smārta* rites. In the vow (rite) called *mahānāmnī* it is recited at the time of touching the ground. This matter is explained in the section *etadvidaṃ brahmacāriṇam* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra by the sūtra *syonā pṛthivi bhaveti samāpya* (Ā. 8-14).

In *smārta* rites too, in the rite called *hemanta-pratyavarohaṇa*, this mantra is to be muttered. This matter is explained in the section *mārgaśīrṣyāṃ pratyavarohaṇam* of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra by the sūtra *tasminn upaviśya syonā pṛthivi bhaveti japitvā* (Ā. Gṛ. 2-3-6).

**स्योना (syonā)** — the commentator says this word indicates two kinds of meaning, 'wide' and 'bringing happiness', and cites the Vājasaneya-brāhmaṇa sentence *indrasyorum āviśa syonaḥ syonam iti vistīrṇo vistīrṇam ity eva tad āha*, which sets forth the meaning 'wide'.

He has cited the explanation Yāska gave of this ṛk:

> सुखा नः पृथिवि भवानृक्षरा निवेशन्यृक्षरः कण्टक ऋच्छतेः कण्टकः कन्तपो वा कृन्ततेर्वा कण्टतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मण उद्गततमो भवति यच्छ नः शर्म शरणं सर्वतः पृथु ॥ (नि० ९-३२)
>
> *sukhā naḥ pṛthivi bhavānṛkṣarā niveśanyṛkṣaraḥ kaṇṭaka ṛcchateḥ kaṇṭakaḥ kantapo vā kṛntatervā kaṇṭatervā syādgatikarmaṇa udgatatamo bhavati yaccha naḥ śarma śaraṇaṃ sarvataḥ pṛthu || (ni0 9-32)*

### Page 114 — Rik 15: Special Topics (end), grammar

According to this derivation, *syonā* = *sukhā*, *anṛkṣarā* = *niṣkaṇṭakā*, *niveśanī* = fit for dwelling, *śarma* = *sukham*, *saprathaḥ* = wide on all sides. That is, it is a prayer to the earth: give a dwelling place, happy, free from thorns (free from troubles) and fit to live in, and happiness.

**अनृक्षरा (anṛkṣarā)** — *akṣara* [as printed; for *ṛkṣara*] means — *ṛcchateḥ gatikarmaṇaḥ kṛntater vā* — the thorn, the trouble, formed from the root *ṛcch*, which conveys the senses of going, obstructing, harming and so on. *Anṛkṣara* means free from such troubles, free from thorns.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**स्योना (syonā)** — the root *ṣivu tantusantāne*. By *siveṣ ṭer yo ca* [as printed] (U. Sū. 3-29 [?]), *naḥ* being carried on from *dhāpṛvasyajyatibhyo naḥ* (U. Sū. 3-26 [?]): the sense of the sūtra is that after the root *ṣiv* the suffix *na* comes, and the substitute *yo* for the *iv*, the *ṭi* of the root. By *anekālśit sarvasya* the substitute *yo* comes for the whole *iv*, not only for the *v*. By *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) *s* for *ṣ*: *syo* + *na*; the suffix accent comes; with *ṭāp* marked by ending in *a*, it becomes *syonā*: so the Veda commentary. In the Uṇādi sūtras as now printed the reading is *siveṣ ṭer yū ca* (U. Sū. 3-29 [?]). On this view the substitute *yū* comes for the *iv*, the *ṭi*: *syū* + *na*. Now by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) *guṇa*, *o* for the *ū*, would be obtained. Yet whether *guṇa* comes after making the short substitute *yu* or after making the long substitute *yū*, it must become *syo*; there is no difference at all. Since there is a saving of a mora, the substitute *yu* alone could have been laid down. Even so, by the force of laying down the long substitute, *guṇa* does not come; by this sūtra the form *syūnaḥ* alone is established. *Syūnaḥ* means the sun. Since there is the word *bahula* in *uṇādayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-1), when only the suffix *na* comes after the root *ṣiv*: *siv* + *na*; by *chvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-19) — when a nasal, or the suffix *kvip*, or a *jhal*-initial suffix that is *kit* or *ṅit* follows, *ś* for the *ch* joined by the augment *tuk*, and *ūṭ* for *v*, come as substitutes — the substitute *ūṭ* for the *v*: *si* + *ū* + *na*; when both the *yaṇ* substitute and *guṇa* are obtained, since the *yaṇ* substitute has its cause inside, it is internal (*antaraṅga*); so by *asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge* (Paribhā. 51 [?]) first the *yaṇ* substitute, then *guṇa* and *ṭāp*: it becomes *syonā*. This description is clear in the *vṛtti* on the sūtra *chvoḥ śūḍ* and in the *Kaiyaṭa* on *yena vidhis tadantasya* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72).

### Page 115 — Rik 15: grammar (continued)

According to the Medinī lexicon, *syonaḥ kiraṇasūryayoḥ*, the meaning ray or sun results for the word *syona*. Yet here, according to the Brāhmaṇa, 'wide', and according to the Nirukta (3-6-14 [?], as read), 'happiness', are the meanings described.

For *pṛthivi*: by *sāmantritam* (Pā. Sū. 2-3-48) — the vocative nominative singular gets the name *āmantrita* — it has the name *āmantrita*. By *subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare* (Pā. Sū. 2-1-2), let the word *syonā*, ending in *sup*, be as a part of the word *pṛthivi*; then by *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) the initial udātta would come, and the *o* in *syo* might be said to be initially udātta. But *subāmantrite* applies only where there is connection in the form of mutual construction. Since *subāmantrite* is a rule about words (*padavidhi*), by the *paribhāṣā* *samarthaḥ padavidhiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-1-1) it results that it comes only where there is that connection. In the present case the two words *sukhena* [as printed] and *pṛthivi* are construed with the verb *bhava*; they have no mutual construction with each other. So, for lack of connection, the treating as part of the following does not come. Thus, since the initial udātta of the vocative does not come by the sixth-book sūtra, the *o* is not initially udātta.

**अनृक्षरा (anṛkṣarā)** — the root *ṛṣī gatau*; with the analysis *ṛṣati*, 'goes inside (within)', it becomes *ṛkṣara*. It means a thorn, that is, a prickle. By *tanyṛṣibhyāṃ ksaran* (U. Sū. 3-75 [?]) — after these roots, *tanu vistāre* and *ṛṣī gatau*, the suffix *ksaran* comes — the suffix *ksaran* after the root *ṛṣ*. With the *it*-name and dropping for the *k*: *ṛṣ* + *sara*. Now by *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-41) — before *s*, *k* for *ṣ* and *ḍh* — the substitute *k* for *ṣ*: *ṛk* + *sara*; by *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-59) — after the *iṇ* vowels and the *ka*-row, *ṣ* for an *s* that is a substitute or part of a suffix — *ṣ* for the *s*: it becomes *ṛkṣara*. *Na vidyamānaḥ ṛkṣaraḥ yasyāṃ sā*: by *nañaḥ 'sty arthānāṃ vācyo vā cottarapadalopaḥ* the *nañ* compound with the dropping of the last member *vidyamāna*; by *nalopo nañaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-73) the *n* of *nañ* is dropped; by *tasmān nuḍ aci* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-74) — the vowel-initial last member after *nañ* with its *n* dropped takes the augment *nuṭ* — the augment *nuṭ*: *anṛkṣara*. By *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member's own accent would be obtained; overriding it, by *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) — in a bahuvrīhi compound the last member after *nañ* and *su* is final udātta — the last member is final udātta.

### Page 116 — Rik 15: grammar (continued)

**निवेशनी (niveśanī)** — *niviśanti asyām iti niveśanī*. After the root *viśa praveśane* preceded by the prefix *ni*, by *karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-117) — in the instrumental sense and in the locative sense, *lyuṭ* comes after roots — the suffix *lyuṭ*; by *yuvor anākau* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the substitute *ana* for *yu*: *niviś* + *ana*, *guṇa* of the light penultimate; by *liti* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the *e* before the suffix is udātta; since the suffix is *ṭit*, by the sūtra *ṭiḍḍhāṇañ…* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-15) *ṅīp*: it becomes *niveśanī*.

**यच्छ (yaccha)** — the root *dāṇ dāne*. By *pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartisartiśadasadāṃ pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchadhauśīyasīdāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78): *pā pāne*, *ghrā gandhopādāne*, *dhmā śabdāgnisaṃyogayoḥ*, *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*, *mnā abhyāse*, *dāṇ dāne*, *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*, *ṛ gatiprāpaṇayoḥ* [as printed: *gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*], *sṛ gatau* — for *sarti*, according to the *vārttika* *sarter vegitāyāṃ gatau dhāvādeśaḥ*, the root *sṛ* conveying going in the form of speed is intended here — *śadḷ śātane*, *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*: when a suffix beginning with the *it*-named *ś* follows, these take in order the substitutes *piba*, *jighra*, *dhama*, *tiṣṭha*, *mana*, *yaccha*, *paśya*, *ṛccha*, *dhau*, *śīya*, *sīda*; so after the root *dāṇ*, after *loṭ*, *sip* and *śap*, the substitute *yaccha*: *yaccha* + *si*. By *ser hy apic ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-87) *hi* for *si*; by *ato heḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-105) *hi* is dropped (*luk*): it becomes *yaccha*. Now by *dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-135) — in a mantra, at the time of the Saṃhitā, the short *a* at the end of a two-vowelled word ending in *tiṅ* is lengthened — lengthening: it becomes *yacchā*.

**सप्रथः (saprathaḥ)** — the root *pratha prakhyāne*. By *sarvadhātubhyo 'sun* (U. Sū. 4-6-28 [?]) the suffix *asun*. *Prathaḥ* is initially udātta by the *nit* accent. *Tena saheti tulyayoge* (Pā. Sū. 2-2-28): *tena* indicates one ending in the third case. Connection in one and the same action, such as going, is called *tulyayoga*. Thus the indeclinable *saha*, which indicates *tulyayoga*, compounds with one ending in the third case, and it is a bahuvrīhi: so the bahuvrīhi compound *prathasā saha vartate*. *Prathaḥ* means breadth. *Śarma* means a house; that both *śarma* and *prathaḥ* are construed in the one action *vartate* is shown by the word *saha*. So the word *saha* is compounded with the word *prathasā* ending in the third case. In *vopasarjanasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-82), from *aluk uttarapade* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-1) *uttarapade* is the heading; from *sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-78) the words *sahasya* and *saḥ* are carried on. *Upasarjanam asya astīty upasarjanam*: so

### Page 117 (upper) — Rik 15: grammar (end)

with the *ac* suffix in the sense of possession; the word *uttarapada* is conventional for the last part of a compound. So, by the maxim *yaṃ vinā yan nopapadyate tat tenaivākṣipyate*, the compound is implied. With *upasarjanasya*, a sixth case, *samāsasya* becomes *upasarjanavataḥ samāsasya*. But since in every compound some member is subordinate, by the force of the qualifier *upasarjanasya* it results to mean a compound whose members are all subordinate. Thus the sense of the sūtra is established: for *saha* before the last member of a compound whose members are all subordinate (a bahuvrīhi), the substitute *sa* comes optionally. By this, when the substitute *sa* comes for *saha*, it becomes *saprathaḥ*. Since this is a bahuvrīhi, and since the *kṛt* accent by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* applies only in a tatpuruṣa compound, it does not come here. By the word *bahula* in *parādiś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199), after compounding, the beginning of the last member is udātta. ॥15॥

> यं विना यन्नोपपद्यते तत्तेनैवाक्षिप्यते ।
>
> *yaṃ vinā yannopapadyate tattenaivākṣipyate |*

### Page 117 (lower) — Sūkta 22, Rik 16 *(the Viṣṇu ṛks begin here)*

>
> *áto devā́ avantu no yáto víṣṇur vicakramé |*

*(Strokes over तो (अतो), अ (अवन्तु) and वि (विष्णुः); bars under दे, नो, तो (यतो) and क्र. Line 2: bars under पृ, थि and स; a stroke over म.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० ६-६, आ० ९-११, आ० १-११, आ० १-५, तै० सं० ५-२-१-१, पा० ५-३-७, पा० ५-३-५, पा० ५-३-१, उ० ३-३९.)*

> प्रातःसवने सोमातिरेक एकं शस्त्रं शंसनीयं । अत्रातो देवा इत्याद्याः षडृचः । सोमातिरेक इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । महाँ इन्द्रो य ओजसातो देवा अवन्तु न इत्यैन्द्रीभिर्वैष्णवीभिश्च । आ० ६-६ । इति ॥ अप्तोर्यामेऽच्छावाकातिरिक्तोक्थेऽप्येताः षडृचः स्तोत्रियानुरूपार्थाः । तथा च यस्य पशव इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । अतो देवा अवन्तु न इति स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ । आ० ९-११ । इति ॥ दर्शपूर्णमासयोः प्रायश्चित्तहोमेऽप्याद्ये विनियुक्ते । तथैव वेदं पत्न्या इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । अतो देवा अवन्तु न इति द्वाभ्यां व्याहृतिभिश्च । आ० १-११ । इति ॥ याज्यानुवाक्ययोर्मध्ये लौकिकभाषणेऽतो देवा इत्येषा जप्या । सूत्रितं हि । आपद्यतो देवा अवन्तु न इति जपेत् । आ० १-५ । इति ॥
>
> *prātaḥsavane somātireka ekaṃ śastraṃ śaṃsanīyaṃ | atrāto devā ityādyāḥ ṣaḍṛcaḥ | somātireka iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | mahām̐ indro ya ojasāto devā avantu na ityaindrībhirvaiṣṇavībhiśca | ā0 6-6 | iti || aptoryāme 'cchāvākātiriktokthe 'pyetāḥ ṣaḍṛcaḥ stotriyānurūpārthāḥ | tathā ca yasya paśava iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | ato devā avantu na iti stotriyānurūpau | ā0 9-11 | iti || darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ prāyaścittahome 'pyādye viniyukte | tathaiva vedaṃ patnyā iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | ato devā avantu na iti dvābhyāṃ vyāhṛtibhiśca | ā0 1-11 | iti || yājyānuvākyayormadhye laukikabhāṣaṇe 'to devā ityeṣā japyā | sūtritaṃ hi | āpadyato devā avantu na iti japet | ā0 1-5 | iti ||*

### Page 118 — Rik 16: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**Translation (application):** "At the morning pressing, at the *somātireka*, one *śastra* is to be recited; here the six ṛks beginning *ato devāḥ*; it is laid down in the section *somātireka*: '*mahāṃ indro ya ojasā* and *ato devā avantu naḥ*, with the ṛks to Indra and to Viṣṇu' (Āśv. 6-6). In the *aptoryāma*, at the extra *uktha* of the *acchāvāka*, these six ṛks serve as *stotriya* and *anurūpa*; so it is laid down in the section *yasya paśavaḥ*: '*ato devā avantu naḥ*, the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*' (Āśv. 9-11). At the *darśapūrṇamāsa*, in the expiatory offering, the first two are used; likewise it is laid down in the section *vedaṃ patnyai*: 'with the two, *ato devā avantu naḥ*, and with the *vyāhṛtis*' (Āśv. 1-11). If there is worldly talk between the *yājyā* and the *anuvākyā*, this ṛk *ato devāḥ* is to be muttered; for it is laid down: 'in a mishap, he should mutter *ato devā avantu naḥ*' (Āśv. 1-5)."

> विष्णुः परमेश्वरः सप्तधामभिः सप्तभिर्गायत्र्यादिभिश्छन्दोभिः साधनभूतैर्यतः पृथिव्या यस्माद्भूप्रदेशाद्विचक्रमे । विविधं पादक्रमणं कृतवान् अतोऽस्मात्पृथिवीप्रदेशान्नोऽस्मान्देवा अवन्तु । विष्णोः पृथिव्यादिलोकेषु छन्दोभिः साधनैर्जयं तैत्तिरीया आमनन्ति । विष्णुमुखा वै देवाश्छन्दोभिरिमाँल्लोकाननपजय्यमभ्यजयन् । तै० सं० ५-२-१-१ । इति । विष्णोस्त्रिविक्रमावतारे पादत्रयक्रमणस्य पृथिव्युपादानं । पृथिवीप्रदेशाद्रक्षणं नाम भूलोके वर्तमानानां पापनिवारणं ॥ अतः । एतच्छब्दात्पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् । पा० ५-३-७ । इति तसिल् । एतदोऽश् । पा० ५-३-५ । इत्यशादेशः । लित्स्वरेणाकार उदात्तः । यतः । तसिलः प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः । पा० ५-३-१ । इति विभक्तिसंज्ञायां त्यदाद्यत्वं । लित्स्वरः । विष्णुः । विषेः किच्च । उ० ३-३९ । इति नुप्रत्ययः । कित्त्वान्न गुणः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तत्वं । विचक्रमे । सुबिति योगविभागाद्विशब्दस्य समासः । समासान्तोदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तयोगान्न निघातः । सप्त । सुपां सुलुगिति भिसो लुक् । धामभिः । दधातेरातो मनिन्निति मनिन् । नित्स्वरः ॥
>
> *viṣṇuḥ parameśvaraḥ saptadhāmabhiḥ saptabhirgāyatryādibhiśchandobhiḥ sādhanabhūtairyataḥ pṛthivyā yasmādbhūpradeśādvicakrame | vividhaṃ pādakramaṇaṃ kṛtavān ato 'smātpṛthivīpradeśānno 'smāndevā avantu | viṣṇoḥ pṛthivyādilokeṣu chandobhiḥ sādhanairjayaṃ taittirīyā āmananti | viṣṇumukhā vai devāśchandobhirimām̐llokānanapajayyamabhyajayan | tai0 saṃ0 5-2-1-1 | iti | viṣṇostrivikramāvatāre pādatrayakramaṇasya pṛthivyupādānaṃ | pṛthivīpradeśādrakṣaṇaṃ nāma bhūloke vartamānānāṃ pāpanivāraṇaṃ || ataḥ | etacchabdātpañcamyāstasil | pā0 5-3-7 | iti tasil | etado 'ś | pā0 5-3-5 | ityaśādeśaḥ | litsvareṇākāra udāttaḥ | yataḥ | tasilaḥ prāgdiśo vibhaktiḥ | pā0 5-3-1 | iti vibhaktisaṃjñāyāṃ tyadādyatvaṃ | litsvaraḥ | viṣṇuḥ | viṣeḥ kicca | u0 3-39 | iti nupratyayaḥ | kittvānna guṇaḥ | nidityanuvṛtterādyudāttatvaṃ | vicakrame | subiti yogavibhāgādviśabdasya samāsaḥ | samāsāntodāttatvaṃ | yadvṛttayogānna nighātaḥ | sapta | supāṃ sulugiti bhiso luk | dhāmabhiḥ | dadhāterāto maninniti manin | nitsvaraḥ ||*

**Translation:** "*Yataḥ pṛthivyāḥ*, from which region of the earth Viṣṇu, the supreme Lord, *vicakrame*, made various steps, *saptadhāmabhiḥ*, with the seven metres Gāyatrī and the rest as means — *ataḥ*, from this region of the earth, may the gods *avantu*, protect, *naḥ*, us. The Taittirīyas record Viṣṇu's conquest of the worlds, the earth and the rest, by the metres as means: 'The gods with Viṣṇu at their head, by the metres, won these worlds so that they cannot be won back' (Tai. Saṃ. 5-2-1-1). In Viṣṇu's incarnation as Trivikrama, the earth is mentioned [as the starting point] of the stepping of three steps. 'Protection from the region of the earth' means the warding off of the sins of those who live in the world of earth." (Grammatical tail: *ataḥ*, *tasil* after the ablative of *etad* by *pañcamyās tasil* (Pā. 5-3-7), the substitute *aś* by *etado 'ś* (Pā. 5-3-5), the *a* udātta by the *lit* accent; *yataḥ*, the suffixes from *tasil* up to *diś* being named *vibhakti* by *prāg diśo vibhaktiḥ* (Pā. 5-3-1), the *a* of the *tyadādi* words; the *lit* accent; *viṣṇuḥ*, the suffix *nu* by *viṣeḥ kic ca* (U. 3-39), no *guṇa* as it is *kit*, initial udātta because *nit* is carried on; *vicakrame*, the compounding of *vi* by the division of the rule at *sup*, the compound-final udātta, no loss of accent because of connection with *yad*; *sapta*, the *bhis* dropped by *supāṃ suluk*; *dhāmabhiḥ*, *manin* by *dadhāter āto manin*, the *nit* accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**यतः (yataḥ)** — from which | **पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ)** — from the earth | **विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ)** — Viṣṇu | **सप्तभिः (saptabhiḥ)** — seven | **धामभिः (dhāmabhiḥ)** — together with the metres Gāyatrī and the rest | **विचक्रमे (vicakrame)** — set out | **अतः (ataḥ)** — from that earth | **देवाः (devāḥ)** — the gods | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **अवन्तु (avantu)** — may they protect.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

When Viṣṇu, as Trivikrama, was taking his steps, from whatever region of the earth he set out, furnished with the metres Gāyatrī and the rest — may the gods protect us who are in that region of the earth.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> May the gods protect us from that portion of the earth whence Vishnu put his steps aided by seven meters.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The application of this mantra is of four kinds. In the rite of pressing soma called the morning pressing, at the time of reciting the mantras called *somātireka* —

### Page 119 — Rik 16: Special Topics (continued)

— this mantra is recited as a *śastra* mantra. This matter is explained in the section *somātireka* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra by the sūtra *mahāṃ indro ya ojasā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-1) *ato devā avantu naḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-16) *ity aindrībhir vaiṣṇavībhiś ca* (Ā. 6-6).

In the soma sacrifice called *aptoryāma*, in the recitation of the *uktha* mantras by the priest called *acchāvāka*, the six ṛks beginning *ato devāḥ* are to be recited as the *stotriya* mantras. This matter is explained in the section *yasya paśavaḥ* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra by the sūtra *ato devā avantu na iti stotriyānurūpau* (Ā. 9-11).

In the *darśapūrṇamāsa* sacrifices, at the time of the expiatory offering, the first two ṛks of this sūkta are used. This matter is stated in the section *vedaṃ patnyai* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra in the sūtra *ato devā avantu na iti dvābhyāṃ vyāhṛtibhiś ca* (Ā. 1-11).

If, at the time of reciting the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* mantras, worldly talk is made between these two mantras for some other reason, this ṛk *ato devāḥ* is to be muttered as an expiatory mantra: so it is stated in the sūtra *āpady ato devā avantu na iti japet* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra (Ā. 1-5).

In this ṛk the subject of Viṣṇu is mentioned for the first time. Though Viṣṇu's pre-eminence is great in the Purāṇas and in the modern Vedānta works, in the Ṛgveda there are only five sūktas devoted to Viṣṇu. Besides, in many places Viṣṇu's name is indicated here and there along with other deities, chiefly with Indra. Viṣṇu's chief feat is said to be the placing of three steps. These three steps are in heaven, mid-air and earth. Besides, Viṣṇu's place called the highest step is reckoned the most excellent position.

In the Ṛgveda Viṣṇu's connection with Indra is seen to be closer than with other deities. Indra seeks Viṣṇu's help when slaying the demon Vṛtra. In the Yajurveda the subject of Viṣṇu is described in many ways. There are many mantras describing Viṣṇu as lord of the sacrifice and of the mountains, as the very form of sacrifice, and as leader of all the gods ("Leader"). The commentator has explained the word *viṣṇu* in this ṛk as *parameśvara* because, as Yāska says —

> विष्णुः अथ यद्विषितो भवति तद्विष्णुर्भवति । विष्णुर्विशतेर्वा व्यश्नोतेर्वा ।
>
> *viṣṇuḥ atha yadviṣito bhavati tadviṣṇurbhavati | viṣṇurviśatervā vyaśnotervā |*

— he is named Viṣṇu because he pervades everything, or because he enters and pervades everything, or because he pervades everything with his rays; so Viṣṇu may also be said to mean the sun: so the word *viṣṇu* has been explained. The explanation of the word *viṣṇu* is in the next ṛk too.

### Page 120 — Rik 16: Special Topics (end), grammar

**विचक्रमे (vicakrame)** — *vividhaṃ pādakramaṇaṃ kṛtavān*: he stepped over the region of the worlds, the earth and the rest, with his feet in various ways, that is, in many manners.

**सप्त धामभिः (sapta dhāmabhiḥ)** — *dhāma* means a place. Here the commentator has said that the word *dhāma* means metres; *sapta dhāmabhiḥ* means the seven metres Gāyatrī and the rest; or, if the meaning is taken as referring to the sun, it may be said to mean the seven rays (or the seven horses). In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā —

> विष्णुमुखा वै देवाश्छन्दोभिरिमाँल्लोकाननपजय्यमभ्यजयन् ॥ (तै० सं० ५-२-१-१)
>
> *viṣṇumukhā vai devāśchandobhirimām̐llokānanapajayyamabhyajayan || (tai0 saṃ0 5-2-1-1)*

— it is said that the gods, with Viṣṇu as their leader, won the worlds with the help of the metres. In the Purāṇas and the like there are extended descriptions of the legend that Viṣṇu, taking the Trivikrama incarnation, by the stepping of three steps gave back to the gods the earth, sky and mid-air that the demons had taken from them. It should be noted that the subtle description seen in the Veda is the source of the legends in the Purāṇas.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**अतः (ataḥ)** — by *pañcamyās tasil* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-7) — after the word *kim*, the pronouns other than *dvi* and the rest, and the word *bahu*, when they end in the fifth case, the suffix *tasil* comes optionally — the suffix *tasil* after the word *etad* ending in the fifth case: *etad* + *ṅasi* + *tas*. Now they make the sūtra *etado 'n* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-5) into two sūtras, *etadaḥ* and *an*. The first, *etadaḥ*, means that when the *prāgdiśīya* suffixes beginning with *r* and *th* follow, the substitutes *eta* and *it* come in order for the word *etad*; examples *etarhi*, *ittham*. *An* is the second sūtra. Here the word *rathoḥ* is not carried on from the previous sūtra. So the meaning is that when a *prāgdiśīya* suffix follows, the substitute *an* comes for the word *etad*. In the present case, when the substitute *an* comes by the second sūtra, since it has more than one letter, by *anekālśit sarvasya* it comes in place of the whole: *an* + *tas*; though the fifth case, a part of a stem ending in a *taddhita*, is dropped (*luk*) by *supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-71), the name *pada* comes because by *pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-62) the mark of the suffix remains. Since the name *pada* is not connected with the stem (*aṅga*), the prohibition of the suffix-mark by *na lumatāṅgasya* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-63) does not come. Thus by *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-7) the *n* of *an* is dropped; with *ru* and *visarga* for the *s* it becomes *ataḥ*. In the Mahābhāṣya the reading *an* ending in *n* is discussed. The author of the *Kaiyaṭa*, saying *iha kecid aśaṃ paṭhanti kecid anam | tatrottarapāṭhāpekṣayā*

### Page 121 — Rik 16: grammar (continued)

*vicāraḥ*, holds that the sūtra is read in two ways, *etado 'ś* and *etado 'n*. The author of the *vṛtti* has adopted the reading *etado 'ś*. Following his view, in the Veda commentary too the reading *etado 'ś* is accepted. On this view, as before, the division of the rule must be made and the meaning described. *Aś*, being *śit*, comes as a substitute for the whole; so it becomes *ataḥ*: only this much is the difference. The suffix is *lit*; so by *liti* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-93, as printed) the *a* before the suffix is udātta.

> इह केचिदशं पठन्ति केचिदनम् । तत्रोत्तरपाठापेक्षया विचारः ।
>
> *iha kecidaśaṃ paṭhanti kecidanam | tatrottarapāṭhāpekṣayā vicāraḥ |*

**यतः (yataḥ)** — *yasmāt yataḥ*: after the word *yad* ending in the fifth case, by *pañcamyās tasil*, *tasil*, and the fifth case is dropped. For this *tasil*, the suffixes laid down from the sūtra *prāg diśo vibhaktiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-1) up to the sūtra *dikśabdebhyaḥ saptamīpañcamīprathamābhyo digdeśakāleṣv astātiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-27) get the name *vibhakti*; so it has the name *vibhakti*. Therefore by *tyadādīnām aḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) — when a *vibhakti* follows, *a* is substituted for the final letter of the words of the *tyadādi* class — *a* for the *d* of the word *yad*; by *ato guṇe* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) the following form. As before, the *lit* accent comes.

**विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ)** — by *viṣeḥ kic ca* (U. Sū. 3-39), the sense of the sūtra is that after the root *viṣḷ vyāptau* the suffix *ṇu* comes, and it is both *kit* and *nit*. The *ṇuḥ* carried on from *snoḥ ṇuḥ* (U. Sū. 3-32 [?]); for *nuḥ* there is no occasion here. *Viṣ* + *ṇu*: since the suffix is *kit*, there is the prohibition *kṅiti ca*, so *guṇa* of the light penultimate does not come. Since the suffix is *nit*, *viṣṇu* is initially udātta by the *nit* accent.

**विचक्रमे (vicakrame)** — in *saha supā* (Pā. Sū. 2-1-4) they make the division of the sūtra into *saha* and *supā*. From *subāmantrite*, *sup* is carried on. From *samarthaḥ padavidhiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-1, as printed) *samarthaḥ* is obtained; it must be changed into one ending in the third case. Thus the sense of the first sūtra is that a word ending in *sup* is compounded with a connected word; since it is said *iṣṭasiddhyarthaṃ yogavibhāgaḥ*, to establish the form, by this sūtra a word ending in *sup* is compounded with a last member ending in *tiṅ*; but it results that this compound comes only in the Veda. By this sūtra the present word *vi*, ending in *sup*, is compounded with the word *cakrame* ending in *tiṅ*; so by *samāsasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223) the final udātta accent comes here. Since there is connection with *yad* in *yataḥ*, by *yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) — a word ending in *tiṅ* after a word in which there is the word *yad* is not unaccented —

### Page 122 (upper) — Rik 16: grammar (end)

— by this prohibition, the total lack of accent by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* does not come. The meaning of the second sūtra *supā* is that a word ending in *sup* is compounded with a connected word ending in *sup*. It is not needed in the present case.

**सप्त (sapta)** — for the instrumental plural suffix *bhis* coming after this word, *luk* by *supāṃ suluk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39).

**धामभिः (dhāmabhiḥ)** — the root *(ḍu)dhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*. It ends in *ā*. By *āto manin kvanib vanipaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-74) — when a word ending in *sup* or a prefix is *upapada*, after a root ending in *ā* the three suffixes *manin*, *kvanip*, *vanip*, and by the word *ca* the suffix *vic* too, come — the suffix *manin* comes. *Dhā* + *man*: by the *nit* accent this is initially udātta. When the instrumental plural suffix *bhis* is put, the *n* is dropped by *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya*: it becomes *dhāmabhiḥ*. ॥16॥

### Page 122 (lower) — Sūkta 22, Rik 17

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इ॒दं विष्णु॒र्वि च॑क्रमे त्रे॒धा नि द॑धे प॒दं ।
> समू॑ळ्हमस्य पांसु॒रे ॥१७॥
>
> *idáṃ viṣṇur ví cakrame tredhā́ ní dadhe padáṃ |*
> *sámūḷham asya pāṃsuré ||17||*

*(Bars under इ, ष्णु, त्रे and प; strokes over च (चक्रमे) and द (दधे). Line 2: a stroke over मू, a bar under सु. The print has समूळ्ह with ळ्ह.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इदं । विष्णुः । वि । चक्रमे । त्रेधा । नि । दधे । पदं ॥
> संऽऊळ्हं । अस्य । पांसुरे ॥१७॥
>
> *idaṃ | viṣṇuḥ | vi | cakrame | tredhā | ni | dadhe | padaṃ ||*
> *saṃ 'ūḷhaṃ | asya | pāṃsure ||17||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० १-६, ३-१०, ४-५, ४-८, नि० १२-१९, पा० ५-३-४६, पा० ६-१-१५, का० ५-२-१०७-१.)*

> वैष्णवोपांशुयाजस्येदं विष्णुरित्येषानुवाक्या । उक्ता देवता इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां । आ० १-६ । इति ॥ गार्हपत्याहवनीययोर्मध्ये श्वातिक्रमणेऽनयैव श्वपदेषु भस्म प्रक्षिपेत् । विध्यपराध इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । भस्मना शुनः पदं प्रतिवपेदिदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे । आ० ३-१० । इति ॥ आतिथ्यायां प्रधानस्य हविष एषैवानुवाक्या । अथातिथ्येळान्तेति खण्डे सूत्रितं । इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे तदस्य प्रियमभि पाथो अश्यां । आ० ४-५ । इति ॥ उपसत्सु वैष्णवस्यैषैवानुवाक्या । अथोपसदिति खण्डे सूत्रितं । गयस्फानो अमीवहेदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे । आ० ४-८ । इति ॥
>
> *vaiṣṇavopāṃśuyājasyedaṃ viṣṇurityeṣānuvākyā | uktā devatā iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | idaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame trirdevaḥ pṛthivīmeṣa etāṃ | ā0 1-6 | iti || gārhapatyāhavanīyayormadhye śvātikramaṇe 'nayaiva śvapadeṣu bhasma prakṣipet | vidhyaparādha iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | bhasmanā śunaḥ padaṃ prativapedidaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame | ā0 3-10 | iti || ātithyāyāṃ pradhānasya haviṣa eṣaivānuvākyā | athātithyeḷānteti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | idaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame tadasya priyamabhi pātho aśyāṃ | ā0 4-5 | iti || upasatsu vaiṣṇavasyaiṣaivānuvākyā | athopasaditi khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | gayasphāno amīvahedaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame | ā0 4-8 | iti ||*

### Page 123 — Rik 17: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English

**Translation (application):** "This ṛk *idaṃ viṣṇuḥ* is the *anuvākyā* of the *upāṃśu-yāja* to Viṣṇu; it is laid down in the section *uktā devatāḥ*: '*idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame*, *trir devaḥ pṛthivīm eṣa etām*' (Āśv. 1-6). If a dog passes between the *gārhapatya* and the *āhavanīya*, with this very ṛk one should throw ashes on the dog's footprints; it is laid down in the section *vidhyaparādha*: 'he should strew ashes on the dog's footprint with *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame*' (Āśv. 3-10). At the *ātithyā* this is the *anuvākyā* of the principal offering; it is laid down in the section *athātithyeḷāntā*: '*idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame*, *tad asya priyam abhi pātho aśyām*' (Āśv. 4-5). At the *upasads* this is the *anuvākyā* of the offering to Viṣṇu; it is laid down in the section *athopasad*: '*gayasphāno amīvahā*, *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame*' (Āśv. 4-8)."

> विष्णुस्त्रिविक्रमावतारधारीदं प्रतीयमानं सर्वं जगदुद्दिश्य वि चक्रमे । विशेषेण क्रमणं कृतवान् । तदा त्रेधा त्रिभिः प्रकारैः पदं नि दधे । स्वकीयं पादं प्रक्षिप्तवान् । अस्य विष्णोः पांसुरे धूलियुक्ते पादस्थाने समूळ्हमिदं सर्वं जगत्सम्यगन्तर्भूतं । सेयमृग्यास्केनैवं व्याख्याता । विष्णुर्विशतेर्वा व्यश्नोतेर्वा । यदिदं किंच तद्विक्रमते विष्णुस्त्रिधा निधत्ते पदं त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः समारोहणे विष्णुपदे गयशिरसीत्यौर्णवाभः समूळ्हमस्य पांसुरेऽप्यायनेऽन्तरिक्षे पदं न दृश्यतेऽपि वोपमार्थे स्यात् पांसुर इव पदं न दृश्यत इति पांसवः पादैः सूयन्त इति वा पन्नाः शेरत इति वा पंसनीया भवन्तीति वा । नि० १२-१९ । इति ॥ त्रेधा । एधाच्च । पा० ५-३-४६ । इत्येधाच्प्रत्ययः । चितोऽन्तोदात्तः । समूळ्हं । वह प्रापणे । निष्ठेति क्तः । वचिस्वपीत्यादिना । पा० ६-१-१५ । संप्रसारणं । ढत्वधत्वष्टुत्वढलोपदीर्घत्वानि । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अस्य । इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्त इत्यशनुदात्तः । प्रत्ययश्च सुप्त्वेन । पांसुरे । नगपांसुपाण्डुभ्यश्चेति वक्तव्यं । का० ५-२-१०७-१ । इति मत्वर्थीयो रः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥
>
> *viṣṇustrivikramāvatāradhārīdaṃ pratīyamānaṃ sarvaṃ jagaduddiśya vi cakrame | viśeṣeṇa kramaṇaṃ kṛtavān | tadā tredhā tribhiḥ prakāraiḥ padaṃ ni dadhe | svakīyaṃ pādaṃ prakṣiptavān | asya viṣṇoḥ pāṃsure dhūliyukte pādasthāne samūḷhamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsamyagantarbhūtaṃ | seyamṛgyāskenaivaṃ vyākhyātā | viṣṇurviśatervā vyaśnotervā | yadidaṃ kiṃca tadvikramate viṣṇustridhā nidhatte padaṃ tredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmantarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ samārohaṇe viṣṇupade gayaśirasītyaurṇavābhaḥ samūḷhamasya pāṃsure 'pyāyane 'ntarikṣe padaṃ na dṛśyate 'pi vopamārthe syāt pāṃsura iva padaṃ na dṛśyata iti pāṃsavaḥ pādaiḥ sūyanta iti vā pannāḥ śerata iti vā paṃsanīyā bhavantīti vā | ni0 12-19 | iti || tredhā | edhācca | pā0 5-3-46 | ityedhācpratyayaḥ | cito 'ntodāttaḥ | samūḷhaṃ | vaha prāpaṇe | niṣṭheti ktaḥ | vacisvapītyādinā | pā0 6-1-15 | saṃprasāraṇaṃ | ḍhatvadhatvaṣṭutvaḍhalopadīrghatvāni | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | asya | idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudātta ityaśanudāttaḥ | pratyayaśca suptvena | pāṃsure | nagapāṃsupāṇḍubhyaśceti vaktavyaṃ | kā0 5-2-107-1 | iti matvarthīyo raḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ ||*

**Translation:** "Viṣṇu, who took the Trivikrama incarnation, *vi cakrame*, stepped in a special way, with regard to *idam*, all this world that appears. Then *tredhā*, in three ways, he *ni dadhe*, put down, his *padam*, foot. *Asya*, of this Viṣṇu, in the *pāṃsura*, dusty, footprint, all this world is *samūḷham*, well contained. This ṛk is explained by Yāska thus: '*Viṣṇu*, from *viś* or from *vyaś*. Whatever there is, that Viṣṇu steps over; he puts down his foot in three ways, for being threefold: on the earth, in the mid-air, in heaven, says Śākapūṇi; at the place of rising, at the Viṣṇupada, at Gayaśiras, says Aurṇavābha. *Samūḷham asya pāṃsure*: in the mid-air, the place of swelling, the foot is not seen; or it may be in the sense of comparison: as in a dusty place the foot is not seen. *Pāṃsavaḥ*, because they are produced by the feet, or because, fallen, they lie, or because they are to be crushed' (Ni. 12-19)." (Grammatical tail: *tredhā*, the suffix *edhāc* by *edhāc ca* (Pā. 5-3-46), final udātta as *cit*; *samūḷham*, *vaha prāpaṇe*, *kta* by *niṣṭhā*, *saṃprasāraṇa* by *vacisvapi…* (Pā. 6-1-15), then *ḍh*, *dh*, *ṭutva*, the dropping of *ḍh* and lengthening; the prefix keeps its own accent by *gatir anantaraḥ*; *asya*, the unaccented *aś* by *idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttaḥ…*, and the suffix unaccented as a *sup*; *pāṃsure*, the suffix *ra* in the sense of *matup* by *nagapāṃsupāṇḍubhyaś ceti vaktavyam* (Kā. 5-2-107-1); the suffix accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ)** — Viṣṇu (who took the Trivikrama incarnation) | **इदं (idaṃ)** — this whole world | **वि चक्रमे (vi cakrame)** — stepped over in a special way (how?) | **त्रेधा (tredhā)** — in three ways | **पदं (padaṃ)** — the planting of the foot | **नि दधे (ni dadhe)** — put down | **अस्य (asya)** — of this Viṣṇu | **पांसुरे (pāṃsure)** — in the dusty footprint | **समूळ्हं (samūḷhaṃ)** — (this whole world) was contained (was absorbed).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Viṣṇu (taking the Trivikrama incarnation) stepped over this whole world by placing his foot in three ways. In the dusty footprint of that Viṣṇu this world was covered over and became as if not seen.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Vishnu traversed this universe; three times he planted his foot and the whole universe was collected in the dust of his footsteps.

### Page 124 — Rik 17: Special Topics

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

In the *upāṃśu-yāga* connected with Viṣṇu, the ṛks *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-17) and *trir devaḥ pṛthivīm eṣa etām* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-3) are to be used as the *puronuvākyā* and *yājyā* mantras: since the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra says so in the section *uktā devatāḥ* (Ā. 1-6), the ṛk *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame* in question is a *puronuvākyā* mantra. If a dog enters between the fire-pits called *gārhapatya* and *āhavanīya* set up in the sacrifice, then to remove that fault one must throw ashes on the place where the dog sat with the mantra *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame*: so it is stated in the section *vidhyaparādha* (Ā. 3-10). And in the offering called *ātithya*, when offering the principal oblation, this very mantra *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame* is the *puronuvākyā* mantra. In the section *athātithyeḷāntā* the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra says that the ṛks *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-17) and *tad asya priyam abhi pātho aśyām* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-5) are to be used as the *puronuvākyā* and *yājyā* mantras (Ā. 4-5). *Ātithya*: in the soma sacrifice, when the soma is brought, the soma is imagined as the king and the seven metres Gāyatrī and the rest as his attendants, and the method is to make an offering for the pleasure of the metres Gāyatrī and the rest so as to give hospitality ("Hospitality") to the king and the king's attendants. On this subject, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda —

> यावद्भिर्वै राजानुचरैरागच्छति सर्वेभ्यो वै तेभ्य आतिथ्यं क्रियते छन्दांसि खलु वै सोमस्य राज्ञोऽनुचराण्यग्नेरातिथ्यमसि विष्णवे त्वेत्याह गायत्रिया एवैतेन करोति सोमस्यातिथ्यमसि विष्णवे त्वेत्याह त्रिष्टुभ एवैतेन करोत्यतिथेरातिथ्यमसि विष्णवे त्वेत्याह जगत्या एवैतेन करोत्यग्नये त्वा रायस्पोषदाव्ने विष्णवे त्वेत्याहानुष्टुभ एवैतेन करोति श्येनाय त्वा सोमभृते विष्णवे त्वेत्याह गायत्रिया एवैतेन करोति ॥
>
> *yāvadbhirvai rājānucarairāgacchati sarvebhyo vai tebhya ātithyaṃ kriyate chandāṃsi khalu vai somasya rājño 'nucarāṇyagnerātithyamasi viṣṇave tvetyāha gāyatriyā evaitena karoti somasyātithyamasi viṣṇave tvetyāha triṣṭubha evaitena karotyatitherātithyamasi viṣṇave tvetyāha jagatyā evaitena karotyagnaye tvā rāyaspoṣadāvne viṣṇave tvetyāhānuṣṭubha evaitena karoti śyenāya tvā somabhṛte viṣṇave tvetyāha gāyatriyā evaitena karoti ||*

— and so on. In these offerings Viṣṇu alone is the chief deity. Likewise in the offering called *upasad*, the ṛks *gayasphāno amīvahā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-12) and *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-17) are to be recited as the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* mantras, says the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra in the section *athopasat* (Ā. 4-8). This is the order of application of this ṛk; and in domestic rites and in *smārta* rites and the like it is customary to use this ṛk on occasions of reciting mantras connected with Viṣṇu.

*(The Taittirīya passage is not given a section number in the print; its gloss is not given in the source.)*

### Page 125 — Rik 17: Special Topics (continued)

The great sage Yāska has given the Nirukta for this ṛk:

> विष्णुः । अथ यद्विषितो भवति तद्विष्णुर्भवति विष्णुर्विशतेर्वा व्यश्नोतेर्वा ॥ (नि० १२-१८)
>
> *viṣṇuḥ | atha yadviṣito bhavati tadviṣṇurbhavati viṣṇurviśatervā vyaśnotervā || (ni0 12-18)*

He has explained the meaning of the word *viṣṇu* in this way:

> यदा विषितो व्याप्तोऽयमेव सूर्यो रश्मिभिर्भवति तदा विष्णुर्भवति ।
> विशतेर्वा यदा विष्टः प्रविष्टः सर्वतो रश्मिभिर्भवति तदा विष्णुर्भवति ।
> व्यश्नोतेर्वा विपूर्वस्य वाश्नोतेः यदा रश्मिभिरतिशयेनायं व्याप्तो भवति व्याप्नोति वा रश्मिभिरयं सर्वं तदा विष्णुरादित्यो भवति ॥
>
> *yadā viṣito vyāpto 'yameva sūryo raśmibhirbhavati tadā viṣṇurbhavati |*
> *viśatervā yadā viṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaḥ sarvato raśmibhirbhavati tadā viṣṇurbhavati |*
> *vyaśnotervā vipūrvasya vāśnoteḥ yadā raśmibhiratiśayenāyaṃ vyāpto bhavati vyāpnoti vā raśmibhirayaṃ sarvaṃ tadā viṣṇurādityo bhavati ||*

That is, when the sun makes everything pervaded by his rays, then he is called Viṣṇu; or he is called Viṣṇu because he enters everything through his rays; or the sun himself is called Viṣṇu because he pervades everything exceedingly with his rays and shines. And —

> तस्यैषा भवति ॥ इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे त्रेधा नि दधे पदं । समूळ्हमस्य पांसुरे ॥ यदिदं किंच तद्विक्रमते विष्णुस्त्रिधा निधत्ते पदं त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः । समारोहणे विष्णुपदे गयशिरसीत्यौर्णवाभः । समूळ्हमस्य पांसुरे प्यायनेऽन्तरिक्षे पदं न दृश्यते । अपि वोपमार्थे स्यात् समूळ्हमस्य पांसुल इव पदं न दृश्यत इति ॥ पांसवः पादैः सूयन्त इति वा, पन्नाः शेरत इति वा, पिंशनीया भवन्तीति वा ॥ (नि० १२-१९)
>
> *tasyaiṣā bhavati || idaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame tredhā ni dadhe padaṃ | samūḷhamasya pāṃsure || yadidaṃ kiṃca tadvikramate viṣṇustridhā nidhatte padaṃ tredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmantarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ | samārohaṇe viṣṇupade gayaśirasītyaurṇavābhaḥ | samūḷhamasya pāṃsure pyāyane 'ntarikṣe padaṃ na dṛśyate | api vopamārthe syāt samūḷhamasya pāṃsula iva padaṃ na dṛśyata iti || pāṃsavaḥ pādaiḥ sūyanta iti vā, pannāḥ śerata iti vā, piṃśanīyā bhavantīti vā || (ni0 12-19)*

— to set forth the meaning of the word *viṣṇu*, he has given this very ṛk *idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame* as an example and explained its meaning.

The view of Śākapūṇi is that Viṣṇu (the sun), to divide this world in three ways, placed three feet: he made three footsteps to separate it into three parts — earth, mid-air and heaven. That is, since he is manifest on the earth by his rays, in the mid-air by lightning, and in heaven by the sun's orb, *tredhā* means he is manifest in three ways: this is the intention.

Aurṇavābha holds that since the sun is seen at dawn when rising (*samārohaṇe*) on the eastern mountain, at midday (*viṣṇupade*) in the mid-air, and in the evening (*gayaśirasi*) on the western mountain, this is the meaning of *tredhā ni dadhe padam*. *Samūḷham asya pāṃsure* means that the lightning, the midday step, in the mid-air, never showing —

### Page 126 — Rik 17: Special Topics (end)

— is hidden: that is the meaning. Or a sense of comparison may be given: as a thing covered by dust (or the trace of a footprint) does not show.

For the word *pāṃsure*: *pādaiḥ sūyante janyante ity arthaḥ*: they arise, come into being, from the feet, that is, they fall off; so the dust fallen from the feet is named *pāṃsura*. Or *pannāḥ śerata iti vā | piṃśanīyāḥ dhvaṃsanīyāḥ dhvaṃsanārhās te bhavanti*: because it settles on the feet, or because what is on the feet must be shaken off and destroyed, the dust of the feet is named *pāṃsura*.

All the matters stated above are the explanations of the great sage Yāska. In the Purāṇas and other works Viṣṇu has a place of pre-eminence. Because he pervades the whole universe, they call Viṣṇu the supreme Lord and the supreme Brahman. Or, among the three forms Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara, who carry out the creation, preservation and dissolution of the world, Viṣṇu is famed as the one who preserves the world. For this work of preserving the world, Viṣṇu had to take many incarnations; so it is the view of the commentator and other scholars that one of those incarnations, the Vāmana or Trivikrama incarnation, is described in this ṛk. Because the incarnations of Viṣṇu and the like are not mentioned in the Ṛgveda, because the deeds of the gods seen here and there in the Veda are described in special ways in the Purāṇas, and because the Veda itself is the source of the Purāṇic stories, Western and modern scholars hold that it is not right to explain the Vedic mantras by fitting to them the incarnations and the like found in the Purāṇas.

According to the story told in the Purāṇas: while the demon called Bali Cakravartin, having conquered the gods, was ruling the kingdom, the defeated gods appealed to Viṣṇu; to protect them Viṣṇu took the Vāmana incarnation and, while Bali Cakravartin was under the consecration for a sacrifice, went to him and asked to be given as much land as three of his steps; Bali agreed and said he would give it accordingly. Then Viṣṇu, the Vāmana, took the Trivikrama incarnation, that is, assumed a huge form so as to pervade the earth and the mid-air, stepped over the whole earth with one foot and the mid-air with another, and asked Bali where to place the third foot; the king, being true to his word, since there was no other place, begged that he be favoured by its being placed on his own head; accordingly Trivikrama placed his third foot on Bali's head, made him go to the nether world and live happily ruling there, and gave him the boon he wanted: there is an extended description of this.
