**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**त्रेधा (tredhā)** — by *edhāc ca* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-46) — for the suffix *dhā* after the words *dvi* and *tri*, the substitute *edhāc* comes — and by *saṃkhyāyā vidhārthe dhā* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-42), for the suffix *dhā* after the word *tri*, the substitute *edhāc*: *tri* + *edhā*; by *yasyeti ca* the *i* is dropped; by *citaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) *tredhā* is final udātta.

**समूळ्हं (samūḷhaṃ)** — the root *vaha prāpaṇe*. After it, by *niṣṭhā* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-102) — after a root in the sense of the past, the suffixes *kta* and *ktavatu* — the suffix *kta*. The *k* of the suffix gets the name *it* and is dropped: *vah* + *ta*. Now by *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-15), the sense of the sūtra is that when a suffix marked *k* follows, the roots *vac*, *svap* and the roots of the *yajādi* class take *saṃprasāraṇa*. The root *vah* belongs to the *yajādi* class counted as *yajir vapir vahiś caiva vasir veñ vyeñ ity api | hveñ vadī śvayatiś ceti yajādyāḥ syur ime nava*. So by the sūtra *vacisvapi…* *saṃprasāraṇa*, *u* for the *v*: *u* + *ah* + *ta*; by *saṃprasāraṇāc ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-108) the preceding form: *uh* + *ta*; by *ho ḍhaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-31) *ḍh* for *h*: *uḍh* + *ta*; by *jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-40) — after a letter of the *jhaṣ* group not belonging to the root *dhā*, *dh* is substituted for *t* and *th* — *dh* for the *t* after the *ḍh*: *uḍh* + *dha*; by *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-41) *ḍh* for the *dh*: *uḍh* + *ḍha*; by *ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-13) — a *ḍh* before a *ḍh* is dropped — the first *ḍh* is dropped: *u* + *ḍha*; by *ḍhralope pūrvasyā dīrgho 'ṇaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-111) — *a*, *i*, *u* standing before the *ḍh* or *r* that caused the dropping of a *ḍh* or *r* are lengthened — the *u* is lengthened: *ū* + *ḍha*; by the traditional saying *ajmadhyasthaḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ | ajmadhyasthaḍhakārasya ḷhakāraṃ vai yathākramam*, *ḷh* for the *ḍh*. By *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the *gati* named *sam* keeps its own accent.

> यजिर्वपिर्वहिश्चैव वसिर्वेञ् व्येञ् इत्यपि । ह्वेञ् वदी श्वयतिश्चेति यजाद्याः स्युरिमे नव ॥
> अज्मध्यस्थडकारस्य ळकारं बह्वृचा जगुः । अज्मध्यस्थढकारस्य ळ्हकारं वै यथाक्रमम् ॥
>
> *yajirvapirvahiścaiva vasirveñ vyeñ ityapi | hveñ vadī śvayatiśceti yajādyāḥ syurime nava ||*
> *ajmadhyasthaḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ | ajmadhyasthaḍhakārasya ḷhakāraṃ vai yathākramam ||*

**अस्य (asya)** — after the word *idam*, the genitive singular *jas* [as printed; for *ṅas*]; by *tyadādīnām aḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) *a* for the *m*: *ida* + *a* + *jas*; by *ato guṇe* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) the following form: *ida* + *jas*; by *ṭāṅasiṅasām inātsyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-12) the substitute *sya* for *jas*: *ida* + *sya*. By *idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-32) the unaccented substitute *aś* for *ida*: *asya*. By *anudāttau suppitau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) *sya* is unaccented; thus *asya* is wholly unaccented.

### Page 128 (upper) — Rik 17: grammar (end)

**पांसुरे (pāṃsure)** — at *ūṣasuṣimuṣkamadho raḥ* (Pā. Sū. 5-2-107) the author of the *vārttika* has read *nagāc ca*. Here the author of the Kāśikā-vṛtti has read *nagapāṃsupāṇḍubhyaś ceti vaktavyam* (Kāśikā 5-2-107-1). Its meaning is: it should be said that after the words *naga*, *pāṃsu*, *pāṇḍu* the suffix *ra* comes in the sense of *matup*. By this, when the suffix *ra* comes after the word *pāṃsu*, it becomes *pāṃsura*. By the suffix accent [the word] is initially udātta [as printed]. In the locative singular it becomes *pāṃsure*. ॥17॥

> *trī́ṇi padā́ ví cakramé víṣṇur gopā́ ádābhyaḥ |*

*(Strokes over णि, च, ष्णु and दा; bars under प (पदा), मे and गो. Line 2: a bar under अ, a stroke over the head of धर्मा (read as over र्मा, as in the Pada [accent ?]), a bar under धा, a stroke over र.)*

> अतः । धर्माणि । धारयन् ॥१८॥
>
> *trīṇi | padā | vi | cakrame | viṣṇuḥ | gopāḥ | adābhyaḥ ||*
> *ataḥ | dharmāṇi | dhārayan ||18||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० ४-८, ऋग्वे० १-१-८.)*

> उपसदि वैष्णवयागस्य प्रातःकाले याज्या सायंकालेऽनुवाक्या त्रीणि पदेत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । त्रीणि पदा वि चक्रम इति स्विष्टकृदादि लुप्यते । आ० ४-८ । इति ॥
>
> *upasadi vaiṣṇavayāgasya prātaḥkāle yājyā sāyaṃkāle 'nuvākyā trīṇi padetyeṣā | sūtritaṃ ca | trīṇi padā vi cakrama iti sviṣṭakṛdādi lupyate | ā0 4-8 | iti ||*

**Translation (application):** "At the *upasad*, for the offering to Viṣṇu, this ṛk *trīṇi padā* is the *yājyā* in the morning and the *anuvākyā* in the evening; and it is laid down: '*trīṇi padā vi cakrame*; the *sviṣṭakṛt* and the rest are omitted' (Āśv. 4-8)."

> अदाभ्यः केनापि हिंसितुमशक्यो गोपाः सर्वस्य जगतो रक्षको विष्णुः पृथिव्यादिस्थानेषु त्रीणि पदानि वि चक्रमे । किं कुर्वन् । धर्माण्यग्निहोत्रादीनि धारयन्पोषयन् ॥ पदा । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेर्डादेशः । तस्य स्थानिवद्भावेनानुदात्तत्वे प्राप्त उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेणोदात्तत्वं । गोपाः । गोपामृतस्य । ऋग्वे० १-१-८ । इत्यत्रोक्तं । अदाभ्यः । दभेरृहलोर्ण्यदिति ण्यत् । नञ्समासः । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । धारयन् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण णिच एव स्वरः शिष्यते ॥
>
> *adābhyaḥ kenāpi hiṃsitumaśakyo gopāḥ sarvasya jagato rakṣako viṣṇuḥ pṛthivyādisthāneṣu trīṇi padāni vi cakrame | kiṃ kurvan | dharmāṇyagnihotrādīni dhārayanpoṣayan || padā | supāṃ sulugityādinā vibhakterḍādeśaḥ | tasya sthānivadbhāvenānudāttatve prāpta udāttanivṛttisvareṇodāttatvaṃ | gopāḥ | gopāmṛtasya | ṛgve0 1-1-8 | ityatroktaṃ | adābhyaḥ | dabherṛhalorṇyaditi ṇyat | nañsamāsaḥ | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | dhārayan | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | śatuśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa ṇica eva svaraḥ śiṣyate ||*

**Translation:** "Viṣṇu, *adābhyaḥ*, whom no one can harm, *gopāḥ*, the protector of the whole world, *vi cakrame*, stepped *trīṇi padā*, three steps, in the places, the earth and the rest. Doing what? *Dhārayan*, supporting, nourishing, the *dharmāṇi*, the rites such as the *agnihotra*." (Grammatical tail: *padā*, the substitute *ḍā* for the case-ending by *supāṃ suluk…*; unaccented would be due by its standing for the original, but it is udātta by the accent of the loss of the udātta; *gopāḥ*, explained at *gopām ṛtasya* (Ṛgve. 1-1-8); *adābhyaḥ*, *ṇyat* after *dabh* by *ṛhalor ṇyat*, a *nañ* compound, the indeclinable first member's accent; *dhārayan*, *śap* unaccented as *pit*, and the *śatṛ* too by the *lasārvadhātuka* accent, so only the accent of *ṇic* remains.)

### Page 129 — Rik 18: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अदाभ्यः (adābhyaḥ)** — who cannot be harmed by anyone | **गोपाः (gopāḥ)** — protecting the whole world | **विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ)** — Viṣṇu | (in the places, the earth and the rest) **धर्माणि (dharmāṇi)** — the works of *dharma* proper to the performance of good rites such as the *agnihotra* | **धारयन् (dhārayan)** — nourishing (protecting) | **अतः (ataḥ)** — by this order of action | **त्रीणि पदा (trīṇi padā)** — three steps | **वि चक्रमे (vi cakrame)** — stepped out.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

No one can harm Viṣṇu. He is the protector of the whole world; therefore, for the upholding of *dharmas* such as the *agnihotra*, Viṣṇu made three strides.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Vishnu, the uninjurable and the protector of the Universe, stepped three steps, thereby preserving the Sacred laws.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The application of this mantra is as follows. In the rite called *upasadana*, when making the offering connected with Viṣṇu, this ṛk is to be used in the morning as the *yājyā* mantra and in the evening as the *puronuvākyā* mantra: so it is stated in the section *trīṇi padā vi cakrama iti sviṣṭakṛdādi lupyate* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra (Ā. 4-8).

**गोपाः (gopāḥ)** — *go* means the earth; because he protects it, Viṣṇu is named *gopāḥ*.

**अदाभ्यः (adābhyaḥ)** — *ahiṃsyaḥ*, one who cannot be harmed. The meaning is that no one has the power to harm him.

**धर्माणि, धारयन् (dharmāṇi, dhārayan)** — according to the saying *sarvasya hi bhagavān viṣṇur āśrayaḥ*, Viṣṇu is not only the protector of the whole world but also the support of all *dharmas* ("Universal laws") and their protector; that is, he is foremost in punishing the wicked and protecting the good. The intention is that among creation, preservation and dissolution, the duties of the three forms Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara, Viṣṇu carries out his own duty, the preservation of the world, that is, punishing the wicked and protecting the good.

> सर्वस्य हि भगवान् विष्णुराश्रयः ।
>
> *sarvasya hi bhagavān viṣṇurāśrayaḥ |*

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**पदा (padā)** — for the accusative plural suffix *śas*, by *supāṃ suluk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39), the substitute *ḍā*; by *sthānivadbhāva* it is unaccented. The substitute *ḍā* coming in place of *śas* —

### Page 130 — Rik 18: grammar (continued)

— should be unaccented; yet, by the force of the suffix being made *ḍit*, even without the name *bha*, the final udātta *a* of the word *pada* is dropped by *ṭeḥ*. So by *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-161) the unaccented *ā* that caused the loss of the udātta *a* becomes udātta.

**गोपाः (gopāḥ)** — the Veda commentary says that the derivation is set out at *gopām ṛtasya* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-8); but the derivation is not seen there in the way the printed text now has it. With the analysis *gāṃ* (the earth) *pāti* (protects), by *kvip ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76), when the object-word *gām* is *upapada*, *kvip* comes after the root *pā rakṣaṇe*; *pā* is udātta by the root accent; an *upapada* compound; by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) that same accent stays by the accent of the *kṛt* final member.

**अदाभ्यः (adābhyaḥ)** — the root *dabh* is not found in Pāṇini's list of roots; yet the commentator describes that this root exists and that it means harming. By *ṛhalor ṇyat* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-124) — after a root ending in *ṛ* or in a consonant, the suffix *ṇyat* — the suffix *ṇyat*: *dabh* + *ya*; by *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) *vṛddhi* of the penultimate: *na dābhyaḥ adābhyaḥ*: by the sūtra *nañ* (Pā. Sū. 2-2-6) the *nañ* compound; by *nalopo nañaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-73) the *n* is dropped; by *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) — in a tatpuruṣa compound these seven first members keep their own accent — *nañ* keeps its own accent.

**धारयन् (dhārayan)** — *dhṛñ dhāraṇe*, *ṇic*: *dhṛ* + *i*; by *aco 'ñṇiti* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115) *vṛddhi*, followed by *r*: it became *dhāri*. After it *laṭ*; by *laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-124) the substitute *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; by *kartari śap* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the *vikaraṇa* *śap*: *dhāri* + *a* + *at*; with *śap* as cause, *guṇa* *e* for the *i* of *ṇic*, the substitute *ay*, and the following form for both *a*'s: *dhārayat*; after it the suffix *su*; by *ugidacām* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70) the augment *n* after the *ya*: *dhārayant* + *s*; by *halṅyābbhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-68) *su* is dropped; by *saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-23) the *t* at the end of the conjunct is dropped; since by *pūrvatrāsiddham* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-1) the dropping of the conjunct-final is *asiddha*, by *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-7) the *n* is not dropped: it becomes *dhārayan*. Here *śap*, being *pit*, is unaccented by *anudāttau suppitau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4). The *śatṛ* too, being an *a*-final original teaching,

### Page 131 (upper) — Rik 18: grammar (end)

and following *śap*, is unaccented by *tāsy anudāttenṅid adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam ahnviṅoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186). The *a* coming by the following form for both of these is unaccented by likeness of place. So, the *i* of *ṇic* staying udātta by the suffix accent, the *e* coming in its place and the substitute *ay* coming in its place are udātta. ॥18॥

> विष्णोः । कर्माणि । पश्यत । यतः । व्रतानि । पस्पशे ॥
> इन्द्रस्य । युज्यः । सखा ॥१९॥

> *viṣṇoḥ | karmāṇi | paśyata | yataḥ | vratāni | paspaśe ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: तै० सं० २-४-१२-२, पा० ७-४-६१.)*

> हे ऋत्विगादयो विष्णोः कर्माणि पालनादीनि पश्यत । यतो यैः कर्मभिर्व्रतान्यग्निहोत्रादीनि पस्पशे सर्वो यजमानः स्पृष्टवान् । विष्णोरनुग्रहादनुतिष्ठतीत्यर्थः । तादृशो विष्णुरिन्द्रस्य युज्यो योज्योऽनुकूलः सखा भवति । विष्णोरिन्द्रानुकूल्यं त्वष्टा हतपुत्र इत्यनुवाकेऽथ वै तर्हि विष्णुरित्यादिना । तै० सं० २-४-१२-२ । प्रपञ्चेन तैत्तिरीया आमनन्ति ॥ पस्पशे । स्पश बाधनस्पर्शनयोः । लिट् । द्विर्भावे शर्पूर्वाः खयः । पा० ७-४-६१ । इति पकारः शिष्यते । सकारो लुप्यते । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । युज्यः । युजेर्बाहुलकात्क्यप् । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । क्यपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । धातुस्वरः ॥
>
> *he ṛtvigādayo viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi pālanādīni paśyata | yato yaiḥ karmabhirvratānyagnihotrādīni paspaśe sarvo yajamānaḥ spṛṣṭavān | viṣṇoranugrahādanutiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ | tādṛśo viṣṇurindrasya yujyo yojyo 'nukūlaḥ sakhā bhavati | viṣṇorindrānukūlyaṃ tvaṣṭā hataputra ityanuvāke 'tha vai tarhi viṣṇurityādinā | tai0 saṃ0 2-4-12-2 | prapañcena taittirīyā āmananti || paspaśe | spaśa bādhanasparśanayoḥ | liṭ | dvirbhāve śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ | pā0 7-4-61 | iti pakāraḥ śiṣyate | sakāro lupyate | yadvṛttayogādanighātaḥ | yujyaḥ | yujerbāhulakātkyap | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | kyapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | dhātusvaraḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O priests and the rest, *paśyata*, behold, the *karmāṇi*, deeds — protecting and the rest — of Viṣṇu, *yataḥ*, by which deeds every sacrificer *paspaśe*, has touched, the *vratāni*, the rites such as the *agnihotra*: that is, he performs them by Viṣṇu's favour. Such a Viṣṇu is the *yujyaḥ*, fit to be joined, favourable, *sakhā*, friend, of Indra. The Taittirīyas record at length Viṣṇu's favour toward Indra in the *anuvāka* *tvaṣṭā hataputraḥ*, beginning *atha vai tarhi viṣṇuḥ* (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12-2)." (Grammatical tail: *paspaśe*, *spaśa bādhanasparśanayoḥ*, *liṭ*; in the reduplication, by *śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ* (Pā. 7-4-61) the *p* remains and the *s* is dropped; no loss of accent because of the connection with *yad*; *yujyaḥ*, *kyap* after *yuj* by *bāhulaka*, no *guṇa* as it is *kit*, *kyap* unaccented as *pit*; the root accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

(O priests and the rest) **यतः (yataḥ)** — by which deeds of Viṣṇu | (the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice) **व्रतानि (vratāni)** — the performance of rites such as the *agnihotra* | **पस्पशे (paspaśe)** — does (did) —

### Page 132 — Rik 19: word-meanings (end), overall sense, English, Special Topics

— (such) **विष्णोः (viṣṇoḥ)** — of Viṣṇu | **कर्माणि (karmāṇi)** — the deeds of protecting and the rest | **पश्यत (paśyata)** — behold | (such a Viṣṇu) **इन्द्रस्य (indrasya)** — of Indra | **युज्यः (yujyaḥ)** — being together (favourable) | **सखा (sakhā)** — a dear friend.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O people — priests, sacrificers and the rest — behold the (wonderful) deeds of Viṣṇu, protecting and the rest. By the greatness of that Viṣṇu alone the sacrificer is able to perform rites such as the *agnihotra*. Such a Viṣṇu is the supreme friend who is with Indra.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> See the deeds of Vishnu, through which (the worshipper) has accomplished the pious acts ; he is the intimate friend of Indra.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

In this ṛk some words have to be supplied (*adhyāhāra*). Since there is the word *paśyata*, 'behold', the vocative word 'O people' is needed. Likewise in *vratāni paspaśe*, 'he performed the rites', the agent word 'the sacrificer' is needed, and along with the words *indrasya sakhā* the word *viṣṇuḥ* too is needed.

**व्रतानि (vratāni)** — the good works to be done by rule, that is, the performance of sacrifice and the like.

**पस्पशे (paspaśe)** — *spṛṣṭavān*, he touched, that is, he began; he started: this is the meaning.

**युज्यः (yujyaḥ)** — *yogyo 'nukūlaḥ* or *yogyaḥ*: favourable to Indra, a dear friend, who is with him, fit: this is the meaning. The commentator has cited an *anuvāka* of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12) which tells of the various bold deeds of Viṣṇu told in this ṛk, Viṣṇu's friendship with Indra, the invoking of Indra and Viṣṇu together, and such matters. Its main intent is as follows —

Tvaṣṭṛ Prajāpati had a son named Viśvarūpa. Though he was the priest of the gods, he was well disposed toward the demons too and kept saying that they too should be given a share in sacrifices and the like. Knowing this, Indra, guessing that this Viśvarūpa might in course of time give his own lordship of heaven to the demons, slew this Viśvarūpa, who favoured the demons' side. By the slaying of his son —

### Page 133 — Rik 19: Special Topics (continued)

— Tvaṣṭṛ, angered, wished for a son able to slay Indra and performed a sacrifice for it. While performing the sacrifice, out of anger at Indra, he did not invite Indra to drink soma in that sacrifice. When Indra said that he too should be invited to the sacrifice, Tvaṣṭṛ said to Indra, 'Because you killed my son I will not invite you', and performed the sacrifice leaving Indra out. But Indra, troubling his sacrifice, drank the soma by force without Tvaṣṭṛ's consent. Then Tvaṣṭṛ took up the remainder of the soma that Indra had left after drinking, went near the *āhavanīya* fire, kindled it so that it blazed well, and in that fire made an offering with the mantra स्वाहेन्द्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्व (*svāhendraśatrur vardhasva*), meaning 'may there be for me a son who will kill Indra'. But since, in uttering the word *indraśatruḥ*, the accent was changed, the meaning of the mantra too changed, and instead of 'a son who will kill Indra' it came to mean 'a son to be killed by Indra'; accordingly a son named Vṛtra was born. Meanwhile the fire established in the sacrifice, knowing that this Vṛtra born in the sacrifice would go to the upper world and trouble the gods, went out before the sacrifice was complete and broke the sacrifice. It is said that if the fire in a sacrifice blazes up brightly with its flames, it brings the sacrificer's wishes to pass, and that if the fire goes out without blazing well, it portends misfortune to the sacrificer. Thus Vṛtra, born of the sacrificial offering, instead of killing Indra became one to be killed by Indra. Then that Vṛtra quickly pervaded the whole world and began to grow each day by as much as the distance an arrow goes from a bow. Because he thus pervaded the world by the growth of his body, he got the name Vṛtra. Seeing this, Indra was afraid. Tvaṣṭṛ, his father, too was frightened. Then Tvaṣṭṛ made a divine thunderbolt weapon, consecrated it with mantras and gave it to Indra. Indra had not the strength even to lift that great thunderbolt, made of austerity. Seeing this, while he was thinking what to do, Viṣṇu appeared to Indra. Then Indra prayed to Viṣṇu thus: 'O Viṣṇu, seeing the strength and power of the demon Vṛtra I am greatly afraid. So I have not even the strength to lift this thunderbolt with my hand. So let the two of us together take away the world-pervading power the demon Vṛtra has. You must help in this.' When he so prayed, Viṣṇu agreed to do so, made his body (or his strength and power) into three parts and placed them in the earth, the mid-air and heaven. Then Indra, accompanied by the third part of Viṣṇu's body that was on the earth, lifted with his hand the thunderbolt that had fallen behind Viṣṇu. Then Vṛtra —

### Page 134 — Rik 19: Special Topics (end), grammar

— frightened, said to Indra: 'O Indra, do not strike my body. I will give you all my strength (power) that pervades the earth'; and accordingly he gave Indra all his strength that was in the earth. Indra accepted it and gave it to Viṣṇu. Viṣṇu too accepted it. Likewise Indra accepted Vṛtra's strength that was in the mid-air and the heavenly world and gave it to Viṣṇu. Then Vṛtra, addressing Indra, asked: 'Let us both make a treaty; give me leave to enter your body.' Indra said, 'What will you do by entering my body? Will you not eat me up?' Vṛtra said, 'No; I will stay in your belly in the form of the digestive fire, digesting the food and the like that you eat, and be there for your enjoyment', and entered Indra's body. From then on Vṛtra stays in the bellies of men in the form of hunger and gives trouble to living beings. As said before, because Indra received the strength from Vṛtra three times and gave it to Viṣṇu, the oblation called *puroḍāśa* offered to Indra and Viṣṇu got the name *tridhātuyukta*. And it became customary, when offering such an oblation, to invoke Indra and Viṣṇu together and make the offering. Since this legend shows Viṣṇu's deeds and the friendship Viṣṇu had for Indra, the commentator has cited this *anuvāka*.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**पस्पशे (paspaśe)** — the root *spaśa bādhanasparśanayoḥ*; after it *liṭ*; by *liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-8) reduplication: *spaś* + *spaś* + *liṭ*. By *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-60) the remaining of only the first letter of the reduplicate would be obtained; but by its exception *śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-61) — the letters *kh*, *ph*, *ch*, *ṭh*, *th*, *c*, *ṭ*, *t*, *k*, *p* following *ś*, *ṣ*, *s* in the reduplicate remain — the *p* remains, and consequently the initial *s* is dropped: *pa* + *spaś* + *liṭ*; for *liṭ* the substitute *ta*, and by *liṭas tajhayor eśirec* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-81) the substitute *eś* for *ta*: it becomes *paspaśe*. By *yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66), since there is the prohibition that a word ending in *tiṅ* after a word containing *yad* is not unaccented, in *yato vratāni paspaśe* the *paspaśe* after the word *yataḥ* is not unaccented. In *pūjanāt pūjitam anudāttam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-67), by the repeated mention of *pūjita*, it is made known that *atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryam iṣyate*. So though there is the separation by the word *vratāni*, the prohibition of the unaccented comes.

### Page 135 (upper) — Rik 19: grammar (end)

**युज्यः (yujyaḥ)** — since there is the word *bahula* in *uṇādayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-1), after the root *yuj* the Uṇādi suffix *kyap* comes. Since the suffix is *kit*, there is the prohibition *kṅiti ca* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-5), so *guṇa* of the light penultimate by *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) does not come. *Kyap* being *pit*, it is unaccented by *anudāttau suppitau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4). Thus the *u* in *yuj* stays udātta by the root accent *dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-162). ॥19॥

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: पा० ५-३-१५, पा० ५-३-६.)*

> सूरयो विद्वांस ऋत्विगादयो विष्णोः संबन्धि परममुत्कृष्टं तच्छास्त्रप्रसिद्धं । पदं स्वर्गस्थानं शास्त्रदृष्ट्या सर्वदा पश्यन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । दिवीव । आकाशे यथाततं सर्वतः प्रसृतं चक्षुर्निरोधाभावेन विशदं पश्यति । तद्वत् ॥ सदा । सर्वैकान्येति । पा० ५-३-१५ । दाप्रत्ययः । सर्वस्य सोऽन्यतरस्यां दि । पा० ५-३-६ । इति सर्वशब्दस्य सभावः । व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वं । दिवि । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । इवेन विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं चेति तदेव शिष्यते । चक्षुः । नब्विषयस्येत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । आततं । तनोतेः कर्मणि क्तः । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिना नलोपः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते गतिरनन्तर इति गतेरुदात्तत्वं ॥
>
> *sūrayo vidvāṃsa ṛtvigādayo viṣṇoḥ saṃbandhi paramamutkṛṣṭaṃ tacchāstraprasiddhaṃ | padaṃ svargasthānaṃ śāstradṛṣṭyā sarvadā paśyanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | divīva | ākāśe yathātataṃ sarvataḥ prasṛtaṃ cakṣurnirodhābhāvena viśadaṃ paśyati | tadvat || sadā | sarvaikānyeti | pā0 5-3-15 | dāpratyayaḥ | sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di | pā0 5-3-6 | iti sarvaśabdasya sabhāvaḥ | vyatyayenādyudāttatvaṃ | divi | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ceti tadeva śiṣyate | cakṣuḥ | nabviṣayasyetyādyudāttatvaṃ | ātataṃ | tanoteḥ karmaṇi ktaḥ | yasya vibhāṣetīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | anudāttopadeśetyādinā nalopaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte gatiranantara iti gaterudāttatvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "The *sūrayaḥ*, the wise — priests and the rest — *sadā paśyanti*, always see, with the eye of scripture, that *paramam*, highest, *padam*, place, the place of heaven, belonging to Viṣṇu, well known from scripture. The illustration for it: *divīva*: as the eye, *ātatam*, spread out on all sides, in the sky, sees clearly because there is no obstruction — so." (Grammatical tail: *sadā*, the suffix *dā* by *sarvaikānya…* (Pā. 5-3-15), the substitute *sa* for *sarva* by *sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di* (Pā. 5-3-6); initial udātta by *vyatyaya*; *divi*, the case-ending udātta by *ūḍidam…*; with *iva*, the non-dropping of the case-ending and the first member's own accent, so that alone remains; *cakṣuḥ*, initial udātta by *nabviṣayasya…*; *ātatam*, *kta* in the object sense after *tan*, the *iṭ* barred by *yasya vibhāṣā*, the *n* dropped by *anudāttopadeśa…*; the accent of the *kṛt* final member being due, the prefix is udātta by *gatir anantaraḥ*.)

### Page 136 — Rik 20: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**सूरयः (sūrayaḥ)** — the wise | **विष्णोः (viṣṇoḥ)** — of Viṣṇu | **तत् (tat)** — that | **परमं (paramaṃ)** — highest | **पदं (padaṃ)** — place (heaven?) | **दिवि (divi)** — in the sky | **आततं (ātataṃ)** — pervading (spread out) | **चक्षुः इव (cakṣuḥ iva)** — like the eye | **सदा (sadā)** — at all times | **पश्यन्ति (paśyanti)** — see.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

As the sight fixed on the sky sees everything, because the sky is very wide, so the wise always see the place called Viṣṇu's highest step (heaven, or Vaikuṇṭha?).

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The wise always contemplate that supreme place of Vishnu as the eye fixed in broad heaven.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**परमं पदं (paramaṃ padaṃ)** — the highest place. The commentator has explained it as heaven. Skandasvāmin, explaining *viṣṇu* as the sun, has said that *viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam* means the shining orb of the sun. Some, as the Purāṇas and others say, hold that Viṣṇu's highest place is the Vaikuṇṭha world. But that meaning, well known in the Purāṇas, does not fit here. The author of the *Vedārthayatna* has explained the word *padam*, as said before at *trīṇi padā*, as the three footsteps. These words *paramaṃ padam* also occur in the next ṛk.

**दिवीव चक्षुराततं (divīva cakṣur ātataṃ)** — the sight fixed on the sky can see very far. That is, the sense is that, as the eye has the power of seeing things that are very far off, the learned have the power of seeing, or knowing, the excellent place of Viṣṇu.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**सदा (sadā)** — the analysis is *sarvasmin kāle*. By *sarvaikānyakiṃyattadaḥ kāle dā* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-15) — after the words *sarva*, *eka*, *anya*, *kim*, *yad*, *tad* ending in the seventh case and in the sense of time, the suffix *dā* comes in its own sense — the suffix *dā* after *sarvasmin*: *sarva* + *ṅi* + *dā*. Since it ends in a *taddhita*, by *kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca* (Pā. Sū. 1-2-46) it gets the name *prātipadika*, and by *supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-71) *ṅi* is dropped —

### Page 137 — Rik 20: grammar (continued)

— (*luk*): *sarva* + *dā*. Now by *sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-6) — when a *d*-initial suffix belonging to the *prāgdiśīya* group follows, the substitute *sa* for the word *sarva* comes optionally — the substitute *sa* for *sarva*: it becomes *sadā*. Although here, by the suffix accent, it would be right for *sadā* to be final udātta, yet by *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85), by interchange, the initial udātta alone comes here.

**दिवि (divi)** — when the locative singular suffix *ṅi* is attached after the word *div*: *div* + *i*, it becomes *divi*. The suffix *ṅi* is a *sup*, so by *anudāttau suppitau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) the unaccented would be obtained. Yet by *ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) — the case-endings other than the *sarvanāmasthāna* after the final-udātta monosyllabic words *ūṭ*, *idam*, the six *padādi* substitutes *pad*, *dat*, *nas*, *mās*, *hṛt*, *niś*, and *ap*, *pums*, *rai*, *div* are udātta — here the *ṅi*, a case-ending other than the *sarvanāmasthāna* after *div*, is udātta. By *ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca* (Pā. Sū. 2-1-4 Vā. 2) — a word ending in *sup* is always compounded with the word *iva*; the case-ending in the compound is not dropped; even after compounding the first member keeps its own accent — so for *divi* + *iva* both the compound, the non-dropping of the case-ending *i*, and the first member's own accent come. By *cādayo 'nudāttāḥ* (Phi. Sū. 84) the word *iva* is unaccented, as set forth at *sa naḥ pitevaḥ* [as printed] (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-9). The final udātta *i* in *divi* and the unaccented *i* in *iva* take the long like vowel as a single substitute for both; but here by *ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-5) the single substitute does not become udātta. Since the word *iva*, beginning with an unaccented vowel, follows, by *svarito vānudātte padādau* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-6) — the single substitute for an udātta with an unaccented vowel at the beginning of the following word is optionally svarita — the svarita accent comes. *Cakṣuḥ* is a word always of neuter gender; so by *nabviṣayasyānisantasya* (Phi. Sū. 26) it is initially udātta.

**आततम् (ātatam)** — after the root *tanu vistāre* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, in the object sense, the suffix *kta*: *ātan* + *ta*; the root is *tan*. Since the root has the *it*-named *u*, by *udito vā* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-56) the augment *iṭ* is laid down optionally for the suffix *ktvā* after a root marked *u*. So by *yasya vibhāṣā* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-15) — for a root for which *iṭ* is anywhere laid down optionally, —

### Page 138 (upper) — Rik 20: grammar (end)

— the suffixes *kta* and *ktavatu* after that root do not take the augment *iṭ* — the augment *iṭ* is barred. Then by *anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37) — the roots ending in a nasal that are taught unaccented, the roots *tanoti* and the rest, and the root *van*, drop the nasal before a *jhal*-initial suffix that is *kit* or *ṅit* — the *n* of *tan* is dropped. *Yami*, *rami*, *nami*, *gami*, *hani*, *mani*: these six roots are taught unaccented; *tanu*, *kṣaṇu*, *kṣiṇu*, *ṛṇu*, *tṛṇu*, *ghṛṇu*, *vanu*, *manu*: these eight roots are the *tanoty-ādi* roots; so it became *ātata*. By *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the own accent of the *kṛt* final member would be due; overriding this, by *thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-144, as read) the final udātta of the last member would be due; overriding that too, by *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) — when a word ending in the suffix *kta* in the object sense follows, the immediately preceding *gati* keeps its own accent — the *gati* *ā* is udātta. ॥20॥

### Page 138 (lower) — Sūkta 22, Rik 21 (last ṛk of the sūkta)

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तद्विप्रा॑सो विप॒न्यवो जागृ॒वांसः॑ समि॑न्धते । [accent ?]
> विष्णो॒र्यत्प॑र॒मं प॒दं ॥२१॥ [accent ?]
>
> *tad víprāso vipanyávo jāgṛvā́ṃsaḥ sám indhate |* [accent ?]
> *víṣṇor yát paramáṃ padáṃ ||21||* [accent ?]

*(Strokes over प्रा, over the end of जागृवांसः (read as over सः) and over मि; bars under प (विपन्यवो) and गृ. Line 2: bars under ष्णो, र (परमं) and प (पदं); a stroke near र्य/त्प (read as over त्प). The positions are not certain [accent ?].)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तत् । विप्रासः । विपन्यवः । जागृऽवांसः । सं । इन्धते ॥
> विष्णोः । यत् । परमं । पदं ॥२१॥
>
> *tat | viprāsaḥ | vipanyavaḥ | jāgṛ 'vāṃsaḥ | saṃ | indhate ||*
> *viṣṇoḥ | yat | paramaṃ | padaṃ ||21||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(The bhāṣya ends with ॥७॥, the close of the seventh varga.)*

> पूर्वोक्तं विष्णोर्यत्परमं पदमस्ति तत्पदं विप्रासो मेधाविनः समिन्धते । सम्यक् दीपयन्ति । कीदृशाः । विपन्यवो विशेषेण स्तोतारो जागृवांसः शब्दार्थयोः प्रमादराहित्येन जागरूकाः ॥ विप्रासः । आज्जसेरसुक् । विपन्यवः । स्तुत्यर्थस्य पनेर्बाहुलक औणादिको युप्रत्ययः । तत्र प्रत्ययस्वरः । जागृवांसः । जागृ निद्राक्षये । लिटः क्वसुः । क्रादिनियमात्प्राप्तस्येटो वस्वेकाजाद्घसामिति नियमान्निवृत्तिः ॥७॥
>
> *pūrvoktaṃ viṣṇoryatparamaṃ padamasti tatpadaṃ viprāso medhāvinaḥ samindhate | samyak dīpayanti | kīdṛśāḥ | vipanyavo viśeṣeṇa stotāro jāgṛvāṃsaḥ śabdārthayoḥ pramādarāhityena jāgarūkāḥ || viprāsaḥ | ājjaserasuk | vipanyavaḥ | stutyarthasya panerbāhulaka auṇādiko yupratyayaḥ | tatra pratyayasvaraḥ | jāgṛvāṃsaḥ | jāgṛ nidrākṣaye | liṭaḥ kvasuḥ | krādiniyamātprāptasyeṭo vasvekājādghasāmiti niyamānnivṛttiḥ ||7||*

**Translation:** "That *paramam padam*, highest place, of Viṣṇu which there is, spoken of before — that place the *viprāsaḥ*, the wise, *sam indhate*, kindle well, make shine. Of what kind? *Vipanyavaḥ*, praisers in a special way, *jāgṛvāṃsaḥ*, wakeful, through freedom from carelessness about word and meaning." (Grammatical tail: *viprāsaḥ*, *asuk* by *āj jaser asuk*; *vipanyavaḥ*, after *pan* in the sense of praising, the Uṇādi suffix *yu* by *bāhulaka*, the suffix accent there; *jāgṛvāṃsaḥ*, *jāgṛ nidrākṣaye*, *kvasu* for *liṭ*; the *iṭ* that would come by the *krādi* restriction is removed by the restriction *vasv ekājād ghasām*.)

### Page 139 — Rik 21: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**विपन्यवः (vipanyavaḥ)** — who make hymns | **विप्रासः (viprāsaḥ)** — the wise people | **विष्णोः (viṣṇoḥ)** — of Viṣṇu | **यत् (yat)** — which, spoken of before | **परमं पदं (paramaṃ padaṃ)** — the highest place there is | **तत् (tat)** — that | **जागृवांसः (jāgṛvāṃsaḥ)** — being wakeful (very alert) | **सं इन्धते (saṃ indhate)** — kindle with hymns, that is, praise.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Wise and discerning people praise greatly with hymns and the like the excellent place called Viṣṇu's highest step, spoken of before.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The wise, vigilant and full of praises, glorify the supreme place of Vishnu.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**विप्रासः (viprāsaḥ)** — *medhāvinaḥ*: the intelligent, the discerning, the wise and so on.

**विपन्यवः (vipanyavaḥ)** — *stutikāmāḥ*: those who wish to make hymns, those who praise.

**जागृवांसः (jāgṛvāṃsaḥ)** — *jāgṛ nidrākṣaye*: the wakeful, those who stay alert.

**सं इन्धते (saṃ indhate)** — they kindle, increase the brightness, that is, they praise with hymns and the like.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**विप्रासः (viprāsaḥ)** — after the word *vipra*, the nominative plural *jas*: *vipra* + *jas*; the *j* is named *it* and dropped. By *āj jaser asuk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50) — the *jas* after a word ending in *a* takes the augment *asuk* — the augment *asuk* for *jas*. Since it is *kit*, by the *paribhāṣā* *ādyantau ṭakitau* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-46) it comes as the final part of *jas*: *vipra* + *as* + *as*; by *prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-102) the lengthening of the like preceding vowel; *ru* and *visarga* for the *s*: *viprāsaḥ* is formed.

**विपन्यवः (vipanyavaḥ)** — in *paṇa vyavahāre stutau ca*, *pana ca*, the root *pan* is read in the senses of dealing and praise. Here the root *pan* meaning praise is to be taken. After it, by the word *bahula* in *uṇādayo*

### Page 140 — Rik 21: grammar (end)

*bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-1), the suffix *yu* by *bāhulaka*: *vipanyu*, a word ending in *u*; *yu* is udātta by the suffix accent; in the nominative plural it becomes *vipanyavaḥ*.

**जागृवांसः (jāgṛvāṃsaḥ)** — the root *jāgṛ nidrākṣaye*; after it *liṭ*; for *liṭ*, by *liṭaḥ kānaj vā* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-106) and *kvasuś ca* (3-2-107), the suffix *kvas*. The reduplication laid down by *liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-8) does not come here, as a Vedic matter. For *vas*, the augment *iṭ* would be due by *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35); then by *neḍ vaśi kṛti* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-8) — a *kṛt* beginning with a *vaś* letter does not take *iṭ* — the prohibition would be due; then the prohibitions of *iṭ* laid down by sūtras such as *kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-13) and *ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt* (7-2-10), conditioned by particular roots (resting on the root), and those laid down by sūtras such as *śryukaḥ kiti* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-11), conditioned by particular suffixes — however many prohibiting rules there are, in the case of *liṭ* they apply only to the *liṭ* after the four roots *kṛ*, *sṛ*, *bhṛ*, *vṛ*: no prohibition of *iṭ* applies to the *liṭ* after roots other than these four, *kṛ* and the rest: this is the substance of the *krādi* restriction. By this restriction, since no prohibiting rule applies to the *liṭ* after the root *jāgṛ*, which is not in the present *krādi* list, the augment *iṭ* would be due; but by the restriction *vasv ekājādghasām* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-67) — on the view that the suffix *vasu* takes the augment *iṭ*, only for the suffix after roots that have one vowel after the reduplication, roots ending in *ā*, and the root *ghasḷ* does the augment *iṭ* come; the *vas* after other roots does not take *iṭ* — since the root *jāgṛ* is not among these roots, it is prevented. So the augment *iṭ* does not come. Nominative plural *jas*: *jāgṛ* + *vas* + *as*; now by *ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70) the augment *num*: *jāgṛvāns* + *as*; by *sānta mahataḥ saṃyogasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-10) lengthening of the *a* before the *n*: *jāgṛvāns* + *as*; by *naś cāpadāntasya jhali* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-24) *anusvāra* for the *n*: *jāgṛvāṃs* + *as* = *jāgṛvāṃsaḥ*. ॥21॥

*(An ornament follows: the close of Sūkta 22.)*

## ॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 23 — *"tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gahi"* ("The Twenty-third Sūkta"; sixth sūkta of the Fifth Anuvāka)

*(Printed pp. 141–233.)*

### Page 141 — Sūkta 23: title and introduction

*(At the head: ॥ श्रीः ॥ and the title ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ("The Twenty-third Sūkta"). Header: Varga 8.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** (introductory note)

*(Numbers as printed: अनु० १२-२, ५-२, १२-१४; आ० ७-६.)*

> तीव्रा इति चतुर्विंशत्यृचं षष्ठं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । तीव्राश्चतुर्विंशतिर्वायव्यैकैन्द्रवायव्यौ मैत्रावरुणमरुत्वतीयवैश्वदेवपौष्णास्तृचाः शेषा आप्योऽन्त्याध्यर्धाग्नेय्यप्स्वन्तः पुरउष्णिक् परानुष्टुप्तिस्रश्चान्त्या एकविंशी प्रतिष्ठेति । ऋषिश्चान्यस्मात् । अनु० १२-२ । इति परिभाषयानुवर्तनान्मेधातिथिः काण्व ऋषिः । अप्स्वन्तरित्येषा पुरउष्णिक् । प्रथमपादस्य द्वादशाक्षरेणाद्यश्चेत्पुर उष्णिक् । अनु० ५-२ । इति लक्षणसद्भावात् । अप्सु मे सोम इत्येषानुष्टुप् । इदमाप इत्याद्यास्तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभः । शिष्टा एकोनविंशतिसंख्याका ऋचो गायत्र्यः । आदौ गायत्रमिति परिभाषितत्वात् । अनु० १२-१४ । आद्या वायुदेवताका । ततो द्वे ऋचाविन्द्रवायूदेवताके । तत एकस्तृचो मित्रावरुणदेवत्यः । तत उत्तरतृचस्य मरुद्गणविशिष्टेन्द्रो देवता । तत एकस्तृचो वैश्वदेवः । तदनन्तरभावी पौष्णः । शिष्टा ऋचोऽब्देवताकाः । पयस्वानग्न इत्यर्धर्चयुक्ता सं माग्न इत्येषा त्वग्निदेवताका ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लिङ्गादवगन्तव्यः । अभिप्लवषडहस्य द्वितीयेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्रे वायव्यतृचस्य तीव्राः सोमास इत्येषा तृतीया । द्वितीयस्य चतुर्विंशेनेति खण्डे सूत्रितं । तीव्राः सोमास आ गहीत्येका । आ० ७-६ । इति । पृष्ठ्यषडहेऽपि द्वितीयेऽहनि प्रउग एषा ॥
>
> *tīvrā iti caturviṃśatyṛcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ | atreyamanukramaṇikā | tīvrāścaturviṃśatirvāyavyaikaindravāyavyau maitrāvaruṇamarutvatīyavaiśvadevapauṣṇāstṛcāḥ śeṣā āpyo 'ntyādhyardhāgneyyapsvantaḥ purauṣṇik parānuṣṭuptisraścāntyā ekaviṃśī pratiṣṭheti | ṛṣiścānyasmāt | anu0 12-2 | iti paribhāṣayānuvartanānmedhātithiḥ kāṇva ṛṣiḥ | apsvantarityeṣā purauṣṇik | prathamapādasya dvādaśākṣareṇādyaścetpura uṣṇik | anu0 5-2 | iti lakṣaṇasadbhāvāt | apsu me soma ityeṣānuṣṭup | idamāpa ityādyāstisro 'nuṣṭubhaḥ | śiṣṭā ekonaviṃśatisaṃkhyākā ṛco gāyatryaḥ | ādau gāyatramiti paribhāṣitatvāt | anu0 12-14 | ādyā vāyudevatākā | tato dve ṛcāvindravāyūdevatāke | tata ekastṛco mitrāvaruṇadevatyaḥ | tata uttaratṛcasya marudgaṇaviśiṣṭendro devatā | tata ekastṛco vaiśvadevaḥ | tadanantarabhāvī pauṣṇaḥ | śiṣṭā ṛco 'bdevatākāḥ | payasvānagna ityardharcayuktā saṃ māgna ityeṣā tvagnidevatākā || sūktaviniyogo liṅgādavagantavyaḥ | abhiplavaṣaḍahasya dvitīye 'hani praugaśastre vāyavyatṛcasya tīvrāḥ somāsa ityeṣā tṛtīyā | dvitīyasya caturviṃśeneti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gahītyekā | ā0 7-6 | iti | pṛṣṭhyaṣaḍahe 'pi dvitīye 'hani prauga eṣā ||*

**Translation:** "The sūkta *tīvrāḥ*, of twenty-four ṛks, is the sixth. Here is the Anukramaṇī: '*tīvrāḥ*, twenty-four: one to Vāyu, two to Indra-Vāyu; tṛcas to Mitra-Varuṇa, to Indra with the Maruts, to the All-gods, to Pūṣan; the rest to the Waters, the last one and a half to Agni; *apsv antaḥ* is a *pura-uṣṇik*, the next an *anuṣṭubh*, and the last three; the twenty-first is a *pratiṣṭhā*.' By the rule 'and the ṛṣi from the other' (Anu. 12-2), carried on, the ṛṣi is Medhātithi Kāṇva. *Apsv antaḥ* is a *pura-uṣṇik*, since the definition 'if the first [pāda] has twelve syllables, it is a *pura-uṣṇik*' (Anu. 5-2) applies. *Apsu me somaḥ* is an *anuṣṭubh*; the three beginning *idam āpaḥ* are *anuṣṭubhs*. The remaining nineteen ṛks are *gāyatrīs*, by the rule 'at the beginning, *gāyatra*' (Anu. 12-14). The first has Vāyu as deity; then two ṛks have Indra-Vāyu; then a tṛca to Mitra-Varuṇa; for the following tṛca the deity is Indra with the host of Maruts; then a tṛca to the All-gods; after that one to Pūṣan. The remaining ṛks have the Waters as deity; but the ṛk *saṃ māgne*, with the half-verse *payasvān agne*, has Agni as deity. The application of the sūkta is to be known from its marks. In the *abhiplava ṣaḍaha*, on the second day, at the *praüga-śastra*, *tīvrāḥ somāsaḥ* is the third of the tṛca to Vāyu; it is laid down in the section *dvitīyasya caturviṃśena*: '*tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gahi*: one' (Āśv. 7-6). In the *pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha* too, on the second day, at the *praüga*, this ṛk."

**Anuvāda (Kannada rendering):** This sūkta *tīvrāḥ* is the sixth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has twenty-four ṛks. About this sūkta the Anukramaṇī says thus: in this sūkta *tīvrāḥ* of twenty-four ṛks the first ṛk has Vāyu as deity; for the next two ṛks Indra and Vāyu are the deities; for the next three ṛks Mitra and Varuṇa; for the next three Indra and the Maruts; for the next three ṛks [the All-gods; for the next three] the deity called Pūṣan; for the next seven and a half ṛks the deity called the Waters (water); and for the last one and a half ṛks Agni is the deity. On the metre: ṛks one to eighteen are in the Gāyatrī metre; it is said that the nineteenth ṛk *apsv antaḥ* is *pura-uṣṇik*, the twentieth and from the twenty-second to the twenty-fourth are in the Anuṣṭubh metre, and the twenty-first ṛk is in the Pratiṣṭhā metre. The ṛṣi is Medhātithi Kāṇva, the ṛṣi of the previous sūkta —

### Page 142 — Sūkta 23: introduction (end), heading block

— as said in Anu. 12-2. The nineteenth ṛk *apsv antaḥ* is in the metre called *pura-uṣṇik*. The Uṣṇik metre has three pādas, with eight syllables each in the first and second pādas and twelve syllables in the third pāda. If instead the first pāda has twelve syllables and the second and third pādas eight syllables each, that ṛk is said to be in the *pura-uṣṇik* metre; so the ṛk *apsv antaḥ* stated above is in the *pura-uṣṇik* metre (Anu. 5-2). The twentieth ṛk *apsu me somaḥ* and the three ṛks *idam āpaḥ pra vahata* are in the Anuṣṭubh metre. In the Anuṣṭubh metre there are four pādas with eight syllables in each pāda: this is the definition of the Anuṣṭubh metre. The first eighteen ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre; in the Gāyatrī metre there are three pādas with eight syllables in each pāda. The twenty-first ṛk is in the metre named Pratiṣṭhā. In the Pratiṣṭhā metre there are three pādas: eight syllables in the first pāda, seven syllables in the second pāda, and six syllables in the third pāda: this is the definition of the Pratiṣṭhā metre. We have stated the deities of the ṛks in the sūkta before. The application of the sūkta is to be known according to the meaning of each ṛk. On the second day of the rite called *abhiplava ṣaḍaha*, when reciting the *praüga-śastra* mantras, the three ṛks *tīvrāḥ somāsaḥ* are to be recited as the tṛca to Vāyu: so it is said in the section *dvitīyasya caturviṃśena* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra (Ā. 7-6). It is said there too that in the *pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha* rite, on the second day, this tṛca is to be recited as the *praüga-śastra* mantra.

*(The Anuvāda says "the three ṛks"; the bhāṣya says the one ṛk *tīvrāḥ somāsaḥ*, the third of the tṛca. Both as printed.)*

**॥ Sūkta — 23 ॥**
**॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 5 ॥ Sūkta — 23 ॥**
**॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 2 ॥ Varga, 8–12 ॥**
**॥ Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 24 ॥**
**॥ Ṛṣiḥ — Medhātithiḥ Kāṇvaḥ ॥**
**॥ Devatā — 1 Vāyuḥ | 2–3 Indravāyū | 4–6 Mitrāvaruṇau | 7–9 Indro marutvān | 10–12 Viśve devāḥ | 13–15 Pūṣā | 16–22½ Āpaḥ | 22½–24 Agniḥ ॥**
**॥ Chandaḥ — 1–18 Gāyatrī | 19 Pura-uṣṇik | 20 Anuṣṭup | 21 Pratiṣṭhā | 22–24 Anuṣṭup ॥**

>
> *he vāyo ime somāsa aindravāyavagrahādirūpāḥ somāḥ sutā abhiṣutāḥ | te ca tīvrāḥ prabhūtatvāttarpayituṃ samarthā āśīrvanta āśirayuktāḥ | atastvamā gahi | asminkarmaṇyāgaccha | prasthitānuttaravediṃ pratyānītāṃstānsomānpiba || somāsaḥ | artistusu ityādinā man | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | ājjaserasuk | gahi | marudbhiragna ā gahi | ṛgve0 1-19-1 | ityatroktaṃ | āśīrvantaḥ | śrīñ pāke | apaspṛdhethāmityādisūtre | pā0 6-1-36 | āṅpūrvasya kvipi śirādeśo nipātitaḥ | karaṇasyāpi śrayaṇadravyasya svavyāpāre kartṛtvavivakṣayā kartari kvip na virudhyate | āśīreṣāmastītyāśīrvantaḥ | chandasīra iti vatvaṃ | vāyo | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | prasthitān | prādisamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ bādhitvā vyatyayenāvyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "O Vāyu! *Ime somāsaḥ*, these somas in the form of the cup to Indra-Vāyu and the rest, are *sutāḥ*, pressed. And they are *tīvrāḥ*, able to satisfy because they are abundant, *āśīrvantaḥ*, furnished with the admixture (*āśir*). So *ā gahi*, come to this rite. *Piba*, drink *tān*, those somas, *prasthitān*, brought to the *uttaravedi*." (Grammatical tail: *somāsaḥ*, *man* by *artistusu…*, initial udātta as *nit*, *asuk* by *āj jaser asuk*; *gahi*, stated at *marudbhir agna ā gahi* (Ṛgve. 1-19-1); *āśīrvantaḥ*, *śrīñ pāke*; in the sūtra *apaspṛdhethām…* (Pā. 6-1-36) the substitute *śir* is given as a set form for the root with *āṅ* before *kvip*; though the mixing substance is an instrument, *kvip* in the agent sense is not contradicted, since it is meant as agent in its own action; 'they have *āśir*': *āśīrvantaḥ*, the *v* by *chandasīraḥ*; *vāyo*, the vocative initial udātta; *prasthitān*, in the *prādi* compound, overriding the accent of the *kṛt* final member, the indeclinable first member's accent by *vyatyaya*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) वायो ((he) vāyo)** — O Vāyu | **इमे सोमासः (ime somāsaḥ)** — these soma juices | **तीव्राः (tīvrāḥ)** — very abundant (or full of essence) | **आशीर्वन्तः (āśīrvantaḥ)** — mixed with the *āśir* substances, curds, barley and the rest | **सुताः (sutāḥ)** — made ready by pressing so as to be fit to drink | **प्रस्थितान् (prasthitān)** — brought to the *uttaravedi* of the sacrifice | **तान् (tān)** — those soma juices | **पिब (piba)** — drink.

### Page 144 — Rik 1: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Vāyu, these soma juices are mixed with *āśir* substances such as curds and are full of essence. We have brought that soma juice, made ready in this way for your drinking, to the *uttaravedi*. Drink it.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> These intoxicating Soma juice flavoured with milk, barley, and butter-milk are extracted and placed for your use. O Vayu, drink those Soma juices.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**तीव्राः (tīvrāḥ)** — the commentator has given the meaning 'in great quantity'; Skandasvāmin 'sharp (pungent or bitter)'; and Veṅkaṭamādhava 'intoxicating'. The pandit Wilson and the author of the *Vedārthayatna* have translated it as "Sharp". Among these various meanings, Veṅkaṭamādhava's meaning is the more fitting. For this word the meaning "full of essence, highly-concentrated, intoxicating" fits rightly here.

**आशीर्वन्तः (āśīrvantaḥ)** — the custom is to use soma juice mixed with substances such as milk, curds and barley, to make it tasty. Such mixed substances are named *āśir* substances. Soma juice mixed with milk is named *gavāśira*, juice mixed with curds *dadhyāśira*, and juice mixed with barley (flour) *yavāśira*. The pandit Wilson has translated this word as "Blessing-bearing". That does not seem right.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**सोमासः (somāsaḥ)** — by *artistusuhusṛdhṛkṣikṣubhāyāvāpadiyakṣinībhyo man* (U. Sū. 1-137 [?]) — after these roots, *ṛ gatau*, *ṣṭuñ stutau*, *ṣuñ abhiṣave*, *hu dānādanayoḥ*, *sṛ gatau*, *dhṛñ dhāraṇe*, *kṣi kṣaye*, *kṣu śabde*, *bhā dīptau*, *yā prāpaṇe*, *vā gatigandhanayoḥ*, *pada gatau*, *yakṣa pūjāyām*, *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*, the suffix *man* comes — the suffix *man* after the root *su*, read as *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; by *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) *s* for the *ṣ*: *su* + *ma*; by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) *guṇa*, *o* for the *u*: *soma* is formed. The *man*

### Page 145 — Rik 1: grammar (continued)

suffix is *nit*; so by *ñnity ādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 [?]) the word *soma* is initially udātta; after it *jas*; by *āj jaser asuk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50) the augment *asuk* for *jas*.

**गहि (gahi)** — the derivation is described at *marudbhir agna ā gahi* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-19-1).

**आशीर्वन्तः (āśīrvantaḥ)** — the root *śrīñ pāke*. In *apaspṛdhethām ānṛcur ānṛhuś cicyuṣe tityāja śrātāḥ śritam āśīr āśīrtāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-36): the root *spardha saṃgharṣe*; after it *laṅ*; for it the middle person dual *āthām*: *spardh* + *āthām*; by *luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ* the augment *aṭ*, *śap*: *a-spardh* + *a* + *āthām*; by *āto ṅitaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-81) — the *ā* of a *ṅit* after a short *a* takes the substitute *iy* — the substitute *iy* for the *ā*: *a-spardh* + *a* + *iyāthām*, *guṇa*, dropping of the *y*: *aspardhethām* results in common usage. Here, in the Veda, the reduplication of the root, *saṃprasāraṇa* *ṛ* for the *r*, and dropping of the *a* of the *spa* of the latter part are all given as set forms; so in *a-spardh-spardh-a-āthām*, in the reduplicate, by *śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-61) the *p* remains. *A-pa-spardh* + *a* + *āthām*: in the second, *ṛ* for the *r* and dropping of the *a* of *spa* having come, the rest of the derivation is set out as before, and it becomes *apaspṛdhethām*. This very part the author of the Mahābhāṣya has made clear by the *vārttika*:

> स्पर्धेर्लङ्यात्मनेपदानां मध्यमपुरुषस्य द्विवचने आथामि द्विर्वचने संप्रसारणमकारलोपश्च ।
>
> *spardherlaṅyātmanepadānāṃ madhyamapuruṣasya dvivacane āthāmi dvirvacane saṃprasāraṇamakāralopaśca |*

This derivation is described according to the branch in which *apaspṛdhethām* is one word; in another branch it is said to consist of two words. On that view, after the root *spardh* preceded by the prefix *apa*, *laṅ*, for it *āthām*, *śap*, the substitute *iy*, *guṇa*, dropping of the *y*; since it is Vedic, the augment *aṭ* does not come. In *apa spṛdhethām*, *ṛ* for the *r* and dropping of the *a* of *spa* are given as set forms. This part becomes clear from the other *vārttika*:

> अपपूर्वात् स्पर्धेर्लङ्यात्मनेपदानां मध्यमपुरुषस्य द्विवचने आथामि संप्रसारणमकारलोपश्च ।
>
> *apapūrvāt spardherlaṅyātmanepadānāṃ madhyamapuruṣasya dvivacane āthāmi saṃprasāraṇamakāralopaśca |*

On the first view *apaspṛdhethām* is initially udātta; on the second view *spṛdhethām* is initially udātta; by *tiṅi codāttavati* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-71, as printed) the *apa* is unaccented. Since in the sūtra the direction is in the monotone, which includes all accents, both, having different accents, are included here. *Ānarcuḥ*, *ānarhuḥ* are, in common usage, the forms of the third person plural of *liṭ* of the roots *arca pūjāyām* and *arha pūjāyām*. In the Veda, *saṃprasāraṇa* of the *r* and dropping of the *a* are given as set forms: it becomes *ānṛcuḥ*, *ānṛhuḥ*. The root *cyuṅ*, *liṭ*, *thās*: it becomes *cucyuṣe*. The root *tyaja*, *liṭ*, third person singular: it becomes *tatyāja*. In the last two, the substitute *i* for the vowel of the reduplicate is given as a set form. According to the *vārttika* —

> श्रीणातेः क्ते श्राभावश्रिभावौ ।
>
> *śrīṇāteḥ kte śrābhāvaśribhāvau |*

### Page 146 — Rik 1: grammar (end)

— when the suffix *kta* is put after the root *śrīñ pāke*, if the substitute *śrā* comes for the root it becomes *śrāta*, and if the substitute *śri* comes it becomes *śrita*. When the suffix *kvip* comes after the root *śrīñ pāke* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, the substitute *śir* for the root is given as a set form by the present sūtra. In *kvip* all letters are dropped; the nominative singular suffix *su*; by *halṅyābbhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-68) *su* is dropped; by *vor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-76) — in the case of a *pada*-end, the *i*, *u*, *ṛ*, *ḷ* penultimate in roots ending in *r* or *v* are lengthened — the *i* is lengthened: it became *āśīr*. With the analysis *āśīḥ eṣām asti*, by *tad asyāsty asminn iti matup* (Pā. Sū. 5-2-94) the suffix *matup*: *āśīr* + *mat*; now by *chandasīraḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-15) — in the Veda, *v* is substituted for the *m* of *matup* after words ending in *i* and in *r* — the substitute *v* for the *m*: *āśīrvat*; after it *jas*, the augment *num* by *ugidacām* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70), *ru* and *visarga*: it becomes *āśīrvantaḥ*.

**वायो (vāyo)** — this ends in the vocative nominative singular. So by *sāmantritam* (Pā. Sū. 2-3-48) — the vocative nominative singular gets the name *āmantrita* — it has the name *āmantrita*. By the sixth-book sūtra *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) the initial udātta accent comes.

**प्रस्थितान् (prasthitān)** — *sthita* ends in the suffix *kta*; by *kugatiprādayaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-2-18) the *prādi* compound. Now, though by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the own accent of the *kṛt* final member would be due, by *vyatyayo bahulam* the indeclinable first member's own accent comes by interchange. *Pra*, by *upasargāś cābhivarjam* (Phi. Sū. 82 [?]) — the prefixes other than *abhi* are initially udātta — is initially udātta; as said before, that same accent stays. ॥1॥

### Page 147 — Rik 2: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> उभा । देवा । दिविऽस्पृशा । इन्द्रवायू इति । हवामहे ॥
> अस्य । सोमस्य । पीतये ॥२॥
>
> *ubhā | devā | divi 'spṛśā | indravāyū iti | havāmahe ||*
> *asya | somasya | pītaye ||2||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० ७-६, पा० ६-३-९-१, ६-३-२६-१, ६-२-१४२, ३-३-९५. The word read इत्यस्मिको is not clear [?].)*

> पूर्वोक्त एव शस्त्र उभा देवा दिविस्पृशेति द्वे ऐन्द्रवायवतृचस्य प्रथमाद्वितीये । तथा च द्वितीयस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितं । उभा देवा दिविस्पृशेति द्वे । आ० ७-६ । इति ॥
>
> *pūrvokta eva śastra ubhā devā divispṛśeti dve aindravāyavatṛcasya prathamādvitīye | tathā ca dvitīyasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | ubhā devā divispṛśeti dve | ā0 7-6 | iti ||*

**Translation (application):** "In the same *śastra* spoken of before, the two ṛks *ubhā devā divispṛśā* are the first and second of the tṛca to Indra-Vāyu; and so it is laid down in the section *dvitīyasya*: '*ubhā devā divispṛśā*: two' (Āśv. 7-6)."

> दिविस्पृशा द्युलोकवर्तिनावुभा देवा द्वौ देवाविन्द्रवायू हवामहे । आह्वयामः । किमर्थं । अस्य सोमस्य पीतये । असकृद्व्याख्यातं ॥ उभा देवा । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । दिविस्पृशा । हृद्द्युभ्यां ङेरुपसंख्यानं । पा० ६-३-९-१ । इति सप्तम्या अलुक् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । इन्द्रवायू । इन्द्रश्च वायुश्चेति द्वन्द्वः । उभयत्र वायोः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः । पा० ६-३-२६-१ । इत्यानङो निषेधः । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति प्राप्तस्योभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वस्य नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादौ । पा० ६-२-१४२ । इति निषेधात्समासान्तोदात्तत्वमेव शिष्यते । हवामहे । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणं । संप्रसारणाच्चेति परपूर्वत्वं । शप् । गुणावादेशौ । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण पदस्याद्युदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते तिङ्ङतिङ इत्यस्मिको [?] निघातः । अस्य । ऊडिदमित्यादिना षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वं । पीतये । पा पाने । स्थागापापचः । पा० ३-३-९५ । इति भावे क्तिन् । घुमास्थेतीत्वं । व्यत्ययेनान्तोदात्तत्वं ॥
>
> *divispṛśā dyulokavartināvubhā devā dvau devāvindravāyū havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | kimarthaṃ | asya somasya pītaye | asakṛdvyākhyātaṃ || ubhā devā | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | divispṛśā | hṛddyubhyāṃ ṅerupasaṃkhyānaṃ | pā0 6-3-9-1 | iti saptamyā aluk | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | indravāyū | indraśca vāyuśceti dvandvaḥ | ubhayatra vāyoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ | pā0 6-3-26-1 | ityānaṅo niṣedhaḥ | devatādvandve ceti prāptasyobhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvasya nottarapade 'nudāttādau | pā0 6-2-142 | iti niṣedhātsamāsāntodāttatvameva śiṣyate | havāmahe | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇaṃ | saṃprasāraṇācceti parapūrvatvaṃ | śap | guṇāvādeśau | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa padasyādyudāttatve prāpte tiṅṅatiṅa ityasmiko [?] nighātaḥ | asya | ūḍidamityādinā ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvaṃ | pītaye | pā pāne | sthāgāpāpacaḥ | pā0 3-3-95 | iti bhāve ktin | ghumāsthetītvaṃ | vyatyayenāntodāttatvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "We *havāmahe*, call, *ubhā devā*, the two gods Indra and Vāyu, *divispṛśā*, dwelling in the world of heaven. For what? *Asya somasya pītaye*: explained more than once." (Grammatical tail: *ubhā devā*, the *ā* by *supāṃ suluk*; *divispṛśā*, the locative not dropped by *hṛddyubhyāṃ ṅer upasaṃkhyānam* (Pā. 6-3-9-1); the *kṛt* final member's accent; *indravāyū*, the *dvandva* 'Indra and Vāyu'; *ānaṅ* barred by *ubhayatra vāyoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ* (Pā. 6-3-26-1); the accent of both members due by *devatādvandve ca* is barred by *nottarapade 'nudāttādau* (Pā. 6-2-142), so only the compound-final udātta remains; *havāmahe*, *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*, *saṃprasāraṇa* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the preceding form by *saṃprasāraṇāc ca*, *śap*, *guṇa* and *av*; *śap* unaccented as *pit*, and the *tiṅ* by the *lasārvadhātuka* accent; when the word would be initially udātta, the loss of accent by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*; *asya*, the genitive udātta by *ūḍidam…*; *pītaye*, *pā pāne*, *ktin* in the action sense by *sthāgāpāpacaḥ* (Pā. 3-3-95), *ī* by *ghumāsthā…*, final udātta by *vyatyaya*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā)** — who are in the world of heaven | **उभा देवा (ubhā devā)** — the two deities | **इन्द्रवायू (indravāyū)** — the deities called Indra and Vāyu | **अस्य सोमस्य (asya somasya)** — of this soma juice made ready here | **पीतये (pītaye)** — for drinking | **हवामहे (havāmahe)** — we call.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

We now call (summon) the two deities Indra and Vāyu, who are in the world of heaven, to drink the soma juice made ready here.

### Page 148 — Rik 2: English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> We invoke the two gods Indra and Vayu that reach the sky, in order that they may drink this Soma.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā)** — this word, ending in the dual, conveys meanings such as 'touching heaven', that is, going to heaven, being in heaven.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**उभा देवा (ubhā devā)** — for the accusative dual suffix *auṭ* after the words *ubha* and *deva*, the substitute *ā* by *supāṃ suluk pūrvasavarṇācchheyāḍāḍyāyājālaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39).

**दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā)** — the analysis is *divaṃ spṛśata iti divispṛśau*; the substitute *ā* for *auṭ* as before. Since the *vārttika* *hṛddyubhyāṃ ṅer upasaṃkhyānam* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-9-1) lays down that the locative singular after the words *hṛt* and *div* is not dropped in a compound, it is made clear by the *vārttika* *anyārthe ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-9-2) that here the locative comes in the sense of the object. So for the locative singular suffix, by the *vārttika* *hṛddyubhyām…*, the *luk* does not come. By *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the final member *spṛk*, ending in a *kṛt*, keeps its own accent. The final member is udātta by the root accent, and that accent stays.

**इन्द्रवायू (indravāyū)** — the analysis is *indraś ca vāyuś ca*. Indra and Vāyu both denote deities. So *indravāyū* is a *dvandva* of deities; by *devatādvandve ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-26) — in a *dvandva* of deities, the word before the last member takes *ānaṅ* — *ānaṅ* would be due for the word *indra*. Yet since there is the prohibition by *devatādvandve ubhayatra vāyoḥ pratiṣedhaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-26-1) — in a *dvandva* compound containing words denoting deities, whether the word *vāyu* is first or last member, the prohibition of the substitute *ānaṅ* must be stated — the substitute *ānaṅ* does not come. The word *indra*, ending in the suffix *ran* by *ṛjrendrāgra…* (U. Sū. 2-186), is initially udātta; the word *vāyu* ends in the suffix *uṇ* by *kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhya uṇ* (U. Sū. 1-1), so it is final udātta by the suffix accent. By *devatādvandve ca* (6-2-141) — in a *dvandva* compound of words denoting deities, both first and last members keep their own accent at the same time — the accent of both members would be due —

### Page 149 — Rik 2: grammar (continued)

— yet by *nottarapade 'nudāttādāv apṛthivīrudrapūṣamanthiṣu* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-142) — when a word beginning with an unaccented vowel, other than the words *pṛthivī* and the rest named in the sūtra, follows, the accent of both members stated in the previous sūtra does not come — the accent of both members does not come. By *samāsasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223) the final udātta alone comes.

**हवामहे (havāmahe)** — the root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *laṭ*, first person plural, the suffix *mahiṅ*. For its *ṭi*, by *ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-79), *e*; the *vikaraṇa* *śap*: *hve* + *a* + *mahe*. Now by *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-34) — in the Veda the root *hveñ* variously takes *saṃprasāraṇa* — *saṃprasāraṇa*, that is *u* for the *v*; then by *saṃprasāraṇāc ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-108) the preceding form: *hu* + *a* + *mahe*; by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) *guṇa* *o* for the *u*; by *eco 'yavāyāvaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-78) the substitute *av* for *o*: *hava* + *mahe*; by *ato dīrgho yañi* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-101) — when a *sārvadhātuka* beginning with a *yañ* letter follows, a stem ending in short *a* is lengthened — lengthening: it became *havāmahe*. *Śap* being *pit*, it is unaccented by *anudāttau suppitau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4); the long vowel coming in its place is unaccented by *sthānivadbhāva*; *mahe*, a *sārvadhātuka* suffix coming in place of *la*, follows *śap*, an *a*-final original teaching. By *tāsy anudāttenṅid adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam ahnviṅoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) it is unaccented; the *ha* is udātta by the root accent; so *havāmahe* had to be an initially udātta word. But by the eighth-book sūtra *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) it becomes wholly unaccented.

**अस्य (asya)** — when the genitive singular suffix is put after the word *idam*: *idam* + *jas* [as printed]; by *tyadādīnām aḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) — when a case-ending follows, *a* comes as the final substitute for the words read in the *tyadādi* class — *a* for the *m*; by *ato guṇe* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) — when the *guṇa* vowels *a*, *e*, *o* follow an *a* not at the end of a *pada*, the following form comes as the single substitute for the preceding and following — the following form: *ida* + *jas*; by *ṭāṅasiṅasām inātsyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-12) — after a word ending in short *a*, *ina*, *āt*, *sya* come in order for *ṭā*, *ṅasi*, *ṅas* — the substitute *sya*; by *hali lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-113) — when a consonant-initial ending of the third case onward follows, the *id* of the word *idam* without *k* is dropped — the *id* is dropped and *asya* is formed. By *phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ* (Phi. Sū. 1) — *phiṭ* means a nominal stem — by this sūtra the *a* of the stem is udātta. For *sya*, by *anudāttau suppitau*

### Page 150 (upper) — Rik 2: grammar (end)

(Pā. Sū. 3-1-4), the unaccented would be due; overriding it, by *ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) — the case-endings other than the *sarvanāmasthāna* after these final-udātta monosyllabic words, the substitute *ūṭh*, the word *idam*, the six *padādi* words laid down by *paddannomās…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-63), and *ap*, *pums*, *rai*, *div*, are udātta — *sya* is udātta. Then by the *śeṣānudātta* accent *anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-158) the *a* of the stem is unaccented. That the soma in front is meant is made known by *asya*. So there is no *anvādeśa*; hence by *idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-32) the unaccented substitute *aś* does not come. Therefore *asya* does not become wholly unaccented.

**पीतये (pītaye)** — the root *pā pāne*; by *sthāgāpāpaco bhāve* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-95) — after these roots, *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*, *gai śabde*, *pā pāne*, *ḍupacaṣ pāke*, the suffix *ktin* in the action sense — the suffix *ktin*: *pā* + *ti*. Either by *ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-10) or by *titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-9) the *iṭ* is barred. By *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66) — when a consonant-initial *ārdhadhātuka* suffix that is *kit* or *ṅit* follows, the roots *dā*, *dhā* with the name *ghu*, and *sthā*, *gā*, *pā*, *jahā*, *ti* [as printed], *sā* take the substitute *ī* — the substitute *ī* for *pā*: it became *pīti*. Since the suffix is *nit*, by *ñnity ādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) the initial udātta would be due; yet by *vyatyaya* the final udātta alone comes. In the dative singular it becomes *pītaye*. ॥2॥

> इ॒न्द्र॒वा॒यू म॑नो॒जुवा॒ विप्रा॑ हवन्त ऊ॒तये॑ ।
> स॒ह॒स्रा॒क्षा धि॒यस्पती॑ ॥३॥ [accent ?]
>
> *indravāyū́ manojúvā víprā havanta ūtáye |*

*(Bars under इ, द्र, वा (वायू), नो, वा (जुवा) and ऊ; strokes over म, प्रा and ये. Line 2: bars under स, ह, स्रा and धि; a stroke over ती (in the Pada a bar under ती and a stroke over इति) [accent ?]. The Pada prints हवंते.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रवायू इति । मनःऽजुवा । विप्राः । हवन्ते । ऊतये ॥
> सहस्रऽअक्षा । धियः । पती इति ॥३॥
>
> *indravāyū iti | manaḥ 'juvā | viprāḥ | havante | ūtaye ||*

### Page 151 — Rik 3: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(The number is printed पा० ५-४-११३.)*

> विप्रा मेधाविन ऋत्विग्यजमाना ऊतये रक्षणार्थमिन्द्रवायू हवन्ते । आह्वयन्ति । कीदृशौ । मनोजुवा मन इव वेगवत्तरौ सहस्राक्षा सहस्रनयनयुक्तौ । यद्यपीन्द्र एव सहस्राक्षस्तथापि छत्रिन्यायेन वायुरपि तथोच्यते । धियस्पती कर्मणो बुद्धेर्वा पालकौ ॥ मनोजुवा । जवतिर्गतिकर्मा । मनोवज्जवत इति मनोजुवा मन इव वेगयुक्तौ । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । विप्राः । औणादिको रन् । रन्प्रत्ययान्त आद्युदात्तः । ऊतये । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन उदात्तत्वं । सहस्राक्षा । सहस्रमक्षीणि ययोस्तौ । बहुव्रीहौ सक्थ्यक्ष्णोः । पा० ५-४-११३ । इति षच्समासान्तः । बहुव्रीहिस्वरे प्राप्ते समासान्तप्रत्ययस्य सति शिष्टत्वाच्चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । धियः । सावेकाच इति ङस उदात्तत्वं । षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेति संहितायां विसर्जनीयस्य सकारः । पती । डत्यन्त आद्युदात्तः ॥
>
> *viprā medhāvina ṛtvigyajamānā ūtaye rakṣaṇārthamindravāyū havante | āhvayanti | kīdṛśau | manojuvā mana iva vegavattarau sahasrākṣā sahasranayanayuktau | yadyapīndra eva sahasrākṣastathāpi chatrinyāyena vāyurapi tathocyate | dhiyaspatī karmaṇo buddhervā pālakau || manojuvā | javatirgatikarmā | manovajjavata iti manojuvā mana iva vegayuktau | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | viprāḥ | auṇādiko ran | ranpratyayānta ādyudāttaḥ | ūtaye | ūtiyūtītyādinā ktina udāttatvaṃ | sahasrākṣā | sahasramakṣīṇi yayostau | bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ | pā0 5-4-113 | iti ṣacsamāsāntaḥ | bahuvrīhisvare prāpte samāsāntapratyayasya sati śiṣṭatvāccita ityantodāttatvaṃ | dhiyaḥ | sāvekāca iti ṅasa udāttatvaṃ | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputreti saṃhitāyāṃ visarjanīyasya sakāraḥ | patī | ḍatyanta ādyudāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "The *viprāḥ*, the wise — priests and sacrificers — *havante*, call, Indra and Vāyu *ūtaye*, for protection. Of what kind are they? *Manojuvā*, swifter, like the mind; *sahasrākṣā*, furnished with a thousand eyes: though only Indra is thousand-eyed, Vāyu too is so called by the maxim of 'the umbrella-bearers'; *dhiyaspatī*, protectors of the rite or of the intellect." (Grammatical tail: *manojuvā*, *javati* in the sense of going; 'they go like the mind': *manojuvā*, swift like the mind; the *kṛt* final member's accent; the *ā* by *supāṃ suluk*; *viprāḥ*, the Uṇādi *ran*, initial udātta as ending in *ran*; *ūtaye*, the *ktin* udātta by *ūtiyūti…*; *sahasrākṣā*, 'whose eyes are a thousand': the compound-final *ṣac* by *bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ…* (Pā. 5-4-113); though the bahuvrīhi accent would be due, the compound-final suffix being *satiśiṣṭa*, final udātta by *citaḥ*; *dhiyaḥ*, the *ṅas* udātta by *sāv ekācaḥ*; in the Saṃhitā *s* for the *visarga* by *ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra…*; *patī*, initial udātta as ending in *ḍati*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**विप्राः (viprāḥ)** — the intelligent (wise) people | **मनोजुवा (manojuvā)** — swift-going like the speed of the mind | **सहस्राक्षा (sahasrākṣā)** — having thousands of eyes | **धियस्पती (dhiyaspatī)** — lords of rites, or lords of the intellect | **इन्द्रवायू (indravāyū)** — the two deities called Indra and Vāyu | **ऊतये (ūtaye)** — for protection | **हवन्ते (havante)** — call.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The deities called Indra and Vāyu have the speed of the mind, are furnished with a thousand eyes, are lords of rites or impellers of the intellect. The wise call such Indra and Vāyu for protection.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The wise invoke for protection Indra and Vayu who are swift as thought, who have a thousand eyes and who are the lords of the pious acts (or of mind).

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**मनोजुवा (manojuvā)** — *mana iva vegayuktau*: swift like the mind. The mind can think in a moment of a thing, however far away it is. So when indicating great speed, it is customary to use the comparison 'swift as the speed of the mind'.

### Page 152 — Rik 3: Special Topics (end), grammar

**सहस्राक्षा (sahasrākṣā)** — *sahasram akṣīṇi yayos tau*: having a thousand eyes. In the Purāṇas and in modern Sanskrit too it is customary to call Indra 'thousand-eyed'. The reason why in the Veda such a meaning, 'having a thousand eyes', arose is this: Indra is in heaven (in the mid-air). In heaven thousands of stars twinkle like eyes. So it seems the custom of calling Indra 'furnished with a thousand eyes' may have come about. Though it is fitting here to call Indra thousand-eyed, it is not right to describe Vāyu by this qualifying word. Either through association with Indra, or because Vāyu, being all-pervading, has the power to see everything, Vāyu may have been addressed as thousand-eyed. Likewise, though the word *manojuvā* fits Vāyu, the address here is such that it fits Indra too. The main intention is that the word *manojuvā* fits only Vāyu, who is always moving or of a moving nature; the word *sahasrākṣā* indicates Indra alone. Yet these words are used here as qualifying words praising both Indra and Vāyu.

**धियस्पती (dhiyaspatī)** — the word *dhī* means rite or understanding. So *dhiyaspatī* means: lords of the good rites such as sacrifice that we perform, that is, those able to protect them so that they are accomplished without hindrance; or those able to make our intellect devoted to good works; or those able to impel our intellect to good works: this is the intention. Likewise the meanings of the words *śubhaspatī*, *jyotiṣaspatī*, *vācaspati*, *śavasaspati* and the like are worth noting.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**मनोजुवा (manojuvā)** — the root *ju* is not read in the list of roots, but it is read in the sūtra *ju caṅkramya…* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-150). In the Kaumudī it is said, *ju iti sautro dhātur gatau vege ca*, that it has both meanings, going and speed. When the sense is *manovat javata iti*, 'they go like the mind (swiftly)', the suffix *kvip* by *kvip ca*, an *upapada* compound; after *manoju* the accusative dual suffix *auṭ*, and for it by *supāṃ suluk…* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute *ā*: *manoju* + *ā*; here, by *aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-77), when the substitute *uvaṅ* comes, it becomes *manojuvā*. By *gatikārakapūrvasyaiveṣyate* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-82 Vā.) — the *yaṇ* in the case of roots ending in *i*, *u* that have some word before them comes only when the first member is named *gati* or *kāraka*; for roots ending in *i*, *u* whose first members are other than *gati* and *kāraka*, *yaṇ* —

### Page 153 — Rik 3: grammar (continued)

— does not come; so the *yaṇ* that would come by *oḥ supi* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-83) is prevented. Here, in the sense of likeness meaning *iva*, the word *manaḥ* in the first case is construed; it is not construed with the action. So it is clear that it is neither a *gati* nor a *kāraka*.

**विप्राः (viprāḥ)** — by the sūtra *ṛjrendrāgravipra…* (U. Sū. 2-186), after the root *ḍuvap bījasantāne*, it is given as a set form ending in the suffix *ran*; the substitute *i* for the *a* of the root is given as a set form in this sūtra; the suffix is *nit*, so by *ñnity ādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) it is initially udātta.

**ऊतये (ūtaye)** — by *ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-97), the word *udāttaḥ* being carried on from the previous sūtra *mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-96), the sense of the sūtra is that the words ending in *ktin*, *ūti* and the rest, are given as set forms with final udātta. In the present case, after the root *ava rakṣaṇe*, the suffix *ktin*: *av* + *ti*; by *jvaratvarasrivyavimavām upadhāyāś ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-20), *ūṭh* for both the *a* and the *v*: *ūti* results. Since the suffix is *nit*, the *nit* accent, initial udātta, would be due; but by this sūtra it is final udātta.

**सहस्राक्षा (sahasrākṣā)** — the analysis is *sahasram akṣīṇi yayos tau*: the two who have a thousand eyes. This is a bahuvrīhi compound. In *bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac* (Pā. Sū. 5-4-113), *bahuvrīhau* is in the seventh case and *sakthyakṣṇoḥ* in the sixth, both in the sense of the fifth; *sakthyakṣṇoḥ* qualifies *bahuvrīhau*. So by *yena vidhis tadantasya* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72) 'ending in it' is obtained; the sūtras *samāsāntāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 5-4-68) and *taddhitāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-76) are the headings. The sense of the sūtra: after a bahuvrīhi compound ending in the words *sakthi*, *akṣi* that denote a limb of one's own body, *ṣac* comes; it is a part at the end of the compound and also has the name *taddhita*. *Adravaṃ mūrtimat svāṅgaṃ prāṇistham avikārajam | atatsthaṃ tatra dṛṣṭaṃ ca tasya cet tat tathāyutam* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-54 *śloka-vārttika*): the definition of *svāṅga* is stated in three ways. That which is not liquid, has a fixed measure, is not born of a disorder such as disease, and is in a living being is called *svāṅga*: this is the first definition. Even if not now in a living being, what has at some time been seen in a living being is called *svāṅga*: this is the second definition. A lifeless substance shaped like a living one — in the case where it is furnished with forms such as breasts that are in a living being — those forms such as breasts, though connected with a lifeless thing, are called *svāṅga*: this is the third definition. For the present *sakthi*, *akṣi*, the first definition alone applies. Thus, when *ṣac* comes by the previous sūtra: *sahasrākṣin* + *a*; by *nas taddhite* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-144) — when a *taddhita* suffix follows, the *ṭi* of a stem ending in *n* and named *bha* is dropped —

> अद्रवं मूर्तिमत्स्वाङ्गं प्राणिस्थमविकारजम् । अतत्स्थं तत्र दृष्टं च तस्य चेत्तत्तथायुतम् ॥
>
> *adravaṃ mūrtimatsvāṅgaṃ prāṇisthamavikārajam | atatsthaṃ tatra dṛṣṭaṃ ca tasya cettattathāyutam ||*

### Page 154 (upper) — Rik 3: grammar (end)

— the *in* is dropped: it became *sahasrākṣa*. By *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member's own accent would be due. Yet by *satiśiṣṭasvaro balīyān anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ*, since the *satiśiṣṭa* accent is stronger, the final udātta *citaḥ*, which is *satiśiṣṭa*, alone comes here. *Ṣac* is *cit*; for the case-ending the substitute *ā* as before.

> सतिशिष्टस्वरो बलीयानन्यत्र विकरणेभ्यः ।
>
> *satiśiṣṭasvaro balīyānanyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ |*

**धियः (dhiyaḥ)** — by *sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168), *su* meaning that the locative plural is intended: the sense of the sūtra is that when the locative plural suffix follows, the case-endings of the third onward after a word that has a single vowel are udātta. In *dhīṣu* the word *dhī* has a single vowel when the locative plural follows; so the genitive after the word *dhī* is udātta. In *dhiyaḥ* + *patī*, by *ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputrapṛṣṭhapārapadapayasposeṣu* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-53) — when the words *pati* and the rest follow, *s* is substituted for a *visarga* belonging to the genitive — the substitute *s* for the *visarga*.

**पती (patī)** — the root *pā rakṣaṇe*; by *pāter ḍatiḥ* (U. Sū. 4-57) the suffix *ḍati*; the suffix is *ḍit*; by the force of its being *ḍit*, even without the name *bha*, the *ṭi*, *ā*, is dropped: it becomes *pati*. And by *ādyudāttaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-3) it is initially udātta. ॥3॥
