### Page 182 — Rik 11: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: उ० ४-२, पा० ३-२-१४०. Printed त्वदीयः, as printed.)*

> मरुतां देवानां तन्यतुः शब्दो धृष्णुया धार्ष्ट्ययुक्तः सन्नेति । गच्छति । केषामिव । जयतां विजययुक्तानां शूराणां भटानामिव । हे नरो नेतारो मरुतो यूयं यद्यदा शुभं शोभनं देवयजनं याथन प्राप्नुथ । तदा त्वदीयः शब्दो गच्छतीति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ तन्यतुः । तनु विस्तारे । ऋतन्यञ्जीत्यादिना । उ० ४-२ । यतुच्प्रत्ययः । धृष्णुया । ञिधृषा प्रागल्भ्ये । त्रसिगृधिधृषिक्षिपेः क्नुः । पा० ३-२-१४० । सुपां सुलुगिति सोर्याजादेशः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । याथन । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति थनादेशः । यच्छब्दयोगान्निघाताभावः ॥
>
> *marutāṃ devānāṃ tanyatuḥ śabdo dhṛṣṇuyā dhārṣṭyayuktaḥ sanneti | gacchati | keṣāmiva | jayatāṃ vijayayuktānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ bhaṭānāmiva | he naro netāro maruto yūyaṃ yadyadā śubhaṃ śobhanaṃ devayajanaṃ yāthana prāpnutha | tadā tvadīyaḥ śabdo gacchatīti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || tanyatuḥ | tanu vistāre | ṛtanyañjītyādinā | u0 4-2 | yatucpratyayaḥ | dhṛṣṇuyā | ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye | trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ | pā0 3-2-140 | supāṃ sulugiti soryājādeśaḥ | cittvādantodāttaḥ | yāthana | taptanaptanathanāśceti thanādeśaḥ | yacchabdayogānnighātābhāvaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "The *tanyatuḥ*, sound, of the Maruts, the gods, *eti*, goes forth, being *dhṛṣṇuyā*, bold. Like whose? *Jayatām iva*, like that of victorious heroes, warriors. O *naraḥ*, leaders, Maruts! *Yat*, when, you *yāthana*, reach, *śubham*, the fine place of worship of the gods, then your sound goes: the construction is with the preceding." (Grammatical tail: *tanyatuḥ*, *tanu vistāre*, the suffix *yatuc* by *ṛtanyañji…* (U. 4-2); *dhṛṣṇuyā*, *ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye*, *knu* by *trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ* (Pā. 3-2-140), the substitute *yāc* for *su* by *supāṃ suluk*, final udātta as *cit*; *yāthana*, the substitute *thana* by *taptanaptanathanāś ca*; no loss of accent because of the connection with *yad*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) नरः ((he) naraḥ)** — O Marut deities, leaders of men (you) | **यत् (yat)** — when | **शुभं (śubhaṃ)** — to the places of good rites such as sacrifice | **याथन (yāthana)** — you go (then) | **मरुतां (marutāṃ)** — of the Marut deities | **तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ)** — the sound (full of joy) | **जयतामिव (jayatām iva)** — like the shout of victory of victorious warriors | **धृष्णुया (dhṛṣṇuyā)** — full of boldness | **एति (eti)** — comes forth.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Marut deities, leaders, when you go to the sacrifices and other good rites, the shout of joy you make is very deep, like the shout of joy of victorious warriors.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Brave Maruts, when you go to the Sacrifice, the shouts of Maruts spreads [sic] with exultation like that of conquerors.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**जयतामिव (jayatām iva)** — as warriors who have come back victorious over enemies in battle make a shout of joy marking victory.

**तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ)** — for this Yāska has explained *tanyatus tanitrī vāco 'nyasyāḥ*: making a sound, the speech of another deity. The word *tanyatuḥ* is also read in the Ṛgveda in the ṛks 1-32-13; 1-116-12 (zoom-checked); 5-25-8; 6-6-2; 7-3-6; 9-100-3; 10-65-13 (numbers in small type, as read).

> तन्यतुस्तनित्री वाचोऽन्यस्याः ।
>
> *tanyatustanitrī vāco 'nyasyāḥ |*

**धृष्णुया (dhṛṣṇuyā)** — full of boldness, deep, very loud.

**यत् (yat)** — *yadā |* when.

### Page 183 — Rik 11: Special Topics (end), grammar

**शुभं (śubhaṃ)** — to the good rite, that is, the performance of sacrifice, worship of the gods and the like. Skandasvāmin has given this word the meaning 'the water in the clouds'. Accordingly the intention is that the Marut deities, with roarings such as lightning and thunder, go near the clouds and make rain fall.

**याथन (yāthana)** — for the sake of the metre the final syllable is long in the Saṃhitā.

**नरः (naraḥ)** — vocative, first case plural. *Netāraḥ*: leaders, chiefs.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ)** — the root *tanu vistāre*. By *ṛtanyañjivanyañjyarpimadyatyaṅgikuyukṛśibhyaḥ katnijyatujalijiṣṭujiṣṭhajisansyanithinulyasāsānukaḥ* (U. Sū. 4-442, read at zoom; the last glyph is the curled 2) — after these twelve roots, *ṛ gatau*, *tanu vistāre*, *añjū vyaktyādau*, *vanu yācane*, *añjū vyaktyādau*, *ṛ gatau* ending in *ṇic*, *madī harṣe*, *ata sātatyagamane*, *agi gatau*, *ku śabde*, *yu miśraṇe*, *kṛśa tanūkaraṇe*, the twelve suffixes *katnic*, *yatuc*, *alic*, *iṣṭuc*, *iṣṭhac*, *isan*, *syan*, *ithin*, *uli*, *asa*, *āsa*, *ānuk* come in order — the suffix *yatuc* comes after the root *tan*.

**धृष्णुया (dhṛṣṇuyā)** — the root *ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye*. After it, by *trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-140) — after *trasī udvege*, *gṛdhu abhikāṅkṣāyām*, *ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye*, *kṣipa preraṇe*, when the agents are of that habit, that nature, or doers of it well, the suffix *knu* comes — the suffix *knu*. In the suffix *nu* remains. *Dhṛṣ* + *nu*; by *raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-1) *ṇ* for the *n*; after *dhṛṣṇu* the first-case singular suffix *su*. For it, by *supāṃ suluk pūrvasavarṇācchheyāḍāḍyāyājālaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) — in the Veda, in place of the *sup* endings, *suluk*, *pūrvasavarṇa*, *ā*, *āt*, *śe*, *yā*, *ḍā*, *ḍyā*, *yāc*, *āl* come according to usage — the substitute *yāc* comes here; it is *cit*, so by *citaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the final udātta accent comes.

**याथन (yāthana)** — the root *yā prāpaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person plural, the suffix *tha*. By *loṭo laṅvat* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) treated like *laṅ*; by *tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) the substitute *ta* for *tha*; the *vikaraṇa* *śap*; for it, by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72), *luk*: *yā* + *ta*. Now by *taptanaptanathanāś ca*

### Page 184 (upper) — Rik 11: grammar (end)

(Pā. Sū. 7-1-45) — for the *ta* coming in place of *loṭ*, one of the substitutes *tap*, *tanap*, *tana*, *thana* comes according to usage — the substitute *thana*: it becomes *yāthana*. Here, though total lack of accent would be due by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28), by *yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) — a word ending in *tiṅ* after a word containing *yad* is not unaccented — the prohibition comes. So total lack of accent does not come. In the Saṃhitā, by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137), it becomes *yāthanā*. ॥11॥

### Page 184 (lower) — Sūkta 23, Rik 12

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ह॒स्का॒रा॒द्वि॒द्यु॒त॒स्पर्य॑तो जा॒ता॑ अवन्तु नः । [accent ?]
> म॒रुतो॑ मृळयन्तु नः ॥१२॥
>
> *haskārād vidyutas páry ato jātā avantu naḥ |* [accent ?]
> *marúto mṛḷayantu naḥ ||12||*

*(Bars under ह, स्का, द्वि, त (द्युतस्) and जा; strokes over र्य and, after जाता, at the start of अवन्तु (read as over ता [accent ?]). Line 2: a bar under म, a stroke over तो.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> हस्कारात् । विऽद्युतः । परि । अतः । जाताः । अवन्तु । नः ॥
> मरुतः । मृळयन्तु । नः ॥१२॥
>
> *haskārāt | vi 'dyutaḥ | pari | ataḥ | jātāḥ | avantu | naḥ ||*
> *marutaḥ | mṛḷayantu | naḥ ||12||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: पा० ३-२-१, ८-३-४६.)*

> हस्काराद्दीप्तिकराद्विद्युतो विशेषेण दीप्यमानादतोऽन्तरिक्षात्परि जाताः सर्वत उत्पन्ना मरुतो नोऽस्मानवन्तु । रक्षन्तु । तथाविधा मरुतो नोऽस्मान्मृळयन्तु । सुखयन्तु ॥ हस्कारात् । हसे हसने । अत्र तु प्रकाशमात्रे वर्तते । अस्मात्संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । अस्मिन्नुपपदे डुकृञ् करण इत्यस्मात्कर्मण्यण् । पा० ३-२-१ । इत्यण्प्रत्ययः । तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थेत्यादिना पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते गतिकारकेत्यादिना कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अतः । कृकमीत्यादिना । पा० ८-३-४६ । विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वं ॥
>
> *haskārāddīptikarādvidyuto viśeṣeṇa dīpyamānādato 'ntarikṣātpari jātāḥ sarvata utpannā maruto no 'smānavantu | rakṣantu | tathāvidhā maruto no 'smānmṛḷayantu | sukhayantu || haskārāt | hase hasane | atra tu prakāśamātre vartate | asmātsaṃpadādilakṣaṇaḥ kvip | asminnupapade ḍukṛñ karaṇa ityasmātkarmaṇyaṇ | pā0 3-2-1 | ityaṇpratyayaḥ | tatpuruṣe tulyārthetyādinā pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte gatikāraketyādinā kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | ataḥ | kṛkamītyādinā | pā0 8-3-46 | visarjanīyasya satvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "May the Maruts, *pari jātāḥ*, born on all sides, *ataḥ*, from this mid-air, *vidyutaḥ*, from the lightning shining in a special way, *haskārāt*, which makes brightness, *avantu*, protect, *naḥ*, us. May such Maruts *mṛḷayantu*, make us happy." (Grammatical tail: *haskārāt*, *hase hasane*, here meaning only 'light'; *kvip* of the *sampadādi* type after it; with this as *upapada*, after *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, *aṇ* by *karmaṇy aṇ* (Pā. 3-2-1); the first-member accent being due by *tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…*, the *kṛt* final member's accent by *gatikāraka…*; *ataḥ*, *s* for the *visarga* by *kṛkami…* (Pā. 8-3-46).)

### Page 185 — Rik 12: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**हस्कारात् (haskārāt)** — making light | **विद्युतः (vidyutaḥ)** — shining especially | **अतः (ataḥ)** — from it, that is, from the mid-air | **परि (pari)** — in the upper part | **जाताः (jātāḥ)** — born | **मरुतः (marutaḥ)** — the Marut deities | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **अवन्तु (avantu)** — may they protect | (and) **नः (naḥ)** — for us | **मृळयन्तु (mṛḷayantu)** — may they make happiness.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

May the Marut deities, born in the upper part of the lightning, which is very bright so as to dazzle in the mid-air, protect us and make happiness for us.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> May the Maruts born from the lightning in the resplendent region protect us and make us happy.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**हस्कारात् (haskārāt)** — *hase hasane atra tu prakāśamātre vartate ||* Though the root *has* means laughing, the commentator says it is used here in the sense of light. *Haḥ* + *kārāt* means: making light. Skandasvāmin explains the word *haḥ* as a sound marking the cry of distress people use when in trouble, and gives this ṛk the sense: removing the cry of distress of the people, may the cloud make rain fall, protect us and make happiness.

**विद्युतः (vidyutaḥ)** — *viśeṣeṇa dīpyamānāt |* shining especially. The meaning 'from the lightning' can also be given to this word.

**परि अतः जाताः (pari ataḥ jātāḥ)** — the Marut deities born in the upper part of the mid-air, covered by light and lightning, that is, in the mid-air above the earth. Since the movement of the Marut deities is always in the mid-air itself, there may be a custom of saying that the Maruts are born in the mid-air.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**हस्कारात् (haskārāt)** — *has*, light; *karoti*, makes: so the analysis. The root *hase hasane*; here the root is in the sense of light, because roots have many meanings. By *sampadādibhyaḥ*

### Page 186 — Rik 12: grammar (end)

*kvip* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-108, Vā. 9) — after the roots read in the *sampadādi* class, *kvip* comes in the action sense — when *kvip* comes after the root *has* and all its letters are dropped, only *has* remains. When the object-word *has* in the accusative singular is *upapada*, by *karmaṇy aṇ* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-1) — when an object-word is *upapada*, *aṇ* comes after the root — the suffix *aṇ* comes after the root *kṛ*, *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*: *has* + *kṛ* + *a*. By *aco 'ñṇiti* (Pā. Sū. 7-11, as printed) *vṛddhi* *ār* for the *ṛ*: it becomes *haskāra*. This is a tatpuruṣa compound. So by *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) — in a tatpuruṣa compound the seven first members beginning with *tulyārthaka* (words meaning 'equal') keep their own accent — the own accent of *has*, ending in the second case, that is, by *dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-162), its being udātta, would be due; overriding it, by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) — in a tatpuruṣa compound, a *kṛt*-final word after a *gati*, a *kāraka* or an *upapada* keeps its own accent — the last member keeps its own accent; the last member *kāra* is final udātta by the suffix accent. So after compounding too that own accent stays. By *tatropapadaṃ saptamīstham* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-92) — in the sūtras under the heading *dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-91), words such as *has* that express the meaning conveyed by words in the seventh case such as *karmaṇi* get the name *upapada* — *has* has the name *upapada*. For the *s* in *has* + *kāra*, by *sasajuṣo ruḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-66) — the final *s* of a *pada* and the word *sajuṣ* take the substitute *ru* — the substitute *ru*; by *kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-15) — at the end of a *pada*, *visarga* comes for an *r* before a *khar* letter and for an *r* at a pause — *visarga*. *Haḥ* + *kāra*: by *ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsakumbhapātrakuśākarṇīṣv anavyayasya* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-46) — when the seven words *kṛ* and the rest follow, for a *visarga* after *a* that does not belong to an indeclinable, *s* comes always in a compound; but a *visarga* in a last member does not get the *s* — so *s* for the *visarga*: *haskāra* is established. ॥12॥

*(An ornament follows.)*

>

*(Strokes over पू, ब, घृ and णं; bars under चि, ष (बर्हिष), ध and दि. Line 2: strokes over आ (आजा) and था; bars under न and प [accent ?].)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आ । पूषन् । चित्रऽबर्हिषं । आघृणे । धरुणं । दिवः ॥
> आ । अज । नष्टं । यथा । पशुं ॥१३॥
>
> *ā | pūṣan | citra 'barhiṣaṃ | āghṛṇe | dharuṇaṃ | divaḥ ||*
> *ā | aja | naṣṭaṃ | yathā | paśuṃ ||13||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(The Uṇādi number is printed उ० ३-५८; the sūtra quoted with it is printed अर्जेर्णिलुक्च.)*

> हे पूषन् चित्रबर्हिषं विचित्रैर्दर्भैर्युक्तं धरुणं यागस्य धारकं सोमं दिव आ द्युलोकादाहरेति शेषः । पूषा विशेष्यते । आघृणे आगतदीप्तियुक्त । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । हे अज गमनशील यथा लोके नष्टं पशुं महारण्यादावन्विष्य कश्चिदाहरति तद्वत् ॥ आघृणे । घृ क्षरणदीप्त्योरित्यस्माद्घृणिः पृश्निरिति निप्रत्ययो निपातितः । ऋवर्णाच्चेति वक्तव्यमिति णत्वं । प्रादिसमासः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । धरुणं । धृञ् धारणे । अस्माण्ण्यन्ताद्धातोरर्जेर्णिलुक्च । उ० ३-५८ । इत्युनन्प्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेन नित्स्वराभावे प्रत्ययस्वरः । दिवः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वं । अज । अज गतिक्षेपणयोः ॥
>
> *he pūṣan citrabarhiṣaṃ vicitrairdarbhairyuktaṃ dharuṇaṃ yāgasya dhārakaṃ somaṃ diva ā dyulokādāhareti śeṣaḥ | pūṣā viśeṣyate | āghṛṇe āgatadīptiyukta | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | he aja gamanaśīla yathā loke naṣṭaṃ paśuṃ mahāraṇyādāvanviṣya kaścidāharati tadvat || āghṛṇe | ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyorityasmādghṛṇiḥ pṛśniriti nipratyayo nipātitaḥ | ṛvarṇācceti vaktavyamiti ṇatvaṃ | prādisamāsaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | dharuṇaṃ | dhṛñ dhāraṇe | asmāṇṇyantāddhātorarjerṇilukca | u0 3-58 | ityunanpratyayaḥ | vyatyayena nitsvarābhāve pratyayasvaraḥ | divaḥ | ūḍidamityādinā ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvaṃ | aja | aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Pūṣan! Bring (*ā*) from the world of heaven (*divaḥ*) the soma, *citrabarhiṣam*, joined with many-coloured *darbha* grass, *dharuṇam*, the upholder of the sacrifice: 'bring' is to be supplied. Pūṣan is qualified: *āghṛṇe*, furnished with brightness that has come. The illustration for it: O *aja*, moving one! *Yathā*, as in the world someone, searching in a great forest and the like, brings back *naṣṭaṃ paśum*, a lost animal — so." (Grammatical tail: *āghṛṇe*, from *ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ*, the suffix *ni* given as a set form in *ghṛṇiḥ pṛśniḥ…*; *ṇ* by *ṛvarṇāc ceti vaktavyam*; a *prādi* compound; the vocative initial udātta; *dharuṇam*, *dhṛñ dhāraṇe*, the suffix *unan* after it in the causative by the sūtra as printed (U. 3-58); with the *nit* accent not applying by *vyatyaya*, the suffix accent; *divaḥ*, the genitive udātta by *ūḍidam…*; *aja*, *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**आघृणे (āghṛṇe)** — furnished with light | **अज (aja)** — of moving nature | **पूषन् (pūṣan)** — O Pūṣan | **चित्रबर्हिषं (citrabarhiṣaṃ)** — together with variegated *darbha* grass | **धरुणं (dharuṇaṃ)** — the soma, the support of the sacrifice | (as a man) **नष्टं (naṣṭaṃ)** — lost | **पशुं (paśuṃ)** — an animal | **यथा (yathā)** — in the manner in which | **आ (harati)** — searches and brings (so) | **दिवः (divaḥ)** — from the world of heaven | **आ (hara)** — bring and give.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Pūṣan, furnished with light, since you are of moving nature, bring us from the world of heaven the soma, which is joined with variegated *darbha* grass and is the support of the sacrifice, just as one searches out and brings back an animal lost in the world.

### Page 188 — Rik 13: English, Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Resplendent and swift-moving Pushan, bring from heaven the Soma juice with the variegated sacred grass as a man brings back a stray animal.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The meaning of this ṛk is somewhat tangled. The main intention is: O Pūṣan, you are of great brightness and can move fast; so, as one searches out and brings back an animal (a cow, a goat and the like) lost in the world, bring and give us from heaven the soma, joined with variegated *darbha* grass and the support of the sacrifice.

**पूषन् (pūṣan)** — since the word *pūṣa* is read among the twenty-one words denoting the earth, *gauḥ*, *gmā*, *jmā* and the rest, *pūṣa* also means the earth. Here the word *pūṣan* is the deity named Pūṣan. Since this deity is well known as one who searches out and brings back lost things, there is such a description in many ṛks. Yāska's explanation of this word —

> पूषा । अथ यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत्पूषा भवति ॥ (नि० १२-१६)
>
> *pūṣā | atha yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tatpūṣā bhavati || (ni0 12-16)*

— is this: because he is full of rays or beams, this deity is named Pūṣā. Since Pūṣā is one of the twelve Ādityas, they say that Pūṣan is a particular form of the sun. For that reason, when describing this deity, they use qualifying words such as furnished with brightness, shining, furnished with light. And Yāska has put *ajāḥ pūṣṇaḥ* (Ni. 2-2[6 or 9], zoom: second group ends in a hooked glyph) among the *ādiṣṭopayojana* words. *Ādiṣṭopayojana* means a qualifying word that sets out a meaning suited to be construed with that particular deity, as is well known in usage. For example *harī indrasya*, *rāsabhāv aśvinoḥ*, *niyuto vāyoḥ* and so on: that is, the word *harī* (Indra's horses) is used in the Veda only to indicate Indra's horses. Likewise the word *rāsabhā* is used in the praise of the Aśvin deities and the word *niyutaḥ* when praising Vāyu. So it is to be known that the word *aja* is used when praising the deity Pūṣan. In this ṛk too there is the use of the word *aja*. The commentator has explained it as 'of moving nature'. Since the sun (Pūṣā) moves through the three worlds and sees everything, it is natural to call him 'of moving nature'. To support the meaning of the word *pūṣā* —

### Page 189 — Rik 13: Special Topics (end)

— Yāska has given two ṛks as examples, *śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1) and *pathas-pathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-49-8).

**चित्रबर्हिषं (citrabarhiṣaṃ)** — *vicitradarbhair yuktam |* The commentator says: joined with variegated *darbha* grass. How the soma is joined with *darbha* grass is not clear. It may be said so because the soma vessel is usually placed on *darbha* grass. Skandasvāmin has also given *citram* the meaning 'worthy of worship'. The author of the *Vedārthayatna* has given the word *citrabarhiṣam* the meaning 'joined with variegated feathers' ("feathers"). That soma has feathers seems strange; that meaning is not quite fitting.

**आघृणे (āghṛṇe)** — since the word *ghṛṇaḥ* is read among the twelve names of day, *vastoḥ*, *dyauḥ* and the rest, *ghṛṇaḥ* is a name of the day (Ni. 2-21, zoom-checked); because he makes the day, the sun (Pūṣā) is named *ghṛṇi*. There is the *śruti* statement *ghṛṇiḥ sūrya ādityaḥ* (Tai. U.). And since the word *ghṛṇiḥ* is read among the eleven words *jamat* and the rest conveying the meaning *jvalataḥ* (Ni. 2-28, zoom-checked), the word *ghṛṇi* means 'shining'. This is the meaning the commentator gives here. Since there is the prefix *ā* with this word, *ā samantāt dīptiyuktaḥ*: having brightness spreading or scattered all round is the meaning.

> घृणिः सूर्य आदित्यः ।
>
> *ghṛṇiḥ sūrya ādityaḥ |*

**धरुणं (dharuṇaṃ)** — *yāgasya dhārakam |* the chief thing that supports the sacrifice, that is, the soma juice: this is the intention.

**दिवः (divaḥ)** — from the world of heaven. Skandasvāmin has joined the word *dharuṇam* with the word *divaḥ* — *divaḥ dharuṇam* = *divaḥ dhartāram* — and given the meaning: upholding heaven, nourishing heaven. Since soma juice is well known to be in heaven, the meaning the commentator gives, 'bring and give the soma juice from heaven', is the fitting one. The *śruti* statement *tṛtīyasyām ito divi soma āsīt* (Tai. Brā. 3-2-1) supports the point that soma was in heaven.

> तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि सोम आसीत् ।
>
> *tṛtīyasyāmito divi soma āsīt |*

**अज (aja)** — *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ |* since the root *aj* has the meaning of going, the meaning 'of moving nature' fits here.

**नष्टं यथा पशुं (naṣṭaṃ yathā paśuṃ)** — as one is glad when a lost animal is found, so we would be glad if the soma in heaven were brought and given to us: to suggest this, the comparison may have been used.

*(The small Nirukta numbers on these pages were zoom-read on Oct 28: 2-2[6/9], 2-21, 2-28.)*

### Page 190 (upper) — Rik 13: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**आघृणे (āghṛṇe)** — the root *ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ*. *Ghṛṇipṛśni…* (U. Sū. 4-52): its meaning has been set out at *ugrā hi pṛśnimātaraḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-10). By this, the suffix *ni*: *ghṛ* + *ni*; by *ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam*, *ṇ* for the *n*; with the prefix *ā*, by *kugatiprādayaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-2-18), the compound; since it is at the beginning of the *pāda*, the total lack of accent by the eighth-book *āmantritasya ca* does not come. By the sixth-book *āmantritasya ca* the initial udātta comes.

**धरुणम् (dharuṇam)** — the root *dhṛñ dhāraṇe*. After it the suffix *ṇic*: *dhṛ* + *i*; now by *dhārer ṇiluk ca* [as printed] (Daśapā. 4) — after the root *dhṛñ* ending in the suffix *ṇic*, the suffix *unan* comes, and the *ṇic* is dropped (*luk*) — when the suffix *unan* and the dropping of *ṇi* come: *dhṛ* + *una*; by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) *guṇa* *ar* for the *ṛ*: *dharuna*; now by *aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-2) *ṇ* for the *n*: it becomes *dharuṇa*. Overriding the initial udātta of the suffix laid down by *ādyudāttaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-3), since the suffix is *nit* the initial udātta would be due by *ñnity ādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197); but here, according to the sūtra *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85), the initial udātta of the suffix alone comes and the *u* becomes udātta.

**दिवः (divaḥ)** — *ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171): here *ekācaḥ* and *antodāttāt* are carried on. *Ekācaḥ*, having nothing to exclude, is not a qualifier of *ūṭh*; even if it qualifies the whole joined with *ūṭh* there is no hindrance; in places like *praṣṭhauh* the *ūh* formed with *ūṭh* is meaningful and is obtained. So the case-endings other than *sarvanāmasthāna* after *ūṭh* and the rest, which are final udātta and monosyllabic, are udātta; so the genitive ending is udātta. Therefore by *anudāttau suppitau* the case-ending does not become unaccented.

**अज (aja)** — formed from the root *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*. ॥13॥

*(An ornament follows.)*

> पू॒षा राजा॑न॒माघृ॑णि॒रप॑गूळ्हं॒ गुहा॑ हि॒तं ।
> अवि॑न्दच्चि॒त्र॑बर्हिषं ॥१४॥ [accent ?]
>
> *pūṣā́ rā́jānam ā́ghṛṇir ápagūḷhaṃ gúhā hitáṃ |*

### Page 191 — Rik 14: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> पूषा । राजानं । आघृणिः । अपऽगूळ्हं । गुहा । हितं ॥
> अविन्दत् । चित्रऽबर्हिषं ॥१४॥
>
> *pūṣā | rājānaṃ | āghṛṇiḥ | apa 'gūḷhaṃ | guhā | hitaṃ ||*
> *avindat | citra 'barhiṣaṃ ||14||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: पा० ८-२-३१, ८-२-४०.)*

> आघृणिः पूषा राजानं सोममविन्दत् । अलभत । कीदृशं । अपगूळ्हमत्यन्तगूढं । तत्र हेतुः । गुहा हितं गुहासदृशे दुर्गमे द्युलोके स्थितं । तथा चित्रबर्हिषं ॥ अपगूळ्हं । गुहू संवरणे । निष्ठेति कर्मणि क्तः । हो ढः । पा० ८-२-३१ । इति ढत्वं । झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः । पा० ८-२-४० । इति धकारः । ष्टुत्वढलोपदीर्घाः । समासे गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । गुहा । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । हितं । निष्ठायां दधातेर्हिः ॥
>
> *āghṛṇiḥ pūṣā rājānaṃ somamavindat | alabhata | kīdṛśaṃ | apagūḷhamatyantagūḍhaṃ | tatra hetuḥ | guhā hitaṃ guhāsadṛśe durgame dyuloke sthitaṃ | tathā citrabarhiṣaṃ || apagūḷhaṃ | guhū saṃvaraṇe | niṣṭheti karmaṇi ktaḥ | ho ḍhaḥ | pā0 8-2-31 | iti ḍhatvaṃ | jhaṣastathordho 'dhaḥ | pā0 8-2-40 | iti dhakāraḥ | ṣṭutvaḍhalopadīrghāḥ | samāse gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | guhā | supāṃ sulugiti saptamyā luk | hitaṃ | niṣṭhāyāṃ dadhāterhiḥ ||*

**Translation:** "*Āghṛṇiḥ*, the bright Pūṣan, *avindat*, found, obtained, *rājānam*, King Soma. Of what kind? *Apagūḷham*, utterly hidden. The reason for that: *guhā hitam*, placed in the world of heaven, hard to reach like a cave. And *citrabarhiṣam*." (Grammatical tail: *apagūḷham*, *guhū saṃvaraṇe*, *kta* in the object sense by *niṣṭhā*, *ḍh* by *ho ḍhaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-31), *dh* by *jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-40), *ṣṭutva*, dropping of *ḍh* and lengthening; in the compound the prefix keeps its own accent by *gatir anantaraḥ*; *guhā*, the locative dropped by *supāṃ suluk*; *hitam*, *hi* for *dhā* by *niṣṭhāyāṃ dadhāter hiḥ*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**आघृणिः (āghṛṇiḥ)** — furnished with brightness | **पूषा (pūṣā)** — Pūṣan | **अपगूळ्हं (apagūḷhaṃ)** — utterly hidden | **गुहा (guhā)** — in a place hard to reach, like a cave | **हितं (hitaṃ)** — kept | **चित्रबर्हिषं (citrabarhiṣaṃ)** — joined with variegated *darbha* grass | **राजानं (rājānaṃ)** — the soma juice | **अविन्दत् (avindat)** — obtained.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The shining Pūṣan brought (for us) the soma juice, joined with variegated *darbha* grass, which was in a most secret place.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The resplendent Pushan found out the Soma (king) although concealed in a secret cave placed upon the sacred grass.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**राजानं (rājānaṃ)** — there is a custom of calling soma 'king'. Such usage is seen more in the Yajurveda than in the Ṛgveda.

### Page 192 — Rik 14: Special Topics (continued)

> सोमं राजानमवसेऽग्निं गीर्भिर्हवामहे ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-१४१-३)
> सोमस्य राज्ञो वरुणस्य धर्मणि बृहस्पतेरनुमत्या उ शर्मणि ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-१६७-३)
>
> *somaṃ rājānamavase 'gniṃ gīrbhirhavāmahe || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-141-3)*
> *somasya rājño varuṇasya dharmaṇi bṛhaspateranumatyā u śarmaṇi || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-167-3)*

— and there are many such examples. In the first *anuvāka* of the second chapter of the sixth book of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-1) there is the explanation that soma is the king and the metres Gāyatrī and the rest are his servants.

**अपगूळ्हं (apagūḷhaṃ)** — *atyantagūḍham | nigūḷham ācchāditam |* the meaning is: kept in a most secret place. On this matter Skandasvāmin has told an old legend —

> अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । असुराः सोमं राजानं दीयमानमग्नेर्हस्तादपहृत्य गुहायां न्यदधुः । तं पर्येषमाणा अन्ये देवा नाविन्दन् । पूषा त्वविन्दत् ।
>
> *atretihāsamācakṣate | asurāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ dīyamānamagnerhastādapahṛtya guhāyāṃ nyadadhuḥ | taṃ paryeṣamāṇā anye devā nāvindan | pūṣā tvavindat |*

— that is: the demons stole the soma from the hand of Agni and kept it in a most secret place, a cave. However much the gods searched for it, they did not find it. Pūṣan alone searched it out and brought it.

**गुहा हितं (guhā hitaṃ)** — that is, hidden in a hard-to-reach secret place like a cave. Here *guhā* can be taken to mean a cave or a secret place. In the Ṛgveda and the Upaniṣads too it is customary to indicate a thing kept in a secret place known to no one by the words *guhā hitam* —

> गुहा त्रीणि निहिता नेङ्गयन्ति तुरीयं वाचो मनुष्या वदन्ति ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-१६४-४५)
> अविन्दद्दिवो निहितं गुहा निधिं वेर्न गर्भं परिवीतमश्मन्यनन्ते अन्तरश्मनि ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-१३०-३)
> गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्हमप्स्वपीवृतं मायिनं क्षियन्तं ॥ (ऋ० सं० २-११-५)
> अभिनक्षन्तो अभि ये तमानशुर्निधिं पणीनां परमं गुहा हितं ॥ (ऋ० सं० २-२४-६)
> तिस्रो महीरुपरास्तस्थुरत्या गुहा द्वे निहिते दर्श्येका ॥ (ऋ० सं० ३-५६-२)
>
> *guhā trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṃ vāco manuṣyā vadanti || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-164-45)*
> *avindaddivo nihitaṃ guhā nidhiṃ verna garbhaṃ parivītamaśmanyanante antaraśmani || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-130-3)*
> *guhā hitaṃ guhyaṃ gūḷhamapsvapīvṛtaṃ māyinaṃ kṣiyantaṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 2-11-5)*

**चित्रबर्हिषं (citrabarhiṣaṃ)** — this word is in the previous ṛk too. What the right meaning of this word is is not clear.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**अपगूळ्हम् (apagūḷham)** — the prefix *apa*, the root *guhū saṃvaraṇe*. After it, by *niṣṭhā* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-102) — after a root in the past sense, the suffixes *kta*, *ktavatu* come — the suffix *kta* in the object sense: *ap* + *guh* + *ta*. Now by *ho ḍhaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-31) — when a *jhal* letter follows, and at the end of a *pada*, *ḍh* is substituted for *h* — for the *h* before the *jhal* letter *t*, the substitute *ḍh*: *guḍh* + *ta*. By *jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-40) — the *t* and *th* after a letter in the *pratyāhāra* *jhaṣ* not belonging to the root *dhā* take *dh* — *dh* for the *t*: *guḍh* + *dha*; by *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-41), by *ṣṭutva*, *ḍh* for the *dh*: *guḍh* + *ḍha*. By *ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-13) — a *ḍh* before a *ḍh* is dropped — the *ḍh* is dropped: *gu* + *ḍha*. By *ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-111) — an *aṇ* before the *ḍh* and *r* that cause the dropping of *ḍh* and *r* is lengthened — the *u* is lengthened: *gū* + *ḍha*: it became *apagūḍha*. Now, according to the tradition of the Bahvṛcas, *ajmadhyasthaḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ | ajmadhyasthaḍhakārasya ḷhakāraṃ vai yathākramam ||*, the *ḍh* between vowels becomes *ḷh*: it becomes *apagūḷham*. *Apa* and *gūḷham* both form a *prādi* compound. By *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) — when a word ending in the suffix *kta* in the object sense follows, the immediately preceding *gati* keeps its own accent — the accent of *apa* alone stays. *Apa* is initially udātta by *upasargāś cābhivarjam* (Phi. Sū. 82).

> अज्मध्यस्थडकारस्य ळकारं बह्वृचा जगुः । अज्मध्यस्थढकारस्य ळ्हकारं वै यथाक्रमम् ॥
>
> *ajmadhyasthaḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ | ajmadhyasthaḍhakārasya ḷhakāraṃ vai yathākramam ||*

**गुहा (guhā)** — for the locative singular suffix after this word, by *supāṃ suluk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) — for the meaning of the sūtra see the eleventh mantra — *luk*; instead of *guhāyām* it stays as *guhā*.

### Page 194 (upper) — Rik 14: grammar (end)

**हितं (hitaṃ)** — after the root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*, the suffix *kta*: *dhā* + *ta*. By *dadhāter hiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-42) — when a *t*-initial *kit* suffix follows, the root *dhā* takes the substitute *hi* — when *hi* comes for *dhā*: *hi* + *ta*; the accusative singular suffix *am*: it becomes *hitam*. ॥14॥

>
> *uto api ca sa pūṣā mahyaṃ yajamānāyendubhiryāgahetubhiḥ somairyuktānṣaḍvasaṃtādīnṛtūnanuseṣidhat | anukrameṇa punaḥpunarvartayanvartata iti śeṣaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | gobhirbalīvardairyavaṃ na carkṛṣat | naśabda upamārthaḥ | yathā yavamuddiśya bhūmiṃ pratisaṃvatsaraṃ punaḥpunaḥ kṛṣati tadvat || mahyaṃ | ṅayi ca | pā0 6-1-212 | ityādyudāttatvaṃ | indubhiḥ | undī kledane | undericcādeḥ | u0 1-13 | ityupratyaya ukārasyekārādeśaśca | nidityanuvṛtterādyudāttatvaṃ | yuktān | dīrghādaṭi samānapāda iti saṃhitāyāṃ nakārasya rutvaṃ | āto 'ṭi nityamiti sānunāsika ākāraḥ | anuseṣidhat | ṣidhu gatyāṃ | dhātorekācaḥ | pā0 3-1-22 | iti yaṅ | yaṅo 'ci ca | pā0 2-4-74 | iti tasya luk | pratyayalakṣaṇena sanyaṅoḥ | pā0 6-1-9 | iti dvirbhāvaḥ | halādiśeṣaḥ | guṇo yaṅlukoḥ | pā0 7-4-82 | ityabhyāsasya guṇaḥ | iṇkoḥ | pā0 8-3-57 | iti ṣatvaṃ | sanāditvāddhātusaṃjñāyāṃ laṭaḥ śatṛ | kartari śap | adādivacceti vacanāttasya luk | nābhyastācchatuḥ | pā0 7-1-78 | iti numpratiṣedhaḥ | pratyayasvare prāpte 'bhyastānāmādirityādyudāttatvaṃ | gobhiḥ | sāvekāca iti bhisa udāttatve prāpte na gośvanniti pratiṣedhaḥ | carkṛṣat | kṛṣa vilekhane | yaṅluki dvirbhāvahalādiśeṣacartvāni | rugrikau ca luki | pā0 7-4-91 | ityabhyāsasya rugāgamaḥ | asmādyaṅlugantālleṭastip | itaśca lopaḥ | leṭo 'ḍāṭāvityaḍāgamaḥ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | laghūpadhaguṇe prāpte nābhyastasyāci piti | pā0 7-3-87 | iti niṣedhaḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||10||*

### Page 195 — Rik 15: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**Translation:** "*Uto*, and also, *saḥ*, that Pūṣan, *mahyam*, for me, the sacrificer, *anuseṣidhat*, keeps turning in order again and again — 'keeps turning' is to be supplied — the six seasons, spring and the rest, *yuktān*, joined *indubhiḥ*, with somas, the means of the sacrifice. The illustration for it: *gobhir yavaṃ na carkṛṣat*: the word *na* is in the sense of comparison: as one, aiming at barley, ploughs the ground again and again every year with bullocks — so." (Grammatical tail: *mahyam*, initial udātta by *ṅayi ca* (Pā. 6-1-212); *indubhiḥ*, *undī kledane*, the suffix *u* and *i* for the initial *u* by *underic cādeḥ* (U. 1-13), initial udātta as *nit* is carried on; *yuktān*, in the Saṃhitā *ru* for the *n* by *dīrghād aṭi samānapāde*, the nasalised *ā* by *āto 'ṭi nityam*; *anuseṣidhat*, *ṣidhu gatyām*, *yaṅ* by *dhātor ekācaḥ…* (Pā. 3-1-22), dropped by *yaṅo 'ci ca* (Pā. 2-4-74); by the mark of the suffix, reduplication by *sanyaṅoḥ* (Pā. 6-1-9), *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*, *guṇa* of the reduplicate by *guṇo yaṅlukoḥ* (Pā. 7-4-82), *ṣ* by *iṇkoḥ* (Pā. 8-3-57); being a root as of the *sanādi* class, *śatṛ* for *laṭ*, *śap*, dropped by the statement *adādivac ca*; *num* barred by *nābhyastāc chatuḥ* (Pā. 7-1-78); the suffix accent being due, initial udātta by *abhyastānām ādiḥ*; *gobhiḥ*, the udātta of *bhis* due by *sāv ekācaḥ* is barred by *na gośvan…*; *carkṛṣat*, *kṛṣa vilekhane*, in *yaṅluk* reduplication, *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* and *cartva*; the augment *ruk* for the reduplicate by *rugrikau ca luki* (Pā. 7-4-91); after this *yaṅluk* stem, *tip* for *leṭ*, *i* dropped by *itaś ca lopaḥ*, the augment *aṭ* by *leṭo 'ḍāṭau*, *śap* dropped by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ*; the *guṇa* of the light penultimate is barred by *nābhyastasyāci piti* (Pā. 7-3-87); loss of accent by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**उतो (uto)** — and | **सः (saḥ)** — that Pūṣan | **मह्यं (mahyaṃ)** — for me who am performing the sacrifice | **इन्दुभिः (indubhiḥ)** — with the soma juices, the chief things in the sacrifice | **युक्तान् (yuktān)** — joined | **षट् (ṣaṭ)** — the six seasons, spring and the rest | (as a farmer) **गोभिः (gobhiḥ)** — with bullocks | **यवं (yavaṃ)** — to obtain the grain called *yava* (wheat [as printed], barley) | **न चर्कृषत् (na carkṛṣat)** — as he ploughs the ground again and again | **अनुसेषिधत् (anuseṣidhat)** — may he carry them on in an order of turning, one after the other.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

As the farmer ploughs the ground again and again, that is, many times, with bullocks to grow the grain called *yava*, so may that Pūṣan make the six seasons, joined with the soma juices that accomplish the sacrifice, go on in an order of turning, one after the other.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> And he has brought to me successively the six (seasons) connected with the drops of the Soma juice as a man repeatedly ploughs a field with bullocks for the sake of barley.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The meaning of this ṛk does not fit very well. The comparison too is not good. The intention of this ṛk may be: as the farmer ploughs the ground again and again to grow the grain *yava*, so may he make the seasons, spring and the rest, and the soma sacrifices we perform in those seasons, come again and again. Since the seasons, spring and the rest, come every year, it came about many times. To grow grain the ground must be ploughed many times. So, to suggest the meaning 'many times', —

### Page 196 — Rik 15: Special Topics (end), grammar

— this comparison may have been given. In this ṛk there is only the word *ṣaṭ*. The commentator has explained *ṣaṭ* as the six seasons.

**इन्दुभिः (indubhiḥ)** — with drops of soma juice: since, when soma juice is pressed with a creeper, it falls drop by drop, it is customary to speak of soma juice by words for drops (*indavaḥ*, *indubhiḥ* and the like).

**गोभिः (gobhiḥ)** — though *gobhiḥ* means 'with cows', the commentator and Skandasvāmin both hold that here *gobhiḥ* must be given the meaning 'with bullocks', the means for the work of farming.

**न (na)** — this word is used here in the sense of comparison.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**मह्यं (mahyaṃ)** — after the word *asmad*, the dative singular suffix *ṅe*: *asmad* + *ṅe*. Now by *tubhyamahyau ṅayi* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-95) — when the suffix *ṅe* follows, the part up to *m* of the words *yuṣmad*, *asmad*, that is *yuṣm*, *asm*, take the substitutes *tubhya*, *mahya* in order — the substitute *mahya* for *asm*: *mahya* + *ad* + *ṅe*; by *ato guṇe* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) the following form: *mahyad* + *ṅe*; by *ṅe prathamayor am* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-28) the substitute *am* for *ṅe*: *mahyad* + *am*; by *śeṣe lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-90) the *ad* is dropped. On the view that *śeṣe lopaḥ* applies to the final letter, when the *d* is dropped, by *ami pūrvaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-107) the preceding form: it becomes *mahyam*. On the view of dropping the final, the single substitute arising by the preceding form would have to be udātta by *ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-5): that is, in *mahyam* the final *a* would turn out udātta. On the view of dropping the *ṭi*, by the accent of the loss of the udātta, *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-161), the case-ending would have to be udātta. If so, by *ṅayi ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-212) — when the suffix *ṅe* follows, the beginning of the words *yuṣmad*, *asmad* is udātta — the initial udātta accent comes.

**इन्दुभिः (indubhiḥ)** — the root *undī kledane*. By *underic cādeḥ* (U. Sū. 1-13), after the root *und*, the suffix *u* and the substitute *i* for the first *u*: so the suffix *u*. With *i* for the *u* it becomes *indu*. By *dhānye nit* (U. Sū. 1-9), *nit* is carried on into this sūtra. So since the suffix is *nit*, and by *ñnity ādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197), this is initially udātta.

**युक्तान् (yuktān)** — *yuktān*, ending in the accusative plural, + *anu*: for these, at the time of the Saṃhitā, by *dīrghād aṭi samānapāde* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-9) — if the *n* and a letter of the *pratyāhāra* *aṭ* are in one and the same *pāda*,

### Page 197 — Rik 15: grammar (continued)

— the *n* before the *aṭ* letter, when it follows a long vowel, takes the substitute *ru* — so the substitute *ru* for the *n*: *yuktār* + *anu*. Now by *āto 'ṭi nityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-3) — the long *ā* before the *ru* that is before an *aṭ* letter always becomes nasal — the *ā* becomes nasal: *yuktā̃r* + *anu*; by *bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo 'śi* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-17) *y* for the *r*; by *lopaḥ śākalyasya* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-19) the *y* is dropped; by *pūrvatrāsiddham* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-1), when making the lengthening of like vowels, the dropping of *y* is *asiddha*. So the lengthening of like vowels does not come.

**अनुसेषिधत् (anuseṣidhat)** — the root *ṣidhu gatyām*. By *dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-22) — when repetition or intensity is shown, *yaṅ* comes after a root that is monosyllabic and begins with a consonant — *yaṅ*: *ṣidh* + *ya*; by *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) *s* for *ṣ*: *sidh* + *ya*. By *yaṅo 'ci ca* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-74) — *yaṅ* is dropped (*luk*) when a vowel-initial suffix follows, and even when none follows — *yaṅ* is dropped (*luk*): it stays as *sidh*. Though *yaṅ* is thus dropped, by *pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-62) — though a suffix is dropped, an operation caused by the suffix comes — whatever operation would come if *yaṅ* were there comes now too. But here the dropping has come by pronouncing the word *luk*. So it may be said that by *na lumatāṅgasya* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-63) the mark of the suffix should be barred. The sense of the sūtra *na lumatāṅgasya*: in places where the dropping has come by pronouncing *luk*, *ślu*, *lup*, words containing *lu*, an operation aimed at the stem caused by the dropped suffix does not come, whether laid down under the *aṅga* heading or not. The present reduplication comes to what ends in *yaṅ*; so it is not an operation aimed at the stem. Therefore this prohibition does not come here. By *sanyaṅoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-9) — the first monosyllabic part of a root ending in *san* or *yaṅ* is reduplicated, and if the root begins with a vowel, the second monosyllabic part — with the reduplication: *sidh* + *sidh*. By *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (7-4-60) — the first consonant of the reduplicate remains, the other consonants of the reduplicate are dropped — the *dh* is dropped: *si* + *sidh*. By *guṇo yaṅlukoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-82) — in *yaṅ* and in *yaṅluk* the reduplicate takes *guṇa* — *guṇa* for *si*, *e* for the *i*: *sesidh*. By *iṇkoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-57) the cerebral substitute (*ṣatva*) for an *s* after the letters of the *pratyāhāra* *iṇ*: so the *s* after *se* becomes *ṣ*: *seṣidh*.

> सन्क्यच्काम्यच्क्यष्क्यङोऽथाचारक्विब्णिज्यङौ तथा । यगाय ईयङ् णिङ् चेति द्वादशामी सनादयः ॥
>
> *sankyackāmyackyaṣkyaṅo 'thācārakvibṇijyaṅau tathā | yagāya īyaṅ ṇiṅ ceti dvādaśāmī sanādayaḥ ||*

— so they count the *sanādi* suffixes. Thus what ends in *yaṅ* ends in a *sanādi* suffix. And so by *sanā-*

### Page 198 — Rik 15: grammar (continued)

*dyantā dhātavaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-32) — what ends in the *sanādi* suffixes gets the name *dhātu* — *seṣidh* gets the name *dhātu*. Thus when *śatṛ* comes for the suffix *laṭ* by *laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-124): *seṣidh* + *at*. By *kartari śap* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the *vikaraṇa* *śap*. *Carkarītaṃ parasmaipadam adādivac ca draṣṭavyam* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-8-4 [as printed]): *carkarīta* is the name for what ends in *yaṅluk*; it is only *parasmaipada*; it is also as if in the *adādi* class; so what ends in *yaṅluk* is as if in the *adādi* class. Therefore by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) *śap* is dropped (*luk*). This very meaning results from the *gaṇasūtra* *carkarītaṃ ca* read in the *adādi* class. Since, having declared *atha trayaḥ parasmaipadinaḥ* and read the roots *ṣasa*, *ṣasti svapne*, *vaśa kāntau*, this *gaṇasūtra* comes after them, it results that what ends in *yaṅluk* is *parasmaipada*. Since it is read in the *adādi* class, it is *adādi* too. So it also results that, after a root of whatever *vikaraṇa*, if *yaṅ* is dropped (*luk*), the *vikaraṇa* *śap* alone comes there and it is dropped. When the suffix *su* is put after *seṣidhat*, by *ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70) *num* would be due; for it, by *nābhyastāc chatuḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-78) — a *śatṛ* suffix after a reduplicated stem does not take *num* — the prohibition comes. By the sixth-book sūtra *ubhe abhyastam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-5) — the whole of a word with reduplication gets the name *abhyasta* — *seṣidh* has the name *abhyasta*; when the accent of the *śatṛ* suffix should remain, by *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) — when a vowel-initial *sārvadhātuka* in place of *la*, without the augment *iṭ*, follows, the beginning of the *abhyasta* is udātta — *se* becomes udātta.

**गोभिः (gobhiḥ)** — by *sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168): *su* means the locative plural; when the locative plural suffix follows, the case-ending of the third onward after whatever word has a single vowel is udātta; so the udātta accent would be due for the case-ending; but by the sūtra stated next the prohibition comes. *Na gośvansāvavarṇarāḍaṅkruṅkṛdbhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-182): the sense of the sūtra is that the case-ending and the *matup* after the words *go*, *śvan*, words ending in *a*/*ā* in the nominative singular, the word *rāṭ* ending in *kvip*, the word *aṅ* formed with *kvin* after the root *añcu*, the word *kruñ* formed with *kvin* after *kruñca gatikauṭilyālpībhāvayoḥ*, and the word *kṛt* formed with *kvip* after the root *kṛñ*, do not take the udātta laid down by the sūtras of the sixth book. At *cau* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-222), introducing the sūtra *na gośvan*, *kasya tarhi? yo 'nena kenacil lakṣaṇena*

### Page 199 — Rik 15: grammar (end)

*prāptasya vibhaktisvarasya pratiṣedham | yadi vibhaktisvarasya pratiṣedhaḥ, vṛkṣavān, plakṣavān, atra na prāpnoti | matubgrahaṇam api prakṛtam anuvartate kva prakṛtam? hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup iti* — in the Mahābhāṣya it is made clear that this is a prohibition of the accent of *matup* and of the case-ending, and that it is a prohibition of the general accents of the sixth book. These points are also established by the *Kaiyaṭa* on this Bhāṣya.

> कस्य तर्हि । योऽनेन केनचिल्लक्षणेन प्राप्तस्य विभक्तिस्वरस्य प्रतिषेधम् । यदि विभक्तिस्वरस्य प्रतिषेधः वृक्षवान् प्लक्षवान् अत्र न प्राप्नोति । मतुब्ग्रहणमपि प्रकृतमनुवर्तते क्व प्रकृतम् । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् इति ।
>
> *kasya tarhi | yo 'nena kenacillakṣaṇena prāptasya vibhaktisvarasya pratiṣedham | yadi vibhaktisvarasya pratiṣedhaḥ vṛkṣavān plakṣavān atra na prāpnoti | matubgrahaṇamapi prakṛtamanuvartate kva prakṛtam | hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup iti |*

**चर्कृषत् (carkṛṣat)** — the root *kṛṣa vilekhane*. By *dhātor ekācaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-22) *yaṅ*; for it, by *yaṅo 'ci ca* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-74), *luk*; by the mark of the suffix it ends in *yaṅ*. By *sanyaṅoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-9) reduplication: *kṛṣ* + *kṛṣ*. By *ur at* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-66) — when a suffix follows, the *ṛ* of the reduplicate takes *a* — *ar* for the *ṛ*; by the mark of the suffix the suffix is to be taken as following. Though *yaṅ* is dropped (*luk*), the author of the *Śekhara* has made clear at the sūtra *na lumatāṅgasya* that *ur at* still comes by the mark of the suffix: *kar* + *kṛṣ*; by *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-60) the *r* is removed. By *abhyāse carc ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-54) — the *jhal* letters of the reduplicate take *car* and *jaś* letters — the first *k* becomes *c*: *cakṛṣ*. By *rugrikau ca luki* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-91) — in *yaṅluk*, the reduplicate of a root with *ṛ* as penultimate takes the augments *ruk*, *rik*, *rīk* — the words *ṛdupadhasya* and *rīk* from *rīg ṛdupadhasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-90) are carried on into the previous sūtra. After *carkṛṣ*, *leṭ* by *liṅarthe leṭ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-7); for it *tip*; by *itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97) — in the *parasmaipada*, the *i* of the *tip* coming in place of *leṭ* is dropped — the *i* is dropped. By *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) the augment *aṭ*: *carkṛṣ* + *at*; the *vikaraṇa* *śap*; by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) *luk*. By *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) — when a *sārvadhātuka* or *ārdhadhātuka* suffix follows, the *ik* vowel of a stem ending in *puk* or with a light penultimate takes *guṇa* — *guṇa* would be due. But by *nābhyastasyāci piti sārvadhātuke* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-87) — when a vowel-initial *sārvadhātuka* suffix marked *p* follows, the *guṇa* of the light penultimate does not come — the prohibition comes. So *guṇa* does not come. By *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) — a word ending in *tiṅ* after a word not ending in *tiṅ* is unaccented — the *tiṅ*-final *carkṛṣat*, after *na*, a word not ending in *tiṅ*, is wholly unaccented. ॥15॥

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> पृ॒ञ्च॒तीर्मधु॑ना॒ पयः॑ ॥१६॥
>
> *ambáyo yanty ádhvabhir jāmáyo adhvarīyatā́ṃ |*
> *pṛñcatī́r mádhunā páyaḥ ||16||*

*(Strokes over यो (अम्बयो), ध्व and यो (जामयो); bars under अ, य (यन्ति), जा and य (अध्वरीयताम्). Line 2: bars under पृ and च, strokes over धु and यः, a bar under ना.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अम्बयः । यन्ति । अध्वऽभिः । जामयः । अध्वरिऽयतां ॥
> पृञ्चतीः । मधुना । पयः ॥१६॥
>
> *ambayaḥ | yanti | adhva 'bhiḥ | jāmayaḥ | adhvari 'yatāṃ ||*
> *pṛñcatīḥ | madhunā | payaḥ ||16||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० ५-१, उ० ४-१३८, उ० ४-११४, म० ७-४-३५, पा० ७-४-३९.)*

> अपोनप्त्रीये एकधनासूपानीतासु स्वयमनुगच्छन्नम्बय इति द्वे अनुब्रूयात् । तृतीययापो देवीरित्यनयैकधनासु हविर्धानं प्रविष्टासु स्वयमनुप्रविशेत् । तथैव सूत्रितं । अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिरिति तिस्र उत्तमयानुप्रपद्येत । आ० ५-१ । इति ॥
>
> *aponaptrīye ekadhanāsūpānītāsu svayamanugacchannambaya iti dve anubrūyāt | tṛtīyayāpo devīrityanayaikadhanāsu havirdhānaṃ praviṣṭāsu svayamanupraviśet | tathaiva sūtritaṃ | ambayo yantyadhvabhiriti tisra uttamayānuprapadyeta | ā0 5-1 | iti ||*

**Translation (application):** "At the *aponaptrīya*, when the *ekadhanā* waters have been brought, going along himself, he should recite the two ṛks *ambayaḥ*; with the third, *āpo devīḥ*, when the *ekadhanā* waters have entered the *havirdhāna*, he should himself enter after them. So it is laid down: '*ambayo yanty adhvabhiḥ*: three; with the last he should go in after' (Āśv. 5-1)."

> अध्वरीयतामध्वरमात्मन इच्छतामस्माकमम्बयो मातृस्थानीया आपः । तथा च कौषीतकिब्राह्मणे समाम्नायते । अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिरित्यापो वा अम्बय इति । ता आपोऽध्वभिर्देवयजनमार्गैर्यन्ति । गच्छन्ति । कीदृश्य आपः । जामयो हितकारिण्यो बन्धवः । तथा मधुना माधुर्यरसेन युक्तं पयः पृञ्चतीर्गवादिषु योजयन्त्यः ॥ अम्बयः । रबि लबि अबि शब्दे । एतस्मादच इः । उ० ४-१३८ । इति प्रकरणे बाहुलकादिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अध्वभिः । अदेर्ध च । उ० ४-११४ । इति क्वनिप् । पित्त्वात्प्रत्ययस्यानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । जामयः । जमु अदने । बाहुलकादिः । अध्वरीयतां । अध्वरशब्दात्सुप आत्मनः क्यजिति क्यच् । क्यचि चेतीत्वं । अपुत्रादीनामिति वक्तव्यं । म० ७-४-३५ । इति वचनान्न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्येतीत्वनिषेधाभावः । सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति कव्यध्वरपृतनस्य । पा० ७-४-३९ । इत्यकारलोपोऽपि न भवति । क्यच्प्रत्ययान्तधातोर्लटः शतृ । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण तयोः क्यचा सहैकादेशः । एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वे सति शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वं । पृञ्चतीः । पृची संपर्के । लटः शतृ । रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् । श्नसोरल्लोपः । अनुस्वारपरसवर्णौ । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । वा छन्दसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वं । शतुरनुम इति ङीप उदात्तत्वं ॥
>
> *adhvarīyatāmadhvaramātmana icchatāmasmākamambayo mātṛsthānīyā āpaḥ | tathā ca kauṣītakibrāhmaṇe samāmnāyate | ambayo yantyadhvabhirityāpo vā ambaya iti | tā āpo 'dhvabhirdevayajanamārgairyanti | gacchanti | kīdṛśya āpaḥ | jāmayo hitakāriṇyo bandhavaḥ | tathā madhunā mādhuryarasena yuktaṃ payaḥ pṛñcatīrgavādiṣu yojayantyaḥ || ambayaḥ | rabi labi abi śabde | etasmādaca iḥ | u0 4-138 | iti prakaraṇe bāhulakādiḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | adhvabhiḥ | aderdha ca | u0 4-114 | iti kvanip | pittvātpratyayasyānudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | jāmayaḥ | jamu adane | bāhulakādiḥ | adhvarīyatāṃ | adhvaraśabdātsupa ātmanaḥ kyajiti kyac | kyaci cetītvaṃ | aputrādīnāmiti vaktavyaṃ | ma0 7-4-35 | iti vacanānna chandasyaputrasyetītvaniṣedhābhāvaḥ | sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyanta iti kavyadhvarapṛtanasya | pā0 7-4-39 | ityakāralopo 'pi na bhavati | kyacpratyayāntadhātorlaṭaḥ śatṛ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | śatuśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa tayoḥ kyacā sahaikādeśaḥ | ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityantodāttatve sati śaturanumo nadyajādī iti ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvaṃ | pṛñcatīḥ | pṛcī saṃparke | laṭaḥ śatṛ | rudhādibhyaḥ śnam | śnasorallopaḥ | anusvāraparasavarṇau | ugitaśceti ṅīp | vā chandasīti pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvaṃ | śaturanuma iti ṅīpa udāttatvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "Of us, *adhvarīyatām*, who wish the sacrifice for ourselves, the *ambayaḥ*, mother-like waters — so it is recorded in the Kauṣītaki-brāhmaṇa: '*ambayo yanty adhvabhiḥ*: the waters indeed are the *ambayaḥ*' — those waters *yanti*, go, *adhvabhiḥ*, by the paths to the place of worship of the gods. Of what kind are the waters? *Jāmayaḥ*, kinsfolk who do good; and *pṛñcatīḥ*, mixing, in cows and the like, the *payaḥ*, milk, joined *madhunā*, with sweet juice." (Grammatical tail: *ambayaḥ*, *rabi labi abi śabde*, *i* after it by *ac iḥ* (U. 4-138) in the section, by *bāhulaka*; the suffix accent; *adhvabhiḥ*, *kvanip* by *ader dha ca* (U. 4-114), with the suffix unaccented as *pit*, the root accent; *jāmayaḥ*, *jamu adane*, *i* by *bāhulaka*; *adhvarīyatām*, *kyac* after *adhvara* by *supa ātmanaḥ kyac*, the *ī* by *kyaci ca*; by the statement *aputrādīnām iti vaktavyam* (Ma. 7-4-35) the bar *na chandasy aputrasya* does not apply; by *sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante* the dropping of *a* by *kavyadhvarapṛtanasya* (Pā. 7-4-39) also does not come; *śatṛ* for *laṭ* after the root ending in *kyac*; *śap* unaccented as *pit*, and *śatṛ* too by the *lasārvadhātuka* accent; their single substitute with *kyac* being final udātta by *ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ*, the genitive is udātta by *śatur anumo nadyajādī*; *pṛñcatīḥ*, *pṛcī saṃparke*, *śatṛ* for *laṭ*, *śnam* by *rudhādibhyaḥ śnam*, *a* dropped by *śnasor allopaḥ*, *anusvāra* and *parasavarṇa*, *ṅīp* by *ugitaś ca*, the long like vowel by *vā chandasi*, the *ṅīp* udātta by *śatur anumaḥ…*.)

### Page 201 — Rik 16: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अध्वरीयतां (adhvarīyatāṃ)** — for us who desire the performance of sacrifice | **जामयः (jāmayaḥ)** — who do good like kinsfolk | **अम्बयः (ambayaḥ)** — the waters in the form of mothers (the deities presiding over the waters) | **पयः (payaḥ)** — the milk of cows | **मधुना (madhunā)** — with sweet juice | **पृञ्चतीः (pṛñcatīḥ)** — making it mixed | **अध्वभिः (adhvabhiḥ)** — by the way of the worship of the gods | **यन्ति (yanti)** — flow.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The waters, for us who desire the performance of sacrifice, are in the form of mothers, that is, worthy of honour like a mother. They do good like kinsfolk. They make the milk of cows sweet. Such water is flowing in our path.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The Sacred waters (dear mothers) of the Sacrificers are flowing by the way mixing the milk (of cows) with sweetness.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**अम्बयः (ambayaḥ)** — in the Kauṣītaki-brāhmaṇa there is the explanation, *ambayo yanty adhvabhir ity āpo vā ambayaḥ*, that the word *ambaya* means the waters. Since it is customary to call a mother *amba*, it is to be known that the water here is addressed by a word expressing affection. In the Ṛgveda it is customary to call the deities presiding over the waters (or the waters) *āpo devīḥ*, with the feeling of honour, like honoured women. Besides, it is customary always to address these deities presiding over the waters in the feminine plural. The sūktas with the Waters as deity are very deep, full of meaning, joined with devotion, and very beautiful.

> अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिरित्यापो वा अम्बयः ।
>
> *ambayo yantyadhvabhirityāpo vā ambayaḥ |*

**जामयः (jāmayaḥ)** — *hitakāriṇyo bandhavaḥ |* kinsfolk who are well-wishers. The use of this word is in the Ṛgveda in the ṛks 1-31-10; 3-52-3 (zoom: the second group's digits are the lobed 5 and a curled 2, not the 4-glyph); 4-25-3; 8-102-13; 9-26-5; 9-65-1; 9-66-8; 9-89-4; 10-10-10 (small type, as read).

### Page 202 — Rik 16: Special Topics (end), grammar

**अध्वरीयतां (adhvarīyatāṃ)** — *adhvareṇa* (by sacrifice) *devayajanaṃ kartum icchatām ||* who desire to perform the sacrifice.

**पृञ्चतीः (pṛñcatīḥ)** — *miśrayantyaḥ*: mixing.

**मधुना पयः (madhunā payaḥ)** — the ṛṣi may have used this expression because water is most needed to support life, because flowing water in rivers and the like is sweet, unlike sea water, and because cows, by drinking such water, give tasty milk.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**अम्बयः (ambayaḥ)** — the root *rabi labi abi śabde*; for the *i* of the root *abi* the *it*-name and dropping have come. So this is *idit*, that is, having *i* as *it*; so by *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58) — after the last vowel of a root marked *i* comes the augment *num* (*n*) — the augment *num*. By *ac iḥ* (U. Sū. 4-528 read at zoom in the small type: the 5-glyph, curled 2, 8-glyph; the bhāṣya prints उ० ४-१३८, so the two differ as printed) — after a root ending in a vowel comes the suffix *i* — this is its meaning. Though the root *amb* does not end in a vowel, since *bahulam* is said in this section, the suffix *i* comes here. By the suffix accent the *i* is udātta.

**अध्वभिः (adhvabhiḥ)** — by *ader dha ca* (U. Sū. 4-[?] in the small type, four lobed glyphs that I cannot separate at zoom; the bhāṣya prints उ० ४-११४) — after the root *ada bhakṣaṇe* the suffix *kvanip* comes, and *dh* for the *d* of the root — when the suffix *kvanip* comes and *dh* for the *d*, it becomes *adhvan*. The suffix *kvanip* is *pit*; so by *anudāttau suppitau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) it is unaccented, and the root accent alone stays.

**जामयः (jāmayaḥ)** — the root *jamu adane*; after it, by the mention of *bahula*, the suffix *i*.

**अध्वरीयतां (adhvarīyatāṃ)** — *na vidyate dhvaraḥ* (*hiṃsā*) *yasmin saḥ adhvaraḥ*; by *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) final udātta. The analysis is *adhvaram ātmanaḥ icchanti iti adhvarīyantaḥ, teṣām adhvarīyatām*. By *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8) and the *paribhāṣā* *pratyayagrahaṇe yasmāt sa vihitas tadādes tadantasya grahaṇam* (Paribhā. 24), in *supaḥ* 'ending in it' is obtained. It became *subantāt*. From *dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-7) the three words *karmaṇaḥ*, *icchāyām*, *vā* are carried on. *Karmaṇaḥ* is a word in the fifth case, so 'from what expresses the object' results. 'The object with regard to what?' — when this expectation arises, *icchāyām* is present, so it results: 'being the object with regard to the root *iṣ*'. The word *ātman* conveys the meaning *sva*, 'oneself'. When purpose is intended, the fourth case *ātmane* would be fitting here; yet intending the purpose as a relation, by *ṣaṣṭhī*

### Page 203 — Rik 16: grammar (continued)

*śeṣe* (Pā. Sū. 2-3-50) the genitive has come. Thus *ātmanaḥ* means 'for one's own purpose'. *Sva* intends the one who wishes. And so the sense of the sūtra: in the sense 'wishes', *kyac* comes after a *sup*-ending word expressing the object that is for the purpose of the one who wishes. This mantra is one with the Waters as deity. Those who praise the Water deity wish the sacrifice for their own purpose: this is the situation. Then *adhvaram* is a *sup*-ending word that is the object with regard to the root *iṣ* in *icchati*. This object is for the purpose of those who wish. Therefore after the word *adhvaram* the suffix *kyac* comes: *adhvara* + *am* + *kyac*. *Kyac* is included among the twelve *sanādi* suffixes counted as *sankyackāmyac…*; so by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-32) — what ends in *san* and the rest gets the name *dhātu* — *adhvarīya* gets the name *dhātu*. By *supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-71) — a *sup* that is part of a root or a nominal stem is dropped (*luk*) — the *am* is dropped (*luk*): *adhvara* + *ya*. By *kyaci ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-33) — when the suffix *kyac* follows, *ī* is substituted for that *a* — the substitute *ī* for the *a* before *ya*: it became *adhvarī* + *ya*. But here by *na chandasy aputrasya* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-35) — when *kyac* follows, for words ending in *a* other than the word *putra*, the substitute *ī* and lengthening do not come — the question arises that the prohibition of *ītva* should come for the word *adhvara* (not being *putra*). To this the author of the *vārttika* has said by the *vārttika* *aputrādīnām iti vaktavyam* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-35 Vā.) that instead of *aputrasya* one should read *aputrādīnām* in the sūtra. Now it means that, leaving aside the words *putra* and the rest, for a word ending in *a*, when *kyac* follows, *ītva* does not come. The answer is that since the word *adhvara* is included among the *putrādi*, the prohibition of *ītva* does not come for it. By *kavyadhvarapṛtanasyarci lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-39) — in the matter of the ṛk, when the suffix *kyac* follows, the final letter of the words *kavi*, *adhvara*, *pṛtanā* is dropped — the dropping of the *a* of the word *adhvara* would be due. But by *sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante* (Paribhā. 36 as read; the 3 is the ಇ-glyph, the 6 the hooked glyph) — in the Veda all operations come optionally — the *a* is not dropped. By *vartamāne laṭ* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-123) *laṭ* comes after the root *adhvarīya* ending in the suffix *kyac*; for it by *laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-124) the substitute *śatṛ*; by *kartari śap* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the *vikaraṇa* *śap* (*a*): it became *adhvarīya* + *a* + *at*. By *citaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the *a* of *kyac*, being *cit*, is udātta. By *anudāttau suppitau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) *śap* is unaccented. *Śatṛ* is a *sārvadhātuka* in place of *la*; it follows the *a*-final original teaching *śap*. So by *tāsy anu-*

### Page 204 — Rik 16: grammar (continued)

*dāttenṅid adupadeśāt…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) *śatṛ* is unaccented; for these two unaccented *a*'s, by *ato guṇe* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97), the following form comes. By *sthānivadbhāva* it is unaccented. For this *a* and the *a* of *kyac*, again by the following form, a short *a* comes. Since it comes in place of both udātta and unaccented, by *ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-5) it becomes udātta. Thus *adhvarīyat* is final udātta. After it the genitive plural *ām*: *adhvarīyat* + *ām*. Here by *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173) — if a word ending in the suffix *śatṛ* without the augment *num* is final udātta, the *nadī*-named suffix and the vowel-initial case-endings *śas* and the rest after it are also udātta — the *ām* is udātta.

**पृञ्चतीः (pṛñcatīḥ)** — the root *pṛcī saṃparke*. After it *laṭ*; for it *śatṛ*: *pṛc* + *at*. By *rudhādibhyaḥ śnam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-78) the *vikaraṇa* *śna*; by the force of being *mit*, it comes after the *ṛ* of *pṛ*: *pṛ* + *na* + *c* + *at*. By *śnasor allopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111) — when a *sārvadhātuka* suffix that is *kit* or *ṅit* follows, the *a* of the suffix *śna* and of the root *as* is dropped — the *a* of the suffix *śna* is dropped: *pṛ* + *n* + *c* + *at*. By *stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-40) the palatalisation of the *n*, the *ñ*, is *asiddha* when making the *anusvāra*; so by *naś cāpadāntasya jhali* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-24) — when a *jhal* letter follows, the *n* and *m* not at the end of a *pada* take *anusvāra* — *anusvāra*; for it by *anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-58) — before a *yay* letter, the *anusvāra* takes the homorganic of the following — before the *c* comes, by place, the homorganic nasal *ñ*. *Pṛñc* + *at*: when making *anusvāra* and *parasavarṇa*, since there is the prohibition *na padānta… svarasavarṇānusvāra…* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-58), the *sthānivadbhāva* for the dropping of *a* by *acaḥ parasmin* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-57) does not come. The *ṛ* of *śatṛ* has the *it*-name; the *ṛ* is in the *pratyāhāra* *uk*; so *śatṛ* is *ugit*. By *ugitaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-6) — when the feminine is intended after a nominal stem ending in an *ugit*, *ṅīp* comes — *ṅīp* comes: *pṛñcat* + *ī*. On the view that it names letters, by *yū stryākhyau nadī* (Pā. Sū. 1-4-3) the *ī* has the name *nadī*; so by *śatur anumo nadyajādī* the *ī* is udātta. After *pṛñcatī*, *jas*; by *vā chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-106) — in the Veda, after a long vowel, if *jas* or an *ic* follows, the long like vowel comes optionally — the long like vowel comes. ॥16॥
