### Page 205 — Sūkta 23, Rik 17

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अ॒मूर्या उप॒ सूर्ये॒ याभि॑र्वा॒ सूर्यः॑ स॒ह ।
> ता नो॑ हिन्वन्त्व॒ध्वरं॑ ॥१७॥
>
> *amū́r yā́ upa sū́rye yā́bhir vā sū́ryaḥ sahá |*
> *tā́ no hinvantv adhváraṃ ||17||*

*(Bars under अ, प (उप), र्ये, वा and स (सह); strokes over भि and र्यः. Line 2: a stroke over नो, a bar under ध्व; the stroke over रं, shown in the Pada, is read in the Saṃhitā too.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अमूः । याः । उप । सूर्ये । याभिः । वा । सूर्यः । सह ॥
> ताः । नः । हिन्वन्तु । अध्वरं ॥१७॥
>
> *amūḥ | yāḥ | upa | sūrye | yābhiḥ | vā | sūryaḥ | saha ||*
> *tāḥ | naḥ | hinvantu | adhvaraṃ ||17||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> या अमूरापः सूर्ये उप समीपेनावस्थिताः । आपः सूर्ये समाहिता इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । वाथवा सूर्यो याभिरद्भिः सह वर्तते । पूर्वत्रापां प्राधान्यमुत्तरत्र सूर्यस्येति विशेषः । तास्तादृश्य आपो नोऽस्मदीयमध्वरं यागं हिन्वन्तु । प्रीणयन्तु ॥ याभिः । सावेकाच इति विभक्त्युदात्तत्वस्य न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषेधः । शेषा तु प्रक्रिया स्पष्टा ॥
>
> *yā amūrāpaḥ sūrye upa samīpenāvasthitāḥ | āpaḥ sūrye samāhitā iti śrutyantarāt | vāthavā sūryo yābhiradbhiḥ saha vartate | pūrvatrāpāṃ prādhānyamuttaratra sūryasyeti viśeṣaḥ | tāstādṛśya āpo no 'smadīyamadhvaraṃ yāgaṃ hinvantu | prīṇayantu || yābhiḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhaktyudāttatvasya na gośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣedhaḥ | śeṣā tu prakriyā spaṣṭā ||*

**Translation:** "Those waters, *yāḥ amūḥ*, which are set *upa*, near, *sūrye*, the sun — from another *śruti*, 'the waters are placed in the sun' — *vā*, or, *yābhiḥ*, the waters with which the sun is *saha*, together; in the first [half] the waters are the chief, in the second the sun: that is the difference. May such waters *hinvantu*, gladden, *naḥ adhvaram*, our sacrifice." (Grammatical tail: *yābhiḥ*, the case-ending udātta by *sāv ekācaḥ* is barred by *na gośvansāvavarṇa…*; the rest of the derivation is clear.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**याः अमूः (yāḥ amūḥ)** — which these waters | **सूर्ये उप (sūrye upa)** — are near the sun | **वा (vā)** — or | **सूर्यः (sūryaḥ)** — the sun | **याभिः (yābhiḥ)** — with which waters | **सह (saha)** — is together | **ताः (tāḥ)** — those waters | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **अध्वरं (adhvaraṃ)** — sacrifice | **हिन्वन्तु (hinvantu)** — may they carry out gladly.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

May those waters which are near the sun, or near which waters the sun is, make our sacrifice come to pass gladly.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Those sacred waters who are near the sun or to whom the sun is near, may they promote our sacrifice.

### Page 206 — Rik 17: Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**या उप सूर्ये (yā upa sūrye)** — the waters near the sun, that is, the water (sea water) drawn up by the sun's rays and in the mid-air in the form of clouds. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka too there is the *śruti* statement *āpaḥ sūrye samāhitāḥ*. *Yābhir vā sūryaḥ saha* — this sentence too has the same meaning; it is said in another way, by changing the case and number. Or, since the sun's rays fall on bodies of water such as rivers, it may be said that the sun is near the water. In sum this mantra suggests that there is a close connection between water and the sun.

> आपः सूर्ये समाहिताः ।
>
> *āpaḥ sūrye samāhitāḥ |*

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**याभिः (yābhiḥ)** — after the word *yad*, *bhis*; by *tyadādīnām aḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) — when a case-ending follows, the final letter of the words read in the *tyadādi* class takes *a* — the *a* for the *d*, the following form, *ṭāp* when the feminine is shown, the lengthening of like vowels; *yā* + *bhis*, *ru* and *visarga* for the *s*: it becomes *yābhiḥ*. *Sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168): the meaning of the sūtra is that when the locative plural suffix *su* follows, the case-ending after a monosyllabic form that conveys the same meaning as the monosyllabic form found before *su* is udātta. In the Mahābhāṣya on this sūtra:

> सावितिकिमिदं प्रथमैकवचनस्य ग्रहणमाहोस्वित्सप्तमीबहुवचनस्य ।
>
> *sāvitikimidaṃ prathamaikavacanasya grahaṇamāhosvitsaptamībahuvacanasya |*

"What is *sau* — is it the taking of the nominative singular or of the locative plural?" — that is, does the word *sau* take the first-case singular suffix *su*, or the locative plural *sup*? The Bhāṣya: *kutaḥ saṃdehaḥ?* — what is the reason for doubt? *Samāno nirdeśaḥ*: even if the locative *ṅi* is put after the nominative singular *su*, it becomes *sau*; when the *p* of the locative plural *sup* is removed by the *it*-name, it stands as *su*, and even if the locative singular *ṅi* is put after it, it becomes *sau*. Since in both the first and the seventh case the form *sau* is the same, doubt arises. Here the author of the *Kaiyaṭa* has described the intention thus:

> यदि शास्त्रीयं सुरूपं गृह्यते तदा प्राथम्यात्प्रथमैकवचनस्य ग्रहणेन भाव्यम् । अथ प्रायोगिकं ततः सप्तमीबहुवचनस्य । तद्धि प्रयोगे सुरूपं श्रूयते । प्रथमैकवचने तु विकृतरूपप्रयोगे न सुरूपमिति संशयानः पृच्छति सावितिकिमिति ।
>
> *yadi śāstrīyaṃ surūpaṃ gṛhyate tadā prāthamyātprathamaikavacanasya grahaṇena bhāvyam | atha prāyogikaṃ tataḥ saptamībahuvacanasya | taddhi prayoge surūpaṃ śrūyate | prathamaikavacane tu vikṛtarūpaprayoge na surūpamiti saṃśayānaḥ pṛcchati sāvitikimiti |*

That is: on the view of taking the form *su* established in the technical usage of the science, by the maxim *prathamopasthite parityāge kāraṇābhāvaḥ*, among the twenty-one suffixes *su* and the rest the first, the nominative singular *su*, is taken; if it is intended to take the *su* heard in usage, the locative plural is taken. For in the nominative singular the order *su* —

> प्रथमोपस्थिते परित्यागे कारणाभावः ।
>
> *prathamopasthite parityāge kāraṇābhāvaḥ |*

### Page 207 — Rik 17: grammar (continued)

— is not heard as the form *su*, because it is changed: for example *rāmaḥ* and the like, where the *su* has become *visarga*. In places like *rāmāsu* the order *su* is heard in the locative plural. So on the view of taking the usage, the seventh would have to be taken. Since there is such doubt, in the Bhāṣya the question has been considered whether the nominative singular or the locative plural is taken. The answer:

> सप्तमीबहुवचनस्य ग्रहणम् ।
> कथं ज्ञायते ।
> यदयं नगोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषेधं शास्ति ।
> कथं कृत्वा ज्ञापकम् ।
> यदि प्रथमैकवचनस्य ग्रहणं स्याद्गोशुनोः प्रतिषेधवचनमनर्थकं स्यात् ।
>
> *saptamībahuvacanasya grahaṇam |*
> *kathaṃ jñāyate |*
> *yadayaṃ nagośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣedhaṃ śāsti |*
> *kathaṃ kṛtvā jñāpakam |*
> *yadi prathamaikavacanasya grahaṇaṃ syādgośunoḥ pratiṣedhavacanamanarthakaṃ syāt |*

"The locative plural is taken. How is it known? Because he teaches the prohibition *nagośvansāvavarṇa…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-182). How does that make it known? If the nominative singular were taken, the statement of prohibition for *go* and *śvan* would be pointless." That is: in the nominative singular the forms are *gauḥ* and *śvā*; in the word *go*, *gauḥ* is a monosyllabic form ending in *au*; in the word *śvan*, *śvā* is a monosyllabic form ending in *ā*. In *gobhyām*, *śvabhyām*, the case-ending is after the *o*-final monosyllable *go* and after the short-vowel-final monosyllable *śva*. So in the nominative singular, after whatever monosyllabic form there is, there is no such case-ending after that monosyllable; so *sāv ekācaḥ* would not apply at all, and the statement of prohibition would be useless. If the locative plural is taken, in the locative plural *goṣu*, *śvasu*, the monosyllabic forms *go* and *śva* are found when the locative plural *su* follows. So after the monosyllables *go*, *śva*, the *bhyām* in *gobhyām*, *śvabhyām* would get the udātta by *sāv ekācaḥ*. To prevent it, the prohibition of the udātta for the case-ending after *go*, *śvan* in the sūtra *nagośvan* is purposeful. So the author of the Bhāṣya has established that the locative plural alone is taken. From the Bhāṣya that states the indication itself it results that in *sāv ekācaḥ* the taking of the form is intended. Otherwise, *sau ya ekāc* —

### Page 208 — Rik 17: grammar (continued)

— since in the nominative singular there are the monosyllables *gauḥ*, *śvā*, if the accent were due, the prohibition would be purposeful and could not indicate the stated meaning; if the taking of the form is intended, *sau yadrūpaviśiṣṭaḥ ekāc*: when the nominative singular *su* follows, whatever monosyllabic form there is, *gauḥ*, *śvā*, after it in *gobhyaḥ*, *śvabhyaḥ* there is no case-ending, so the prohibition is incongruous and indicates the stated meaning.

If the nominative singular is taken, a fault comes in *yātā*, where *laṭ* comes after the root *yā*, *śatṛ* for it, *luk* for *śap*, and the instrumental singular *ṭā*: for in the nominative singular, since the dropping of the conjunct-final is *asiddha*, whether as *yān* or as *yānt*, there is a monosyllabic form. After it there is no case-ending of the third onward, but after *yāt* there is the third case-ending. So in the nominative singular, *yadarthaviśiṣṭam ekājrūpam*, since there is no case-ending of the third onward after the monosyllable qualified by that meaning, *sāv ekācaḥ* would not come here. By taking the changed form *yānt* in the nominative singular, the original form *yāt* cannot be taken; and the maxim —

> यदागमास्तद्गुणीभूतास्तद्ग्रहणेन गृह्यन्ते ।
>
> *yadāgamāstadguṇībhūtāstadgrahaṇena gṛhyante |*

— 'augments, being subordinate to it, are taken by its mention' — says that where the mention is of what lacks the augment, what has the augment is also taken; so by the mention of *yāns*, which has the augment, *yāt*, which lacks it, cannot be taken. And *tanmadhyapatitas tadgrahaṇena gṛhyate* (Paribhā. 90 as printed, zoom-checked on p. 208: the 9-glyph and the ring) makes known only that by the mention of the bare thing the qualified one is taken; by the qualified *yānt* the bare *yāt* cannot be taken.

> तन्मध्यपतितस्तद्ग्रहणेन गृह्यते ।
>
> *tanmadhyapatitastadgrahaṇena gṛhyate |*

In *sāv ekācaḥ* one does not describe the meaning by intending the taking of the form, 'whatever monosyllabic form expressing a meaning there is before *su*'. Rather the meaning of the sūtra *sāv ekācaḥ* is: when *su* follows, whatever word is monosyllabic, the case-ending of the third onward after that word is udātta. Thus, since the word *yāt* is monosyllabic in the nominative singular, the case-ending after it may get the udātta. But though in *yātā* there is no fault, a fault comes in *doṣabhyām*. In the nominative singular *doḥ* the word *doṣ* is monosyllabic. When *bhyām* comes after it, after the substitute *doṣan* by *paddannomāshṛnniśasanyūṣandoṣan…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-63), in *doṣan* + *bhyām* too the *bhyām* would have to be udātta. The mid-udātta accent *doṣabhyām* is what is desired here. So the taking of the form must be intended. Now the monosyllabic form before *su* is *doḥ*. After it there is no *bhyām*. So by *sāv ekācaḥ* the case-ending does not get the udātta; but by *anudāttau suppitau* it is unaccented. The word *doṣ* —

### Page 209 — Rik 17: grammar (continued)

— ends in the suffix *ḍosi* by *damer ḍosiḥ* (U. Sū. 3-28 at zoom: the first digit is a heavy-headed glyph that looks like a 3 with a dot above, then 2 and 8 [lobed]; Vol 3 elsewhere reads this as 2-28), and is final udātta by the suffix accent. When the substitute *doṣan* coming in its place is also final udātta, the mid-udātta *doṣabhyām* is established. Even if *sau* is intended as the locative plural, if one does not intend the taking of the form in *sāv ekācaḥ* as said before, the fault comes in *doṣabhyām*. Thus, since the intention to take the form in *sāv ekācaḥ* is needed to prevent the udātta of the case-ending in *doṣabhyām*, once that is established, if the nominative singular is taken, the udātta cannot come in *yātā*. For that it must be held that the locative plural alone is taken. Now since in the locative *yātsu* is the form, *sau yad ekājrūpaṃ yāt*, and the case-ending after it exists, the udātta accent is established in places like *yātā*, *yādbhyām*. Even if *sāv ekācaḥ* is held to be the locative and the taking of the form is intended, the fault comes in *doṣabhyām*. In *doḥṣu*, when *su* follows, there is the form *doḥ*. This is not heard in *doṣabhyām*. Yet since in place of *doṣ* the substitute *doṣan* has come, by the *sthānivadbhāva* of *sthānivad ādeśaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-56) the form *doṣan* becomes like the form *doḥ*. So in the locative plural, since there is a case-ending of the third onward after whatever form there is, the *bhyām* would have to be udātta. In the Taittirīya, *doṣabhyāṃ svāhā* is mid-udātta, so it cannot be said that the udātta of the case-ending is desired. Only where the form found when the locative plural follows is actually heard does *sāv ekācaḥ* come. Where it is not directly heard, we say that, imagining by *sthānivadbhāva* and the like that the same form is there, the present sūtra does not enter. Thus in *doṣabhyām*, since *doḥ* is not heard, *sāv ekācaḥ* does not come here. Then on this view the examples *śunaḥ*, *śunā* given by the author of the Bhāṣya at the sūtra *nagośvan* would have to be incongruous. In the locative plural form *śvasu*, the form *śva* is heard here; since the dropping of *n* is an accent rule, even though by *nalopaḥ supsvara…* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-2) it is *asiddha*, it becomes as if *śvan* were there. In *śunaḥ*, *śunā* the form *śvan*, heard in the Veda, is not heard as either *śva* or *śvan*; so here *sāv ekācaḥ* does not apply at all. Then why should the prohibition come here? So it is to be held that there is no strict requirement that the form be directly heard. Now, though by *saṃprasāraṇa* *u* has come for the *v*, a part of *śvan*, and a change has come to the part, by *ekadeśavikṛtam ananyavat*, imagining that *śvan* itself is there, *sāv ekācaḥ* would be due; to avoid it, the example *śunaḥ*, *śunā* of the prohibition becomes congruous. Likewise in *doṣabhyām*, by *sthānivadbhāva* the form *doḥ* —

> एकदेशविकृतमनन्यवत् ।
>
> *ekadeśavikṛtamananyavat |*

### Page 210 — Rik 17: grammar (continued)

— being there, one may object that the case-ending should be udātta. The answer: according to usage we repeat *ekācaḥ*. So the meaning drawn out of the sūtra is: when the *su* suffix follows, whatever monosyllabic word expressing a meaning is heard, on the view that the case-ending after such a form is after that very monosyllable, it gets the udātta. *Doṣabhyām* follows the polysyllable *doṣa*, so the udātta accent does not come here. If the word *sau* were not there, it would mean *ekācaḥ paraṃ tṛtīyādir vibhaktir udāttā syāt*. In *rājñā* the *ṭā* is after the monosyllable *rājñ*, so it would have to be udātta. If *ekācaḥ* were not there, the meaning of the sūtra *sāv ekācaḥ* would be *sau vartamānāt śabdāt parā tṛtīyādir vibhaktir udāttā syāt*. Then too in *rājñā*, since the *ṭā* is after the word found in *sau*, it would have to be udātta. On this view of *sau*, a word like *dvābhyām*, for which being followed by *su* is not possible, would have to be excluded. So here both *sau* and *ekācaḥ* must be there. The conclusion has been reached that by *sau* the locative plural alone is to be taken and that the taking of the form is also intended.

Even so, in the feminine, in words like *ābhyām* and in forms like *ebhiḥ*, *eṣām*, the case-ending would have to be udātta by *sāv ekācaḥ*. So the total lack of accent cannot be obtained. In the feminine the locative form is *āsu*; so when *su* follows, the monosyllabic form *ā* is heard; in *ābhyām* the *bhyām* after such an *ā* would have to get the udātta by *sāv ekācaḥ*. In the masculine and neuter the locative form is *eṣu*. So, though when *su* follows *e* is monosyllabic, in *ebhiḥ*, *eṣām* the *bhis* and *ām* after such an *e* would have to get the udātta by *sāv ekācaḥ*.

When the case-ending thus gets the udātta, by the *śeṣānudātta* accent *anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-158) the stem's being unaccented is established anyway. That being so, in the sūtra *idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-32) the rule laying down the unaccented for *aś* becomes useless. Being useless, it makes known that when *aś* has come in *anvādeśa*, the case-ending there does not get the udātta. So it cannot be said that in places like *ebhiḥ* the case-ending cannot be udātta. For if the rule of the unaccented for *aś* were wholly useless, by the maxim —

> व्यर्थं सत् किंचिदर्थं ज्ञापयति ।
>
> *vyarthaṃ sat kiṃcidarthaṃ jñāpayati |*

— it could be said to make known the stated meaning. But it is not wholly useless. Where by *sāv ekācaḥ* the case-ending must not get the udātta, there, by *śeṣanighāta*, the stem cannot be unaccented; there the rule of the unaccented is purposeful. For example, the masculine —

### Page 211 (upper) — Rik 17: grammar (end)

— and neuter *ābhyām* and the like: in the masculine and neuter, when *su* follows, the monosyllabic form is *e*, not *ā*; so in the locative plural there is no such monosyllabic form. In the feminine *āsu*, when the locative plural follows, the form *ā* does exist; but the meaning is different: it is a monosyllabic form expressing the feminine, while the *ā* of the masculine and neuter *ābhyām* is a monosyllabic form expressing masculine and neuter. So, since what follows *sau yadarthaviśiṣṭam ekājrūpam* is not there, the udātta is not established for the masculine-neuter *ābhyām*; so the stem does not become unaccented by *śeṣanighāta*. Here, to obtain the unaccented, the rule of the unaccented is purposeful. Therefore the rule of the unaccented cannot make known that in the matter of *anvādeśa* the case-ending accent does not come. Since in the nominative singular it does not end in *a*/*ā*, it cannot be said that in *ebhiḥ* and the like the udātta is barred by *nagośvan*. In *ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) *antodāttāt* is carried on. In *ābhyām* the stem is unaccented. So since there is no case-ending after a final udātta, the udātta of the case-ending cannot be established by *ūḍidam*. So it cannot be said that the udātta accent of the case-ending is what is desired. In Vedic usages like *ebhir agne piba* [as printed] and *ebhir agne duvo giraḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-1) total lack of accent alone is heard. Here, even taking the refined meaning of *sāv ekācaḥ*, the case-ending would have to be udātta. So in places like *ebhiḥ* the total lack of accent must be held to be Vedic. The author of the *Uddyota*, when describing the *Pradīpa*'s intention, says, *ebhir agne ityādau sarvānudāttapadaśravaṇaṃ tu chāndasam iti tadbhāvaḥ* (Uddyota 6-1-168) and so on. It seems that the work that resolved this, which the *Candrakalā* saw in the *Śekhara* of the present sūtra, is lost. It now results that, even taking the refined meaning of *sāv ekācaḥ* in the manner of the available *Śekhara*, its application in *ebhiḥ* cannot be stopped. Considering the present case: in *yābhiḥ* the udātta of the case-ending would be due by *sāv ekācaḥ*. For that, by *nagośvansāvavarṇarāḍaṅkruṅkṛdbhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-182) — after the word *go*, the word *śvan*, words ending in *a*/*ā* in the nominative singular, the word *rāṭ* ending in *kvip*, the word *aṅ* formed with *kvip* after the root *añc*, the word *kruñ* formed with *kvin* after the root *kruñc*, and the word *kṛt* formed with *kvip* after the root *kṛ*, the case-ending and the *matup* do not get the udātta — since in the nominative singular *yā* ends in *a*/*ā*, the *bhis* after *yā* does not get the udātta. The rest of the derivation is clear. ॥17॥

> एभिरग्ने इत्यादौ सर्वानुदात्तपदश्रवणं तु छान्दसमिति तद्भावः ।
>
> *ebhiragne ityādau sarvānudāttapadaśravaṇaṃ tu chāndasamiti tadbhāvaḥ |*

> एभिरग्ने पिब सोमं ।
> एभिरग्ने दुवो गिरः ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-१४-१)

> *ebhiragne piba somaṃ |*

### Page 212 — Sūkta 23, Rik 18

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अ॒पो दे॒वीरुप॑ ह्वये॒ यत्र॒ गावः॒ पिब॑न्ति नः ।
> सि॒न्धुभ्यः॒ कर्त्वं॑ ह॒विः ॥१८॥
>
> *apó devī́r úpa hvaye yátra gā́vaḥ píbanti naḥ |*
> *sindhúbhyaḥ kártvaṃ havíḥ ||18||*

*(Bars under अ, दे, ये (ह्वये), त्र (यत्र) and वः; strokes over प (उप) and ब (पिबन्ति). Line 2: bars under सि, भ्यः and ह; a stroke over र्त्वं.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अपः । देवीः । उप । ह्वये । यत्र । गावः । पिबन्ति । नः ॥
> सिन्धुऽभ्यः । कर्त्वं । हविः ॥१८॥
>
> *apaḥ | devīḥ | upa | hvaye | yatra | gāvaḥ | pibanti | naḥ ||*
> *sindhu 'bhyaḥ | kartvaṃ | haviḥ ||18||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(The number is printed पा० ३-४-१४.)*

> नोऽस्मदीया गावो यत्र यास्वप्सु पिबन्ति पानं कुर्वन्ति ता आपो देवीरुप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । सिन्धुभ्यः स्यन्दनशीलाभ्योऽद्भ्यो देवताभ्यो हविः कर्त्वं । अस्माभिः कर्तव्यं ॥ अपः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना शस उदात्तत्वं । पिबन्ति । पाघ्रेत्यादिना पिबादेशः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ निपातैर्यद्यदीत्यादिना निघाताभावः । कर्त्वं । डुकृञ् करणे । कृत्यार्थे तवैकेन्केन्यत्वनः । पा० ३-४-१४ । इति कर्मणि त्वन्प्रत्ययः । गुणः । नित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥
>
> *no 'smadīyā gāvo yatra yāsvapsu pibanti pānaṃ kurvanti tā āpo devīrupa hvaye | āhvayāmi | sindhubhyaḥ syandanaśīlābhyo 'dbhyo devatābhyo haviḥ kartvaṃ | asmābhiḥ kartavyaṃ || apaḥ | ūḍidamityādinā śasa udāttatvaṃ | pibanti | pāghretyādinā pibādeśaḥ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvareṇādyudāttatvaṃ || nipātairyadyadītyādinā nighātābhāvaḥ | kartvaṃ | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ | pā0 3-4-14 | iti karmaṇi tvanpratyayaḥ | guṇaḥ | nitsvareṇādyudāttatvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "I *upa hvaye*, call, the *āpaḥ devīḥ*, divine waters, *yatra*, in which waters *naḥ gāvaḥ*, our cows, *pibanti*, drink. *Havis* is *kartvam*, to be made by us, *sindhubhyaḥ*, for the deities, the waters that are of flowing nature." (Grammatical tail: *apaḥ*, the *śas* udātta by *ūḍidam…*; *pibanti*, the substitute *piba* by *pāghrā…*, *śap* unaccented as *pit*, and the *tiṅ* by the *lasārvadhātuka* accent, so initial udātta by the root accent; no loss of accent by *nipātair yadyadi…*; *kartvam*, *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, the suffix *tvan* in the object sense by *kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-14), *guṇa*, initial udātta by the *nit* accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**नः (naḥ)** — our | **गावः (gāvaḥ)** — cows | **यत्र (yatra)** — in which body of water | **पिबन्ति (pibanti)** — drink water | **(ताः) अपः देवीः ((tāḥ) apaḥ devīḥ)** — that excellent water | **उप ह्वये (upa hvaye)** — I call | **सिन्धुभ्यः (sindhubhyaḥ)** — with regard to those flowing waters | **हविः (haviḥ)** — the giving of the oblation | **कर्त्वं (kartvaṃ)** — must be made.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

I call that excellent water, in whatever body of water, a river and the like, our cows drink. With regard to that flowing water we must necessarily make the giving of oblations.

### Page 213 — Rik 18: English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> I invoke hither the sacred waters at which our cows drink; our oblations are to be made to those streams.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**सिन्धुभ्यः (sindhubhyaḥ)** — *syandanaśīlābhyo devatābhyaḥ |* In this ṛk and in other ṛks that set forth the deities presiding over the waters, the ṛṣis have made hymns with regard to *āpo devīḥ*, that is, excellent or honoured flowing water. On some occasions the water of lakes, tanks and the like, which do not flow, is also indicated. So sweet water fit for drinking is especially praised. Sea water is not seen to have so much pre-eminence.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**अपः (apaḥ)** — after the word *ap*, the accusative plural suffix *śas*; for the *ś*, by *laśakv ataddhite* (Pā. Sū. 1-3-8) the *it*-name comes, and by *tasya lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 1-3-9) it is dropped: *ap* + *as* = *apas*; for the *s*, by *sasajuṣo ruḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-66) *ru*, by *kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-15) the *visarga*: it becomes *apaḥ*. Here in *ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171), *ekācaḥ* from *sāv ekācaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168), *antodāttāt* from *antodāttād uttarapadāt…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-169), and *asarvanāmasthānam* from *añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-170) are carried on. *Ūṭh* is not a monosyllabic form. Because it is not monosyllabic, *ekācaḥ* is not its qualifier, *asaṃbhavāt*: the maxim is *saṃbhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ syād viśeṣaṇam arthavat* — *saṃbhava*, fitness; *vyabhicāra*, exclusion of others. Now the meaning of the sūtra: the case-ending other than *sarvanāmasthāna* after *ūṭh*, which is final udātta and stands penultimate, and after the word *idam*, the six *padādi* words, *ap*, *pums*, *rai*, *div*, which are final udātta and monosyllabic, is udātta. If by *ūṭh* the whole containing *ūṭh* is intended, then *ekācaḥ* is a qualifier for *ūṭh* too. Then the meaning for the part *ūṭh*: the case-ending other than *sarvanāmasthāna* after a monosyllabic word containing *ūṭh*, final udātta and penultimate, is udātta. Examples *praṣṭhauhaḥ*, *viśvauhaḥ* and the like. Since *ekācaḥ* is mentioned in the sūtra, the qualifier, by *śrutānumitayoḥ śrutasaṃbandho balīyān*, is not a qualifier of the stem. So, though the stems *praṣṭhauh*, *viśvauh* are polysyllabic, since *ūh* is monosyllabic, the accent applies; likewise in places like *brāhmaṇapadā* —

> संभवव्यभिचाराभ्यां स्याद्विशेषणमर्थवत् ।
> श्रुतानुमितयोः श्रुतसंबन्धो बलीयान् ।
>
> *saṃbhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ syādviśeṣaṇamarthavat |*
> *śrutānumitayoḥ śrutasaṃbandho balīyān |*

### Page 214 — Rik 18: grammar (continued)

— the final udātta is established. The present word *ap* is final udātta and monosyllabic. So the *śas*, a non-*sarvanāmasthāna* case-ending after it, is udātta.

**पिबन्ति (pibanti)** — the root *pā pāne*; after it *laṭ*, the third person plural suffix *jhi*; by *jho 'ntaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-3) the substitute *ant* for *jh*: *pā* + *anti*; by *kartari śap* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the *vikaraṇa* *śap*: *pā* + *a* + *anti*. Now by *pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartisartiśadasadāṃ pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchadhauśīyasīdāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78) — when a suffix beginning with the *it*-named *ś* follows, the eleven roots *pā* and the rest take the eleven substitutes *piba* and the rest. Whether the substitute is *piba* ending in *a* or *pib* ending in *b* has been explained at the sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-18-11 [as printed]). When the substitute *piba* comes: *piba* + *a* + *anti*; twice, by *ato guṇe* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) — if the *guṇa* letters *a*, *e*, *o* follow a short *a* not at the end of a *pada*, the following form comes as a single substitute for the places before and after — the following form: it becomes *pibanti*. On this view, by the *vārttika* *pibādeśo nipātanāt* (Pā. Sū. Vā. 6-1-162) read in the sūtra *dhātoḥ*, the *i* of *pi* is udātta, the *a* of *ba* unaccented by the *śeṣānudātta*; the *a* of the *vikaraṇa* *śap* is unaccented by *anudāttau suppitau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) since it is *pit*; the *a* coming by the following form in place of these unaccented *a*'s is unaccented by *sthānivadbhāva*; by the *lasārvadhātuka* accent of *tāsy anudātten…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the *a* of *anti* is unaccented. Again, the following form is unaccented by *sthānivadbhāva*. This unaccented follows the udātta *i*. So by *udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-66) it is svarita: this is the situation on the view of the *a*-final substitute. On the view of the consonant-final substitute *pib*, by *dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-162) the *i* of *pi* is udātta, *śap* unaccented as before, *anti* likewise, the following form likewise, the svarita likewise. On the first view there is no occasion at all for *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86): since *piba* ends in *a*, the *b* is the penultimate; a light vowel is not the penultimate. On the second view, by *aṅgavṛtte punarvṛttāv avidhir niṣṭhitasya* (Paribhā. 90, zoom-checked on p. 214) — once a stem-section rule has come and a form is completed, another stem-section rule does not come — after the substitute *piba* has come, *guṇa* does not come for the penultimate letter; so *guṇa* is warded off; and it must be known that the sixth *adhyāya*'s fourth *pāda* and the whole of the seventh *adhyāya* are the stem section. *Nipātair yadyadihantakuvinnec ceccaṇkaccid yatrayuktam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30): the word *yatra* in *yad* and the rest is a single word ending in a dropped third case; here, if a compound with the word *yukta* is intended, the qualifier *nipātaiḥ* is unconnected. If a compound is accepted, the word ending in *yatra* would be a part of the compound. Then by *padārthaḥ padārthenānveti na tu tadekadeśena*, the meaning of one word —

> अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावविधिर्निष्ठितस्य ।
> पदार्थः पदार्थेनान्वेति न तु तदेकदेशेन ।
>
> *aṅgavṛtte punarvṛttāvavidhirniṣṭhitasya |*
> *padārthaḥ padārthenānveti na tu tadekadeśena |*

### Page 215 — Rik 18: grammar (end)

— is construed only with the meaning of the qualified presented by another word; it is not construed with a part; so for *nipātaiḥ* there is no construction with the word ending in *yatra*, a part of the compound. If such construction is intended, since there is no connection (*sāmarthya*), the compound cannot come. That is why all teachers accept that in *ṛddhasya rājapuruṣaḥ* there is no construction of *ṛddhasya* with *rājñaḥ*, a part of the compound. Thus the meaning of the sūtra results: since by this sūtra there is the prohibition that a *tiṅ*-final word joined with the particles *yat*, *yadi*, *hanta*, *kuvit*, *net*, *cet*, *caṇ*, *kaccit*, *yatra* is not unaccented, the total lack of accent by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) does not come for *pibanti*.

> ऋद्धस्य राजपुरुषः ।
>
> *ṛddhasya rājapuruṣaḥ |*

**कर्त्वम् (kartvam)** — the root *(ḍu)kṛñ karaṇe*. *Kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-14): in the sūtra *tayor eva kṛtyaktakhalarthāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-70) it is said that the *kṛtya* suffixes, the suffix *kta* and the *khalartha* suffixes come only in the two senses of action and object. So action and object are both *kṛtya* senses. The sūtra *kṛtyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-95) is a heading up to the sūtra *ṇvultṛcau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-133). In the science of grammar the suffixes belonging to this heading are called *kṛtya* suffixes. And so the meaning of the sūtra: in the *kṛtya* sense, in the form of action and object, the suffixes *tavai*, *ken*, *kenya*, *tvan* come after a root. By this, when *tvan* comes in the object sense after the root *kṛ*: *kṛ* + *tvan*; by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) — when *sārvadhātuka* and *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes follow, the *ik* end of a stem takes *guṇa* — when the *ārdhadhātuka* *tva* follows, *guṇa* for the *ṛ*; it comes followed by *r*: *kar* + *tvan*; the *n* has the *it*-name and is removed: *kartva*; this is initially udātta by *ñnity ādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197). In the nominative singular it becomes *kartvam*. ॥18॥

> अ॒प्स्व१॒॑न्तर॒मृत॑म॒प्सु भे॑ष॒जम॒पामु॒त प्रश॑स्तये । [accent ?]

### Page 216 — Rik 19: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अप्ऽसु । अन्तः । अमृतं । अप्ऽसु । भेषजं । अपां । उत । प्रऽशस्तये ॥
> देवाः । भवत । वाजिनः ॥१९॥
>
> *ap 'su | antaḥ | amṛtaṃ | ap 'su | bheṣajaṃ | apāṃ | uta | pra 'śastaye ||*
> *devāḥ | bhavata | vājinaḥ ||19||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: पा० ६-२-११६, ६-२-५०.)*

> अप्सु जलेष्वन्तर्मध्येऽमृतं पीयूषं वर्तते । तस्याब्विकारत्वात् । अमृतं वा आप इति श्रुत्यन्तराच्च । तथैवाप्सु भेषजमौषधं वर्तते । क्षुद्रोगनिवर्तकस्यान्नस्याप्कार्यत्वात् । उतापि च तादृशीनामपां देवतानां प्रशस्तये प्रशंसार्थं हे देवा ऋत्विजादयो ब्राह्मणाः । एते वै देवाः प्रत्यक्षं यद्ब्राह्मणा इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । वाजिनो वेगवन्तो भवत । शीघ्रं स्तुतिं कुरुतेत्यर्थः ॥ अप्सु । ऊडिदमित्यादिना सप्तम्या उदात्तत्वं । संहितायामुदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरित इति स्वरितत्वं । अमृतं । नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः । पा० ६-२-११६ । इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । प्रशस्तये । तादौ च निति । पा० ६-२-५० । इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । भवत । आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदिति पूर्वस्यामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वेन पादादित्वान्न निघातः ॥
>
> *apsu jaleṣvantarmadhye 'mṛtaṃ pīyūṣaṃ vartate | tasyābvikāratvāt | amṛtaṃ vā āpa iti śrutyantarācca | tathaivāpsu bheṣajamauṣadhaṃ vartate | kṣudroganivartakasyānnasyāpkāryatvāt | utāpi ca tādṛśīnāmapāṃ devatānāṃ praśastaye praśaṃsārthaṃ he devā ṛtvijādayo brāhmaṇāḥ | ete vai devāḥ pratyakṣaṃ yadbrāhmaṇā iti śrutyantarāt | vājino vegavanto bhavata | śīghraṃ stutiṃ kurutetyarthaḥ || apsu | ūḍidamityādinā saptamyā udāttatvaṃ | saṃhitāyāmudāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarita iti svaritatvaṃ | amṛtaṃ | naño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ | pā0 6-2-116 | ityuttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | praśastaye | tādau ca niti | pā0 6-2-50 | iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | bhavata | āmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavaditi pūrvasyāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvena pādāditvānna nighātaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "*Apsu antaḥ*, within the waters, is *amṛtam*, nectar, because it is a product of water, and from the other *śruti* 'the waters indeed are nectar'. Likewise *apsu*, in the waters, is *bheṣajam*, medicine, since food, which removes the disease of hunger, is a product of water. *Uta*, and, *praśastaye*, for the praise of such waters, the deities, O *devāḥ*, priests and the rest, the brāhmaṇas — from the other *śruti* 'these indeed are the visible gods, the brāhmaṇas' — *bhavata*, be, *vājinaḥ*, swift: that is, make the praise quickly." (Grammatical tail: *apsu*, the locative udātta by *ūḍidam…*; in the Saṃhitā svarita by *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ*; *amṛtam*, the last member's initial udātta by *nañño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ* (Pā. 6-2-116); *praśastaye*, the prefix keeps its own accent by *tādau ca niti…* (Pā. 6-2-50); *bhavata*, since the preceding vocative is treated as not there by *āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat*, it is at the beginning of the *pāda*, so no loss of accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अप्सु अन्तः (apsu antaḥ)** — in the midst of the waters (in water) | **अमृतं (amṛtaṃ)** — there is nectar | **अप्सु (apsu)** — in water | **भेषजं (bheṣajaṃ)** — there is medicine that destroys disease | **उत (uta)** — and | **(हे) देवाः ((he) devāḥ)** — O deities (and people, priests, sacrificers and the rest) | **अपां (apāṃ)** — of the waters | **प्रशस्तये (praśastaye)** — for praise, or to make hymns | **वाजिनः (vājinaḥ)** — swift (ready quickly) | **भवत (bhavata)** — be.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

There is nectar in water; in water there is the power that cures disease, that is, of medicine. Therefore, O deities and people, priests, sacrificers and the rest, be ready quickly to praise those waters.

### Page 217 — Rik 19: English, Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> (There is) ambrosia in the waters, (there is) medicine in the waters; therefore divine priests, be prompt in their praise.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The *śruti* statement of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad describes very well the qualities and pre-eminence of water —

> आपो वा इदꣳ सर्वं विश्वा भूतान्यापः प्राणा वा आपः पशव आपोऽन्नमापोऽमृतमापः सम्राडापो विराडापः स्वराडापश्छन्दाꣳस्यापो ज्योतीꣳष्यापो यजूꣳष्यापः सत्यमापः सर्वा देवता आपो भूर्भुवः सुवराप ओं ॥
>
> *āpo vā idam̐ sarvaṃ viśvā bhūtānyāpaḥ prāṇā vā āpaḥ paśava āpo 'nnamāpo 'mṛtamāpaḥ samrāḍāpo virāḍāpaḥ svarāḍāpaśchandām̐syāpo jyotīm̐ṣyāpo yajūm̐ṣyāpaḥ satyamāpaḥ sarvā devatā āpo bhūrbhuvaḥ suvarāpa oṃ ||*

— that is, everything has arisen from water. All living beings and animals live by water; that is, water itself is the support of all living creatures and plants. Without water no living being can live. So water itself is said to be life. Since plants, trees and the vegetable kingdom grow by water, water is directly and indirectly food for living beings. Without food one can live some days; without water it is impossible to live. In our body most is water; since blood and the rest are in liquid form, water is most necessary for living. So it is no exaggeration to call water nectar. Since water is one of the five elements, since there is the *śruti* statement *āpo vā idam agre salilam āsīt*, and since the *śruti* says that other things were created from water, it is fitting to say that everything is the very form of water, or that water is the root of all things. So the *śruti* proclaims that water is the form of all the deities.

> आपो वा इदमग्रे सलिलमासीत् ।
>
> *āpo vā idamagre salilamāsīt |*

**अमृतं भेषजं (amṛtaṃ bheṣajaṃ)** — since water is most necessary for living beings and is the support of life, it is called nectar. Since nectar is in liquid form, and since all liquid things are indicated by the word *āpaḥ*, 'water', it is right to call water nectar. Many diseases can be cured by water; and since medicines are generally in liquid form mixed with water, it is also fitting to say that medicines are in water. How great the pre-eminence of water is in the matter of curing disease is described specially in medical works such as the Āyurveda.

**देवाः (devāḥ)** — though the deities are addressed here as *devāḥ*, it may be said to mean either people such as priests and sacrificers, or the deities. Or since *śruti* statements such as —

### Page 218 — Rik 19: Special Topics (end), grammar

> एते वै देवाः प्रत्यक्षं यद्ब्राह्मणाः ।
>
> *ete vai devāḥ pratyakṣaṃ yadbrāhmaṇāḥ |*

— say that brāhmaṇa priests are visible deities, the brāhmaṇas have been addressed by the word *deva*.

**वाजिनः (vājinaḥ)** — *vegavantaḥ, śīghragāminaḥ*: quickly, promptly, without delay, and so on. Or, since there is the *śruti* statement *annaṃ vai vājaḥ*, that *vāja* means food, it may be explained as: furnished with food or oblation, that is, praise with offerings of oblation and the like.

> अन्नं वै वाजः ।
>
> *annaṃ vai vājaḥ |*

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**अप्सु (apsu)** — after the word *ap*, the locative plural suffix *su*; for the meaning of *ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) see the previous mantra. By this the case-ending *su* is udātta. In place of this udātta *u*, at the time of the Saṃhitā, when the vowel of the word *antaḥ* follows, by *iko yaṇ aci* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-77) the *yaṇ* *v* comes. And so this *v* is a *yaṇ* that has come in place of an udātta; by *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) — an unaccented after a *yaṇ* that has come in place of an udātta or svarita becomes svarita — the unaccented *a* of the word *antaḥ* becomes svarita.

**अमृतं (amṛtaṃ)** — when a bahuvrīhi compound of *nañ* with the word *mṛta* comes, the *n* is dropped and only *a* remains. By *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the own accent would be due; overriding it, by *nañño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-116) — in a bahuvrīhi compound, the four words *jara*, *mara*, *mitra*, *mṛta* after *nañ* take the initial udātta — the last member *mṛta* gets the initial udātta accent.

**प्रशस्तये (praśastaye)** — the prefix *pra*, the root *śaṃsu stutau*. By *striyāṃ ktin* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-94) the suffix *ktin*; the *n* is dropped by *aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24): *praśasti*; dative singular *praśastaye*. Here by *tādau ca niti kṛty atau* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50) — when a *kṛt* suffix other than *tu*, without the marker *n* and beginning with *t*, follows, the immediately preceding *gati* keeps its own accent — the *gati* *pra* gets its own accent. This is an exception to the *kṛt* accent laid down by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139); *pra* is initially udātta by *upasargāś cābhivarjam* (Phi. Sū. 81). This same accent stays after compounding, in the manner shown before.

**भवत (bhavata)** — before it is the *āmantrita* *devāḥ*; by *āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) — a preceding word ending in a vocative first case is as if not there — the treatment as not there comes. And so *bhavata* does not follow a *pada*. It comes to be at the beginning of the *pāda* —

### Page 219 (upper) — Rik 19: grammar (end)

— too. Since in the rule of the unaccented there is the heading *padāt* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-17), the unaccented comes only for what follows a *pada*. Since it is said *anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-18), the unaccented does not come for what is at the beginning of a *pāda*. So for the word *bhavata* the total lack of accent by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) does not come. ॥19॥

### Page 219 (lower) — Sūkta 23, Rik 20

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अ॒प्सु मे॒ सोमो॑ अब्रवीद॒न्तर्विश्वा॑नि भेष॒जा ।
> अ॒ग्निं च॑ वि॒श्वशं॑भुव॒माप॑श्च वि॒श्वभे॑षजीः ॥२०॥
>
> *apsú me sómo abravīd antár víśvāni bheṣajā́ |*
> *agníṃ ca viśváśaṃbhuvam ā́paś ca viśvábheṣajīḥ ||20||*

*(Bars under अ (अप्सु), मे, द (अब्रवीद्) and ष (भेषजा); strokes over मो and श्वा. Line 2: bars under अ, व (विश्व), व (भुवम्) and व (विश्वभे); strokes over च, शं, प (आपश्) and भे.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अप्ऽसु । मे । सोमः । अब्रवीत् । अन्तः । विश्वानि । भेषजा ॥
> अग्निं । च । विश्वऽशंभुवं । आपः । च । विश्वऽभेषजीः ॥२०॥
>
> *ap 'su | me | somaḥ | abravīt | antaḥ | viśvāni | bheṣajā ||*
> *agniṃ | ca | viśva 'śaṃbhuvaṃ | āpaḥ | ca | viśva 'bheṣajīḥ ||20||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० २-१३, तै० सं० २-६-६-१, पा० ६-२-१०६. The bhāṣya ends with ॥११॥, the close of the eleventh varga.)*

> कारीर्यामुत्तरस्याज्यभागस्याप्सु म इत्येषानुवाक्या । वर्षकामेष्टिरिति खण्डेऽप्स्वग्ने सधिष्टवाप्सु मे सोमो अब्रवीत् । आ० २-१३ । इति सूत्रितं ॥
>
> *kārīryāmuttarasyājyabhāgasyāpsu ma ityeṣānuvākyā | varṣakāmeṣṭiriti khaṇḍe 'psvagne sadhiṣṭavāpsu me somo abravīt | ā0 2-13 | iti sūtritaṃ ||*

**Translation (application):** "At the *kārīrī* [*iṣṭi*], this ṛk *apsu me* is the *anuvākyā* of the second *ājyabhāga*; it is laid down in the section *varṣakāmeṣṭi*: '*apsv agne sadhiṣ ṭava*, *apsu me somo abravīt*' (Āśv. 2-13)."

> अप्सु जलेष्वन्तर्मध्ये विश्वानि भेषजा सर्वाण्यौषधानि सन्तीति मे मह्यं मन्त्रदर्शिने मुनये सोमो देवोऽब्रवीत् । तथा विश्वशंभुवं सर्वस्य जगतः सुखकरमेतन्नामकं चाग्निं चाप्सु वर्तमानं सोमोऽब्रवीत् । तथा च तैत्तिरीया अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायांस इत्यनुवाके सोऽपः प्राविशदित्यग्नेरप्सु प्रवेशमामनन्ति । तै० सं० २-६-६-१ । लतागुल्मवृक्षमूलादीनामौषधानां वृष्टिजन्यत्वेन जलवर्तित्वं प्रसिद्धं । विश्वभेषजीः । विश्वानि भेषजानि यासु तथाविधा अपोऽप्यब्रवीत् ॥ भेषजा । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । विश्वशंभुवं । भवतेरन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्क्विप् । व्यत्ययेन पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । यद्वा । विश्वे सर्वेऽपि व्यापाराः सुखकरा यस्य । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायां । पा० ६-२-१०६ । इति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । आपः । कर्मणि शसि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन जस् । अप्तृन्नित्यादिनोपधादीर्घः । विश्वभेषजीः । विश्वशंभुरितिवत् ॥११॥
>
> *apsu jaleṣvantarmadhye viśvāni bheṣajā sarvāṇyauṣadhāni santīti me mahyaṃ mantradarśine munaye somo devo 'bravīt | tathā viśvaśaṃbhuvaṃ sarvasya jagataḥ sukhakarametannāmakaṃ cāgniṃ cāpsu vartamānaṃ somo 'bravīt | tathā ca taittirīyā agnestrayo jyāyāṃsa ityanuvāke so 'paḥ prāviśadityagnerapsu praveśamāmananti | tai0 saṃ0 2-6-6-1 | latāgulmavṛkṣamūlādīnāmauṣadhānāṃ vṛṣṭijanyatvena jalavartitvaṃ prasiddhaṃ | viśvabheṣajīḥ | viśvāni bheṣajāni yāsu tathāvidhā apo 'pyabravīt || bheṣajā | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | viśvaśaṃbhuvaṃ | bhavaterantarbhāvitaṇyarthātkvip | vyatyayena pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | yadvā | viśve sarve 'pi vyāpārāḥ sukhakarā yasya | bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyāṃ | pā0 6-2-106 | iti pūrvapadāntodāttatvaṃ | āpaḥ | karmaṇi śasi prāpte vyatyayena jas | aptṛnnityādinopadhādīrghaḥ | viśvabheṣajīḥ | viśvaśaṃbhuritivat ||11||*

**Translation:** "*Somaḥ*, the god Soma, *abravīt*, told *me*, me, the seer who saw the mantra, that *apsu antaḥ*, within the waters, are *viśvāni bheṣajā*, all medicines. Likewise Soma told of Agni, *viśvaśambhuvam*, the bringer of happiness to the whole world, so named, who is in the waters. And so the Taittirīyas record in the *anuvāka* *agnes trayo jyāyāṃsaḥ* Agni's entry into the waters: 'he entered the waters' (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6-1). That medicines such as creepers, bushes, the roots of trees and the like are in water, as they are produced by rain, is well known. *Viśvabheṣajīḥ*: he told also of the waters, such that all medicines are in them." (Grammatical tail: *bheṣajā*, the *ā* by *supāṃ suluk*; *viśvaśambhuvam*, *kvip* after *bhū* with the causative sense included; the first member's own accent by *vyatyaya*; or: 'whose all activities make happiness': in the bahuvrīhi the first member is final udātta by *bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām* (Pā. 6-2-106); *āpaḥ*, *śas* being due in the object sense, *jas* by *vyatyaya*; the lengthening of the penultimate by *aptṛn…*; *viśvabheṣajīḥ*, as for *viśvaśambhuḥ*.)

### Page 220 — Rik 20: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अप्सु अन्तः (apsu antaḥ)** — in the midst of the waters | **विश्वानि (viśvāni)** — all | **भेषजा (bheṣajā)** — medicines that destroy disease, that there are | **अग्निं च (agniṃ ca)** — Agni | **विश्वशंभुवं (viśvaśambhuvaṃ)** — as the one who makes happiness for the whole world | **आपः (āpaḥ)** — the waters | **विश्वभेषजीः (viśvabheṣajīḥ)** — as furnished with all medicines that destroy disease | **सोमः (somaḥ)** — the deity Soma | **मे (me)** — to me | **अब्रवीत् (abravīt)** — told.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

In the midst of the waters are all the medicines that remove diseases. Agni makes happiness for the whole world; the waters are joined with all medicines. So the deity Soma told me.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Soma has revealed to me that in the waters are all medicaments; that Agni is the benefactor of the Universe, the waters contain all the healing medicines.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

In the *kārīrī* sacrifice this ṛk *apsu me* is recited as the *puronuvākyā* mantra when making the *ājyabhāga* offering. On this matter, in the section *varṣakāmeṣṭi* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, it is said that the ṛks *apsv agne sadhiṣ ṭava* (8-43-9) and *apsu me somo abravīt* (1-23-20) are to be used as the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* mantras (Ā. 2-13). The main intention of this ṛk: Soma himself told me that Agni, who makes happiness for the whole world, is in the waters in the form of lightning, and that all the herbs that cure the diseases of living beings are in the waters themselves. On the point that Agni is in the waters, the commentator has cited the sentence *so 'paḥ prāviśat taṃ devatāḥ praiṣam aicchan* from the *anuvāka* *agnes trayo jyāyāṃso bhrātara āsan* in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6-1). We have explained before ( [blank in the print] ) its explanation and the explanation on this subject in the Ṛgveda.

> सोऽपः प्राविशत्तं देवताः प्रैषमैच्छन् ।
>
> *so 'paḥ prāviśattaṃ devatāḥ praiṣamaicchan |*

**अग्निं च विश्वशंभुवं (agniṃ ca viśvaśambhuvaṃ)** — there is no need to explain at length the benefit that comes to the whole world from Agni. Besides giving us warmth when it is cold, we use Agni for cooking food and in many other useful or most necessary works.

### Page 221 — Rik 20: Special Topics (end), grammar

Since this matter is known by everyone's experience, there is no need to say more.

**आपश्च विश्वभेषजीः (āpaś ca viśvabheṣajīḥ)** — we have explained in the previous ṛk itself what the part of water is in curing diseases.

**सोमः (somaḥ)** — for the word *soma* the commentator has said *somadevaḥ*, the deity Soma. Soma here is to be known as the Moon, the presiding deity of plants and trees.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**भेषजा (bheṣajā)** — by *supāṃ suluk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute *ā* for the nominative plural *jas*.

**विश्वशंभुवम् (viśvaśambhuvam)** — *viśvasya śaṃ bhavatīti* (*bhāvayatīti*) *viśvaśambhūḥ, tam*: so the analysis. Here after the root *bhū* with the causative sense included, by *kvip ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) *kvip*; the *sup*, a part of a nominal stem, is dropped (*luk*): *viśvaśambhū*; after it the accusative singular *am*; by *na bhūsudhiyoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-85) the *yaṇ* is barred; by *aci śnudhātu…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-77) the substitute *uvaṅ*: it becomes *viśvaśambhuvam*. Here, though by *samāsasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223) the final udātta (which is *satiśiṣṭa*) would be right, by *vyatyaya* [it is said that] the first member *viśva* gets the final udātta. By *śeṣanighāta* the other letters are unaccented. Among them the unaccented *ś* syllable becomes svarita by *udāttād anudāttasya…* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-66). The other two letters, by *svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām* (Pā. Sū. 1-2-39), are in the monotone (*pracaya*): this is the situation. Here the word *viśva* is formed by the suffix *kvan* by *aśūpruṣilaṭi…* (U. Sū. 1-149). So at (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-9-1) it has been described as initially udātta by *ñnity ādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197). So if the first member's own accent is said here by *vyatyaya*, the initial udātta would have to come; then the form *viśvaśambhuvam* [with that accent] would not result: it must be *viśvaśambhuvam* [with final udātta on *viśva*]. So in the Veda commentary *vyatyayena pūrvapadāntodāttatvam* is the right reading. Yet through the carelessness of the proof-readers and others it may have dropped to *vyatyayena pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam*. However this may be, in describing the meaning there is no description by the commentator of a meaning that fits this derivation. So it is clear that the commentator was not pleased with this derivation. That is why he begins with *yadvā* and gives another derivation: *viśve* — all activities; *śambhuvaḥ* — that make happiness; *yasya* — whose; *saḥ* — he is *viśvaśambhūḥ*, *tam*: a bahuvrīhi compound. On this view the compound-final udātta —

> व्यत्ययेन पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् ।
> व्यत्ययेन पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ।
>
> *vyatyayena pūrvapadāntodāttatvam |*
> *vyatyayena pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam |*

### Page 222 — Rik 20: grammar (end)

— overriding it, by *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member's own accent would be due. But in *bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-106), *pūrvapadam* from *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) is carried on. It must be changed into the genitive case to suit the meaning of the present sentence; *antaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-92) is the heading. So it becomes *pūrvapadasya antaḥ*; by *ādir udāttaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-64) *udāttaḥ* is carried on. *Saṃjñāyām* is a qualifier of the whole; and so, when a name is shown by the whole, the end of the word *viśva*, the first member of a bahuvrīhi compound, is udātta: so *viśva* is final udātta. On this view there is no trouble of having to establish the accent by *vyatyaya*.

**आपः (āpaḥ)** — this is the object word with regard to the root *abravīt*. So when the object sense is intended, by the teaching *karmaṇi dvitīyā* (Pā. Sū. 2-3-2) the second case; and since the word *ap* always ends in the plural, when the plurality of the object sense is intended, by *bahuṣu bahuvacanam* (Pā. Sū. 1-4-21) it would be right for the accusative plural *śas* to come. Yet by *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85), by interchange, the nominative plural case-ending *jas* has come here: *ap* + *as*. Now since the suffix *as*, named *sarvanāmasthāna*, follows, by *aptṛntṛc…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-11) — when a *sarvanāmasthāna* other than the vocative follows, the penultimate letter of the word *ap* and of words ending in the suffixes *tṛn* and the rest is lengthened — lengthening: *āpas*; for the *s*, *ru* and *visarga*.

**विश्वभेषजीः (viśvabheṣajīḥ)** — *viśvāni bheṣajāni yāsu tāḥ*: so the analysis; here, overriding the first member's own accent caused by the bahuvrīhi, the first member gets the final udātta in the manner stated at *viśvaśambhuvam*. By *bhiyaḥ ṣug ghrasvaś ca* (U. Sū. 1-135 as printed at zoom: ∩, ∩, ಇ, lobed 5; the last digit is not clear between 5 and 4) — after the root *ñibhī bhaye*, the suffix *aj* and the augment *ṣuk* for the root — when the suffix *aj*, shortening of the root and the augment *ṣuk* come after the root *bhī*, it becomes *bhiṣaj*. *Bhiṣajaḥ imāḥ*: so the analysis. By *tasyedam* (Pā. Sū. 4-3-120) the suffix *aṇ*: *bhiṣaj* + *a*; now since the suffix is *ṇit*, by *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-117) *vṛddhi* in *bhi* would give *bhai*; yet by set form *e* comes for the *ī* of *bhi*. When the feminine is intended, *ṅīṣ* comes and it becomes *bheṣajī*. The *ī* of *ṅīṣ* is udātta by the suffix accent.

### Page 224 — Rik 21: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O waters (or O deities presiding over the waters), so that my body may be without disease, make the excellent medicine full (make it ready); then, free from disease, may I see the sun for a long time, that is, may I live long.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Waters, grant me a medicament that shall be an armour to my body that I may long behold the Sun.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**पृणीत (pṛṇīta)** — *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ ||* make full: the intention is, make the body without diseases and the like, and able to do its work in order.

**वरूथं (varūthaṃ)** — *varaṇīyam, roganivārakam ||* to be desired, that is, warding off disease.

**ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे (jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe)** — seeing the sun for a long time, that is, living long. There are some ṛks in the Ṛgveda that suggest this same intention —

> तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्ज्योक्पश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरन्तं । (ऋ० सं० ४-२५-४)
> तव क्रत्वा तवोतिभिर्ज्योक्पश्येम सूर्यं ॥ (ऋ० सं० ९-४-६)
> शं नः क्षेत्रमुरु ज्योतींषि सोम ज्योङ्नः सूर्यं दृशये रिरीहि ॥ (ऋ० सं० ९-९१-६)
> उद्यन्तं त्वा मित्रमहो दिवेदिवे ज्योग्जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्य ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-३७-७)
> ज्योक्पश्येम सूर्यमुच्चरन्तमनुमते मृळया नः स्वस्ति ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-५९-६)
>
> *tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarma yaṃsajjyokpaśyātsūryamuccarantaṃ | (ṛ0 saṃ0 4-25-4)*
> *tava kratvā tavotibhirjyokpaśyema sūryaṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 9-4-6)*
> *śaṃ naḥ kṣetramuru jyotīṃṣi soma jyoṅnaḥ sūryaṃ dṛśaye rirīhi || (ṛ0 saṃ0 9-91-6)*
> *udyantaṃ tvā mitramaho divedive jyogjīvāḥ prati paśyema sūrya || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-37-7)*
> *jyokpaśyema sūryamuccarantamanumate mṛḷayā naḥ svasti || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-59-6)*

*(Glosses of these quotations are not given in the source.)* Besides these, in the Yajurveda too there are many sentences suggesting this intention, such as —

> पश्येम शरदः शतं … ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे ।
> ज्योक् च पश्यामि सूर्यं ।
>
> *paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ … jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe |*
> *jyok ca paśyāmi sūryaṃ |*

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**पृणीत (pṛṇīta)** — the root *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*. *Loṭ*, second person plural, the suffix *tha*: *pṝ* + *tha*. By *loṭo laṅvat* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) [the extension] —

### Page 225 — Rik 21: grammar (continued)

— the operations of *laṅ* come to *loṭ*: so the treatment as *laṅ*. By *tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) — for the four suffixes *tas*, *thas*, *tha*, *mip* the substitutes *tām*, *tam*, *ta*, *am* come in order — the substitute *ta* for *tha*: *pṝ* + *ta*. By *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-81) — when a *sārvadhātuka* suffix in the agent sense follows, the *vikaraṇa* suffix *śnā* (*nā*) comes after a root of the *kryādi* class — so when *śnā* comes: *pṝ* + *nā* + *ta*. By *pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-80) — the roots read in the list of roots beginning with *pūñ pavane* are shortened — the *ṝ* of *pṝ* is shortened to *ṛ*: *pṛ* + *nā* + *ta*. By *ī halyaghoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-113) — when a consonant-initial *sārvadhātuka* that is *kit* or *ṅit* follows, the *ā* of the suffix *śnā* and the *ā* of a reduplicated stem take the substitute *ī* — when the substitute *ī* comes: *pṛ* + *nī* + *ta*. *Ṛvarṇāc ceti vaktavyam*: this is a paraphrase of the meaning of *raṣābhyāṃ ṇatve ṛkāragrahaṇam* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-1, *vārttika* 1). Its meaning is that *ṇ* is substituted for the *n* after *ṛ*. By this the *n* gets the substitute *ṇ*, and it becomes *pṛṇīta*.

**आपः (āpaḥ)** — this ends in the vocative first case. So by *sāmantritam* (Pā. Sū. 2-3-48) — what ends in the vocative first case gets the name *āmantrita* — it has the name *āmantrita*. So by *āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) — the preceding *āmantrita* is *avidyamānavat*, that is, as if not there though it is there — the treatment as not there comes. So *pṛṇīta* does not follow a *pada*; it is at the beginning of the *pāda*. So since there is no word not ending in *tiṅ* before the word ending in *tiṅ*, the total lack of accent by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ* does not come. *Satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ*: in the matter of *vikaraṇas*, though it is *satiśiṣṭa*, that is, comes last, that accent is not stronger: so they say with *anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ*. The *ta*, the *tiṅ* suffix, gets the initial udātta by the suffix accent. The others are unaccented by the *śeṣānudātta* accent.

**वरूथम् (varūtham)** — the root *vṛñ varaṇe*. By *jṝvṛñbhyām ūthan* (U. Sū. 2-163, zoom-checked) — after the roots *jṝ vayohānau* of the *kryādi* class, *jṝṣ vayohānau* of the *divādi* class, and *vṛñ varaṇe*, the suffix *ūthan* comes — when *ūthan* comes: *vṛ* + *ūtha*. The *ṛ* takes *guṇa*; it becomes *ar*: it becomes *varūtha*. The suffix is *nit*; so by the *nit* accent initial udātta comes.

**तन्वे (tanve)** — the root *tanu vistāre*. By *bhṛmṛśītṛcaritsaritanidhanimimasjibhya uḥ* (U. Sū. 1-7, zoom-checked: the flat-footed 7) — after the roots *bhṛñ bharaṇe*, *mṛṅ prāṇatyāge*, *śīṅ svapne*, *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*, *cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ*, *tsara chadmagatau*, *tanu vistāre*, *dhana dhānye*, *ḍumiñ prakṣepaṇe*, *ṭumasjo śuddhau*, the suffix *u* comes — so after the root *tan* the suffix *u*: *tan* + *u* = *tanu*, final udātta by the suffix accent. After it the dative case-ending *ṅe*: *tanu* + *e*. *Ṅiti hrasvaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 1-4-6):

### Page 226 — Rik 21: grammar (end)

here, since there is the word *ca*, two sentences result. *Yū stryākhyau nadī* is carried on: *īś ca ūś ca = yū*. Since it is a sūtra, though there is an *ic* vowel after the long vowel, the prohibition of the long like vowel by *dīrghāj jasi ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-105) does not come. *Striyam evācakṣāte iti stryākhyau*: those that convey only the feminine, that is, always feminine: this is the meaning. *Neyaṅuvaṅsthānāv astrī* (Pā. Sū. 1-4-4): the whole sūtra except *na* is carried on: *iyaṅuvaṅoḥ sthānaṃ = sthitiḥ yayoḥ tau*: the meaning is, fit to get the substitutes *iyaṅ*, *uvaṅ*. By *vāmi* (Pā. Sū. 1-4-5) *vā* comes; and so when a suffix with the *it*-name *ṅ* follows, words ending in *ī* and *ū*, always feminine, fit to get the substitutes *iyaṅ*, *uvaṅ*, other than the word *strī*, optionally get the name *nadī*: this is the meaning of the first sentence *ṅiti*. *Hrasvaś ca* is the second sentence. Here the words *yū stryākhyau nadī vā ṅiti* are carried on. And so, when a suffix with the *it*-name *ṅ* follows, words ending in short *i* or short *u* optionally get the name *nadī*: this is its meaning. The meaning of the first sentence does not apply here. Though the meaning of the second sentence applies, since it says 'optionally' there, here the word *tanu* does not have the name *nadī*. So by *āṇ nadyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-112) the augment *āṭ* does not come; by the *yaṇ* substitute, when *v* comes for the *u*, it becomes *tanve*. Here, since *e* is a *sup*, by *anudāttau suppitau* the unaccented would be due. Overriding it, by *udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-174) — *y*, *v*, *l* that have come in place of an udātta letter and are after a consonant: the *nadī*-named letters and the case-endings *śas* and the rest coming after such *y*, *v*, *l* are also udātta — the udātta would be due for the *e* after the *v*. Yet since it is said *vyatyayo bahulam*, here, contrary to this, by *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) — the unaccented after a *yaṇ* that has come in place of an udātta or svarita becomes svarita — the unaccented *e* becomes svarita. To make this svarita known, the numeral ३ is indicated after it.

**दृशे (dṛśe)** — the root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*. *Dṛśe vikhye ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-11): the meaning is that in the sense of the suffix *tumun*, that is, in the action sense, the two forms *dṛśe* and *vikhye* are given as set forms. Here, after the root *dṛś* and after the root *khyā* preceded by the prefix *vi*, the suffix *ke* is given as a set form in the sense of the suffix *tumun*. *Dṛś* + *e*: the suffix is *kit*, so *dṛś* does not take *guṇa* of the light penultimate. In *vikhyā* + *e*, since the suffix is *kit*, by *āto lopa iṭi ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-64) the *ā* is dropped. ॥21॥

### Page 227 — Sūkta 23, Rik 22

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इ॒दमा॑पः॒ प्र व॑हत॒ यत्किं च॑ दुरि॒तं मयि॑ ।
> यद्वा॒हम॑भिदु॒द्रोह॒ यद्वा॑ शे॒प उ॒तानृ॑तं ॥२२॥
>
> *idám āpaḥ prá vahata yát kíṃ ca duritáṃ máyi |*
> *yad vāhám abhidudróha yád vā śepá utā́nṛtaṃ ||22||*

*(Bars under इ, पः, त (वहत) and रि; strokes over मा, व (वहत), च and यि. Line 2: bars under द्वा, दु and शे; strokes over म (अहम्), द्वा (the second यद्वा) and नृ; a bar under उ (उत).)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इदं । आपः । प्र । वहत । यत् । किं । च । दुःऽइतं । मयि ॥
> यत् । वा । अहं । अभिऽदुद्रोह । यत् । वा । शेपे । उत । अनृतं ॥२२॥
>
> *idaṃ | āpaḥ | pra | vahata | yat | kiṃ | ca | duḥ 'itaṃ | mayi ||*
> *yat | vā | ahaṃ | abhi 'dudroha | yat | vā | śepe | uta | anṛtaṃ ||22||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० ३-५, ६-१३, पा० ६-४-१२०.)*

> पशौ मार्जन इदमापः प्र वहतेत्येषा विनियुक्ता । हुतायां वपायामिति खण्डे सूत्रितं । इदमापः प्रवहत । आ० ३-५ । इति ॥ एषैवावभृथेष्टौ स्नाने विनियुक्ता । पत्नीसंयाजैश्चरित्वेति खण्ड इदमापः प्र वहत सुमित्र्या न आप ओषधयः सन्तु । आ० ६-१३ । इति सूत्रितं ॥
>
> *paśau mārjana idamāpaḥ pra vahatetyeṣā viniyuktā | hutāyāṃ vapāyāmiti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | idamāpaḥ pravahata | ā0 3-5 | iti || eṣaivāvabhṛtheṣṭau snāne viniyuktā | patnīsaṃyājaiścaritveti khaṇḍa idamāpaḥ pra vahata sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu | ā0 6-13 | iti sūtritaṃ ||*

**Translation (application):** "At the animal sacrifice, at the cleansing, this ṛk *idam āpaḥ pra vahata* is used; it is laid down in the section *hutāyāṃ vapāyām*: '*idam āpaḥ pra vahata*' (Āśv. 3-5). This same ṛk is used at the bath in the *avabhṛtha-iṣṭi*; it is laid down in the section *patnīsaṃyājaiś caritvā*: '*idam āpaḥ pra vahata*, *sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu*' (Āśv. 6-13)."

> मयि यजमाने यत्किं च दुरितमज्ञानान्निष्पन्नं । वाथवाहं यजमानोऽभिदुद्रोह सर्वतो बुद्धिपूर्वकं द्रोहं कृतवानस्मि वाथवा शेपे साधुजनं शप्तवानस्मीति यदस्ति । उतापि चानृतमुक्तवानिति यदस्ति । तदिदं सर्वमपराधजातं प्र वहत । मत्तोऽपनीय प्रवाहेणान्यतो नयत ॥ मयि । मपर्यन्तस्य त्वमावेकवचन इति मादेशे कृतेऽतो गुण इति पररूपे च सति योऽचीति दकारस्य यकारादेशः । एकादेशस्वरेण मकारात्परस्याकारस्योदात्तत्वं । दुद्रोह । द्रुह जिघांसायां । णलि गुणे द्विर्वचनह्रस्वहलादिशेषाः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः । शेपे । शप आक्रोशे । लिटि व्यत्ययेन तङ् । उत्तमैकवचनमिट् । टेरेत्वं । अत एकहल्मध्ये । पा० ६-४-१२० । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वं । पूर्ववन्निघाताभावः ॥
>
> *mayi yajamāne yatkiṃ ca duritamajñānānniṣpannaṃ | vāthavāhaṃ yajamāno 'bhidudroha sarvato buddhipūrvakaṃ drohaṃ kṛtavānasmi vāthavā śepe sādhujanaṃ śaptavānasmīti yadasti | utāpi cānṛtamuktavāniti yadasti | tadidaṃ sarvamaparādhajātaṃ pra vahata | matto 'panīya pravāheṇānyato nayata || mayi | maparyantasya tvamāvekavacana iti mādeśe kṛte 'to guṇa iti pararūpe ca sati yo 'cīti dakārasya yakārādeśaḥ | ekādeśasvareṇa makārātparasyākārasyodāttatvaṃ | dudroha | druha jighāṃsāyāṃ | ṇali guṇe dvirvacanahrasvahalādiśeṣāḥ | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvaṃ | yadvṛttayogānnighātābhāvaḥ | śepe | śapa ākrośe | liṭi vyatyayena taṅ | uttamaikavacanamiṭ | ṭeretvaṃ | ata ekahalmadhye | pā0 6-4-120 | ityetvābhyāsalopau | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvaṃ | pūrvavannighātābhāvaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "Whatever *duritam*, sin arising from ignorance, there is *mayi*, in me, the sacrificer; or, *yad vā*, what there is of my, the sacrificer's, having *abhidudroha*, done hurt knowingly on all sides; or of my having *śepe*, cursed, good people; *uta*, and also of my having spoken *anṛtam*, falsehood — *idam*, all this mass of offences, *pra vahata*, carry away: taking it from me, lead it elsewhere by your current." (Grammatical tail: *mayi*, after the substitute *ma* by *tvamāv ekavacane* for the part up to *m*, and the following form by *ato guṇe*, *y* for the *d* by *yo 'ci*; the *a* after *m* udātta by the single-substitute accent; *dudroha*, *druha jighāṃsāyām*, with *ṇal*, *guṇa*, reduplication, shortening and *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; the syllable before the suffix udātta by *liti*; no loss of accent because of connection with *yad*; *śepe*, *śapa ākrośe*, in *liṭ* the middle endings by *vyatyaya*, first person singular *iṭ*, *e* for the *ṭi*, the *e* and the dropping of the reduplicate by *ata ekahalmadhye…* (Pā. 6-4-120); final udātta by the suffix accent; no loss of accent as before.)

### Page 228 — Rik 22: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**मयि (mayi)** — in me, the sacrificer | **यत्किं च (yat kiṃ ca)** — whatever | **दुरितं (duritaṃ)** — sins done through ignorance there are | **वा (vā)** — or | **अहं (ahaṃ)** — I | **यत् अभिदुद्रोह (yat abhidudroha)** — though I have done hurt (to anyone) knowingly | **वा (vā)** — or | **यत् शेपे (yat śepe)** — though I have spoken evil words about someone | **उत (uta)** — and | **अनृतं (anṛtaṃ)** — though (I have spoken) a lie | **इदं (idaṃ)** — such sin | **आपः (āpaḥ)** — the waters | **प्र वहत (pra vahata)** — (separating it from me) may they carry it away in the form of a current.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

May the waters (the flowing water) carry away in their current all such sins: the sins that may be in me, done through ignorance; or if I have done hurt to anyone; or if I have spoken evil words; and if I have told lies.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Waters, whatever sin there is in me, whatever ill-will I may have borne to others, whatever imprecations I may have uttered, and whatever falschood [sic] I may have told, wash it away all from me.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

In the animal sacrifice this ṛk *idam āpaḥ pra vahata* is recited for the cleansing (sprinkling). In the section *hutāyāṃ vapāyām* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra it is said that the ṛk *idam āpaḥ pra vahata* is to be recited as the cleansing mantra (Ā. 3-5). Besides this, in the *avabhṛtha-iṣṭi* performed at the end of the sacrifice, this mantra is used at the time of bathing. This matter is stated in the section *patnīsaṃyājaiś caritvā*, that the mantras *idam āpaḥ pra vahata* and *sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu* are to be recited (Ā. 6-13).

**दुरितं (duritaṃ)** — *ajñānān niṣpannaṃ kāyikaṃ pāpam ||* the sin in the form of acts done through ignorance or knowingly, that is, sins done by the use of force, such as beating someone: this is the meaning.

**अभिदुद्रोह (abhidudroha)** — thinking evil with the mind is called *droha*. This is a sin of the mind.

**शेपे, अनृतं (śepe, anṛtaṃ)** — cursing, telling lies and the like are sins done by speech. These are of speech. The prayer is that the flowing water may carry away these three kinds of sins.

### Page 229 (upper) — Rik 22: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**मयि (mayi)** — the word *yuṣmad* [as printed; for *asmad*], locative singular; for the part up to *m*, by *tvamāv ekavacane* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-97) the substitute *ma*: *ma* + *ad* + *i*; by *ato guṇe* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) the following form: *mad* + *i*; by *yo 'ci* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-89) — when a vowel-initial case-ending without a substitute follows, the *d* of the words *yuṣmad*, *asmad* takes *y* — so when *y* comes it becomes *tvayi* [as printed; *mayi*].

**दुद्रोह (dudroha)** — the root *druha jighāṃsāyām*. *Liṭ*, *parasmaipada*, third person singular *ti*; by *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇal…* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-82) *ṇal*: *druh* + *a*. By *liṭi dhātoḥ…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-8) reduplication. By *hrasvaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-59) shortening: though it is already short here, since it is said *parjanyaval lakṣaṇaṃ pravartate* (Paribhā. 120), the shortening comes. By *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-60) the *r* and *h* of the first *druh* are dropped: *dudruh* + *a*, *guṇa* of the light penultimate. *Yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66): a word ending in *tiṅ* after a word in which there is the word *yad* is not unaccented. Here, by the further mention of *pūjita* in *pūjanāt pūjitam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-67), it is made known that *atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryam iṣyate*. So even though there is an intervention, the prohibition of the unaccented comes by this. In the same way in *śepe* too the unaccented is barred.

> पर्जन्यवल्लक्षणं प्रवर्तते ।
> अत्र प्रकरणे पञ्चमीनिर्देशेऽपि नानन्तर्यमिष्यते ।
>
> *parjanyavallakṣaṇaṃ pravartate |*
> *atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryamiṣyate |*

**शेपे (śepe)** — the root *śapa ākrośe*; *liṭ*: though this is a *parasmaipada* root, the middle-voice suffix comes by *vyatyaya*. First person singular, *iṭ*: *śap* + *i*. By *ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-79) *e* for the *i*; reduplication; by *ata ekahalmadhye 'nādeśāder liṭi* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-120) — when a *liṭ* that is *kit* follows, a short *a* standing between single consonants and belonging to a stem whose initial is not a substitute takes *e*, and the reduplicate is dropped — when the *e* and the dropping of the reduplicate come, it becomes *śepe*. ॥22॥

### Page 230 — Rik 23: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आपः । अद्य । अनु । अचारिषं । रसेन । सं । अगस्महि ॥
> पयस्वान् । अग्ने । आ । गहि । तं । मा । सं । सृज । वर्चसा ॥२३॥
>
> *āpaḥ | adya | anu | acāriṣaṃ | rasena | saṃ | agasmahi ||*
> *payasvān | agne | ā | gahi | taṃ | mā | saṃ | sṛja | varcasā ||23||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: आ० ३-६, पा० ७-२-३५, ७-२-४, ७-२-२, १-३-२९, १-२-१३.)*

> पशावाहवनीयोपस्थान आपो अद्यान्वचारिषमित्येषा । मनोतायै संप्रेषित इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । एत्योपतिष्ठन्त आपो अद्यान्वचारिषं । आ० ३-६ । इति ॥
>
> *paśāvāhavanīyopasthāna āpo adyānvacāriṣamityeṣā | manotāyai saṃpreṣita iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | etyopatiṣṭhanta āpo adyānvacāriṣaṃ | ā0 3-6 | iti ||*

**Translation (application):** "At the animal sacrifice, at the attendance on the *āhavanīya*, this ṛk *āpo adyānv acāriṣam*; it is laid down in the section *manotāyai saṃpreṣite*: 'having come, they attend with *āpo adyānv acāriṣam*' (Āśv. 3-6)."

> अद्यास्मिन्दिनेऽवभृथार्थमापोऽन्वचारिषं । जलान्यनुप्रविष्टोऽस्मि । प्रविश्य च रसेन जलसारेण समगस्महि । संगताः स्मः । हे अग्ने पयस्वान् जले वर्तमानत्वेन पयोयुक्तस्त्वमा गहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । तं मा तादृशं स्नातं मां वर्चसा तेजसा सं सृज । संयोजय ॥ आपः । कर्मणि शसि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन जस् । अचारिषं । चर गत्यर्थः । लुङि च्लेः सिच् । आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः । पा० ७-२-३५ । इतीट् । नेटि । पा० ७-२-४ । इति वृद्धिप्रतिषेधेऽप्राप्ते तदपवादतयातो ल्रान्तस्य । पा० ७-२-२ । इत्युपधाया वृद्धिः । अगस्महि । समो गम्यृच्छिभ्यामित्यात्मनेपदं । पा० १-३-२९ । च्लेः सिच् । मन्त्रे घसेत्यादिना च्लेर्लुगभावश्छान्दसः । एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तादितीट्प्रतिषेधः । वा गमः । पा० १-२-१३ । इति सिचः कित्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । गहि । लोटि गमेः सिपो हिः । अपित्त्वेन ङित्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । अतो हेरिति लुग्न भवति । असिद्धवदत्राभादिति मलोपस्यासिद्धत्वात् ॥
>
> *adyāsmindine 'vabhṛthārthamāpo 'nvacāriṣaṃ | jalānyanupraviṣṭo 'smi | praviśya ca rasena jalasāreṇa samagasmahi | saṃgatāḥ smaḥ | he agne payasvān jale vartamānatvena payoyuktastvamā gahi | asminkarmaṇyāgaccha | taṃ mā tādṛśaṃ snātaṃ māṃ varcasā tejasā saṃ sṛja | saṃyojaya || āpaḥ | karmaṇi śasi prāpte vyatyayena jas | acāriṣaṃ | cara gatyarthaḥ | luṅi cleḥ sic | ārdhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ | pā0 7-2-35 | itīṭ | neṭi | pā0 7-2-4 | iti vṛddhipratiṣedhe 'prāpte tadapavādatayāto lrāntasya | pā0 7-2-2 | ityupadhāyā vṛddhiḥ | agasmahi | samo gamyṛcchibhyāmityātmanepadaṃ | pā0 1-3-29 | cleḥ sic | mantre ghasetyādinā clerlugabhāvaśchāndasaḥ | ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāditīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | vā gamaḥ | pā0 1-2-13 | iti sicaḥ kittvādanudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | gahi | loṭi gameḥ sipo hiḥ | apittvena ṅittvādanudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | ato heriti lugna bhavati | asiddhavadatrābhāditi malopasyāsiddhatvāt ||*

**Translation:** "*Adya*, on this day, for the *avabhṛtha*, I *anv acāriṣam*, have entered after, the *āpaḥ*, waters. And having entered, *rasena*, with the essence of the waters, we *sam agasmahi*, have come together. O Agni, *payasvān*, furnished with water as being in the waters, *ā gahi*, come, to this rite. *Tam mā*, me, such a one, bathed, *saṃ sṛja*, join, *varcasā*, with splendour." (Grammatical tail: *āpaḥ*, *śas* being due in the object sense, *jas* by *vyatyaya*; *acāriṣam*, *cara* in the sense of going, *sic* for *cli* in *luṅ*, *iṭ* by *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* (Pā. 7-2-35); since the bar on *vṛddhi* by *neṭi* (Pā. 7-2-4) does not apply, as its exception *ato lrāntasya* (Pā. 7-2-2) gives *vṛddhi* of the penultimate; *agasmahi*, middle voice by *samo gamyṛcchibhyām* (Pā. 1-3-29); *sic* for *cli*; the absence of *luk* of *cli* by *mantre ghasa…* is Vedic; *iṭ* barred by *ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt*; *sic* is *kit* by *vā gamaḥ* (Pā. 1-2-13), so the nasal is dropped by *anudāttopadeśa…*; *gahi*, *hi* for *sip* of *gam* in *loṭ*; being *ṅit* as not *pit*, the nasal dropped by *anudāttopadeśa…*; *hi* is not dropped by *ato heḥ*, since the dropping of *m* is *asiddha* by *asiddhavad atrābhāt*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अद्य (adya)** — now (on this day) | **आपः (āpaḥ)** — the water | **अन्वचारिषं (anvacāriṣaṃ)** — I have entered (for the *avabhṛtha* bath) | (then) **रसेन (rasena)** — with the essence of water | **समगस्महि (samagasmahi)** — we have come together | **(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne)** — O Agni | **पयस्वान् (payasvān)** — you, joined with water, that is, being in the water | **आ गहि (ā gahi)** — come (into this bathing rite) | (and) **तं मा (taṃ mā)** — me (who have bathed) | **वर्चसा (varcasā)** — with splendour | **संसृज (saṃsṛja)** — join.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Now I have entered the water for the (*avabhṛtha*) bath. May all the essence that is in the water join with us. O Agni, since you are in the water, come to this bathing rite and make me, who have bathed, splendid.

### Page 231 — Rik 23: English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> I have this day entered into the waters; we have mingled with their essence; O Agni, existing in the waters, approach and fill me with vigour.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

In the animal sacrifice, at the time of attending on the *āhavanīya* fire, they recite the ṛk *āpo adyānv acāriṣam*. This matter is stated in the section *manotāyai saṃpreṣite* of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the sūtra *etyopatiṣṭhanta āpo adyānv acāriṣam* (Ā. 3-6).

**आपः (āpaḥ)** — Skandasvāmin too says *dvitīyārthe prathamā*: the word *āpaḥ*, in the first case, is to be given the meaning of the second case.

**रसेन (rasena)** — *jalasāreṇa*: with the essence of water, "essence of water". The intention is: may pure water remove the faults (the dirt) inside and outside my body.

**पयस्वान् (payasvān)** — *payasā jalena yuktaḥ*, or *payasi tiṣṭhatīti payasvān*: he who is in the water. In the Yajurveda, sentences such as *so 'paḥ prāviśat* say that Agni hid himself in the water. So it is said on many occasions that Agni is in the water. The second half of this ṛk has Agni as its deity.

> सोऽपः प्राविशत् ।
>
> *so 'paḥ prāviśat |*

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**आपः (āpaḥ)** — in the object sense it would be right for *śas* to come and form *apaḥ*. But here by *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85) the case-ending *jas* comes instead of *śas* in the object sense.

**अचारिषम् (acāriṣam)** — the root *cara gatau*; by *luṅ*, *cleḥ sic*, *sic*; *mip* with the substitute *am*, the augment *aṭ*: *a* + *car* + *s* + *am*. By *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35) an *ārdhadhātuka* beginning with a consonant other than *y* takes the augment *iṭ*. When *iṭ* comes: *acar* + *is* + *am*. *Vṛddhi* would be due by *sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-1); then by *neṭi* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-4), when a *sic* beginning with *iṭ* follows, *vṛddhi* does not come: so the bar on *vṛddhi* would be due. But by its exception *ato lrāntasya* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-2) — when a *sic* in the *parasmaipada* follows, the short *a* of a stem ending in *r* or *l* that follows the short *a* takes *vṛddhi* — the *vṛddhi* comes; *ṣatva*: it becomes *acāriṣam*.

### Page 232 (upper) — Rik 23: grammar (end)

**अगस्महि (agasmahi)** — by *samo gamyṛcchibhyām* (Pā. Sū. 1-3-29) — the substitutes of *la* after the intransitive roots *gam* and *ṛcch* following the prefix *sam* are middle — the middle-voice suffix comes. *Luṅ*, first person plural *mahiṅ*; for *cli*, *sic*: *gam* + *s* + *mahi*, the augment *aṭ*. By *mantre ghasahvaraṇaśavṛdahādvṛc kṛgamijanibhyo leḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-80) the *luk* of *cli* would be due; yet since this is Vedic, by *sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante* the *luk* of *cli* does not come. By *ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-10) — a *val*-initial *ārdhadhātuka* after a root that is monosyllabic in its teaching and taught unaccented does not take the augment *iṭ* — the *iṭ* is barred. By *vā gamaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 1-2-13) — the *jhal*-initial *liṅ* and *sic* after the root *gam* are optionally *kit* — *sic* is *kit*. So by *anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37) the nasal *m* is dropped, the augment *aṭ*: it becomes *agasmahi*. ॥23॥

*(An ornament follows.)*
