### Page 232 (lower) — Sūkta 23, Rik 24 (last ṛk of the sūkta)

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> सं मा॑ग्ने॒ वर्च॑सा सृज॒ सं प्र॒जया॒ समायु॑षा ।
> वि॒द्युर्मे॑ अ॒स्य दे॒वा इन्द्रो॑ वि॒द्यात्स॒ह ऋषि॑भिः ॥२४॥ [accent ?]
>
> *sáṃ māgne várcasā sṛja sáṃ prajáyā sám ā́yuṣā |*
> *vidyúr me asyá devā́ índro vidyā́t sahá ṛ́ṣibhiḥ ||24||* [accent ?]

*(Strokes over मा, र्च and यु; bars under ग्ने, ज (सृज), प्र and या. Line 2: bars under वि, अ, दे, वि (विद्यात्) and ह (सह); strokes over मे, द्रो and षि; read with the Pada [accent ?].)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> सं । मा । अग्ने । वर्चसा । सृज । सं । प्रऽजया । सं । आयुषा ॥
> विद्युः । मे । अस्य । देवाः । इन्द्रः । विद्यात् । सह । ऋषिऽभिः ॥२४॥
>
> *saṃ | mā | agne | varcasā | sṛja | saṃ | pra 'jayā | saṃ | āyuṣā ||*
> *vidyuḥ | me | asya | devāḥ | indraḥ | vidyāt | saha | ṛṣi 'bhiḥ ||24||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: पा० ३-४-१०८, ७-२-७९, ६-१-९६, ६-१-१२८. The bhāṣya ends with ॥१२॥ (the twelfth varga) and ॥४॥ (the end of the fourth sūkta of the anuvāka [as read]).)*

> हे अग्ने वर्चःप्रजायुर्भिर्मां संयोजय । देवाः सोमपातारोऽस्य मे यजमानस्य विद्युः । अनुष्ठानं जानीयुः । किंच इन्द्रश्च ऋषिगणैः सह ममानुष्ठानं विद्यात् । जानीयात् ॥ विद्युः । विद ज्ञाने । लिङो झेर्जुस् । पा० ३-४-१०८ । यासुट् । लिङः सलोपः । पा० ७-२-७९ । इति सकारलोपः । उस्यपदान्तात् । पा० ६-१-९६ । इति पररूपत्वं । यासुट उदात्तत्वेऽप्येकादेश उकारोऽप्युदात्तः ॥ अस्य । इदमोऽन्वादेश इत्यशनुदात्तः । विभक्तिरपि सुप्त्वेनानुदात्ता । सह ऋषिभिरित्यत्र ऋत्यकः । पा० ६-१-१२८ । इति प्रकृतिभावः ॥१२॥ ॥४॥
>
> *he agne varcaḥprajāyurbhirmāṃ saṃyojaya | devāḥ somapātāro 'sya me yajamānasya vidyuḥ | anuṣṭhānaṃ jānīyuḥ | kiṃca indraśca ṛṣigaṇaiḥ saha mamānuṣṭhānaṃ vidyāt | jānīyāt || vidyuḥ | vida jñāne | liṅo jherjus | pā0 3-4-108 | yāsuṭ | liṅaḥ salopaḥ | pā0 7-2-79 | iti sakāralopaḥ | usyapadāntāt | pā0 6-1-96 | iti pararūpatvaṃ | yāsuṭa udāttatve 'pyekādeśa ukāro 'pyudāttaḥ || asya | idamo 'nvādeśa ityaśanudāttaḥ | vibhaktirapi suptvenānudāttā | saha ṛṣibhirityatra ṛtyakaḥ | pā0 6-1-128 | iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ ||12|| ||4||*

### Page 233 — Rik 24: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**Translation:** "O Agni, join me with splendour, offspring and life. May the gods, the soma-drinkers, *vidyuḥ*, know, the rite *asya me*, of me, this sacrificer. And may Indra too, *saha ṛṣibhiḥ*, together with the hosts of ṛṣis, *vidyāt*, know my rite." (Grammatical tail: *vidyuḥ*, *vida jñāne*, *jus* for *jhi* of *liṅ* by *liṅo jher jus* [as printed; *jher jus*] (Pā. 3-4-108), *yāsuṭ*, the *s* dropped by *liṅaḥ salopaḥ…* (Pā. 7-2-79), the following form by *usy apadāntāt* (Pā. 6-1-96); since *yāsuṭ* is udātta, the single substitute *u* is also udātta; *asya*, the unaccented *aś* by *idamo 'nvādeśe…*, and the case-ending too unaccented as a *sup*; in *saha ṛṣibhiḥ* the original state by *ṛty akaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-128).)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**हे अग्ने (he agne)** — O Agni | **मा (mā)** — me | **वर्चसा (varcasā)** — with splendour (with power) | **प्रजया (prajayā)** — with sons and descendants | **आयुषा (āyuṣā)** — with life | **सं सृज (saṃ sṛja)** — join | **देवाः (devāḥ)** — the gods (who have drunk soma) | **अस्य मे (asya me)** — my performance of sacrifice (may they know) | **इन्द्रः (indraḥ)** — Indra | **ऋषिभिः सह (ṛṣibhiḥ saha)** — together with the ṛṣis | **विद्यात् (vidyāt)** — may he know the sacrifice I have performed.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, grant me splendour, sons and descendants, and long life. May the gods, and Indra together with the ṛṣis, know the sacrifice I have performed.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Agni, confer upon me vigour, progeny and long life; the gods may know of this my sacrifice and Indra, with the Rishis may know it.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The meaning of the first half of this ṛk can be known easily. Agni is prayed to give splendour, sons and descendants, and long life. The meaning of the second half is not so clear; for the words *vidyur me asya* the commentator has explained the meaning "the performance of sacrifice I do". In the sentence *indro vidyāt saha ṛṣibhiḥ*, why the word *ṛṣibhiḥ* is used is also unclear. It seems the ṛṣi's intention is that this sacrifice, or hymn, made with regard to the deities, should be known to Indra, to the deities and to the other ṛṣis.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**विद्युः (vidyuḥ)** — *vida jñāne*; *liṅ*, third person plural *jhi*; by *jher jus* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-96 [as printed; for 3-4-108]) *jus* comes for the *jhi* in place of *liṅ*; *jus*, the augment *yāsuṭ*: *vid* + *yās* + *us*; dropping of the *s*,

### Page 234 (upper) — Rik 24: grammar (end)

*vidyā* + *us*: by *usy apadāntāt* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-96) — when *us* follows an *a*/*ā* not at the end of a *pada*, the following form comes as a single substitute — when the following form comes, *vidyus*; *ru* and *visarga*.

**सह ऋषिभिः (saha ṛṣibhiḥ)** — by *ṛty akaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-128) — when a short *ṛ* follows, the *a*, *i*, *u*, *ṛ* at the end of a *pada* are made short and also keep their original state — shortening and the original state come. So *guṇa* does not come. ॥24॥

*(An ornament follows: the close of Sūkta 23. The header of p. 234 reads "Maṃ. 1 A. 6 Sū. 24", the new anuvāka.)*

## ॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 24 — *"kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānām"* ("The Twenty-fourth Sūkta"; first sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)
*(Printed pp. 234 lower–294.)*

### Page 234 (lower) — Sūkta 24: title and introduction

*(Title: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ("The Twenty-fourth Sūkta"). The header of this page reads "Maṃ. 1 A. 6 Sū. 24".)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** (introductory note)

*(Numbers as printed: आ० ९-३ and ऐ० ब्रा० ७-१८; the Aitareya number ७-१८ is settled at zoom (first glyph = flat-footed 7).)*

> प्रथममण्डलस्य षष्ठेऽनुवाके सप्त सूक्तानि । तत्र कस्य नूनमिति पञ्चदशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं । अजीगर्तपुत्रस्य शुनःशेपस्यार्षं । त्रैष्टुभं । अभि त्वा देवेति तृचो गायत्रः । आद्याया अनिरुक्तत्वात्प्रजापतिर्देवता । अग्नेर्वयमित्यस्याग्निः । अभि त्वा देवेत्यस्य तृचस्य सविता । भगभक्तस्येत्येषा भगदेवताका वा । शेषा वारुण्यः । तथा चानुक्रान्तं । कस्य पञ्चोनाजीगर्तिः शुनःशेपः स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातो वारुणं तु त्रैष्टुभमादौ काय्याग्नेय्यौ सावित्रस्तृचो गायत्रोऽस्यान्त्या भागी वेति ॥ राजसूयेऽभिषेचनीयेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये परिसमाप्ते सत्येतदादिकं सूक्तसप्तकमभिषिक्तस्य पुत्रादिभिः परिवृतस्य राज्ञः पुरस्ताद्धोत्राख्यातव्यं । तथा च सूत्रेऽभिहितं । संस्थिते मरुत्वतीये दक्षिणत आहवनीयस्य हिरण्यकशिपावासीनोऽभिषिक्ताय पुत्रामात्यपरिवृताय राज्ञे शौनःशेपमाचक्षीत । आ० ९-३ । इति । ब्राह्मणं च भवति । तदेतत्परऋक्शतगाथं शौनःशेपमाख्यानं तद्धोता राज्ञेऽभिषिक्तायाचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीन आचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीनः प्रतिगृणाति । ऐ० ब्रा० ७-१८ । इति ॥
>
> *prathamamaṇḍalasya ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke sapta sūktāni | tatra kasya nūnamiti pañcadaśarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktaṃ | ajīgartaputrasya śunaḥśepasyārṣaṃ | traiṣṭubhaṃ | abhi tvā deveti tṛco gāyatraḥ | ādyāyā aniruktatvātprajāpatirdevatā | agnervayamityasyāgniḥ | abhi tvā devetyasya tṛcasya savitā | bhagabhaktasyetyeṣā bhagadevatākā vā | śeṣā vāruṇyaḥ | tathā cānukrāntaṃ | kasya pañconājīgartiḥ śunaḥśepaḥ sa kṛtrimo vaiśvāmitro devarāto vāruṇaṃ tu traiṣṭubhamādau kāyyāgneyyau sāvitrastṛco gāyatro 'syāntyā bhāgī veti || rājasūye 'bhiṣecanīye 'hani marutvatīye parisamāpte satyetadādikaṃ sūktasaptakamabhiṣiktasya putrādibhiḥ parivṛtasya rājñaḥ purastāddhotrākhyātavyaṃ | tathā ca sūtre 'bhihitaṃ | saṃsthite marutvatīye dakṣiṇata āhavanīyasya hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīno 'bhiṣiktāya putrāmātyaparivṛtāya rājñe śaunaḥśepamācakṣīta | ā0 9-3 | iti | brāhmaṇaṃ ca bhavati | tadetatparaṛkśatagāthaṃ śaunaḥśepamākhyānaṃ taddhotā rājñe 'bhiṣiktāyācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīna ācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīnaḥ pratigṛṇāti | ai0 brā0 7-18 | iti ||*

**Translation:** "In the sixth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala there are seven sūktas. Of these the first is the sūkta *kasya nūnam*, of fifteen ṛks; its ṛṣi is Śunaḥśepa, son of Ajīgarta; it is in *triṣṭubh*; the tṛca *abhi tvā deva* is in *gāyatrī*. Because the first ṛk does not name its deity, Prajāpati is its deity; of *agner vayam*, Agni; of the tṛca *abhi tvā deva*, Savitṛ; *bhagabhaktasya* has Bhaga as deity, optionally; the rest are to Varuṇa. And so the Anukramaṇī: '*kasya*, fifteen less five [as printed: *pañcona*]; Ājīgarti Śunaḥśepa, he, the adopted Vaiśvāmitra Devarāta; to Varuṇa, in *triṣṭubh*; at the beginning one to Ka and one to Agni; a tṛca to Savitṛ in *gāyatrī*, of which the last is to Bhaga, optionally.' In the *rājasūya*, on the day of the consecration, when the *marutvatīya* is finished, this group of seven sūktas beginning here is to be narrated by the *hotṛ* before the consecrated king, surrounded by his sons and the rest. And so it is said in the sūtra: 'When the *marutvatīya* is finished, seated on a golden cushion to the south of the *āhavanīya*, he should tell the Śaunaḥśepa to the consecrated king, surrounded by his sons and ministers' (Āśv. 9-3). And there is the brāhmaṇa: 'This is the Śaunaḥśepa story, of more than a hundred ṛks and with *gāthās*; the *hotṛ* tells it to the consecrated king; seated on a golden cushion he tells it; seated on a golden cushion [the *adhvaryu*] responds' (Ai. Brā. 7-18 [as read])."

**Anuvāda (Kannada rendering):** With this sūkta the sixth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala begins. In it there are seven sūktas. In the first sūkta, *kasya nūnam*, there are fifteen ṛks. For all seven sūktas in this anuvāka the ṛṣi is Śunaḥśepa, son of Ajīgarta. The three ṛks beginning *abhi tvā deva savitaḥ* are in the Gāyatrī metre. The remaining ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. Since in the first ṛk no deity is set forth by name, —

### Page 235 — Sūkta 24: introduction (continued)

— Prajāpati himself is its deity; for the ṛk *agner vayam*, Agni is the deity; for the three ṛks *abhi tvā*, Savitṛ is the deity. But among these three ṛks, for the third ṛk, *bhagabhaktasya*, Savitṛ or Bhaga is the deity; for all the remaining ṛks Varuṇa is the deity. On this matter the Anukramaṇī says thus —

> कस्य पञ्चोनाजीगर्तिः शुनःशेपः स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातो वारुणं तु त्रैष्टुभमादौ काय्याग्नेय्यौ सावित्रस्तृचो गायत्रोऽस्यान्त्या भागी वेति ॥
>
> *kasya pañconājīgartiḥ śunaḥśepaḥ sa kṛtrimo vaiśvāmitro devarāto vāruṇaṃ tu traiṣṭubhamādau kāyyāgneyyau sāvitrastṛco gāyatro 'syāntyā bhāgī veti ||*

— that is: for the sūkta *kasya nūnam*, containing fifteen ṛks, the ṛṣi is Śunaḥśepa, son of Ajīgarta. This Śunaḥśepa is well known by the name Devarāta as the adopted son of the ṛṣi Viśvāmitra. This sūkta has Varuṇa as deity and is made of ṛks in the Triṣṭubh metre. But for the first two ṛks Ka, that is Prajāpati, and Agni are the deities. For the next ṛks, that is 3–5, Savitṛ is the deity; for the fifth ṛk it is said that Savitṛ or Bhaga is the deity. These three ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. For all the remaining ṛks Varuṇa is the deity and the metre is Triṣṭubh.

Its application: in the *rājasūya* sacrifice, on the day of consecration, after the recitation of the *marutvatīya-śastra* mantras, the *hotṛ* must recite the seven sūktas beginning *kasya nūnam* (the seven sūktas of this anuvāka) facing the consecrated king, surrounded by sons and other kinsfolk. On this matter the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra says thus —

> संस्थिते मरुत्वतीये दक्षिणत आहवनीयस्य हिरण्यकशिपावासीनोऽभिषिक्ताय पुत्रामात्यपरिवृताय राज्ञे शौनःशेपमाचक्षीत ॥ (आ० ९-३)
> ब्राह्मणं च भवति — तदेतत्परऋक्शतगाथं शौनःशेपमाख्यानं तद्धोता राज्ञेऽभिषिक्तायाचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीन आचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीनः प्रतिगृणाति ॥ (ऐ० ब्रा० ७-१८)
>
> *saṃsthite marutvatīye dakṣiṇata āhavanīyasya hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīno 'bhiṣiktāya putrāmātyaparivṛtāya rājñe śaunaḥśepamācakṣīta || (ā0 9-3)*
> *brāhmaṇaṃ ca bhavati — tadetatparaṛkśatagāthaṃ śaunaḥśepamākhyānaṃ taddhotā rājñe 'bhiṣiktāyācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīna ācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīnaḥ pratigṛṇāti || (ai0 brā0 7-18)*

— that is: in the *rājasūya* sacrifice, after the recitation of the *marutvatīya-śastra* mantras, the consecrated king must sit, together with his sons and ministers, on a golden seat (cushion) to the south of the *āhavanīya* fire. Then the *hotṛ* must recite the seven sūktas, connected with Śunaḥśepa, that is, having Śunaḥśepa as ṛṣi, beginning *kasya nūnam* (Ā. 9-3).

### Page 236 (upper) — Sūkta 24: introduction (end), heading block

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa too it is said on this matter: the *hotṛ* must recite the hundred ṛks (97 ṛks [as printed]) of the seven sūktas beginning *kasya nūnam*, which contain the Śunaḥśepa story, while sprinkling the king who has been consecrated and is seated on the golden seat (Ai. Brā. 7-18).

*(An ornament follows.)*

### Page 237 — Rik 1: bhāṣya, word-meanings

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(Numbers as printed: ऐ० ब्रा० ७-१६ [the 7 as read], पा० ५-३-९३, २-४-७७, म० ३-१-८६-२, पा० ३-१-८६, ७-४-१६.)*

> कस्येत्यनयर्चा शुनःशेपो यूपे बद्धः कांदिशीकः कं देवमुपधावानीति विचिकित्सति । तथा चाम्नायते । हन्ताहं देवता उपधावामीति स प्रजापतिमेव प्रथमं देवतानामुपससार । ऐ० ब्रा० ७-१६ । इति ॥ वयं शुनःशेपनामका अमृतानां देवतानां मध्ये कतमस्य किंजातीयस्य कस्य देवस्य चारु शोभनं नाम मनामहे । उच्चारयामः । को देवो मां मुमूर्षुं पुनरपि मह्यै महत्यै अदितये पृथिव्यै दात् । दद्यात् । तेन दानेनाहममृतः सन्पितरं मातरं च दृशेयं । पश्येयं । को ह वै नाम प्रजापतिरिति श्रुतेः कस्येति शब्दसामान्यादनया प्रजापतिरेवोपसृत इति गम्यते ॥ कतमस्य । किंशब्दाद्वा बहूनां जातिपरिप्रश्ने डतमच् । पा० ५-३-९३ । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । अमृतानां । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते नञो जरमरमित्रमृता इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । मनामहे । मन ज्ञाने । व्यत्ययेन शप् । पादादित्वादनिघातः । मह्यै । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । दात् । गातिस्था । पा० २-४-७७ । इति सिचो लुक् । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडागमाभावः । दृशेयं । दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे । आशीर्लिङि मिपोऽम् । दृशेरग्वक्तव्यः । म० ३-१-८६-२ । इत्यक्प्रत्ययः । शपोऽपवादः । कित्त्वाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । लिङ्याशिष्यङ् । पा० ३-१-८६ । इत्यङि हि सति ऋदृशोऽङि गुणः । पा० ७-४-१६ । इति गुणः स्यात् । यासुट् । सलोपः । अतो येयः । आद्गुणः । यासुटः स्वरेणैकार उदात्तः । मातरं चेत्यत्र चशब्दाद्दृशेयमित्यनुषज्यते । अतस्तदपेक्षयैषा तिङ्विभक्तिः प्रथमेति चवायोगे प्रथमेति न निहन्यते ॥
>
> *kasyetyanayarcā śunaḥśepo yūpe baddhaḥ kāṃdiśīkaḥ kaṃ devamupadhāvānīti vicikitsati | tathā cāmnāyate | hantāhaṃ devatā upadhāvāmīti sa prajāpatimeva prathamaṃ devatānāmupasasāra | ai0 brā0 7-16 | iti || vayaṃ śunaḥśepanāmakā amṛtānāṃ devatānāṃ madhye katamasya kiṃjātīyasya kasya devasya cāru śobhanaṃ nāma manāmahe | uccārayāmaḥ | ko devo māṃ mumūrṣuṃ punarapi mahyai mahatyai aditaye pṛthivyai dāt | dadyāt | tena dānenāhamamṛtaḥ sanpitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca dṛśeyaṃ | paśyeyaṃ | ko ha vai nāma prajāpatiriti śruteḥ kasyeti śabdasāmānyādanayā prajāpatirevopasṛta iti gamyate || katamasya | kiṃśabdādvā bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac | pā0 5-3-93 | cita ityantodāttatvaṃ | amṛtānāṃ | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatve prāpte naño jaramaramitramṛtā ityuttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | manāmahe | mana jñāne | vyatyayena śap | pādāditvādanighātaḥ | mahyai | udāttayaṇo halpūrvāditi vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | dāt | gātisthā | pā0 2-4-77 | iti sico luk | bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge 'pītyaḍāgamābhāvaḥ | dṛśeyaṃ | dṛśir prekṣaṇe | āśīrliṅi mipo 'm | dṛśeragvaktavyaḥ | ma0 3-1-86-2 | ityakpratyayaḥ | śapo 'pavādaḥ | kittvāllaghūpadhaguṇābhāvaḥ | liṅyāśiṣyaṅ | pā0 3-1-86 | ityaṅi hi sati ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ | pā0 7-4-16 | iti guṇaḥ syāt | yāsuṭ | salopaḥ | ato yeyaḥ | ādguṇaḥ | yāsuṭaḥ svareṇaikāra udāttaḥ | mātaraṃ cetyatra caśabdāddṛśeyamityanuṣajyate | atastadapekṣayaiṣā tiṅvibhaktiḥ prathameti cavāyoge prathameti na nihanyate ||*

**Translation:** "With this ṛk *kasya*, Śunaḥśepa, bound to the sacrificial post and not knowing where to turn, wonders: 'which god should I run to?' And so it is handed down: 'Come, I shall run to the gods' — he went first of the gods to Prajāpati himself (Ai. Brā. 7-16). We, named Śunaḥśepa, *manāmahe*, utter, the *cāru*, fine, *nāma*, name, of which, *katamasya*, of what kind, *kasya devasya*, god, among the *amṛtānām*, immortal gods? Which god will give me, who am about to die, again *mahyai aditaye*, to the great earth? By that gift, being immortal, may I *dṛśeyam*, see, my father and mother. From the *śruti* 'Ka is indeed the name of Prajāpati', by the common word *kasya* it is understood that by this ṛk Prajāpati himself was approached." (Grammatical tail: *katamasya*, *ḍatamac* in asking about a class among many (Pā. 5-3-93), final udātta by *citaḥ*; *amṛtānām*, the last member's final udātta by *nañsubhyām* being due, the last member's initial udātta by *nañño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ*; *manāmahe*, *mana jñāne*, *śap* by *vyatyaya*, not unaccented as it begins the *pāda*; *mahyai*, the case-ending udātta by *udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt*; *dāt*, the *luk* of *sic* by *gātisthā…* (Pā. 2-4-77), no augment *aṭ* by *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi*; *dṛśeyam*, *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*, *am* for *mip* in the benedictive *liṅ*, the suffix *ak* by *dṛśer ag vaktavyaḥ* (Ma. 3-1-86-2), an exception to *śap*; no *guṇa* of the light penultimate as it is *kit*; for if *aṅ* came by *liṅy āśiṣy aṅ* (Pā. 3-1-86), *guṇa* would come by *ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ* (Pā. 7-4-16); *yāsuṭ*, dropping of *s*, *iy* by *ato yeyaḥ*, *guṇa* by *ād guṇaḥ*; the *e* udātta by the accent of *yāsuṭ*; in *mātaraṃ ca*, by the word *ca*, *dṛśeyam* is to be supplied again; so with regard to it this *tiṅ*-ending is the first one, and by *cavāyoge prathamā* it is not made unaccented.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

(**वयं (vayaṃ)** — we, named Śunaḥśepa) **अमृतानां (amṛtānāṃ)** — among the gods | **कतमस्य (katamasya)** — belonging to which class | **कस्य देवस्य (kasya devasya)** — of which god | **चारु (cāru)** — auspicious | **नाम (nāma)** — the name | **मनामहे (manāmahe)** — shall we utter? | **कः (kaḥ)** — which god | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **मह्यै (mahyai)** — great | **अदितये (aditaye)** — to the earth (so as to be on the earth, that is, so as to live) | **दात् (dāt)** — will give? (by his so giving, I) | **पितरं च (pitaraṃ ca)** — (my) father | **मातरं च (mātaraṃ ca)** — (my) mother | **पुनः (punaḥ)** — again | **दृशेयं (dṛśeyaṃ)** — shall I see?

### Page 238 — Rik 1: overall sense, explanation, English, Special Topics

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Who among the gods is the best? By remembering (praising) which god will this trouble of mine be removed and release from bondage come, and who will favour me to live on the earth like everyone? When shall I see my father and mother again?

**॥ Viśeṣārthaḥ ॥** *(explanation)*

In the sacrifice performed by the king named Hariścandra, the ṛṣi named Śunaḥśepa, bound as a victim to the sacrificial post, not knowing where to turn and seeing death before him, speaks thus, with a cry of distress, thinking which god he should take refuge with so as to be released from bondage: the gods are many. Among them who is the best? By uttering whose name, or praising whom, will he free me, who am facing death, from the noose, and protect me so as to live again like the other people on the earth? When shall I, escaped from this trouble, see my father and mother? Lamenting in this way he first remembers Prajāpati. Afterwards, knowing from him that if he remembers Agni he will be released from bondage, he praises Agni in the next ṛk.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Of many immortal gods whose good name should we contemplate? Who will deliver us back to the vast earth that I may again behold my father and mother?

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

It has been said before that all seven sūktas in this anuvāka are used in the *rājasūya* sacrifice for sprinkling the consecrated king, the sacrificer. On this matter the legend about Śunaḥśepa is described at length in the Purāṇas and the like, and in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. Since the legend in the Purāṇas and the like differs, and since it is not so fit to be taken as authority, we explain here only the legend in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. This story is described thus in the 33rd *adhyāya* of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa —

*The legend of Śunaḥśepa (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa), as printed.* *(The print gives it as continuous prose, the khaṇḍas closed by ॥१॥, ॥२॥ … ; the line-breaks below follow the sentences.)*

**§ 1 — Hariścandra and Nārada (printed pp. 238 lower–239).**

> हरिश्चन्द्रो ह वैधस ऐक्ष्वाको राजापुत्र आस । तस्य ह शतं जाया बभूवुस्तासु पुत्रं न लेभे । तस्य ह पर्वतनारदौ गृह ऊषतुः स ह नारदं पप्रच्छ —
> यं न्विमं पुत्रमिच्छन्ति ये विजानन्ति ये च न । किंस्वित्पुत्रेण विन्दते तन्म आचक्ष्व नारदेति ॥
> स एकया पृष्टो दशभिः प्रत्युवाच —
> ऋणमस्मिन्संनयत्यमृतत्वं च गच्छति । पिता पुत्रस्य जातस्य पश्येच्चेज्जीवतो मुखं ॥
> यावन्तः पृथिव्यां भोगा यावन्तो जातवेदसि । यावन्तो अप्सु प्राणिनां भूयान्पुत्रे पितुस्ततः ॥
> शश्वत्पुत्रेण पितरोऽत्यायन्बहुलं तमः । आत्मा हि जज्ञ आत्मनः स इरावत्यतितारिणी ॥
> किं नु मलं किमजिनं किमु श्मश्रूणि किं तपः । पुत्रं ब्रह्माण इच्छध्वं स वै लोकोऽवदावदः ॥
> अन्नं ह प्राणः शरणं ह वासो रूपं हिरण्यं पशवो विवाहाः । सखा ह जाया कृपणं ह दुहिता ज्योतिर्ह पुत्रः परमे व्योमन् ॥
> पतिर्जायां प्रविशति गर्भो भूत्वा स मातरं । तस्यां पुनर्नवो भूत्वा दशमे मासि जायते ॥
> तज्जाया जाया भवति यदस्यां जायते पुनः । आभूतिरेषा भूतिर्बीजमेतन्निधीयते ॥
> देवाश्चैतामृषयश्च तेजः समभरन्महत् । देवा मनुष्यानब्रुवन्नेषा वो जननी पुनः ॥
> नापुत्रस्य लोकोऽस्तीति तत्सर्वे पशवो विदुः । तस्मात्तु पुत्रो मातरं स्वसारं चाधिरोहति ।
> एष पन्था उरुगायः सुशेवो यं पुत्रिण आक्रमन्ते विशोकाः । तं पश्यन्ति पशवो वयांसि च तस्मात्ते मात्रापि मिथुनी भवन्ति ।
> इति हास्मा आख्याय ॥१॥
>
> *hariścandro ha vaidhasa aikṣvāko rājāputra āsa | tasya ha śataṃ jāyā babhūvustāsu putraṃ na lebhe | tasya ha parvatanāradau gṛha ūṣatuḥ sa ha nāradaṃ papraccha —*
> *yaṃ nvimaṃ putramicchanti ye vijānanti ye ca na | kiṃsvitputreṇa vindate tanma ācakṣva nāradeti ||*
> *sa ekayā pṛṣṭo daśabhiḥ pratyuvāca —*
> *ṛṇamasminsaṃnayatyamṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati | pitā putrasya jātasya paśyeccejjīvato mukhaṃ ||*
> *yāvantaḥ pṛthivyāṃ bhogā yāvanto jātavedasi | yāvanto apsu prāṇināṃ bhūyānputre pitustataḥ ||*
> *śaśvatputreṇa pitaro 'tyāyanbahulaṃ tamaḥ | ātmā hi jajña ātmanaḥ sa irāvatyatitāriṇī ||*
> *kiṃ nu malaṃ kimajinaṃ kimu śmaśrūṇi kiṃ tapaḥ | putraṃ brahmāṇa icchadhvaṃ sa vai loko 'vadāvadaḥ ||*
> *annaṃ ha prāṇaḥ śaraṇaṃ ha vāso rūpaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavo vivāhāḥ | sakhā ha jāyā kṛpaṇaṃ ha duhitā jyotirha putraḥ parame vyoman ||*
> *patirjāyāṃ praviśati garbho bhūtvā sa mātaraṃ | tasyāṃ punarnavo bhūtvā daśame māsi jāyate ||*
> *tajjāyā jāyā bhavati yadasyāṃ jāyate punaḥ | ābhūtireṣā bhūtirbījametannidhīyate ||*
> *devāścaitāmṛṣayaśca tejaḥ samabharanmahat | devā manuṣyānabruvanneṣā vo jananī punaḥ ||*
> *nāputrasya loko 'stīti tatsarve paśavo viduḥ | tasmāttu putro mātaraṃ svasāraṃ cādhirohati |*
> *eṣa panthā urugāyaḥ suśevo yaṃ putriṇa ākramante viśokāḥ | taṃ paśyanti paśavo vayāṃsi ca tasmātte mātrāpi mithunī bhavanti |*
> *iti hāsmā ākhyāya ||1||*

**Translation:** "Hariścandra, son of Vedhas, of the line of Ikṣvāku, was a king without a son. He had a hundred wives; among them he obtained no son. Parvata and Nārada lived in his house. He asked Nārada: 'This son whom people desire, those who understand and those who do not — what does one gain by a son? Tell me that, Nārada.' Asked in one verse, he answered in ten: (1) He pays off his debt in him and reaches immortality — the father who sees the face of his son born living. (2) As many enjoyments as there are on earth, as many in fire, as many in the waters for living beings — greater than those is the father's in a son. (3) Always by a son have fathers crossed over the abundant darkness; for the self is born of the self; he is a boat laden with food that carries across. (4) What is the dirt, what the antelope-skin, what the beard, what the austerity? Desire a son, O brahmins; he is the world that is well spoken of. (5) Food is life, clothing is shelter, gold is beauty, cattle are marriages; a wife is a friend, a daughter is a pity; a son is light in the highest heaven. (6) The husband enters the wife; becoming an embryo, he enters the mother; becoming new again in her, he is born in the tenth month. (7) That is the wife's wifehood (*jāyā*), that he is born (*jāyate*) in her again; she is the source, the becoming; the seed is placed in her. (8) The gods and the seers brought great splendour to her; the gods said to men: 'She is your mother again.' (9) 'For the sonless there is no world': all animals know this; therefore the son mounts even mother and sister. (10) This is the wide, pleasant path which those with sons tread without sorrow; animals and birds see it; therefore they mate even with the mother. Having told him this, —"

**§ 2 — The vow to Varuṇa; Rohita (pp. 239–240).**

> अथैनमुवाच वरुणं राजानमुपधाव पुत्रो मे जायतां तेन त्वा यजा इति । तथेति स वरुणं राजानमुपससार पुत्रो मे जायतां तेन त्वा यजा इति तथेति तस्य पुत्रो जज्ञे रोहितो नाम ।
> तं होवाचाजनि वै ते पुत्रो यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै पशुर्निर्दशो भवत्यथ स मेध्यो भवति निर्दशो न्वस्त्वथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति ।
> स ह निर्दश आस तं होवाच निर्दशो न्वभूद्यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै पशोर्दन्ता जायन्तेऽथ मेध्यो भवति दन्ता न्वस्य जायन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति ।
> तस्य ह दन्ता जज्ञिरे तं होवाचाज्ञत वा अस्य दन्ता यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै पशोर्दन्ताः पद्यन्तेऽथ स मेध्यो भवति दन्ता न्वस्य पद्यन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति ।
> तस्य ह दन्ताः पेदिरे तं होवाचापत्सत वा अस्य दन्ता यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै पशोर्दन्ताः पुनर्जायन्तेऽथ स मेध्यो भवति दन्ता न्वस्य पुनर्जायन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति ।
> तस्य ह दन्ताः पुनर्जज्ञिरे तं होवाचाज्ञत वा अस्य पुनर्दन्ता यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै क्षत्रियः सांनाहुको भवत्यथ स मेध्यो भवति संनाहं नु प्राप्नोत्वथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति ।
> स ह संनाहं प्रापत्तं होवाच संनाहं नु प्राप्नोद्यजस्व माऽनेनेति स तथेत्युक्त्वा पुत्रमामन्त्रयामास ततायं वै मह्यं त्वामददाद्धन्त त्वयाहमिमं यजा इति ।
> स ह नेत्युक्त्वा धनुरादायारण्यमुपातस्थौ स संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार ॥२॥
>
> *athainamuvāca varuṇaṃ rājānamupadhāva putro me jāyatāṃ tena tvā yajā iti | tatheti sa varuṇaṃ rājānamupasasāra putro me jāyatāṃ tena tvā yajā iti tatheti tasya putro jajñe rohito nāma |*
> *taṃ hovācājani vai te putro yajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai paśurnirdaśo bhavatyatha sa medhyo bhavati nirdaśo nvastvatha tvā yajā iti tatheti |*
> *sa ha nirdaśa āsa taṃ hovāca nirdaśo nvabhūdyajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai paśordantā jāyante 'tha medhyo bhavati dantā nvasya jāyantāmatha tvā yajā iti tatheti |*
> *tasya ha dantā jajñire taṃ hovācājñata vā asya dantā yajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai paśordantāḥ padyante 'tha sa medhyo bhavati dantā nvasya padyantāmatha tvā yajā iti tatheti |*
> *tasya ha dantāḥ pedire taṃ hovācāpatsata vā asya dantā yajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai paśordantāḥ punarjāyante 'tha sa medhyo bhavati dantā nvasya punarjāyantāmatha tvā yajā iti tatheti |*
> *tasya ha dantāḥ punarjajñire taṃ hovācājñata vā asya punardantā yajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai kṣatriyaḥ sāṃnāhuko bhavatyatha sa medhyo bhavati saṃnāhaṃ nu prāpnotvatha tvā yajā iti tatheti |*
> *sa ha saṃnāhaṃ prāpattaṃ hovāca saṃnāhaṃ nu prāpnodyajasva mā 'neneti sa tathetyuktvā putramāmantrayāmāsa tatāyaṃ vai mahyaṃ tvāmadadāddhanta tvayāhamimaṃ yajā iti |*
> *sa ha netyuktvā dhanurādāyāraṇyamupātasthau sa saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra ||2||*

**Translation:** "— he said to him: 'Go to king Varuṇa: "Let a son be born to me; with him I shall sacrifice to you."' 'So be it.' He went to king Varuṇa: 'Let a son be born to me; with him I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' A son named Rohita was born to him. [Varuṇa] said to him: 'A son has been born to you; sacrifice to me with him.' He said: 'When an animal is more than ten days old, then it is fit for sacrifice; let him be more than ten days old, then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' He became more than ten days old. [Varuṇa] said: 'He is more than ten days old; sacrifice to me with him.' He said: 'When an animal's teeth come, then it is fit for sacrifice; let his teeth come, then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' His teeth came. [Varuṇa] said: 'His teeth have come; sacrifice to me with him.' He said: 'When an animal's teeth fall, then it is fit; let his teeth fall …' His teeth fell. '… When an animal's teeth come again, then it is fit; let his teeth come again …' His teeth came again. [Varuṇa] said: 'His teeth have come again; sacrifice to me with him.' He said: 'When a kṣatriya is armed, then he is fit for sacrifice; let him obtain his armour, then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' He obtained his armour. [Varuṇa] said: 'He has obtained his armour; sacrifice to me with him.' He said 'So be it', and called his son: 'My dear, he gave you to me; come, let me sacrifice to him with you.' He said 'No', took his bow and went off to the forest; he wandered a year in the forest."

**§ 3 — Hariścandra afflicted; Indra's counsel *caraiva*; Śunaḥśepa bought (printed p. 240).**

*Printed as one paragraph ending ॥३॥; the five verses carry no numbers in the print. As printed: अशनया परीतम् (*aśanayā parītam*), हतश्चरैवेति (*hataś caraiveti*), मध्यमे (*madhyame*).*

> अथ हैक्ष्वाकं वरुणो जग्राह तस्य होदरं जज्ञे तदु ह रोहितः शुश्राव सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच —
> नानाश्रान्ताय श्रीरस्तीति रोहित शुश्रुम । पापो नृषद्वरो जन इन्द्र इच्चरतः सखा चरैवेति ॥
> चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह द्वितीयं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच —
> पुष्पिण्यौ चरतो जङ्घे भूष्णुरात्मा फलग्रहिः । शेरेऽस्य सर्वे पाप्मानः श्रमेण प्रपथे हतश्चरैवेति ॥
> चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह तृतीयं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच —
> आस्ते भग आसीनस्योर्ध्वस्तिष्ठति तिष्ठतः । शेते निपद्यमानस्य चराति चरतो भगश्चरैवेति ॥
> चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह चतुर्थं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच —
> कलिः शयानो भवति संजिहानस्तु द्वापरः । उत्तिष्ठंस्त्रेता भवति कृतं संपद्यते चरंश्चरैवेति ॥
> चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह पञ्चमं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच —
> चरन्वै मधु विन्दति चरन्स्वादुमुदुम्बरम् । सूर्यस्य पश्य श्रेमाणं यो न तन्द्रयते चरंश्चरैवेति ॥
> चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह षष्ठं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽजीगर्तं सौयवसिमृषिमशनया परीतमरण्य उपेयाय ।
> तस्य ह त्रयः पुत्रा आसुः शुनःपुच्छः शुनःशेपः शुनोलाङ्गूल इति तं होवाच ऋषेऽहं ते शतं ददाम्यहमेषामेकेनाऽऽत्मानं निष्क्रीणा इति स ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं निगृह्णान उवाच नन्विममिति नो एवेममिति कनिष्ठं माता तौ ह मध्यमे संपादयाञ्चक्रतुः शुनःशेपे तस्य ह शतं दत्त्वा स तमादाय सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय ।
> स पितरमेत्योवाच तत हन्ताहमनेनाऽऽत्मानं निष्क्रीणा इति स वरुणं राजानमुपससारानेन त्वा यजा इति तथेति भूयान्वै ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियादिति वरुण उवाच तस्मा एतं राजसूयं यज्ञक्रतुं प्रोवाच तमेतमभिषेचनीये पुरुषं पशुमालेभे ॥३॥
>
> *atha haikṣvākaṃ varuṇo jagrāha tasya hodaraṃ jajñe tadu ha rohitaḥ śuśrāva so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca —*
> *nānāśrāntāya śrīrastīti rohita śuśruma | pāpo nṛṣadvaro jana indra iccarataḥ sakhā caraiveti ||*
> *caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha dvitīyaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca —*
> *puṣpiṇyau carato jaṅghe bhūṣṇurātmā phalagrahiḥ | śere 'sya sarve pāpmānaḥ śrameṇa prapathe hataścaraiveti ||*
> *caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha tṛtīyaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca —*
> *āste bhaga āsīnasyordhvastiṣṭhati tiṣṭhataḥ | śete nipadyamānasya carāti carato bhagaścaraiveti ||*
> *caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha caturthaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca —*
> *kaliḥ śayāno bhavati saṃjihānastu dvāparaḥ | uttiṣṭhaṃstretā bhavati kṛtaṃ saṃpadyate caraṃścaraiveti ||*
> *caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha pañcamaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca —*
> *caranvai madhu vindati caransvādumudumbaram | sūryasya paśya śremāṇaṃ yo na tandrayate caraṃścaraiveti ||*
> *caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha ṣaṣṭhaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'jīgartaṃ sauyavasimṛṣimaśanayā parītamaraṇya upeyāya |*
> *tasya ha trayaḥ putrā āsuḥ śunaḥpucchaḥ śunaḥśepaḥ śunolāṅgūla iti taṃ hovāca ṛṣe 'haṃ te śataṃ dadāmyahameṣāmekenātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇā iti sa jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ nigṛhṇāna uvāca nanvimamiti no evemamiti kaniṣṭhaṃ mātā tau ha madhyame saṃpādayāñcakratuḥ śunaḥśepe tasya ha śataṃ dattvā sa tamādāya so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya |*
> *sa pitarametyovāca tata hantāhamanenātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇā iti sa varuṇaṃ rājānamupasasārānena tvā yajā iti tatheti bhūyānvai brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyāditi varuṇa uvāca tasmā etaṃ rājasūyaṃ yajñakratuṃ provāca tametamabhiṣecanīye puruṣaṃ paśumālebhe ||3||*

**Translation:** "Then Varuṇa seized the Aikṣvāka [Hariścandra]; his belly swelled [dropsy]. Rohita heard of it. He came from the forest to the village. Indra, in the form of a man, came round to him and said: 'There is no fortune for one who has not toiled, Rohita; so we have heard. The man who sits among men is bad; Indra is the friend of the wanderer. Wander on!' 'A Brahmin has told me to wander' — so he wandered a second year in the forest. He came from the forest to the village; Indra, in the form of a man, came round to him and said: 'The wanderer's legs are flowering; his body grows and gathers fruit; all his sins lie slain by the toil on the road. Wander on!' … a third year …: 'The fortune of one who sits, sits; it stands up for one who stands; it lies down for one who lies; it moves for one who moves. Wander on!' … a fourth year …: 'Kali is the one lying down; Dvāpara the one getting up; Tretā the one standing; Kṛta is attained by the one who moves. Wander on!' … a fifth year …: 'The wanderer finds honey, the wanderer the sweet *udumbara* fruit. See the splendour of the Sun, who never tires as he moves. Wander on!' 'A Brahmin has told me to wander' — so he wandered a sixth year in the forest. He came in the forest upon the seer Ajīgarta Sauyavasi, overcome by hunger. He had three sons: Śunaḥpuccha, Śunaḥśepa and Śunolāṅgūla. [Rohita] said to him: 'Seer, I give you a hundred [cows]; with one of these I shall ransom myself.' He, holding back the eldest son, said: 'Surely not this one.' 'Nor this one,' said the mother of the youngest. The two of them settled on the middle one, Śunaḥśepa. Having given a hundred for him, [Rohita] took him and came from the forest to the village. He came to his father and said: 'Father, look, I ransom myself with this one.' He went to king Varuṇa: 'With this one I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it,' said Varuṇa, 'a Brahmin is worth more than a kṣatriya.' He taught him this sacrificial rite, the Rājasūya; at the Abhiṣecanīya he took him as the human victim."

**§ 4 — The priests; Śunaḥśepa's prayers and release (printed pp. 240–241).**

*Page 241 begins at मानुषमिव. As printed: निःशान (*niḥśāna*), कनीय (*kanīya*).*

> तस्य ह विश्वामित्रो होताऽऽसीज्जमदग्निरध्वर्युर्वसिष्ठो ब्रह्माऽयास्य उद्गाता तस्मा उपाकृताय नियोक्तारं न विविदुः स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिर्मह्यमपरं शतं दत्ताहमेनं नियोक्ष्यामीति तस्मा अपरं शतं ददुस्तं स निनियोज ।
> तस्मा उपाकृताय नियुक्तायाऽऽप्रीताय पर्यग्निकृताय विशसितारं न विविदुः स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिर्मह्यमपरं शतं दत्ताहमेनं विशसिष्यामीति तस्मा अपरं शतं ददुः सोऽसिं निःशान एयाय ।
> अथ ह शुनःशेप ईक्षाञ्चक्रेऽमानुषमिव वै मा विशसिष्यन्ति हन्ताहं देवता उपधावामीति स प्रजापतिमेव प्रथमं देवतानामुपससार — कस्य नूनं कतमस्यामृतानामित्येतयर्चा ।
> तं प्रजापतिरुवाचाग्निर्वै देवानां नेदिष्ठस्तमेवोपधावेति सोऽग्निमुपससाराग्नेर्वयं प्रथमस्यामृतानामित्येतयर्चा ।
> तमग्निरुवाच सविता वै प्रसवानामीशे तमेवोपधावेति स सवितारमुपससाराभि त्वा देव सवितरित्येतेन तृचेन ।
> तं सवितोवाच वरुणाय वै राज्ञे नियुक्तोऽसि तमेवोपधावेति स वरुणं राजानमुपससारात उत्तराभिरेकत्रिंशता ।
> तं वरुण उवाचाग्निर्वै देवानां मुखं सुहृदयतमस्तं नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति सोऽग्निं तुष्टावात उत्तराभिर्द्वाविंशत्या ।
> तमग्निरुवाच विश्वान्नु देवान् स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स विश्वान्देवांस्तुष्टाव — नमो महद्भ्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्य इत्येतयर्चा ।
> तं विश्वे देवा ऊचुरिन्द्रो वै देवानामोजिष्ठो बलिष्ठः सहिष्ठः सत्तमः पारयिष्णुतमस्तं नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स इन्द्रं तुष्टाव यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इति चैतेन सूक्तेनोत्तरस्य च पञ्चदशभिः ।
> तस्मा इन्द्रः स्तूयमानः प्रीतो मनसा हिरण्यरथं ददौ तमेतया प्रतीयाय शश्वदिन्द्र इति ।
> तमिन्द्र उवाचाश्विनौ नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति सोऽश्विनौ तुष्टावात उत्तरेण तृचेन ।
> तमश्विना ऊचतुरुषसं नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स उषसं तुष्टावात उत्तरेण तृचेन ।
> तस्य ह स्मर्च्यृच्युक्तायां विपाशो मुमुचे कनीय ऐक्ष्वाकस्योदरं भवत्युत्तमस्यामेवर्च्युक्तायां विपाशो मुमुचेऽगद ऐक्ष्वाक आस ॥४॥
>
> *tasya ha viśvāmitro hotāsījjamadagniradhvaryurvasiṣṭho brahmā 'yāsya udgātā tasmā upākṛtāya niyoktāraṃ na vividuḥ sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasirmahyamaparaṃ śataṃ dattāhamenaṃ niyokṣyāmīti tasmā aparaṃ śataṃ dadustaṃ sa niniyoja |*
> *tasmā upākṛtāya niyuktāyāprītāya paryagnikṛtāya viśasitāraṃ na vividuḥ sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasirmahyamaparaṃ śataṃ dattāhamenaṃ viśasiṣyāmīti tasmā aparaṃ śataṃ daduḥ so 'siṃ niḥśāna eyāya |*
> *atha ha śunaḥśepa īkṣāñcakre 'mānuṣamiva vai mā viśasiṣyanti hantāhaṃ devatā upadhāvāmīti sa prajāpatimeva prathamaṃ devatānāmupasasāra — kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānāmityetayarcā |*
> *taṃ prajāpatiruvācāgnirvai devānāṃ nediṣṭhastamevopadhāveti so 'gnimupasasārāgnervayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānāmityetayarcā |*
> *tamagniruvāca savitā vai prasavānāmīśe tamevopadhāveti sa savitāramupasasārābhi tvā deva savitarityetena tṛcena |*
> *taṃ savitovāca varuṇāya vai rājñe niyukto 'si tamevopadhāveti sa varuṇaṃ rājānamupasasārāta uttarābhirekatriṃśatā |*
> *taṃ varuṇa uvācāgnirvai devānāṃ mukhaṃ suhṛdayatamastaṃ nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti so 'gniṃ tuṣṭāvāta uttarābhirdvāviṃśatyā |*
> *tamagniruvāca viśvānnu devān stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa viśvāndevāṃstuṣṭāva — namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhya ityetayarcā |*
> *taṃ viśve devā ūcurindro vai devānāmojiṣṭho baliṣṭhaḥ sahiṣṭhaḥ sattamaḥ pārayiṣṇutamastaṃ nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa indraṃ tuṣṭāva yacciddhi satya somapā iti caitena sūktenottarasya ca pañcadaśabhiḥ |*
> *tasmā indraḥ stūyamānaḥ prīto manasā hiraṇyarathaṃ dadau tametayā pratīyāya śaśvadindra iti |*
> *tamindra uvācāśvinau nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti so 'śvinau tuṣṭāvāta uttareṇa tṛcena |*
> *tamaśvinā ūcaturuṣasaṃ nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa uṣasaṃ tuṣṭāvāta uttareṇa tṛcena |*
> *tasya ha smarcyṛcyuktāyāṃ vipāśo mumuce kanīya aikṣvākasyodaraṃ bhavatyuttamasyāmevarcyuktāyāṃ vipāśo mumuce 'gada aikṣvāka āsa ||4||*

**Translation:** "Viśvāmitra was his Hotṛ, Jamadagni the Adhvaryu, Vasiṣṭha the Brahman, Ayāsya the Udgātṛ. When he had been brought forward, they found no one to bind him [to the post]. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'Give me another hundred and I shall bind him.' They gave him another hundred, and he bound him. When he had been brought forward, bound, propitiated with the Āprī verses and had fire carried round him, they found no one to slaughter him. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'Give me another hundred and I shall slaughter him.' They gave him another hundred; he came sharpening his knife. Then Śunaḥśepa reflected: 'They will slaughter me as if I were not a man. Look, I shall run to the deities.' He went first of the deities to Prajāpati, with the ṛk *kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānām*. Prajāpati said to him: 'Agni is the nearest of the gods; run to him.' He went to Agni with the ṛk *agner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām*. Agni said to him: 'Savitṛ rules over the impulses; run to him.' He went to Savitṛ with the triplet *abhi tvā deva savitaḥ*. Savitṛ said to him: 'You have been bound for king Varuṇa; run to him.' He went to king Varuṇa with the thirty-one [ṛks] that follow. Varuṇa said to him: 'Agni is the mouth of the gods, the most kind-hearted; praise him, and then we shall release you.' He praised Agni with the twenty-two that follow. Agni said to him: 'Praise the All-gods, and then we shall release you.' He praised the All-gods with the ṛk *namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ*. The All-gods said to him: 'Indra is the most vigorous, strongest, most powerful, truest of the gods, the best at bringing across; praise him, and then we shall release you.' He praised Indra with the sūkta *yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ* and with fifteen [ṛks] of the next. Indra, pleased as he was praised, gave him in his mind a golden chariot; he acknowledged it with the ṛk *śaśvad indra*. Indra said to him: 'Praise the Aśvins, and then we shall release you.' He praised the Aśvins with the triplet that follows. The Aśvins said to him: 'Praise Uṣas, and then we shall release you.' He praised Uṣas with the triplet that follows. As each ṛk was spoken, the fetter came loose and the Aikṣvāka's belly grew smaller; when the last ṛk was spoken, the fetter came off and the Aikṣvāka was well."

**§ 5 — The Añjaḥsava; Devarāta; Ajīgarta's plea; Viśvāmitra adopts Śunaḥśepa (printed pp. 241–242).**

*As printed: शुनःशेपोऽञ्जस्सवं (*śunaḥśepo 'ñjassavaṃ*; the conjunct is crowded, so the reading is not certain), शुनश्शेपो (*śunaśśepo*) once, ज्ञपयोऽऽराजपुत्र (*jñapayo 'rājaputra*; the print is not clear and the reading is doubtful). Page 242 begins at निह्नुवे.*

> तमृत्विज ऊचुस्त्वमेव नोऽस्याह्नः संस्थामधिगच्छेत्यथ हैतं शुनःशेपोऽञ्जस्सवं ददर्श तमेताभिश्चतसृभिरभिसुषाव यच्चिद्धि त्वं गृहे गृह इत्यथैनं द्रोणकलशमभ्यवनिनायोच्छिष्टं चम्वोर्भरेत्येतयर्चा ।
> अथ हास्मिन्नन्वारब्धे पूर्वाभिश्चतसृभिः स स्वाहाकाराभिर्जुहवाञ्चकाराथैनमवभृथमभ्यवनिनाय त्वं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वानित्येताभ्यामथैनमत ऊर्ध्वमग्निमाहवनीयमुपस्थापयाञ्चकार शुनश्चिच्छेपं निदितं सहस्रादिति ।
> अथ ह शुनश्शेपो विश्वामित्रस्याङ्कमाससाद स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिर्ऋषे पुनर्मे पुत्रं देहीति नेति होवाच विश्वामित्रो देवा वा इमं मह्यमरासतेति स ह देवरातो वैश्वामित्र आस तस्यैते कापिलेयबाभ्रवाः ।
> स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिस्त्वं वेहि विह्वयावहा इति स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिराङ्गिरसो जन्मनाऽस्याजीगर्तिः श्रुतः कविः । ऋषे पैतामहात्तन्तोर्माऽपगाः पुनरेहि मामिति
> स होवाच शुनःशेपोऽदर्शुस्त्वा शासहस्तं न यच्छूद्रेष्वलप्सत । गवां त्रीणि शतानि त्वमवृणीथा मदङ्गिर इति ।
> स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिस्तद्वै मा तात तपति पापं कर्म मया कृतं । तदहं निह्नुवे तुभ्यं प्रतियन्तु शता गवामिति
> स होवाच शुनःशेपो यः सकृत्पापकं कुर्यात्कुर्यादेनत्ततोऽपरं । नापागाः शौद्रान्न्यायादसन्धेयं त्वया कृतमिति ।
> असन्धेयमिति ह विश्वामित्र उपससाद स होवाच विश्वामित्रो भीम एव सौयवसिः शासेन विशिशासिषुः । अस्थान्मैतस्य पुत्रो भूर्ममैवोपेहि पुत्रतामिति ।
> स होवाच शुनःशेपः स वै यथा नो ज्ञपयोऽऽराजपुत्र तथा वद । यथैवाऽऽङ्गिरसः सन्नुपेयां तव पुत्रतामिति
> स होवाच विश्वामित्रो ज्येष्ठो मे त्वं पुत्राणां स्यास्तव श्रेष्ठा प्रजा स्यात् । उपेया दैवं मे दायं तेन वै त्वोपमन्त्रय इति ।
> स होवाच शुनःशेपः संज्ञानानेषु वै ब्रूयात्सौहार्द्याय मे श्रियै । यथाहं भरतऋषभोपेयां तव पुत्रतामित्यथ ह विश्वामित्रः पुत्रानामन्त्रयामास
> मधुच्छन्दाः शृणोतन ऋषभो रेणुरष्टकः । ये के च भ्रातरः स्थ नास्मै ज्यैष्ठ्याय कल्पध्वमिति ॥५॥
>
> *tamṛtvija ūcustvameva no 'syāhnaḥ saṃsthāmadhigacchetyatha haitaṃ śunaḥśepo 'ñjassavaṃ dadarśa tametābhiścatasṛbhirabhisuṣāva yacciddhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛha ityathainaṃ droṇakalaśamabhyavanināyocchiṣṭaṃ camvorbharetyetayarcā |*
> *atha hāsminnanvārabdhe pūrvābhiścatasṛbhiḥ sa svāhākārābhirjuhavāñcakārāthainamavabhṛthamabhyavanināya tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvānityetābhyāmathainamata ūrdhvamagnimāhavanīyamupasthāpayāñcakāra śunaścicchepaṃ niditaṃ sahasrāditi |*
> *atha ha śunaśśepo viśvāmitrasyāṅkamāsasāda sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasirṛṣe punarme putraṃ dehīti neti hovāca viśvāmitro devā vā imaṃ mahyamarāsateti sa ha devarāto vaiśvāmitra āsa tasyaite kāpileyabābhravāḥ |*
> *sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasistvaṃ vehi vihvayāvahā iti sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasirāṅgiraso janmanā 'syājīgartiḥ śrutaḥ kaviḥ | ṛṣe paitāmahāttantormā 'pagāḥ punarehi māmiti*
> *sa hovāca śunaḥśepo 'darśustvā śāsahastaṃ na yacchūdreṣvalapsata | gavāṃ trīṇi śatāni tvamavṛṇīthā madaṅgira iti |*
> *sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasistadvai mā tāta tapati pāpaṃ karma mayā kṛtaṃ | tadahaṃ nihnuve tubhyaṃ pratiyantu śatā gavāmiti*
> *sa hovāca śunaḥśepo yaḥ sakṛtpāpakaṃ kuryātkuryādenattato 'paraṃ | nāpāgāḥ śaudrānnyāyādasandheyaṃ tvayā kṛtamiti |*
> *asandheyamiti ha viśvāmitra upasasāda sa hovāca viśvāmitro bhīma eva sauyavasiḥ śāsena viśiśāsiṣuḥ | asthānmaitasya putro bhūrmamaivopehi putratāmiti |*
> *sa hovāca śunaḥśepaḥ sa vai yathā no jñapayo 'rājaputra tathā vada | yathaivāṅgirasaḥ sannupeyāṃ tava putratāmiti*
> *sa hovāca viśvāmitro jyeṣṭho me tvaṃ putrāṇāṃ syāstava śreṣṭhā prajā syāt | upeyā daivaṃ me dāyaṃ tena vai tvopamantraya iti |*
> *sa hovāca śunaḥśepaḥ saṃjñānāneṣu vai brūyātsauhārdyāya me śriyai | yathāhaṃ bharataṛṣabhopeyāṃ tava putratāmityatha ha viśvāmitraḥ putrānāmantrayāmāsa*
> *madhucchandāḥ śṛṇotana ṛṣabho reṇuraṣṭakaḥ | ye ke ca bhrātaraḥ stha nāsmai jyaiṣṭhyāya kalpadhvamiti ||5||*

**Translation:** "The priests said to him: 'You yourself bring the rite of this day to its completion for us.' Then Śunaḥśepa saw the Añjaḥsava [the quick pressing of soma]. He pressed the soma with these four [ṛks], *yac cid dhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛhe*. Then he poured it into the droṇa-kalaśa with the ṛk *ucchiṣṭaṃ camvor bhara*. Then, while [the king] kept hold of him, he made the offerings with the four preceding [ṛks] that end in *svāhā*. Then he led him to the Avabhṛtha [the final bath] with the two [ṛks] *tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvān*. After that he had him attend upon the Āhavanīya fire with *śunaś cic chepaṃ niditaṃ sahasrāt*. Then Śunaḥśepa sat down in Viśvāmitra's lap. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'Seer, give me back my son.' 'No,' said Viśvāmitra, 'the gods have given him to me.' He became Devarāta Vaiśvāmitra; the Kāpileyas and Bābhravas are his descendants. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'You come here; let the two of us call to him.' Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'You are an Āṅgirasa by birth, the son of Ajīgarta, a renowned seer. Seer, do not leave the line of your grandfathers; come back to me.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'They saw you with the knife in your hand, a thing not found even among Śūdras. You chose three hundred cows over me, O Aṅgiras.' Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'That evil deed I did torments me, my son. I make amends to you: let the hundreds of cows go back.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'He who does an evil thing once will do the next one too. You have not turned away from the ways of a Śūdra; what you did cannot be mended.' 'Cannot be mended,' Viśvāmitra repeated, and came forward. Viśvāmitra said: 'Terrible was Sauyavasi, wanting to cut you up with the knife. Do not stay his son; come to be my son.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'Tell us, prince, as you make it known, how I, being an Āṅgirasa, may become your son.' Viśvāmitra said: 'You shall be the eldest of my sons, and your offspring the best. You shall receive my divine inheritance; with that I call you.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'If they agree, say it, for my friendship and my fortune, so that I may become your son, bull of the Bharatas.' Then Viśvāmitra called his sons: 'Madhucchandas, hear, and Ṛṣabha, Reṇu and Aṣṭaka, and all you who are brothers: grant him the seniority.'"

**§ 6 — Viśvāmitra's sons; the recitation of the legend (printed p. 242).**

*As printed: पुर एत्रा (*pura etrā*), देवराताय (*devarātāya*), परऋक्शतगाथं (*paraṛkśatagāthaṃ*; zoom of PDF 256, Oct 28: the printed word reads तदेतत्…ऋक्कृतगाथं (-ṛkkṛtagāthaṃ), not -क्शत-; the two letters between तत् and ऋ are a crowded conjunct I cannot settle [?], so the form परऋक्शतगाथं above is superseded). The end of the passage carries no paragraph number.*

> तस्य ह विश्वामित्रस्यैकशतं पुत्रा आसुः पञ्चाशदेव ज्यायांसो मधुच्छन्दसः पञ्चाशत्कनीयांसः ।
> तद्ये ज्यायांसो न ते कुशलं मेनिरे ताननु व्याजहारान्तान्वः प्रजा भक्षीष्टेति त एतेऽन्ध्राः पुण्ड्राः शबराः पुलिन्दा मूतिबा इत्युदन्त्या बहवो वैश्वामित्रा दस्यूनां भूयिष्ठाः ।
> स होवाच मधुच्छन्दाः पञ्चाशता सार्धं यन्नः पिता संजानीते तस्मिंस्तिष्ठामहे वयं । पुरस्त्वा सर्वे कुर्महे त्वामन्वञ्चो वयं स्मसीति ।
> अथ ह विश्वामित्रः प्रतीतः पुत्रांस्तुष्टाव । ते वै पुत्राः पशुमन्तो वीरवन्तो भविष्यथ । ये मानं मेऽनुगृह्णन्तो वीरवन्तमकर्त मा ।
> पुर एत्रा वीरवन्तो देवरातेन गाथिनाः । सर्वे राध्याः स्थ पुत्रा एष वः सद्विवाचनं ।
> एष वः कुशिका वीरो देवरातस्तमन्वित । युष्मांश्च दायं म उपेता विद्यां यामु च विद्मसि ।
> ते सम्यञ्चो वैश्वामित्राः सर्वे साकं सरातयः । देवराताय तस्थिरे धृत्यै श्रैष्ठ्याय गाथिनाः ।
> अधीयत देवरातो रिक्थयोरुभयोर्ऋषिः । जह्नूनां चाधिपत्ये दैवे वेदे च गाथिनां ।
> तदेतत्परऋक्शतगाथं शौनःशेपमाख्यानं । तद्धोता राज्ञेऽभिषिक्तायाऽऽचष्टे ।
> हिरण्यकशिपावासीन आचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीनः प्रतिगृह्णाति यशो वै हिरण्यं यशसैवैनं तत्समर्धयति ।
> ओमित्यृचः प्रतिगर एवं तथेति गाथाया ओमिति वै दैवं तथेति मानुषं दैवेन चैवैनं तन्मानुषेण च पापादेनसः प्रमुञ्चति ।
> तस्माद्यो राजा विजिती स्यादप्ययजमान आख्यापयेतैवैतच्छौनःशेपमाख्यानं न हास्मिन्नल्पं चनैनः परिशिष्यते ।
> सहस्रमाख्यात्रे दद्याच्छतं प्रतिगरित्र एते चैवाऽऽसने श्वेतश्चाश्वतरीरथो होतुः ।
> पुत्रकामा हाप्याख्यापयेरँल्लभन्ते ह पुत्राँल्लभन्ते ह पुत्रान् ॥
>
> *tasya ha viśvāmitrasyaikaśataṃ putrā āsuḥ pañcāśadeva jyāyāṃso madhucchandasaḥ pañcāśatkanīyāṃsaḥ |*
> *tadye jyāyāṃso na te kuśalaṃ menire tānanu vyājahārāntānvaḥ prajā bhakṣīṣṭeti ta ete 'ndhrāḥ puṇḍrāḥ śabarāḥ pulindā mūtibā ityudantyā bahavo vaiśvāmitrā dasyūnāṃ bhūyiṣṭhāḥ |*
> *sa hovāca madhucchandāḥ pañcāśatā sārdhaṃ yannaḥ pitā saṃjānīte tasmiṃstiṣṭhāmahe vayaṃ | purastvā sarve kurmahe tvāmanvañco vayaṃ smasīti |*
> *atha ha viśvāmitraḥ pratītaḥ putrāṃstuṣṭāva | te vai putrāḥ paśumanto vīravanto bhaviṣyatha | ye mānaṃ me 'nugṛhṇanto vīravantamakarta mā |*
> *pura etrā vīravanto devarātena gāthināḥ | sarve rādhyāḥ stha putrā eṣa vaḥ sadvivācanaṃ |*
> *eṣa vaḥ kuśikā vīro devarātastamanvita | yuṣmāṃśca dāyaṃ ma upetā vidyāṃ yāmu ca vidmasi |*
> *te samyañco vaiśvāmitrāḥ sarve sākaṃ sarātayaḥ | devarātāya tasthire dhṛtyai śraiṣṭhyāya gāthināḥ |*
> *adhīyata devarāto rikthayorubhayorṛṣiḥ | jahnūnāṃ cādhipatye daive vede ca gāthināṃ |*
> *tadetatparaṛkśatagāthaṃ śaunaḥśepamākhyānaṃ | taddhotā rājñe 'bhiṣiktāyācaṣṭe |*
> *hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīna ācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīnaḥ pratigṛhṇāti yaśo vai hiraṇyaṃ yaśasaivainaṃ tatsamardhayati |*
> *omityṛcaḥ pratigara evaṃ tatheti gāthāyā omiti vai daivaṃ tatheti mānuṣaṃ daivena caivainaṃ tanmānuṣeṇa ca pāpādenasaḥ pramuñcati |*
> *tasmādyo rājā vijitī syādapyayajamāna ākhyāpayetaivaitacchaunaḥśepamākhyānaṃ na hāsminnalpaṃ canainaḥ pariśiṣyate |*
> *sahasramākhyātre dadyācchataṃ pratigaritra ete caivāsane śvetaścāśvatarīratho hotuḥ |*
> *putrakāmā hāpyākhyāpayeram̐llabhante ha putrām̐llabhante ha putrān ||*

**Translation:** "Viśvāmitra had a hundred and one sons: fifty older than Madhucchandas and fifty younger. The older ones did not think it right. He pronounced on them: 'Your offspring shall inherit the ends [of the land].' These are the Andhras, Puṇḍras, Śabaras, Pulindas and Mūtibas, many dwelling at the borders; the descendants of Viśvāmitra are the most numerous of the Dasyus. Madhucchandas, together with the fifty, said: 'What our father agrees to, by that we stand. We all put you in front; we follow after you.' Then Viśvāmitra, pleased, praised his sons: 'You, my sons, will be rich in cattle and rich in heroes, you who, honouring my wish, have made me rich in heroes. Gāthins, with Devarāta going before, you will be rich in heroes. You are all to prosper, my sons; this is a true word for you. This hero of yours, Kuśikas, is Devarāta; follow him. He will receive you as my inheritance, and the knowledge we know. Those Vaiśvāmitras, the Gāthins, all of one mind, all sharing the gift, stood by Devarāta for his steadiness and his seniority. Devarāta the seer was placed in both inheritances: in the lordship of the Jahnus and in the divine Veda of the Gāthins.' This is the Śaunaḥśepa legend, with more than a hundred ṛks and with gāthās. The Hotṛ tells it to the anointed king. Seated on a golden cushion he tells it; seated on a golden cushion [the Adhvaryu] responds. Gold is glory: with glory he thus makes him prosper. *Om* is the response to a ṛk, *tathā* to a gāthā; *om* is divine, *tathā* human. With the divine and the human he thus frees him from sin and guilt. Therefore a king who is victorious, even if he is not sacrificing, should have this Śaunaḥśepa legend told; then not the least guilt remains in him. He should give a thousand to the teller and a hundred to the responder, and these two seats; and to the Hotṛ a white chariot drawn by mules. Those who want sons should also have it told; they obtain sons, they obtain sons."

### Page 243 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (Śunaḥśepākhyānavu)

*Title, as printed: ಶುನಶ್ಶೇಪಾಖ್ಯಾನವು ("The Śunaḥśepa story"). The Kannada retelling runs to p. 249 and is translated here in full, page by page. The bracketed summaries in small type are the source's own.*

*[Hariścandra's wish for a son is granted. The praise of having sons.]*

Hariścandra, son of Vedhas, born in the Ikṣvāku line, had a hundred wives, yet no son was born to him. Once, when the seers Parvata and Nārada came to his house, Hariścandra said to Nārada: "O Nārada, human beings, who have the power of discernment, and also the other creatures, which lack it, long eagerly for offspring. What is gained by the birth of offspring?" So he asked.

To the question Hariścandra asked in one sentence, Nārada gives his answer in ten sentences, as set out below:

(1) The father, together with the joy he feels at seeing the face of the son born to him, also pays off his debt to the ancestors through that son and attains immortality.

(2) A father's joy at gaining a son is greater than the enjoyment to be had from the earth, greater than the help to be had from fire, and beyond the use to be had from water. The enjoyment that comes from gaining a son is far greater than all these enjoyments.

(3) Through his son a father crosses many great dangers. Since the father is himself born again as a son, the son carries the father across the sorrows of this world and the next in the sea of worldly life, just as a boat stocked beforehand with provisions carries a man across a river or a sea.

(4) What is the use of a householder's life without children? Why brahmacarya? Why the vānaprastha stage? Why become a wandering ascetic? What is the use of these? "**O best of Brahmins, desire offspring**": so the world says of people who give up married life in order to practise the Vedic rites.

(5) Food protects life. Clothes protect from cold. Gold gives the use of ornaments. Marriage and the like bring wealth in the form of cattle. The wife becomes a friend. The daughter becomes an object of affection. But the son alone shines in the highest world of the gods as a lamp that lights up the self.

### Page 244 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

(6) The husband enters the wife in the form of seed. When the seed changes into the form of an embryo, he makes her a mother. Afterwards he is born from her again, in the tenth month.

(7) Only when the husband is born in her womb does the wife truly receive the meaningful name "**jāyā**". The seed produced in her she raises in the form of a son, makes it shine and makes it beautiful.

(8) The gods and the seers have granted the highest radiance to her who has become a *jāyā*. Then the gods declared to human beings: "**She becomes your mother.**"

(9) Even animals know that one without offspring has no lasting state; and among them the male young even covers its own mother or sister.

(10) This is the road on which those who have sons walk free of sorrow. Even beasts and birds know it. In these words he praised the having of sons.

*[A son is born to Hariścandra. Varuṇa comes again and again and insists that the son be given to him as an offering in sacrifice. But Hariścandra puts forward one reason after another, keeps postponing the sacrifice and slips out of it.]*

Then Nārada advised Hariścandra: "Go to Varuṇa and pray to him to grant you a son. And give him your word that, after the son is born, you will offer that very son to him in sacrifice." Hariścandra went to Varuṇa as told and prayed: "Grant me a son. I shall give him to you as an offering." At once a son named Rohita was born. Varuṇa came and said: "A son has been born to you. Give him as an offering." To that Hariścandra said: "Before any creature becomes fit to be an offering, ten days must pass. Let ten days pass for my son too. Then I shall offer him to you." When ten days had passed for Rohita, Varuṇa came and asked for him. Then Hariścandra said: "For any creature to be given as an offering, its teeth must have come. When my son's teeth have come, I shall offer him." After Rohita's teeth had come, Varuṇa came and asked for him. Then Hariścandra said: "No creature should be given as an offering until its teeth have fallen. Let this one's teeth fall too." Varuṇa came again: "Rohita's teeth are falling; give him as an offering." Hariścandra asked for time until his teeth had grown again.

### Page 245 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

Then, when Varuṇa came, he said: "One born in a warrior family is not fit to be an offering until he puts on a warrior's armour. Wait until then." When that time also came and Varuṇa firmly demanded Rohita, Hariścandra called his son and said: "Child, I must now give you as an offering to Varuṇa, who granted you to me." Rohita said: "That shall never be." He took up his bow, fled to escape into a lonely forest, and wandered there for one year.

*[Rohita wanders aimlessly in the forest for six years. Then he buys from his parents a Brahmin's son named Śunaḥśepa, to give to Varuṇa as the offering in his place.]*

After Rohita had escaped and gone, Varuṇa seized Hariścandra, and Hariścandra was struck with dropsy (*mahodara*). Rohita heard the news, left the forest and came to a village. Indra came in human form, met him and said: "O Rohita, there is no happiness for one who does not travel. However excellent a man may be, if he grows up among the people of one caste he falls into wrong ways and is ruined. So go about in lonely regions. Indra becomes the friend of the man who travels like this. You too go about." So he advised.

Rohita understood that a Brahmin had advised him to travel, and he wandered in the forest for a second year as well. Then, as he was coming to a village, Indra came again in human form and said: "The feet of a man who travels are like the nectar of flowers. From that flower the self grows and gains the fruit of good health. All his sins are removed by the toil of travelling. So go about."

Following that word, Rohita went about for a third year as well. Just when he was entering the village again, Indra came and said: "The fortune of a man sitting in one place sits in one place like him. If he goes about, it too goes about and grows. So go about."

In the same way a fourth year passed. At the time he again entered the village, Indra came, described the nature of the four *yugas*, and told Rohita to go about once more. Rohita completed the fifth year in the same way. Just as he was entering the village, Indra came and said: "Honey and the sweet *udumbara* fruit come to the man who travels. See the radiance of the Sun, who does not tire even with his ceaseless moving. Like him, you too go about."

### Page 246 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

Rohita wandered in the forest for the sixth year as well. Then he met a seer named Ajīgarta, son of one called Suyavas. That Ajīgarta, through poverty, was fasting in the forest without food. He had three children, named Śunaḥpuccha, Śunaḥśepa and Śunolāṅgūla. Rohita went to the seer and said: "O seer, I shall give you a hundred cows. Give me one of your three sons. I shall give him to Varuṇa as the offering in my place and so escape." Ajīgarta agreed to it, but he would not send away his eldest son. His wife would not let go of the youngest. Leaving those two, only the middle one was obtained. As agreed, Rohita gave Ajīgarta the hundred cows, brought Śunaḥśepa to his father and told him of the arrangement he had made. Hariścandra went to Varuṇa and said: "In place of my son I shall give you this one as the offering." Varuṇa agreed that this would do, since a Brahmin is greater than a kṣatriya. Then Varuṇa explained the procedure of the Rājasūya sacrifice to the king and arranged for a human sacrifice, in place of the animal sacrifice, on the day of the rite.

*[Four great seers become the priests. The appointed time of the human sacrifice draws near. To escape a terrible death, Śunaḥśepa appeals to the gods. The gods he appealed to and the mantras he uttered.]*

For this human sacrifice Viśvāmitra was appointed Hotṛ, Jamadagni Adhvaryu, Vasiṣṭha Brahman and Ayāsya Udgātṛ. After the rites that come before the sacrifice were over, no one would agree to tie Śunaḥśepa to the sacrificial post. "If you give me another hundred cows, I shall tie him," said Ajīgarta, and came forward. They agreed and gave him a hundred cows. Then Ajīgarta tied his son to the post. Next, after the Āprī hymn had been recited and fire carried round him, no one would agree to cut him. "If you give me another hundred cows, I myself will cut him," said Ajīgarta, and came forward for that too. He took the hundred cows in the same way, sharpened his knife and got ready to kill his son. Śunaḥśepa woke to the fact that they would cut him like an animal. He resolved, "I shall take refuge among the gods," and appealed to Prajāpati with the sūkta "**kasya nūnaṃ katamasya**" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-1). Prajāpati appeared and said: "Agni is the deity nearest to all of you; take refuge in him." Then, when Śunaḥśepa prayed to Agni with the ṛk "**agner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām**", Agni came and said: "Savitṛ is the lord of all beings; take refuge in him." Then

### Page 247 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

he prayed with the three ṛks beginning with the ṛk "**abhi tvā deva savitaḥ**". Then Savitṛ came and said: "You have been bound by Varuṇa, who is the lord; take refuge in him." Then, when he prayed to Varuṇa with thirty-one ṛks, Varuṇa came and said: "Agni is, as it were, the mouth of all the gods and is most merciful. If you pray to him now, we shall all release your bond." When he again prayed to Agni with twenty-two ṛks, Agni came and said: "If you pray to the Viśvedevas, you will be released." Then Śunaḥśepa entreated them with "**namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ**" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-27-13). They came and said: "Indra is the most powerful of all, very strong and enduring; among the gods he is the nearest to truth, and he knows the means of bringing every matter to its end. If you pray to him, we shall release you." Then, when Śunaḥśepa prayed with the sūkta "**yac cid dhi satya somapā**" and with fifteen ṛks of the sūkta after it, Indra came, was pleased with his hymn and granted him a chariot made of gold. Śunaḥśepa accepted it with the words "**śaśvad indra**". Indra again instructed him: "Pray to the Aśvin deities. Then we shall release you." The Aśvins, being prayed to, came and said: "Pray to the goddess Uṣas. We shall release you." While the prayer to Uṣas went on, as he spoke the three ṛks one by one, the noose of Varuṇa's bond gradually loosened and Hariścandra's dropsy kept getting better. When he uttered the last ṛk, the noose was taken off completely and Hariścandra regained his health as before.

*[Śunaḥśepa's release; his way of pressing the soma juice in the form of the Añjaḥsava. Viśvāmitra accepts him as his son.]*

Then the priests said to Śunaḥśepa: "Now you too are a priest, like us. Take part with us in this special rite." Then he learnt the procedure of pressing the soma juice, which in the form of the Añjaḥsava is done very quickly. After he had pressed it, he took it and went, reciting the four ṛks "**yac cid dhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛhe**". Uttering the ṛk "**ucchiṣṭaṃ camvoḥ**", he brought it into the droṇa-kalaśa. As soon as Hariścandra touched [him], he uttered the mantra "**yatra grāvā**" and offered the oblation with the word "*svāhā*". Then he came with the implements needed for the *avabhṛtha*, recited the ṛk "**tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya**" and performed the *avabhṛtha*. After this he called Hariścandra to the Āhavanīya fire and recited the mantra "**śunaś cic chepaṃ niditam**".

### Page 248 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

At last Śunaḥśepa went to Viśvāmitra's side. Ajīgarta too came up to him and said: "O seer, give my son back." Viśvāmitra said: "That cannot be. The gods have given him to me as a gift." From then on he became Viśvāmitra's son, named Devarāta ("given by the gods"). (Later the Kāpileyas and the Babhrus were born from him.) Then Ajīgarta called Śunaḥśepa: "You are a seer who belongs to the family of Ajīgarta. So do not forget your line; come back to us." Śunaḥśepa answered his father: "Not even a Caṇḍāla takes a knife in his hand to kill his son. To you the three hundred cows were worth more than I. Out of greed for them you took the knife to cut me, your son." When he mocked him so, Ajīgarta said: "Child, what I did before was wrong. I shall rid myself of this sin. I shall give you a hundred cows too. Come home." In answer Śunaḥśepa said: "You, who once did not shrink from this sinful deed, will not fear to do such deeds again and again. For this deed of yours there is no reconciliation at all." Viśvāmitra too said: "Yes, for this deed there is no expiation at all."

Viśvāmitra said to Śunaḥśepa: "When he held the knife in his hand to kill you, Ajīgarta was terrible to look at. Do not be his son again. Come to my house and be my son." Then Śunaḥśepa voiced his doubt: "How can one born in the line of Aṅgiras become a kinsman of Viśvāmitra?" Viśvāmitra then called all his children and declared: "O Madhucchandas and the rest, from today you have no right of seniority in my property. From today all of it is Śunaḥśepa's. He is the eldest of all."

*[Viśvāmitra's descendants. The reward for those who recite the story of Śunaḥśepa.]*

The seer Viśvāmitra had a hundred children. Fifty were older than Madhucchandas and the rest were younger. The older fifty did not accept that Śunaḥśepa should be the heir to Viśvāmitra's property. When they opposed it, Viśvāmitra cursed them to have low offspring. As the result of that curse, various low clans were born, such as the Śabaras and the Pulindas. Madhucchandas and the younger fifty bowed to Viśvāmitra's decision and honoured Śunaḥśepa: "O Śunaḥśepa, we shall always be obedient to our father's command, and as he wishes we shall give you the place of first honour." Viśvāmitra was pleased with their obedience and said: "O children, because you agreed to my wish, honoured me and made my fatherhood fruitful, may abundant cows and offspring be your reward. Having taken this Devarāta as your leader,

### Page 249 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (end); word note

be victorious. This Devarāta has gained the eminence of the Jahnu line and the divine knowledge of the Gāthi line, and is renowned as a seer. May you, who walk under this seer's leadership, and your children gain every prosperity." So he blessed them.

This story of Śunaḥśepa is told in more than a hundred ṛks. After holy water has been sprinkled on the king, the Hotṛ sits on a jewelled blanket adorned with gold thread and recites it. The Adhvaryu, who gives the response "*oṃ tathā*", sits in the same way and increases the king's glory. With the divine word "*oṃ*", which belongs to the ṛks (they are *apauruṣeya*, not of human authorship), and with the human assent "*tathā*", the Adhvaryu makes the king free of sin. Therefore every king who wishes to be victorious should hear this Śunaḥśepa story, both for his victory and for the cleansing of the sinful acts that come with it. To those who recite this story a thousand cows should be given; and to the Adhvaryu, who encourages the king by giving the needed words of assent, a hundred cows. To the Hotṛ a silver chariot yoked with excellent horses should be given. Those who have no son, whether they recite this tale or hear it, will surely obtain sons.

**॥ ಶುನಶ್ಶೇಪಾಖ್ಯಾನವು ಮುಗಿದುದು ॥** (The Śunaḥśepa story ends.)

This story of Śunaḥśepa is told at length in Vālmīki's Rāmāyaṇa. There Śunaḥśepa is said to be the son of a seer named Ṛcīka; and in place of the name of king Hariścandra there is the name of a king Ambarīṣa, lord of Ayodhyā and other lands. The Bhāgavata and Viṣṇu Purāṇas also give an account of this tale. But in the Purāṇas and similar works the tale comes with small differences; in its main points it is like this one.

**कस्य देवस्य अथवा कस्य कतमस्य देवस्य (kasya devasya athavā kasya katamasya devasya)** — the meaning is "of which god, of what kind of god". Here Śunaḥśepa recites this ṛk while thinking to himself which god he should take refuge in (or praise) to be freed from the sacrificial post to which the sacrificial victim is tied. Although the word **kasya** has the general sense "which", here the word also means Prajāpati. So the commentator, explaining it, says that Śunaḥśepa first asked Prajāpati for help, and on this point cites the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence:

> हन्ताहं देवता उपधावामीति स प्रजापतिमेव प्रथमं देवतानामुपससार ।
>
> *hantāhaṃ devatā upadhāvāmīti sa prajāpatimeva prathamaṃ devatānāmupasasāra |*

"Look, I shall run to the deities": so saying, he went first of the deities to Prajāpati (Ai. Brā. 7-16).

### Page 250 — Rik 1: word notes and grammar

**अमृतानां (amṛtānāṃ)** — मरणरहितानां देवानां (*maraṇarahitānāṃ devānāṃ*), "of the gods who are free from death".

**मह्यै अदितये (mahyai aditaye)** — among the twenty-one names of the earth beginning with *gauḥ, gmā*, the words **mahī** and **aditiḥ** are read (Ni. 1-1), so these words mean *pṛthivī*, the earth. Since both words here convey the same sense, the word *mahī* can be given the meaning "broad, great".

**पुनर्दात्, पितरं च दृशेयं मातरं च (punar dāt, pitaraṃ ca dṛśeyaṃ mātaraṃ ca)** — Śunaḥśepa, tied to the sacrificial post and standing in the victim's place, understood that death was near and was at a loss for fear. He laments: "Shall I again become a creature that belongs to the earth as before? That is, which deity will favour me so that I may live on the earth again? And how shall I be freed from this noose of death and see my father and mother?" In the next ṛk he prays to Agni to be freed from his bond.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**कतमस्य (katamasya)** — by the sūtra (Pā. Sū. 5-3-93)

> वा बहूनां जातिपरिप्रश्ने डतमच्
>
> *vā bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac*

the suffix *ḍatamac* comes after the words *kim*, *yat* and *tad* when one out of many is singled out and a class is meant, and after the word *kim* when a question about the class is meant. Kaiyaṭa (*kaiyaṭakāraru*) says, on the words

> किमादीनां द्विबह्वर्थे प्रत्ययविधानादुपाध्यानर्थक्यं
> पूर्वसूत्रे द्वयोरिति अत्र सूत्रे जातिपरिप्रश्ने इति च न कर्तव्यमिति भावः
>
> *kimādīnāṃ dvibahvarthe pratyayavidhānādupādhyānarthakyaṃ*
> *pūrvasūtre dvayoriti atra sūtre jātiparipraśne iti ca na kartavyamiti bhāvaḥ*

"since the suffix is enjoined for *kim* and the rest in the sense of two and of many, the limiting conditions (*upādhi*) are pointless"; and "the sense is that in the earlier sūtra the word *dvayoḥ*, and in this sūtra the words *jātiparipraśne*, need not be stated". Therefore the suffix also comes when action, quality or name is meant, as in *katama eṣāṃ pācakaḥ* ("which of these is the cook?"), *śūraḥ*, *devadattaḥ*. *kim* + *atama*: loss of the *ṭi*.

**अमृतानां (amṛtānāṃ)** — the acute on the last syllable of the second member, due by *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172), is set aside by *nañjo jaramaramitramṛtāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-116): in a bahuvrīhi compound, the first syllable of the second members *jara*, *mara*, *mitra* and *mṛta* after *nañ* is acute. So the first syllable of *mṛta* is acute.

**मनामहे (manāmahe)** — the root *mana jñāne*, of the Divādi class. So the *vikaraṇa* *śyan* would be expected, but *śap* comes by the Vedic interchange. *laṭ*, first person plural, *mahiṅ*, *e*-substitution; lengthening by *akṛtsārva[dhātukayor dīrghaḥ]* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-25).

**दात् (dāt)** — *ḍudāñ dāne*; *luṅ*, third person singular *tip*, *cli*; *sic* in its place: *dā* + *s* + *ti*; loss of *i* by *itaś ca lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97); by *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77)

### Page 251 (upper) — Rik 1: grammar (end)

the *sic* after the roots *gai*, *sthā*, *dā*, *dhā*, *pā* and *bhū* is dropped (*luk*); so *sic* is dropped. The *aṭ* augment does not come, because this is Vedic.

**दृशेयं (dṛśeyaṃ)** — the root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*. *āśīrliṅ*, first person singular *mip*, substituted by *am*. By *dṛśer agvaktavyaḥ* (Pā. Ma. 3-1-87-3 [as printed]), when the benedictive *liṅ* follows the root *dṛś*, *a* comes; so *aṅ* in place of *śap*. Since *aṅ* is *kit*, the *laghūpadha* guṇa does not come. By *liṅy āśiṣy aṅ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-86), in the Veda *aṅ* comes after the root when the benedictive *liṅ* follows. When *aṅ* comes, guṇa is required by *ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-16): when *aṅ* follows, roots ending in *ṛ* and the root *dṛś* take guṇa. The *yāsuṭ* augment: *dṛś* + *yās* + *am*; loss of the *s*. By *ato yeyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-8 [as printed; for 7-2-80]), *iy* comes for the *yā* that is part of a *sārvadhātuka* after short *a*: so *iy*, then guṇa. ॥1॥

> अ॒ग्नेर्व॒यं प्र॑थ॒मस्या॒मृता॑नां॒ मना॑महे॒ चारु॑ दे॒वस्य॒ नाम॑ ।
> स नो॑ म॒ह्या अदि॑तये॒ पुन॑र्दात्पि॒तरं॑ च दृ॒शेयं॑ मा॒तरं॑ च ॥२॥
>
> *agnér vayáṃ prathamásyāmṛ́tānāṃ mánāmahe cā́ru devásya nā́ma |*

Line 2: strokes over नो, दि, न (पुन), रं (पितरं), यं (दृशेयं) and रं (मातरं); bars under म (मह्या), ये, त्पि, दृ and मा. In Ṛk 1 the stroke in दृशेयं stands over शे; here it stands over यं.)*

> अग्नेः । वयं । प्रथमस्य । अमृतानां । मनामहे । चारु । देवस्य । नाम ।
> सः । नः । मह्यै । अदितये । पुनः । दात् । पितरं । च । दृशेयं । मातरं । च ॥२॥

### Page 252 — Rik 2: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> इत्थं प्रथमयर्चा विचिकित्सां कृत्वा प्रजापतेः सकाशात्तं देवमग्निं निश्चित्यानयर्चा तुष्टाव । तथा च श्रूयते । तं प्रजापतिरुवाचाग्निर्वै देवानां नेदिष्ठस्तमेवोपधावेति सोऽग्निमुपससाराग्नेर्वयं प्रथमस्यामृतानामित्येतयर्चा । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१६ । इति । पूर्ववद्योजना । दाद्ददातु दृशेयं पश्यानीत्येवमाशीःपरत्वेन पदद्वयं योज्यं ॥
>
> *itthaṃ prathamayarcā vicikitsāṃ kṛtvā prajāpateḥ sakāśāttaṃ devamagniṃ niścityānayarcā tuṣṭāva | tathā ca śrūyate | taṃ prajāpatiruvācāgnirvai devānāṃ nediṣṭhastamevopadhāveti so 'gnimupasasārāgnervayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānāmityetayarcā | ai. brā. 7-16 | iti | pūrvavadyojanā | dāddadātu dṛśeyaṃ paśyānītyevamāśīḥparatvena padadvayaṃ yojyaṃ ||*

*Gist:* Having voiced his doubt in the first ṛk and learnt from Prajāpati that the god is Agni, he praised Agni with this ṛk. So it is heard: "Prajāpati said to him: 'Agni is the nearest of the gods; run to him.' He went to Agni with this ṛk, *agner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām*" (Ai. Brā. 7-16). The construction is as before. The two words are to be construed as a wish: *dāt* = "may he give", *dṛśeyam* = "may I see".

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**वयं (vayaṃ)** — we (Śunaḥśepa) | **अमृतानां (amṛtānāṃ)** — (among the gods) who are free from death | **प्रथमस्य (prathamasya)** — who is the first | **देवस्य (devasya)** — who is a god | **अग्नेः (agneḥ)** — of Agni | **चारु (cāru)** — auspicious | **नाम (nāma)** — the name | **मनामहे (manāmahe)** — let us utter | **सः (saḥ)** — that god Agni | **नः (naḥ)** — us (who are facing death) | **मह्यै (mahyai)** — to the great | **अदितये (aditaye)** — to the earth | **पुनः दात् (punaḥ dāt)** — may he give again | **पितरं मातरं च (pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca)** — father and mother | **दृशेयं (dṛśeyaṃ)** — may I see.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Having learnt from Prajāpati that Agni is the first among the gods, I (Śunaḥśepa) utter the auspicious name of Agni, the chief of the gods. May Agni (pleased by this) send me (who am facing death) back to the great earth. (Freed from death by Agni's grace,) I shall see my father and mother.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed)*

> Of many immortal gods we shall contemplate the god Agni's name first; he will deliver us back to this vast earth that I may again behold my father and mother.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

As said before, Śunaḥśepa learnt from Prajāpati that Agni is able to protect him. So Śunaḥśepa first prays to Agni, as the best among the gods, to protect him, to let him live on the earth again, and to grant that he see his father and mother again.

The special explanation given under the previous ṛk applies to this ṛk too.

**वयं (vayaṃ)** — although the plural "we" is used here, it is to be understood as applying to Śunaḥśepa, who is praying to Agni.

### Page 253 (upper) — Rik 2: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

**मह्यै (mahyai)** — meaning *mahatyai*, "to the great". By *vartamāne pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-…; the digits are not clear [?]), these words are formed irregularly (*nipātana*) as ending in the suffix *ati*. Because they are treated like words in *śatṛ*, by *ugitaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-6) *ṅīp* comes; the *at* is dropped as a Vedic usage. By *bṛhanmahator upasaṅkhyānam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173 vā. 1) the *ṅīp* is acute. The suffix *ṅe* follows the word *mahī*. By *āṇ nadyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-12 [as printed; for 7-3-112]), *āṭ* comes before a *ṅit* case-ending after a stem ending in a *nadī*; by *āṭaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 [as printed; for 6-1-90]), *vṛddhi*. *mahī* + *ai*: *yaṇ* substitution. By *udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-17 [as printed; for 6-1-174]), after a *yaṇ* standing in place of an acute vowel and preceded by a consonant, a *nadī* ending and a case-ending from *śas* onwards are acute. So the case-ending is acute.

**दृशेयं (dṛśeyaṃ)** — its derivation is given under the previous mantra. Through the *ca* in *mātaraṃ ca*, *dṛśeyaṃ* is drawn in (*anukṛṣṭa*). Compared with that, the *dṛśeyaṃ* that stands in the mantra is the one uttered first. By *cavāyoge prathamā* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-59), a finite verb uttered first does not become unaccented when there is a connection with *ca* or *vā*; so the loss of all accents is blocked. ॥2॥
