### Pages 429–432 — Sūkta 28, Rik 7 *(Gāyatrī riks begin)*

**॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आयजी वाजसातमा ता ह्युच्चा विजर्भृतः ।
> हरी इवान्धांसि बप्सता ॥ ७ ॥

*āyajī vājasātamā tā hy uccā vijarbhṛtaḥ | harī ivāndhāṃsi bapsatā || 7 ||*

**॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आयजी इत्याऽयजी । वाजऽसातमा । ता । हि । उच्चा । विऽजर्भृतः ॥ हरी इवेति हरी ऽइव । अन्धांसि । बप्सता ॥ ७ ॥

*āyajī ity ā-yajī | vāja-sātamā | tā | hi | uccā | vi-jarbhṛtaḥ || harī ivā iti harī-iva | andhāṃsi | bapsatā || 7 ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(p. 429)*

> ये उलूखलमुसले आयजी सर्वतो यज्ञसाधने वाजसातमा अतिशयेनान्नप्रदे ता ते खलूच्चा प्रौढध्वनिर्यथा भवति तथा विजर्भृतः । निशेषेण पुनःपुनर्निहारं कुरुतः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अन्धांस्यन्नानि चणकादीनि खाद्यानि बप्सता भक्षयन्तौ हरी इव इन्द्रस्याश्वाविव । अत्र यास्क एवं व्याचक्ष्व आयजी आयष्टव्ये अन्नानां संभर्तृक्रमेते हि उच्चैर्विहियेते हरी इवान्नानि भुञ्जाने । नि. ९-४२ [?] इति ॥ आयजी । यजेरौणादिकः करणे इप्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वाजसातमा । वाजं सनोतीति वाजसाः । षणु दाने । जनसनेत्यादिना विट्प्रत्ययः । विद्वनोरनुनासिकस्यादित्यात्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अतिशायनिकस्तमप् । सुपां सुलुगिति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । विजर्भृतः । हृञ् हरणे । अस्माद्यङ्लुक्‑ । अभ्यासहलादिशेषोरत्‑ जश्त्वेषु कृतेषु रुग्रिकौ च लुकि । पा. ७-४-९१ । इति रुगागमः । ततः प्रत्ययलक्षणेन धातुसंज्ञायां लटि द्विवचनं तस् । आदादिवच्चेति वचनाच्छपो लुक् । गुणे प्राप्ते क्ङिति च इति प्रतिषेधः । हृग्रहोर्भश्छन्दसीति भत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । निघातप्रतिषेधः । बप्सता । भस भर्त्सनदीप्त्योः । जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः । बभस्‑ । लटः शतृ । घसिभसोर्हलि च । पा. ६-४-१०० । इत्युपधालोपः । नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः । पा. ७-१-७८ । इति नुम्प्रतिषेधः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

*ye ulūkhalamusale āyajī sarvato yajñasādhane vājasātamā atiśayenānnaprade tā te khalūccā prauḍhadhvanir yathā bhavati tathā vijarbhṛtaḥ | niśeṣeṇa punaḥpunar nihāraṃ kurutaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | andhāṃsy annāni caṇakādīni khādyāni bapsatā bhakṣayantau harī iva indrasyāśvāv iva | atra yāska evaṃ vyācakṣva āyajī āyaṣṭavye annānāṃ saṃbhartṛkrametehi uccair vihiyete harī ivānnāni bhuñjāne | ni. 9-42 [?] iti || āyajī | yajer auṇādikaḥ karaṇe ipratyayaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | vājasātamā | vājaṃ sanotīti vājasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanety ādinā viṭpratyayaḥ | viḍvanor anunāsikasyād ityātvam | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | atiśāyanikas tamap | supāṃ suluk iti pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ | vijarbhṛtaḥ | hṛñ haraṇe | asmād yaṅluk … abhyāsahalādiśeṣorat jaśtveṣu kṛteṣu rugrikau ca luki | pā. 7-4-91 | iti rugāgamaḥ | tataḥ pratyayalakṣaṇena dhātusaṃjñāyāṃ laṭi dvivacanaṃ tas | ādādivac ceti vacanāc chapo luk | guṇe prāpte kṅiti ceti pratiṣedhaḥ | hṛgrahor bhaś chandasīti bhatvam | pratyayasvaraḥ | nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | bapsatā | bhasa bhartsanadīptyoḥ | juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ | babhas… | laṭaḥ śatṛ | ghasibhasor hali ca | pā. 6-4-100 | ity upadhālopaḥ | nābhyastāc chatuḥ | pā. 7-1-78 | iti numpratiṣedhaḥ | abhyastānām ādir ity ādyudāttatvam ||*

**Translation:** "These two, mortar and pestle — *āyajī*, the instruments of sacrifice on every side; *vājasātamā*, most bountiful givers of food — *tā te khalu* — they, indeed, *uccā* — with a loud sound — *vijarbhṛtaḥ*: they keep working back and forth, repeatedly. An illustration: like the two horses of Indra (*harī iva*) that are eating (*bapsatā*) *andhāṃsi* — grain such as gram. Here Yāska explains: '*āyajī* are things to be offered to; the two collectors of food, they move noisily up and down, like the two [horses] eating their food' (Ni. 9-42 [?]). *Āyajī*: *i* in the instrumental sense by the Uṇādi rule; the *kṛdanta* second member's accent. *Vājasātamā*: 'who gives (*sanoti*) food (*vāja*)' — *viṭ* by P. 3-2-67; *ā* for the nasal by P. 6-4-41; *tamap* in the sense of excess; *supāṃ suluk*. *Vijarbhṛtaḥ*: *hṛñ haraṇe* with *yaṅ-luk*, *rugāgama* by P. 7-4-91; the dual *tas*; the *śap* is lost as in the *adādi* class; no guṇa by P. 1-1-5; *bha* for *ha* by *hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi*; the suffix's accent; no lowering of the verb. *Bapsatā*: *bhasa bhartsanadīptyoḥ*; *śluḥ*; doubling; *śatṛ*; loss of the penultimate by P. 6-4-100; no *num* by P. 7-1-78; first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-189." *(Grammar pages 431–432, noted briefly: the words treated are* āyajī *[*ā* + *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu* + *i* in the instrumental sense (an Uṇādi suffix), the compound with the *gati* *ā* takes the *kṛdanta*-final accent by P. 6-2-139; dual *au* → *ī* by P. 7-1-39 *supāṃ suluk*; the word is end-acute],* vājasātamā *[*vājaṃ sanoti*; *ṣaṇu dāne*, *tanādi*; *viṭ* by P. 3-2-67 *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ*; the nasal of the root → *ā* by P. 6-4-41 *viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt*; *vājasā*; *tamap* + dual with *ā* by *supāṃ suluk*; the second member's accent by P. 6-2-139],* vijarbhṛtaḥ *[*hṛñ haraṇe*, *bhvādi*, here with *yaṅ-luk* — 'repeated going': doubling of the root; *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; the reduplicate's *a* by *urat* P. 7-4-66; *jaśtva* — *ja* for *ha*; the augment *ruk* by P. 7-4-91 *rugrikau ca luki*; so *jarhṛ* → the root *jarbhṛ*; *tas* for *laṭ* 3rd dual; *śap* lost; the *ṅit*-treatment blocks guṇa; *hṛ* → *bhṛ* by *hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi*; the suffix accent; the verb is not lowered since *hi* precedes (P. 8-1-34 *hi ca*)] and* bapsatā *[*bhasa bhartsanadīptyoḥ*, *juhotyādi*; *śatṛ*; *śluḥ* P. 2-4-75; *bhas* doubled — *babhas-at*; the penultimate *a* lost by P. 6-4-100 *ghasibhasajaṇasanaśāṃ…* [the print: *ghasibhasorhali ca*]; *bh* → *p* before *s* by *khari ca* P. 8-4-55 so *bapsat*; the dual *au* → *ā*; no *num* — P. 7-1-78 *nābhyastācchatuḥ*; first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-189 *abhyastānām ādiḥ*]; numerals as read, pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 430)* **आयजी (āyajī)** — the two implements of the sacrifice | **वाजसातमा (vājasātamā)** — the two great givers of food | **ता (tā)** — they, the mortar and the pestle | **हि (hi)** — [as is known] | **उच्चा (uccā)** — [making] a loud sound | **अन्धांसि (andhāṃsi)** — grains such as gram | **बप्सता (bapsatā)** — [two] that are chewing | **हरी इव (harī iva)** — like the two horses of Indra | **विजर्भृतः (vijarbhṛtaḥ)** — they sport [they move to and fro].

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** The implements of the sacrifice, which are also the givers of food, the mortar and the pestle, strike together and sound loudly, and sport like the two horses of Indra chewing their gram and the like.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> For, these two implements of sacrifice (mortar and pounder) bestowers of food are sporting like the horses of Indra chewing their fodder (grains).

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(pp. 430–431)* **आयजी** — *sarvato yajñasādhane*: the two implements of sacrifice on every side, i.e. the mortar and the pestle; this is a dual form. **वाजसातमा** — *vājaṃ sanotīti vājasāḥ*; *atiśayena vājasāḥ vājasātamau*: *vāja* means food; by giving it the mortar and the pestle are called *vājasātamā*; by pounding grain in the mortar with the help of the pestle one prepares food; so they are said to give the food and the like. **उच्चा** — *uccaiḥ*, with a loud sound: when grain is pounded with the pestle in the mortar, a loud sound is natural. **विजर्भृतः** — *hṛñ haraṇe*: they sport; they seem to sport. **हरी इव** — like Indra's horses; the two horses of Indra are called *harī*; Yāska gives the derivation *harī indrasya* ('the two bay horses of Indra'). **अन्धांसि** — foods: *andhaḥ* (Ni. [3-?]) is a name for food. **बप्सता** — *bhasa bhartsanadīptyoḥ*: eating, chewing; the sound made as horses chew gram and the like is compared to the sound made by pounding in the mortar with the pestle.

### Pages 432–435 — Sūkta 28, Rik 8

**॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ता नो अद्य वनस्पती ऋष्वावृष्वेभिः सोतृभिः ।
> इन्द्राय मधुमत्सुतम् ॥ ८ ॥

*tā no adya vanaspatī ṛṣvāv ṛṣvebhiḥ sotṛbhiḥ | indrāya madhumat sutam || 8 ||*

**॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ता । नः । अद्य । वनस्पती इति । ऋष्वौ । ऋष्वेभिः । सोतृऽभिः ॥ इन्द्राय । मधुऽमत् । सुतम् ॥ ८ ॥

*tā | naḥ | adya | vanaspatī iti | ṛṣvau | ṛṣvebhiḥ | sotṛ-bhiḥ || indrāya | madhu-mat | sutam || 8 ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(p. 433)*

> अद्यास्मिन्कर्मणि हे वनस्पती उलूखलमुसलस्वरूपौ तौ युवामृष्वेभिर्दर्शनीयैः सोतृभिरभिषवहेतुभिः सह ऋष्वौ दर्शनीयौ भूत्वेन्द्रायेन्द्रार्थं मधुमन्माधुर्योपेतं सोमद्रव्यं नोऽस्मदीयं सुतं । अभिषुणुतम् ॥ ता । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । नो अद्य । प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमिति प्रकृतिभावः । वनस्पती । उभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते आमन्त्रितस्येति सर्वानुदात्तत्वम् । प्लुतप्रगृह्या अचि । पा. ६-१-१२५ । इति प्रकृतिभावः । सुतम् । षुञ् अभिषवे । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । निघातः ॥

*adyāsmin karmaṇi he vanaspatī ulūkhalamusalasvarūpau tau yuvām ṛṣvebhir darśanīyaiḥ sotṛbhir abhiṣavahetubhiḥ saha ṛṣvau darśanīyau bhūtvendrāyendrārthaṃ madhuman mādhuryopetaṃ somadravyaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ sutaṃ | abhiṣuṇutam || tā | supāṃ suluk ity ākāraḥ | no adya | prakṛtyāntaḥpādam iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ | vanaspatī | ubhayapadaprakṛtisvare prāpte āmantritasyeti sarvānudāttatvam | plutapragṛhyā aci | pā. 6-1-125 | iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ | sutam | ṣuñ abhiṣave | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | nighātaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "Today (*adya*), in this rite, O *vanaspatī* — two [mortar and pestle] — you two, with the *ṛṣvebhiḥ* — beautiful — *sotṛbhiḥ* — pressers [the pounders], being yourselves *ṛṣvau* — beautiful — press (*sutam*) for Indra (*indrāya*) the *madhumat* — sweet — soma-substance, ours. *Tā*: *ā* by *supāṃ suluk*. *No adya*: the particle *o* in the pāda stays unchanged by P. 6-1-115. *Vanaspatī*: the dual vocative is *pragṛhya* (P. 1-1-11), so no sandhi before a vowel by P. 6-1-125. *Sutam*: *ṣuñ abhiṣave*, with the *vikaraṇa* lost; the lowering of the accent." *(Grammar pages 434–435, noted briefly: the words treated are* tā *[*tad* + dual *au*; the final *ā* by P. 7-2-102 *tyadādīnām aḥ*? and *ā* by P. 7-1-39; the lengthening of the preceding vowel; the vowel of *tā* — end],* no adya *[*naḥ* + *adya*: the *o* of the *naḥ* → *no* before *a*; P. 6-1-115 *prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare*: *prakṛtibhāva*, so the *a* of *adya* is not elided],* vanaspatī *[dual: the print explains that though the two members would each retain their accent (P. 6-2-140 *ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat*), the word, being a vocative with *āmantrita* status, is wholly anudātta by P. 8-1-19; the dual ending *ī* is *pragṛhya* by P. 1-1-11 *īdūd dvivacanaṃ pragṛhyam* so, though a vowel follows, there is no sandhi; *plutapragṛhyā aci nityam*],* sutam *[*ṣuñ abhiṣave*, *loṭ* 2nd dual *thas* → *tam* by P. 3-4-101 *tasthasthamipāṃ tāntantāmaḥ*; *śnu* lost by *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the root remains with *ṣ* → *s*; *sārvadhātuka*-*ṅit* so no guṇa; the verb is lowered since *indrāya madhumat* are acute-bearing words]; numerals as read, pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 433)* **(वनस्पती) ((vanaspatī))** — O mortar and pestle in the form of trees | **ऋष्वौ (ṛṣvau)** — [being] beautiful | **ऋष्वेभिः सोतृभिः (ṛṣvebhiḥ sotṛbhiḥ)** — with beautiful pressing-implements | **अद्य (adya)** — now | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **इन्द्राय (indrāya)** — for Indra | **मधुमत् (madhumat)** — sweet | **सुतम् (sutam)** — press out [the soma].

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** O mortar and pestle, you who are in the form of trees! Beautiful as you are, and with the beautiful pressing-implements, press out sweet soma-juice for Indra at this our rite.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Lords of the forest, (mortar and pounder) of pleasing appearance, prepare the sweet Soma-juice for Indra to drink.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(pp. 433–434)* **अद्य** — now; i.e. in the sacrificial rite we are performing. **वनस्पती** — here the mortar and pestle are addressed as in the previous rik by the word *vanaspati*; since they are made of wood, they are called *vanaspatī*. **ऋष्वौ, ऋष्वेभिः** — *darśanīyau, darśanīyaiḥ*: beautiful to look at, giving delight; *ṛṣvau* is an epithet of *vanaspatī*, *ṛṣvebhiḥ* of *sotṛbhiḥ*; the sense 'giving pleasure, desirable' may also be taken. **सोतृभिः** — with the things that press out the soma-juice, that is: the mortar, the pestle, the soma-creeper, the stone, the straining cloth, the *kalaśa* (jar) which receives the juice, and so on. **मधुमत्** — *mādhuryopetam*: of sweet, tasty soma-juice. **सुतम्** — *sunoti*, the dual *loṭ* second person of the root.

### Pages 435–437 — Sūkta 28, Rik 9 *(closing rik; the Soma is poured into the cow-hide filter)*

**॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥**

> उच्छिष्टं चम्वोर्भर सोमं पवित्र आ सृज ।
> नि धेहि गोरधि त्वचि ॥ ९ ॥

*ucchiṣṭaṃ camvor bhara somaṃ pavitra ā sṛja | ni dhehi gor adhi tvaci || 9 ||*

**॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥**

> उत् । शिष्टम् । चम्वोः । भर । सोमम् । पवित्रे । आ । सृज ॥ नि । धेहि । गोः । अधि । त्वचि ॥ ९ ॥

*ut | śiṣṭam | camvoḥ | bhara | somam | pavitre | ā | sṛja || ni | dhehi | goḥ | adhi | tvaci || 9 ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(p. 435)*

> हे ऋत्विग्विशेष हरिश्चन्द्र वा चम्वोः सोमस्य भक्षणसंपादकयोरधिषवणफलकयोः शिष्टमभिषवावशिष्टं सोममुद्धर । शकटत्यक्तमस्योपरि हर [?] । पवित्रे दशापवित्रे आ सृज । आनीय प्रक्षिप । प्रक्षेपे सत्यवशिष्टं सोमं गोस्त्वचि आनडुहे चर्मण्यधि नि धेहि । अध्यारोप्य स्थापय ॥ चम्वोः । चमु अदने । चम्यते भक्ष्यतेऽत्रेति चमूः । कृषिचमितनिधनीति । उ. १-८१ । ऊप्रत्ययः । तिङादि उप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । सप्तमीद्विवचनस्योदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरित इति स्वरितत्वम् । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति नास्ति नियम इति …। भर । हृञ् हरणे । हृग्रहोर्भः । धेहि । ध्वसोरेद्धावभ्यासलोपश्च । पा. ६-४-११९ । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ । निघातः । त्वचि । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥

*he ṛtvigviśeṣa hariścandra vā camvoḥ somasya bhakṣaṇasaṃpādakayor adhiṣavaṇaphalakayoḥ śiṣṭam abhiṣavāvaśiṣṭaṃ somam uddhara | śakaṭatyaktam asyopari hara [?] | pavitre daśāpavitre ā sṛja | ānīya prakṣipa | prakṣepe satyavaśiṣṭaṃ somaṃ gostvaci ānaḍuhe carmaṇy adhi ni dhehi | adhyāropya sthāpaya || camvoḥ | camu adane | camyate bhakṣyate 'treti camūḥ | kṛṣicamitanidhanī | u. 1-81 | ūpratyayaḥ | tiṅādi upratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | saptamīdvivacanasyodāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarita iti svaritatvam | udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti nāsti niyama iti … | bhara | hṛñ haraṇe | hṛgrahor bhaḥ | dhehi | dhvasor eddhāv abhyāsalopaś ca | pā. 6-4-119 | ity etvābhyāsalopau | nighātaḥ | tvaci | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvam ||*

**Translation:** "O priest [or Hariścandra]! Take up (*ud bhara*) the *śiṣṭam* — the remaining — soma left over after pressing, in the *camvoḥ* — the two pressing-boards that provide the soma [literally 'the eating']; [carry] what remains over to the [filter]. Pour (*ā sṛja*) it into the *pavitra* — the ten-fringed filter. Having brought it, put it in; and then place the remaining soma on (*adhi ni dhehi*) the cow's hide (*goḥ tvaci*) — the ox-skin: set it on top. *Camvoḥ*: *camu adane*; 'that in which it is eaten [drunk] is *camū*'; the suffix *ū* by Uṇ. 1-81; the accent of the suffix; the dual locative's acute and *yaṇ* → *svarita* by P. 8-2-4. *Bhara*: *hṛñ haraṇe*, with *bha* for *ha*. *Dhehi*: *dhā* + *hi* with *e* and loss of the reduplicate by P. 6-4-119; the lowering. *Tvaci*: the case-ending's acute by *sāvekāca*." *(Grammar pages 436–437, noted briefly: the words treated are* camvoḥ *[*camu adane*, *bhvādi* — 'that in which one drinks/eats'; *ū* by Uṇ. 1-81 *kṛṣicamitanidhanisaṃtanikaṭibhyaḥ ūḥ*? — the Uṇ. rule gives the *ū*-suffix; the locative dual *os*: the *ū* → *v* by P. 6-4-77; the accent of the suffix; by P. 8-2-4 the *yaṇ* of an *udātta* becomes *svarita*; the print adds a scholastic argument on P. 6-1-174 *udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt* — whether the ending takes the acute — read as: the ending is not acute here because the *yaṇ* is preceded by a vowel],* bhara *[*hṛñ haraṇe*, *bhvādi*; *loṭ* 2nd singular *hi*, lost by P. 6-4-105; *ha* → *bha* by P. 7-4-… *hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi*; guṇa],* dhehi *[*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*, *juhotyādi*; *loṭ* 2nd singular *sip* → *hi*; *śap* → *śluḥ* P. 2-4-75; doubling P. 6-1-10; *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; *jaśtva*; *dadhā* + *hi* → *dhehi* by P. 6-4-119 *ghvasoreddhāv abhyāsalopaś ca*: the root's *ā* → *e*, the reduplicate lost; the verb is lowered by P. 8-1-28] and* tvaci *[*tvac* + *ṅi*; the acute on the ending by P. 6-1-168 *sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ*]; numerals as read, pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 436)* **शिष्टम् (śiṣṭam)** — the remaining [soma, left unpressed] | **चम्वोः (camvoḥ)** — in the two vessels [boards] | **उद्भर (ud bhara)** — bring up | **सोमम् (somam)** — the soma-juice | **पवित्रे (pavitre)** — in the filter | **आ सृज (ā sṛja)** — pour it | **गोः त्वचि (goḥ tvaci)** — on the cow-hide | **अधि नि धेहि (adhi ni dhehi)** — place it above.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** Take what remains of the soma in the two vessels; pour the juice into the strainer; and place it on the cow-hide.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Fill the remaining Soma in the two jars, pour it on the sieve, and put it on the cow-hide.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 436–437)* In this rik the seer, addressing Hariścandra, the sacrificer, or some priest (the *adhvaryu*, perhaps), tells him what is to be done with the remaining soma. **उच्छिष्टम्** — *śiṣṭam*, the remainder: the soma-creeper is placed in the mortar and crushed, and the juice, standing on top of the stone (*grāvan*), flows down; the remainder, small in amount, is what stays in the mortar [and on the boards]. **चम्वोः** — *camū* is a wooden vessel used in the soma-pressing, used for offering the soma to the gods; here it means the two wooden boards (*adhiṣavaṇa-phalaka*) between which the soma-creeper is pressed. Skandasvāmin explains *camasa* as the drinking-vessel of the priests; the dual here, by *vyatyaya*, stands for 'the two *camasa* vessels'. **पवित्रे** — Yāska explains *pavitra* as 'what purifies' (*punāti*), listing its many senses — *mantra*, ray, water, fire — but here it must be understood as the filter or sieve with which the soma-juice is strained. In some places *kuśa* grass is placed over the vessel in which the soma is strained, and the juice is poured over it so that the pure juice falls into the vessel; hence *pavitra* here means the 'filter'. **गोः त्वचि** — on the cow-hide: besides pouring the soma into *droṇakalaśa* and other wooden vessels, there are descriptions in the Ṛgveda of the soma being poured on a sieve made of cow-hide, or of the hide being spread under the stalks, so that the juice falls on it and goes down — so a cow-hide was used in the soma-pressing.

**॥ Close of Sūkta 28 ॥** *(p. 437: the grammar of Rik 9 ends without a colophon; printed p. 438 begins Sūkta 29. The printed page 437 carries no closing note of the usual kind; I note this rather than supply one.)*
**[Correction note on Sūkta 28's close.]** *Printed p. 438 opens with the last lines of the Rik 9 grammar of Sūkta 28 (on* tvaci*) followed by the large closing line "The twenty-eighth sūkta is ended" (Kannada: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೆಂಟನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಸಮಾಪ್ತವಾಗಿದೆ). The note written at the end of Sūkta 28 above said that no colophon was printed and that the sūkta ended on p. 437; that was wrong — the sūkta ends on p. 438 with this colophon (varga number not given). Earlier text is left untouched, as the file is append-only.*

## ॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 29 — *"yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ"* ("The Twenty-ninth Sūkta"; sixth sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)

*(Printed pp. 438 lower half–446. The introductory note is on p. 438, the heading block on p. 439; Rik 1 begins on p. 439.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 438)** *(read at 130 dpi; doubtful words marked [?])*

> यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इति षष्ठं सूक्तं सप्तर्चं शुनःशेपस्यार्षं पाङ्क्तमैन्द्रम् । अनुक्रमणिका च — यच्चिद्धि सप्त पाङ्क्तमिति ॥ पृष्ठ्यषडहस्य पञ्चमेऽहनि माध्यंदिने सवने होत्रका यच्चिद्धीति सप्तर्चं सूक्तं त्रींस्तृचानन्त्यात्सस्सशस्त्र एकैकं तृचमावपेरन् । चतुर्थेऽहनीति खण्डे यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इत्येकैकमेवमेव । आ. ८-११ [?] इति सूत्रितम् ॥

*yac cid dhi satya somapā iti ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ saptarcaṃ śunaḥśepasyārṣaṃ pāṅktam aindram | anukramaṇikā ca — yac cid dhi sapta pāṅktam iti || pṛṣṭhyaṣaḍahasya pañcame 'hani mādhyaṃdine savane hotrakā yac cid dhīti saptarcaṃ sūktaṃ trīṃs tṛcān antyāt sas[ta]śastra ekaikaṃ tṛcam āvaperan [?] | caturthe 'hanīti khaṇḍe yac cid dhi satya somāpā ity ekaikam evam eva | ā. 8-11 [?] iti sūtritam ||*

**Translation:** "The sixth sūkta, beginning *yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ*, has seven riks; its seer is Śunaḥśepa; the metre is Pankti; the deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā too says: '*yac cid dhi* — seven, Pāṅkta.' In the *Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, on the fifth day, at the midday pressing, the *hotrakas* [assistants of the Hotṛ] recite the seven-rik sūkta *yac cid dhi*; [taking] one triplet each [?] … in the section *caturthe 'hani* … (Āś. 8-11 [?]) — so it is laid down. [The reading of this note is partly doubtful.]"

**॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥** *(p. 438)* *Yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ* is the sixth sūkta of the sixth anuvāka and has seven riks. Śunaḥśepa is the seer; the metre is Pankti. The Anukramaṇikā says '*yac cid dhi sapta pāṅktam*', that is, the sūkta *yac cid dhi* has seven riks. In the Soma-sacrifice called *Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, on the fifth day, at the *mādhyandina-savana* (midday pressing), three priests who are assistants of the Hotṛ (the *hotrakas*) are to take the three triplets of this sūkta — *tṛca*, *tṛca*, [and the remaining rik] — and use them, each at his own *śastra* recitation: so it is explained in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra in the section *caturthe 'hani*, in the sūtra *yac cid dhi satya somapā* (Āś. [8-11]).

**॥ Heading block of the sūkta (p. 439) ॥**

> मण्डल १ — अनुवाक ६ — सूक्त २९ । अष्टक १ — अध्याय २ — वर्ग [२५?] [?] । ऋक्संख्या ७ ।
> ऋषिः — शुनःशेप आजीगर्तिः । देवता — इन्द्रः । छन्दः — पङ्क्तिः ।

*Maṇḍala 1 — Anuvāka 6 — Sūkta 29. Aṣṭaka 1 — Adhyāya 2 — Varga [25?] [?]. Riks: 7. Ṛṣi: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti. Devatā: Indra. Metre: Pankti.* *(Varga numeral read at 130 dpi, marked [?].)*

### Pages 439–442 — Sūkta 29, Rik 1

**॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥**

> यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा अनाशस्ता इव स्मसि ।
> आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥ १ ॥

*yac cid dhi satya somapā anāśastā iva smasi | ā tū na indra śaṃsaya goṣv aśveṣu śubhriṣu sahasreṣu tuvīmagha || 1 ||*

**॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥**

> यत् । चित् । हि । सत्य । सोमऽपाः । अनाशस्ताःऽइव । स्मसि ॥ आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ १ ॥

*yat | cit | hi | satya | soma-pāḥ | anāśastāḥ-iva | smasi || ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 1 ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(pp. 439–440)*

> विश्वैर्देवैः प्रेरितः शुनःशेप एतदादिकाभिर्द्वाविंशतिसंख्याकाभिर्ग्भिरिन्द्रं तुष्टाव । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् — तं विश्वे देवा ऊचुरिन्द्रो वै देवानामोजिष्ठो बलिष्ठः सहिष्ठः सत्तमः पारयिष्णुतममस्मिन्नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स इन्द्रं तुष्टाव यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इत्येतेन सूक्तेनोत्तरस्य च पञ्चदशभिः । ऐ. ब्रा. २-१८ [?] इति ॥ हे सोमपाः सोमस्य पातः सत्य सत्यवादिन्निन्द्र यच्चिद्धि यद्यपि वयमनाशस्ता इव स्मसि अप्रशस्ता इव भवामः तथापि हे तुवीमघ बहुधनेन्द्र त्वं गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु शोभनेषु सहस्रेषु सहस्रसंख्याकेषु च निमित्तभूतेषु नोऽस्मान्शंसय । सर्वतः प्रशस्तान्कुरु । अस्मद्दोषमनपेक्ष्य गवादीन्दत्त्वेत्यर्थः ॥ सोमपाः । … अनाशस्ता इव । शंसु स्तुतौ । निष्ठेति क्तः … नञ्समासः । स्मसि । अस भुवि … तुवीमघ । …

*viśvair devaiḥ preritaḥ śunaḥśepa etadādikābhir dvāviṃśatisaṃkhyākābhir gbhir indraṃ tuṣṭāva | tathā ca brāhmaṇam — taṃ viśve devā ūcur indro vai devānām ojiṣṭho baliṣṭhaḥ sahiṣṭhaḥ sattamaḥ pārayiṣṇutamam asminn u stuhy atha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa indraṃ tuṣṭāva yac cid dhi satya somapā ity etena sūktenottarasya ca pañcadaśabhiḥ | ai. brā. 2-18 [?] iti || he somapāḥ somasya pātaḥ satya satyavādinn indra yac cid dhi yady api vayam anāśastā iva smasi apraśastā iva bhavāmaḥ tathāpi he tuvīmagha bahudhanendra tvaṃ goṣv aśveṣu śubhriṣu śobhaneṣu sahasreṣu sahasrasaṃkhyākeṣu ca nimittabhūteṣu no 'smān śaṃsaya | sarvataḥ praśastān kuru | asmaddoṣam anapekṣya gavādīn dattvety arthaḥ || somapāḥ | … anāśastā iva | śaṃsu stutau | niṣṭheti ktaḥ … nañsamāsaḥ | smasi | asa bhuvi … tuvīmagha | …*

**Translation:** "Impelled by the Viśvedevas, Śunaḥśepa praised Indra with the twenty-two riks beginning with this one. So the Brāhmaṇa says: 'The Viśvedevas said to him: "Indra is the most vigorous, the strongest, the mightiest, the best, the most capable of carrying across of the gods; praise him now; then we shall release you." He praised Indra with the sūkta *yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ* and fifteen [riks] of the next' (Ai. Brā. 2-18 [?]). O *somapāḥ* — drinker of soma! *Satya* — truth-speaking Indra! *Yac cid dhi* — although we are *anāśastā iva* — as if undeserving of praise, as if unworthy — yet, O *tuvīmagha* — O Indra of much wealth — *śaṃsaya*: make us praised on all sides *goṣu aśveṣu* — with cows, with horses — *śubhriṣu* — good ones — *sahasreṣu* — in thousands: the sense is: giving us cows and the like without regard to our fault." *(Grammar pages 441–442, noted briefly: the words treated are* somapāḥ *[*somaṃ pibati*, *pā pāne*, *bhvādi*; *viṭ* by P. 3-2-67/*ātaś ca* [print: P. 3-2-74 *ato manin-kvanip-vanipaś ca* is read as *ato mani…*]; all letters lost in *viṭ*; the *ā*-ending word; in the vocative the lowering by P. 8-1-19],* anāśastā iva *[*śaṃsu stutau*; *kta* by P. 3-2-102 *niṣṭhā*; the *iṭ* is optionally blocked by P. 7-2-15 *yasya vibhāṣā*, so no *iṭ* here; loss of the nasal by P. 6-4-24; *śasta*; the *nañ* compound: the first member's accent by P. 6-2-2; the *n* lost, P. 6-3-73 *nalopo nañaḥ*, and the *ā* before the *tatpuruṣa* is by *tasmān nuḍ aci*; the accent: by P. 6-2-172 *nañsubhyām* the second member would take the end-acute, but the first member's accent is kept],* smasi *[*as bhuvi*, *adādi*; *laṭ* 1st plural *mas* → *masi*; *a* of *as* lost by P. 6-4-111 *śnasor allopaḥ*; *s* + *masi* → the augment *iṭ*-less … *smasi*],* tū na *[*tu* lengthened before *na* in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-133 *ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām*],* goṣu *[*go* + *sup*: the acute that P. 6-1-168 would give to the ending is blocked by P. 6-1-182 *na gośvansāvavarṇarāḍaṅkrukṛtkṛdbhyaḥ*, so the first syllable is acute],* aśveṣu *[*aśū vyāptau* + *kvan* by Uṇ. 1-151 *aśipruṣiliṭikaṇikhaṭivišipatibhyaḥ kvan* — *aśva*; *kvan* is *nit* — first-syllable acute] and* śubhriṣu *[*śubha dīptau* + *krin* by Uṇ. 4-… *adibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin*; locative plural; being *nit*, the first syllable would be acute, but by *vyatyaya* the end-acute — middle-acute, *śubhriṣu*]; numerals as read, pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 440)* **सोमपाः (somapāḥ)** — O drinker of soma | **सत्य (satya)** — O truth-speaking | **इन्द्र (indra)** — O Indra | **यत् चित् हि (yat cit hi)** — if perchance | **अनाशस्ताः इव स्मसि (anāśastāḥ iva smasi)** — we are as if unworthy | **तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha)** — O one of abundant wealth | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **सहस्रेषु (sahasreṣu)** — in thousands | **शुभ्रिषु (śubhriṣu)** — auspicious | **गोषु (goṣu)** — cows | **अश्वेषु (aśveṣu)** — horses | **आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya)** — make [us] fit to receive [the praise-worthy].

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** O truth-speaking Indra, drinker of soma! Although we are not worthy of obtaining your wealth, you, who have abundant wealth, make us worthy of thousands of auspicious cows and horses, and fill us with your riches.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O truth-speaking Indra, drinker of Soma juice, although we do not deserve it, yet you Indra, of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 441)* Śunaḥśepa, having prayed to the Viśvedevas with the rik *namo mahadbhyaḥ*, [was told by them:] "Śunaḥśepa, among the gods Indra is the strongest, the most glorious, the most patient (*sahiṣṇu*); praise him, so that you may be released from this bond"; and, with their consent, Śunaḥśepa praises Indra with this sūkta *yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ* and with the next fifteen riks of the sūkta *kaya* [*kadā*?] *yathā* — twenty-two riks in all. (Ai. Brā. [2-18]). We have explained this matter in the Śunaḥśepa story itself.

**सत्य** — *satyavādin*: one who speaks truth. **सोमपाः** — *somasya pātā*: the drinker of soma. **अनाशस्ता इव** — *anāśastā iva apraśastā iva*: [*śaṃsu stutau*] unworthy of praise: we are, in praising you, not fit [for it]; yet because we praise you, may you be pleased and give us the cows and horses we need. **आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ** — the sense of *śaṃsaya* — 'make [us] praiseworthy among cows and horses' — appears to be: 'give us thousands of cows and horses, and make us renowned as persons possessing them'. **तुवीमघ** — *tuvi* means 'much' (Ni. [3-?]), *magha* means 'wealth' (Ni. [2-10?]); hence *tuvīmagha* is 'having much wealth'.

### Pages 443–445 — Sūkta 29, Rik 2

**॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥**

> शिप्रिन्वाजानां पते शचीवस्तव दंसना ।
> आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥ २ ॥

*śiprin vājānāṃ pate śacīvas tava daṃsanā | ā tū na indra śaṃsaya goṣv aśveṣu śubhriṣu sahasreṣu tuvīmagha || 2 ||*

**॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥**

> शिप्रिन् । वाजानाम् । पते । शचीवः । तव । दंसना ॥ आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ २ ॥

*śiprin | vājānām | pate | śacīvaḥ | tava | daṃsanā || ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 2 ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(p. 443)*

> हे शचीवः शक्तिमन्शिप्रिन्शोभनहनुयुक्त वाजानां पते अन्नानां पालकेन्द्र तव दंसना कर्मविशेषोऽनुग्रहरूपः सर्वदा वर्तते । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ शिप्रिन् । शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । नि. ६-१७ [?] इति यास्कः । आतो ऽनिनौ । मत्वर्थीये इनिः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । वाजानां पते । सुबामन्त्रित इति परागवद्भावात्षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितसमुदायनिघातः । न चामन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदिति शिप्रिन्नित्यस्याविद्यमानत्वेन पदादपरत्वात्पादादित्वाच्च न निघातः । नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनमित्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधात् । शचीवः । छन्दसीर इति मतुपो वत्वम् । मतुवसोरुरिति रुत्वे खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः । पा. ८-३-१५ । पादादित्वादामन्त्रितनिघाताभावः ॥

*he śacīvaḥ śaktimañ śiprin śobhanahanuyukta vājānāṃ pate annānāṃ pālakendra tava daṃsanā karmaviśeṣo 'nugraharūpaḥ sarvadā vartate | anyat pūrvavat || śiprin | śipre hanū nāsike vā | ni. 6-17 [?] iti yāskaḥ | āto 'ninau | matvarthīye iniḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | vājānāṃ pate | subāmantrita iti parāṅgavadbhāvāt ṣaṣṭhyāmantritasamudāyanighātaḥ | na cāmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavad iti śiprinn ity asyāvidyamānatvena padād aparatvāt pādāditvāc ca na nighātaḥ | nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam ity avidyamānavattvapratiṣedhāt | śacīvaḥ | chandasīra iti matupo vatvam | matuvasor ru iti rutve kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ | pā. 8-3-15 | pādāditvād āmantritanighātābhāvaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O *śacīvaḥ* — powerful! *Śiprin* — fair-jawed! *Vājānāṃ pate* — lord of foods, protector of food, Indra! Your *daṃsanā* — your special acts of favour — are always present. The rest is as before. *Śiprin*: '*śipre* are the two jaws or the nose' says Yāska (Ni. 6-17 [?]); *ini* in the sense of possession. *Vājānāṃ pate*: the vocative group is lowered as a whole ... [argument on whether *śiprin* is treated as non-existent: it is not, by P. 8-1-74 *nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam*]. *Śacīvaḥ*: *v* for *m* of *matup* in the Veda; *s* → *ru* by P. 8-2-… ; *visarga* by P. 8-3-15." *(Grammar pages 444–445, noted briefly: the words treated are* śiprin *[*śipra* + *ini* in the sense 'possessing' by P. 5-2-115 *ata ini-ṭhanau*, *śipre asya stha iti śipri*; the vocative with first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-198],* vājānāṃ pate *[*pate* is a vocative; P. 2-1-2 *subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare* makes the preceding genitive part of the vocative group, which is lowered as a whole; the question is then raised whether *śiprin*, a vocative before it, makes the group non-initial and so lowered; the answer: since *śiprin* and *pate* are co-referential (*samānādhikaraṇa*), P. 8-1-74 prevents *śiprin* from being treated as non-existent (*avidyamānavat*) — so the group *vājānāṃ pate*, standing at the head of the pāda, is not lowered (P. 8-1-18 *āpādādau*)],* śacīvaḥ *[*śacī asya asti* — *matup*; *m* → *v* by P. 8-2-15 *chandasīraḥ* [after a stem ending in *ī*, *r* …]; *ru* by P. 8-2-66; vocative; the *visarga* before a pause by P. 8-3-15 *kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ*; the accent is first-syllable because it is at the head of the pāda]; numerals as read, pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 443)* **शचीवः (śacīvaḥ)** — O powerful | **शिप्रिन् (śiprin)** — O fair-jawed | **वाजानां पते (vājānāṃ pate)** — O lord of foods | **इन्द्र (indra)** — O Indra | **तव (tava)** — your | **दंसना (daṃsanā)** — [favourable] acts | **[सर्वदा] ([sarvadā])** — always | **नः (naḥ)** — to us | **सहस्रेषु (sahasreṣu)** — in thousands | **शुभ्रिषु (śubhriṣu)** — of auspicious | **गोषु अश्वेषु (goṣu aśveṣu)** — cows and horses | **तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha)** — O one of abundant wealth | **आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya)** — [make us] worthy.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** O Indra — powerful, handsome, the lord and protector of foods! Your favour toward us is constant. Therefore, O Indra of abundant wealth, make us fit to receive thousands of auspicious cows and horses, and fill us with your wealth.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Handsome and mighty lord of food, your exploits are ever before us; therefore, Indra of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 444)* **शिप्रिन्** — *śobhanahanu-yukta*: one with fair jaws, i.e. a good mouth, good-looking. **शचीवः, दंसना** — the words *śacī* and *daṃsas* are read among the twenty-six names for 'act' beginning *apaḥ, apnaḥ* (Ni. [2-1]); hence *śacīvaḥ* means 'one with strength, powerful', and *daṃsanā* 'a bold act, or favour in the form of an act'.

### Pages 445–448 — Sūkta 29, Rik 3

**॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥**

> नि ष्वापया मिथूदृशा सस्तामबुध्यमाने ।
> आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥ ३ ॥

*ni ṣvāpayā mithūdṛśā sastām abudhyamāne | ā tū na indra śaṃsaya goṣv aśveṣu śubhriṣu sahasreṣu tuvīmagha || 3 ||*

**॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥**

> नि । स्वापय । मिथूऽदृशा । सस्ताम् । अबुध्यमाने इति । आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ ३ ॥

*ni | svāpaya | mithū-dṛśā | sastām | abudhyamāne iti | ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 3 ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(p. 446)*

> मिथूदृशा परस्परं संगतेत्वेन दृश्यमाने यमदूत्यौ नि स्वापय । नितरां सुप्ते कुरु । ते चास्मान्मारयितुमबुध्यमाने सत्यौ सस्तां निद्रां प्राप्नुताम् । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ नि ष्वापय । सुषामादित्वात्षत्वम् । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घः । मिथूदृशा । मिथुनतया मिथुनरूपेण पश्येते इति मिथूदृशा । क्विप्च । दृशेः कर्तरि क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पूर्ववत्तस्य पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घः । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । सस्ताम् । वस स्वप्ने । लोटि तसस्ताम् । आदिप्रभृत्यः शपः । इति शपो लुक् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । पादादित्वान्नि घाताभावः । अबुध्यमाने । नञ्समासेऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

*mithūdṛśā parasparaṃ saṃgatetvena dṛśyamāne yamadūtyau ni svāpaya | nitarāṃ supte kuru | te cāsmān mārayitum abudhyamāne satyau sastāṃ nidrāṃ prāpnutām | anyat pūrvavat || ni ṣvāpaya | suṣāmādityāt ṣatvam | anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti dīrghaḥ | mithūdṛśā | mithunatayā mithunarūpeṇa paśyete iti mithūdṛśā | kvip ca | dṛśeḥ kartari kvip | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | pūrvavat tasya pūrvapadasya dīrghaḥ | supāṃ suluk iti vibhakter ākāraḥ | sastām | vasa svapne | loṭi tasastām | ādiprabhṛtyaḥ śapaḥ | iti śapo luk | pratyayasvaraḥ | pādāditvān nighātābhāvaḥ | abudhyamāne | nañsamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||*

**Translation:** "Put to sleep (*ni svāpaya*) the two *yamadūtyau* [female messengers of Yama] who appear (*dṛśyamāne*) together (*mithūdṛśā*), in a pair; make them fall into deep sleep; and may they, *abudhyamāne* — not waking — to kill us, *sastām* — sleep. The rest as before. *Ni ṣvāpaya*: *ṣa* since *su*-... belongs to the *suṣāmādi* group; lengthening [*svāpaya*] by P. 6-3-137. *Mithūdṛśā*: 'the two who see in pairs'; *kvip* of *dṛś* in the sense of agent; the preceding member is lengthened; the dual ending *ā* by *supāṃ suluk*. *Sastām*: *vasa svapne* ['to sleep'], *loṭ* 3rd dual *tām*; *śap* lost by P. 2-4-72; the suffix accent; no lowering since at the head of the pāda. *Abudhyamāne*: in the *nañ*-compound the first member's accent." *(Grammar pages 447–448, noted briefly: the words treated are* ni ṣvāpaya *[*ṣvap śaye*, *ṇic*; *ṣatva* in *ni ṣvāpaya* by P. 8-3-65 [*upasargāt sunoti…*] / P. 8-3-… *suṣāmādiṣu ca* — here *ṣa* appears because *svāpaya* is read in the *suṣāmādi* list; the lengthening by P. 6-3-137 *anyeṣām api dṛśyate*],* mithūdṛśā *[*mithunatayā paśyataḥ* — 'seeing as a pair'; *dṛś* + *kvip* by P. 3-2-61 *satsūdviṣadruhaduhayujavidabhidachidajinīrājām upasargepi kvip*; all lost; compound with the upapada *mithuna*; the preceding member lengthened (*mithū*) by P. 6-3-116 *ṛtvijaḥ…* [*kvau*]; the accent: *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* P. 6-2-139 — the *kṛdanta* second member's accent, with the *ṛ* — *dṛ* acute; the dual ending *au* → *ā* by *supāṃ suluk*],* sastām *[*vasa svapne*? — the print gives the root as *ṣasa svapne* (*adādi*), *loṭ* 3rd dual *tām*; the *tām* by P. 3-4-101; *śap* lost by P. 2-4-72 *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*; the *s* of the root with the augment…: *sastām*; the verb is not lowered since it begins the pāda? — here it stands in the middle but follows a *nañ*-word; numerals not read] and* abudhyamāne *[*budha avagamane*, *divādi*; *śānac* in the middle with *yak*; the *nañ*-tatpuruṣa with *avyaya* first member keeps its own accent, P. 6-2-2]; numerals as read, pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 446)* **मिथूदृशा (mithūdṛśā)** — the two who look at each other [the two messengers of Yama] | **निस्वापय (ni svāpaya)** — put to sleep | **अबुध्यमाने (abudhyamāne)** — not awakening | **सस्ताम् (sastām)** — let [them] sleep | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **इन्द्र (indra)** — O Indra | **सहस्रेषु (sahasreṣu)** — in thousands | **शुभ्रिषु (śubhriṣu)** — of auspicious | **गोषु अश्वेषु (goṣu aśveṣu)** — cows and horses | **तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha)** — one of abundant wealth | **आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya)** — [make us] worthy.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** Send to sleep the two female messengers of Yama, who have come to kill us and who look at each other, so that they do not wake again. And, O Indra of abundant wealth, make us fit for thousands of auspicious cows and horses.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Send to sleep the two females that see each other, let them sleep and not be wakeful; Indra, of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(pp. 446–447)* The sense of this rik is not clear. The commentator says: Śunaḥśepa, who is expecting death, prays to Indra that the two female messengers of Yama who may come to take away his life at the time of his death should not do so, but fall asleep without waking. Both the commentator and Skandasvāmin explain the sense by supplying words here and there. In the rik there is no word *yamadūtī* ('Yama's messenger') nor any word suggesting the time of death; the rik speaks only of two persons — females — looking at each other: *abudhyamāne* is feminine dual; hence the commentator says that *mithūdṛśā* is 'the two Yama-messengers looking at each other' [by supplying the word]. The seer's intention is not clear.

**नि स्वापय** — *nitarāṃ supte kuru*: put them into a deep sleep. **मिथूदृशा** — *mithunatayā paśyantī* [those who see as a pair]: two persons seeing each other: the word *yamadūtyau* ('two messengers of Yama') the commentator supplies; this is a dual word. **सस्ताम्** — *vasa svapne*: 'let them sleep'. **अबुध्यमाने** — [two] not waking: a dual word.
### Pages 448–450 — Sūkta 29, Rik 4

**॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ससन्तु त्या अरातयो बोधन्तु शूर रातयः ।
> आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥ ४ ॥

*sasantu tyā arātayo bodhantu śūra rātayaḥ | ā tū na indra śaṃsaya goṣv aśveṣu śubhriṣu sahasreṣu tuvīmagha || 4 ||*

**॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ससन्तु । त्याः । अरातयः । बोधन्तु । शूर । रातयः ॥ आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ ४ ॥

*sasantu | tyāḥ | arātayaḥ | bodhantu | śūra | rātayaḥ || ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 4 ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(p. 448)*

> त्या अस्माभिरदृश्यमानाः परोक्षाः शास्त्राः आरातयोऽदानशीलाः शत्रवः सत्वन्तु निद्रां कुर्वन्तु । हे शूर शौर्ययुक्तेन्द्र रातयो दानशीला बन्धवो बोधन्तु अस्मान्पृथ्यंताम् [?] । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ सस॑न्तु । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अरातयः । रा दाने । मन्त्रे वृषेषपचेति भावे क्तिन् । न विद्यते रातिर्येष्विति बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । नञ्सुभ्यामित्यादि सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति न भवति । यद्वा । क्रीङ्क्ता च संज्ञायामिति कर्तरि क्तिच् । नञ्समासेऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । बोधन्तु । पादादित्वात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघाताभावः ॥

*tyā asmābhir adṛśyamānāḥ parokṣāḥ [śāstrāḥ?] ārātayo 'dānaśīlāḥ śatravaḥ sasantu nidrāṃ kurvantu | he śūra śauryayuktendra rātayo dānaśīlā bandhavo bodhantu asmān pṛthyaṃtām [?] | anyat pūrvavat || sasantu | pratyayasvaraḥ | arātayaḥ | rā dāne | mantre vṛṣeṣapaceti bhāve ktin | na vidyate rātir yeṣv iti bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | nañsubhyām ity ādi sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyanta iti na bhavati | yadvā | krīṅktā ca saṃjñāyām iti kartari ktic | nañsamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | bodhantu | pādāditvāt tiṅ atiṅa iti nighātābhāvaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "Those enemies of ours, unseen — out of sight [the word *śāstrāḥ* is doubtful here] — *arātayaḥ*, niggardly, may they *sasantu* — sleep, fall into slumber. O *śūra* — heroic Indra! May [our] *rātayaḥ* — generous kinsmen — wake (*bodhantu*) [to us] [the last words doubtful]. The rest as before. *Arātayaḥ*: *rā dāne*; *ktin* in the sense of the action by P. 3-3-97 [the *mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrāḥ* rule]; a *bahuvrīhi* 'in whom there is no giving' with the first member's accent; the rules beginning *nañsubhyām* are optional in the Veda, so [the end-acute] does not apply; or *ktic* in the agent sense by [*kriṅktā ca saṃjñāyām*]. *Bodhantu*: no lowering because it begins the pāda." *(Grammar pages 449–450, noted briefly: the words treated are* sasantu *[*vasa svapne*? — the print has *ṣasa svapne*, *adādi*; *loṭ* 3rd plural *jhi* → *antu*; the *jhi*'s *anta* by P. 7-1-3 *jho 'ntaḥ*; doubling of the root is not done for *adādi* here; the accent: the root's, middle-acute through the suffix],* arātayaḥ *[*rā dāne*, *adādi*; *ktin* by P. 3-3-97 *mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ*; *rāti*; the *nañ*-bahuvrīhi *na vidyate rātir yeṣu*: the first member's accent by P. 6-2-1 *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*; the end-acute by P. 6-2-172 *nañsubhyām* is not taken since *sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante*; or alternatively *ktic* by P. 3-3-174 *kriñ ktic ca saṃjñāyām* and the *nañ*-tatpuruṣa with *avyaya* — P. 6-2-2 — first member's accent; so *arātayaḥ* is first-syllable acute] and* bodhantu *[*budha avagamane*, *bhvādi*; *loṭ* 3rd plural; *śap* anudātta; the root's accent; the verb stands at the head of the pāda so it is not lowered, P. 8-1-18]; numerals as read, pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 449)* **शूर (śūra)** — O valiant Indra | **त्याः (tyāḥ)** — those [unseen, remote] | **अरातयः (arātayaḥ)** — enemies who do not give | **सस॑न्तु (sasantu)** — let them sleep | **रातयः (rātayaḥ)** — [our] generous friends | **बोधन्तु (bodhantu)** — let them awake [be alert, to know us] | **तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha)** — O one of abundant wealth | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **सहस्रेषु शुभ्रिषु (sahasreṣu śubhriṣu)** — in thousands of auspicious | **गोषु अश्वेषु (goṣu aśveṣu)** — cows and horses | **आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya)** — [make us] worthy.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** O valiant Indra! May those enemies of ours, who are out of sight, fall asleep there, so that they do not know of us; and may our generous friends be wakeful, so that they know us. And, O Indra of abundant wealth, make us fit for thousands of auspicious cows and horses.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O hero, may our enemies sleep and our friends be wakeful; Indra, of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 449)* **त्याः** — *tya* is a word of the sense of *tad*; hence *tyāḥ* means 'those' (*tāḥ*). **रातयः, अरातयः** — *rā dāne*: *adānaśīlāḥ* are *arātayaḥ*. The root *rā* has the sense of giving; so those who give to us, who help, are *rātayaḥ*, 'friends'; those who give us nothing and obstruct us are *arātayaḥ*, 'enemies'. **शूर** — Indra of great prowess.

### Pages 450–452 — Sūkta 29, Rik 5

**॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥**

> समिन्द्र गर्दभं मृण नुवन्तं पापयामुया ।
> आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥ ५ ॥

*sam indra gardabhaṃ mṛṇa nuvantaṃ pāpayāmuyā | ā tū na indra śaṃsaya goṣv aśveṣu śubhriṣu sahasreṣu tuvīmagha || 5 ||*

**॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥**

> सम् । इन्द्र । गर्दभम् । मृण । नुवन्तम् । पापयाः । अमुया ॥ आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ ५ ॥

*sam | indra | gardabham | mṛṇa | nuvantam | pāpayā | amuyā || ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 5 ||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(p. 451)*

> हे इन्द्र अमुयानयेत्यस्माभिः श्रूयमाणया पापया निन्दारूपया वाचा नुवन्तं स्तुवन्तं । आशकीर्तिं प्रकटयन्तमित्यर्थः । तादृशं गर्दभं गर्दभसमानवैरिणं सं मृण । सम्यक्मारय । यथा गर्दभः श्रोत्रमसह्यं परुषं शब्दं करोति तथा शत्रुरपि । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यत इति गर्दभः नर्द गर्द शब्दे । क्नुग्नुश्वकलिगर्दिभ्योऽभच् । उ. ३-१३३ [?] । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । मृण । मृण हिंसायाम् । तौदादिकः । शस्य जित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । नुवन्तं । णु स्तुतौ । शतृप्रत्ययः । अदादिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपो लुक् । शतुर्जित्त्वाद्गुणाभाव उवङादेशः । प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

*he indra amuyānayety asmābhiḥ śrūyamāṇayā pāpayā nindārūpayā vācā nuvantaṃ stuvantam | āśakīrtiṃ prakaṭayantam ity arthaḥ | tādṛśaṃ gardabhaṃ gardabhasamānavairiṇaṃ saṃ mṛṇa | samyak māraya | yathā gardabhaḥ śrotram asahyaṃ paruṣaṃ śabdaṃ karoti tathā śatrur api | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti gardabhaḥ narda garda śabde | knugnuśvakaligardibhyo 'bhac | u. 3-133 [?] | cita ity antodāttatvaṃ | mṛṇa | mṛṇa hiṃsāyām | taudādikaḥ | śasya jittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | nuvantaṃ | ṇu stutau | śatṛpratyayaḥ | adādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapo luk | śaturjittvād guṇābhāva uvaṅādeśaḥ | pratyayādyudāttatvam ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra! *Gardabham* — the ass-like enemy who, with this harsh speech that we hear [*amuyā pāpayā*] — a blaming speech — *nuvantam* — praises, [rather] proclaims [our] ill-fame: such a *gardabha*, an enemy like an ass — *saṃ mṛṇa* — destroy utterly; kill completely. As the ass (*gardabha*) makes an unbearable harsh noise for the ear, so does the enemy. *Gardabham*: from *narda garda śabde* ['to sound']; the suffix *abhac* (Uṇ. 3-133 [?]); end-acute through *cit*. *Mṛṇa*: *mṛṇa hiṃsāyām*, of the *tudādi* class; *śa* is *ṅit*-like so no guṇa. *Nuvantam*: *ṇu stutau* ['to praise'], with *śatṛ*; the *śap* is lost as in the *adādi* class; no guṇa because *śatṛ* is *ñit*; *uvaṅ* [*uv*] substituted; the accent of the suffix." *(Grammar pages 452, noted briefly: the words treated are* gardabham *[*narda garda śabde*, *bhvādi*; *abhac* by Uṇ. 3-… *kraśvagnuśvakaligardibhyo 'bhac*; the form is also derived by P. 3-2-75 *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante* ; being *cit*, the end-acute by P. 6-1-163; accusative singular],* mṛṇa *[*mṛṇa hiṃsāyām*, *tudādi*; *loṭ* 2nd singular *sip* → *hi* by P. 3-4-87; *śa* by P. 3-1-77; since *śa* is *apit* it is *ṅit* by P. 1-2-4 *sārvadhātukam apit*, so no guṇa; *hi* is lost by P. 6-4-105 *ato heḥ*; the verb is lowered, P. 8-1-28] and* nuvantam *[*ṇu stutau*, *adādi*; *śatṛ* in the sense of agent; *śap* lost by P. 2-4-72; *śatṛ* is *ñit* [*śatuḥ*], so no guṇa; *uvaṅ* in place of *u* before a vowel-beginning *sārvadhātuka* by P. 6-4-87/88; *num* in the accusative by P. 7-1-70 *ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ*; the accent: the middle syllable, from the suffix]; numerals as read, pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 451)* **इन्द्र (indra)** — O Indra | **अमुया (amuyā)** — with this | **पापया (pāpayā)** — with ill [harsh, blaming] | **नुवन्तम् (nuvantam)** — [speech] who utters [the words] | **गर्दभम् (gardabham)** — [him who is like] an ass, an enemy | **सं मृण (saṃ mṛṇa)** — destroy completely | **तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha)** — O Indra of abundant wealth | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **गोषु अश्वेषु (goṣu aśveṣu)** — in cows and horses | **शुभ्रिषु (śubhriṣu)** — auspicious | **सहस्रेषु (sahasreṣu)** — in thousands | **आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya)** — [make us] worthy.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** O Indra! Destroy utterly this enemy, who is like an ass, who is wearing out our ears with this harsh blaming speech. And, O Indra of abundant wealth, make us fit for thousands of auspicious cows and horses.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Indra, kill this ass (enemy) praising you with such harsh speech; Indra, of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(pp. 451–452)* **गर्दभम्** — [it means] 'an ass'; here the commentator explains it as 'an enemy who is like an ass', that is, one whose voice harasses us like an ass's bray. **नुवन्तं पापया अमुया** — the sense: 'with this harsh speech, which is blaming and cruel to hear, one who reviles you'. [*My note:* the Kannada says 'reviles you', following the commentator's *stuvantam*, 'praising', as a euphemism for 'noisy, calling out'; the English the source prints, 'praising you with such harsh speech', follows the Sanskrit.]

### Pages 452–454 — Sūkta 29, Rik 6

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(p. 452)*

> पताति कुण्डृणाच्या दूरं वातो वनादधि ।
> आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥ ६ ॥

> *patāti kuṇḍṛṇācyā dūraṃ vāto vanādadhi |*
> *ā tū na indra śaṃsaya goṣvaśveṣu śubhriṣu sahasreṣu tuvīmagha ‖ 6 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha** *(p. 453)*

> पताति । कुण्डृणाच्या । दूरम् । वातः । वनात् । अधि ।
> आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुवीमघ ॥ ६ ॥

> *patāti | kuṇḍṛṇācyā | dūram | vātaḥ | vanāt | adhi |*
> *ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvīmagha ‖ 6 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 453)*

> वातोऽस्मत्प्रतिकूलो वायुः कुण्डृणाच्या कुटिलगत्या स त्वस्मान्परित्यज्य वनादरण्यादधिकं [?] दूरं देशं पताति । पतेत् । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥

> *vāto 'smatpratikūlo vāyuḥ kuṇḍṛṇācyā kuṭilagatyā sa tvasmānparityajya vanādaraṇyādadhikaṃ [?] dūraṃ deśaṃ patāti | patet | anyatpūrvavat ‖*

*Gist (mine):* "The wind that is hostile to us, going by a crooked course, leaving us, may fall (blow) far away, beyond the forest. *Patāti* = *patet*. The rest as before."

*Grammar (pp. 453–454), noted briefly:* the printed note treats *patāti* (*pata gatau*; *leṭ*, with the *aḍāgama* by P. 3-4-94 *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* [as read]) and *kuṇḍṛṇācyā* (from *kuḍi dāhe*; the *ṛ* for *a* is Vedic; *ñc*-affix, *kvin*, the *nalopa* and the lengthening before the instrumental ending are discussed with many sūtras whose numerals I could not read reliably: [?]).

**Pratipadārtha** *(p. 453, Kannada, rendered)* — **वातः** the wind (hostile to us); **कुण्डृणाच्या** by a crooked course (leaving us); **वनादधि** beyond the forest; **दूरम्** to a far region; **पताति** may it blow; **तुवीमघ** O possessor of abundant wealth; **इन्द्र** O Indra; **नः** us; **सहस्रेषु** in thousands; **शुभ्रिषु** excellent; **गोषु** in cows; **अश्वेषु** in horses; **आ शंसय** make [us] fully worthy (that is, give us thousands of cows and horses).

**Bhāvārtha** *(p. 453)* — O Indra of abundant wealth! Let the wind that is hostile to us and goes by a crooked course blow far from us, beyond the forest; and give us thousands of excellent cows and horses, making us wealthy.

**English Translation** *(as printed, p. 454)*

> Let the (adverse) wind with crooked course blow away to far off places beyond the forest; Indra of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

**Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu** *(p. 454)* — **वातः कुण्डृणाच्या** — *kuḍi dāhe*; *kuṭilagatyā*: by a bad, crooked path: the wind that blows against us. **दूरं वनादधि पताति** — may it go to a region far beyond the forest; may it not be near us.

### Pages 455–457 — Sūkta 29, Rik 7 (last rik of the sūkta)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(p. 455)*

> सर्वं परिक्रोशं जहि जम्भया कृकदाश्वम् ।
> आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥ ७ ॥

> *sarvaṃ parikrośaṃ jahi jambhayā kṛkadāśvam |*
> *ā tū na indra śaṃsaya goṣvaśveṣu śubhriṣu sahasreṣu tuvīmagha ‖ 7 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha** *(p. 455)*

> सर्वम् । परिऽक्रोशम् । जहि । जम्भय । कृकदाश्वम् ।
> आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुवीमघ ॥ ७ ॥

> *sarvam | pari 'krośam | jahi | jambhaya | kṛkadāśvam |*
> *ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvīmagha ‖ 7 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 455)*

> परिक्रोशमस्मद्विषये सर्वतः आक्रोशकर्तारं सर्वं पुरुषं जहि । मारय । कृकदाश्वमस्मद्विषये हिंसाप्रदं शत्रुं जम्भय । मारय । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥
> परिक्रोशम् । क्रुश आह्वाने । परितः क्रोशयतीति परिक्रोशः । पचाद्यच् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जहि । हन हिंसागत्योः । हन्तेर्जः । पा. ६-४-३६ [?] । इति जादेशः । असिद्धवदत्राभादित्यसिद्धत्वादतो हेरिति हेर्लुग्न भवति । जम्भय । जभी नाशने । चुरादित्वात्स्वार्थिको णिच् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे णिच एव स्वरः शिष्यते । कृकदाश्वम् । कृकं हिंसायाम् [?] … कन् । उ. ३-४० [?] … कृके वचः कश्च । उ. १-६ [?] इत्युण् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । द्वितीयायामपि पूर्वरूपत्वे प्राप्ते वा छन्दसीति तस्य बाधितत्वाद्यण्-आदेशः । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः इति विभक्तेः स्वरितत्वम् ॥ ७ ॥

> *parikrośamasmadviṣaye sarvataḥ ākrośakartāraṃ sarvaṃ puruṣaṃ jahi | māraya | kṛkadāśvamasmadviṣaye hiṃsāpradaṃ śatruṃ jambhaya | māraya | anyatpūrvavat ‖*
> *parikrośam | kruśa āhvāne | paritaḥ krośayatīti parikrośaḥ | pacādyac | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | jahi | hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ | hanterjaḥ | pā. 6-4-36 [?] | iti jādeśaḥ | asiddhavadatrābhādityasiddhatvādato heriti herlugna bhavati | jambhaya | jabhī nāśane | curāditvātsvārthiko ṇic | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatve ṇica eva svaraḥ śiṣyate | kṛkadāśvam | kṛkaṃ hiṃsāyām [?] … kan | u. 3-40 [?] … kṛke vacaḥ kaśca | u. 1-6 [?] ityuṇ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | dvitīyāyāmapi pūrvarūpatve prāpte vā chandasīti tasya bādhitatvādyaṇ-ādeśaḥ | udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ iti vibhakteḥ svaritatvam ‖ 7 ‖*

*Gist (mine):* "Kill (*jahi*) every man who abuses (*parikrośam*) us from all sides; destroy (*jambhaya*) the enemy who deals harm (*kṛkadāśvam*). The rest as before." The grammatical tail (printed in compressed form on p. 455; the Kannada grammar on pp. 456–457 gives the same) treats *parikrośam* (*pacādi ac*), *jahi* (*hanter jaḥ*, with the principle *asiddhavad atrābhāt*), *jambhaya* (*curādi ṇic*) and *kṛkadāśvam* (*kṛka* from *kṛñ hiṃsāyām*, *dāś dāne* with an Uṇādi *uṇ*; the accusative *-vam* by *yaṇ*); words with [?] are doubtful readings.

**Pratipadārtha** *(p. 456, rendered)* — **परिक्रोशम्** [him] who reviles and blames us; **सर्वम्** every one; **जहि** destroy; **कृकदाश्वम्** the enemy who does us harm; **जम्भय** kill; **तुवीमघ** [Indra] of plentiful wealth; **इन्द्र** O Indra; **नः** us; **सहस्रेषु** in thousands; **शुभ्रिषु** excellent; **गोषु** in cows; **अश्वेषु** in horses; **आ शंसय** make [us] worthy (give us thousands of cows and horses).

**Bhāvārtha** *(p. 456)* — O Indra, destroy every enemy who reviles us and speaks ill of us; kill all who do us harm. O Indra of abundant wealth, give us thousands of excellent cows and horses and make us rich.

**English Translation** *(as printed, p. 456)*

> Strike down everyone who reviles us; destroy everyone that does us injury; O Indra of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

**Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu** *(p. 456)* — **परिक्रोशम्** — *kruśa āhvāne*; *paritaḥ krośayatīti parikrośaḥ*: one who, out of hostility, rages at us or speaks ill. **जहि** — *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*: restrain, injure, destroy. **जम्भय** — *jabhi nāśane*: destroy. **कृकदाश्वम्** — *kṛñ hiṃsāyām*; *kṛko hiṃsā | tāṃ dāśati prayacchatīti kṛkadāśuḥ*: a man who deals injury, who brings us harm.

**Grammar pages (pp. 456–457), noted briefly:** the Kannada grammar treats *parikrośam* (*pacādi ac*, P. 3-1-134 *nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ*; the *kṛt*-final accent by P. 6-2-139 *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*), *jahi* (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*, *adādi*, *loṭ*; *hi*; *hanter jaḥ* [P. 6-4-36 [?]]; *asiddhavad atrābhāt*, P. 6-4-22; *ato heḥ* P. 6-4-105 therefore not applied), *jambhaya* (*jabhi nāśane*, *curādi*; *ṇic* by P. 3-1-25 *satyāpapāśarūpa…*; *num* from the *it*; *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* P. 3-1-32; *loṭ*; the *śap*'s *luk*; *ṇic* keeps the accent) and *kṛkadāśvam* (*kṛñ hiṃsāyām*, *kryādi*; *kan* by an Uṇādi sūtra *kṛdāṅ…* [Uṇ. 3-40 [?]]; *dāś dāne* with *uṇ* by *kṛke vacaḥ kaś ca* [Uṇ. 1-6 [?]]; *ami pūrvaḥ* P. 6-1-107 / *vā chandasi* P. 6-1-106; *yaṇ* and the *svarita* by P. 8-2-4 *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya*).

**Close of Sūkta 29** *(p. 457)* — *ippattombhattaneya sūktavu samāptavāgide* — "The twenty-ninth sūkta is ended." *(At the foot of p. 457: sheet-mark "58" and "VOLUME 3".)*

## ॥ ಮೂವತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 30 — *"ā va indram"* ("The Thirtieth Sūkta"; seventh sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)

**Heading** *(p. 458)*: "The thirtieth sūkta." Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka **6**; Sūkta 30. Aṣṭaka 1; Adhyāya 2; Varga **28, 29, 30, 31**. Number of Riks in the sūkta: **22**. Ṛṣi: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti. Devatā: Riks 1–16 Indra; 17–19 the Aśvins; 20–22 Uṣas. Chandas: Riks 1–10, 12–15, 17–22 Gāyatrī; Rik 11 Gāyatrī *pādanicṛt*; Rik 16 Triṣṭubh.

*(p. 458 is read from the old scan, `scans/Rig_Vol3.pdf` PDF 473: the better scan's PDF 472 is a wrong page, headed 358.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, introductory note** *(p. 458)*

> आ व इन्द्रमिति द्वाविंशत्यृचं सप्तमं सूक्तं शुनःशेपस्यार्षं गायत्रम् । अस्माकमित्येषा पादनिचृद्गायत्री । त्रयः सप्तकाः पादनिचृत् । अनु. ४-४ । इत्युक्तत्वात् । शश्वदिन्द्र इत्येषा त्रिष्टुप् । आदितः षोडशर्च ऐन्द्र्यः । अश्विनावश्वावत्येत्याद्यास्तिस्र आश्विन्यः । कस्त उष इत्याद्यास्तिस्र उषोदेवताकाः । तथा चानुक्रमणिका । आ वो द्व्यधिकास्माकं पादनिचृच्छश्वत्त्रिष्टुप्स्परौ तृचावाश्विनोषस्याविति ॥

> *ā va indramiti dvāviṃśatyṛcaṃ saptamaṃ sūktaṃ śunaḥśepasyārṣaṃ gāyatram | asmākamityeṣā pādanicṛdgāyatrī | trayaḥ saptakāḥ pādanicṛt | anu. 4-4 | ityuktatvāt | śaśvadindra ityeṣā triṣṭup | āditaḥ ṣoḍaśarca aindryaḥ | aśvināvaśvāvatyetyādyāstisra āśvinyaḥ | kasta uṣa ityādyāstisra uṣodevatākāḥ | tathā cānukramaṇikā | ā vo dvyadhikāsmākaṃ pādanicṛcchaśvattriṣṭupsparau tṛcāvāśvinoṣasyāviti ‖*

*Translation:* "*Ā va indram* is the seventh sūkta [of the anuvāka]; it has twenty-two Riks; its seer is Śunaḥśepa; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Rik *asmākam* is *pādanicṛd* Gāyatrī; [the Anukramaṇikā rule] 'three [pādas] of seven [syllables] are *pādanicṛt*' (Anu. 4-4) having been stated. The Rik *śaśvad indra* is Triṣṭubh. From the beginning, sixteen Riks are Indra's (*aindryaḥ*); the three beginning *aśvināv aśvāvatyā* are the Aśvins'; the three beginning *kas ta uṣaḥ* have Uṣas as deity. The Anukramaṇikā says so: '*ā vo* [has] two more [than twenty]; *asmākam* is *pādanicṛt*; *śaśvat* is Triṣṭubh; the last two triplets are the Aśvins' and Uṣas's.'"

**Anuvāda** *(p. 458, rendered)* — *Ā va indram* is the seventh sūkta in the sixth anuvāka and has twenty-two Riks. Śunaḥśepa is the seer; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Rik *asmākam it* is *pādanicṛt* Gāyatrī; *śaśvad indraḥ* is Triṣṭubh. The first sixteen Riks have Indra as deity; the three from *aśvināv aśvāvatyā* have the Aśvins; the three from *kas ta uṣaḥ* have Uṣas. The Anukramaṇikā says: *ā vo dvyadhikāsmākaṃ pādanicṛc chaśvat triṣṭup sparau tṛcāv āśvinoṣasyāv iti*.

### Pages 459–461 — Sūkta 30, Rik 1

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(p. 459)*

> आ व॒ इन्द्रं॒ क्रिविं॑ यथा वाज॒यन्तः॑ श॒तक्र॑तुं ।
> मंहि॑ष्ठं सिञ्च॒ इन्दु॑भिः ॥ १ ॥

> *ā va índraṃ kríviṃ yathā vājayántaḥ śatákratuṃ |*
> *máṃhiṣṭhaṃ siñca índubhiḥ || 1 ||*

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> आ । वः । इन्द्रं । क्रिविं । यथा । वाजऽयन्तः । शतऽक्रतुं ।
> मंहिष्ठं । सिञ्चे । इन्दुऽभिः ॥ १ ॥

> *ā | vaḥ | indraṃ | kriviṃ | yathā | vāja 'yantaḥ | śata 'kratuṃ |*
> *maṃhiṣṭhaṃ | siñce | indu 'bhiḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 459)*

*As printed: क्रिविशब्दो वप्रिः (so printed; the sense of* वप्रिः *here is unclear to me); उ. ४-५६ (the grammar page, p. 461, prints ४-४६); फि. ४-१७ (the last digit is the flat-footed glyph also used for 7 in पा. ७-४-३७ on p. 461; the grammar page prints फि. सू. ८५).*

> वाजयन्तोऽन्नमिच्छन्तो वयं शुनःशेपा हे ऋत्विग्यजमाना वो युष्माकं संबन्धिनमिममिन्द्रमिन्दुभिः सोमैरासिञ्चे । सर्वतः सिञ्चामहे । तर्पयामः । कीदृशम् । शतक्रतुं शतसंख्याककर्मोपेतं मंहिष्ठमतिशयेन प्रवृद्धम् । सेचने दृष्टान्तः । यथा येन प्रकारेण क्रिविमवटं जलेन पूरयन्ति तद्वत् । क्रिविशब्दो वप्रिः । काटुरित्यादिषु चतुर्दशसु कूपनामसु क्रिविः कूपः सूद इति पठितम् ॥ क्रिविम् । कृती छेदने । कृन्तत इति क्रिविः । क्रिविघृष्विच्छविस्थवीत्यादौ । उ. ४-५६ । क्विन्प्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । अत एव तशब्दलोपः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । यथा । यथेति पादान्ते । फि. ४-१७ । इति सर्वानुदात्तत्वम् । वाजयन्तः । वाजमात्मन इच्छन्तः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्येतीत्वदीर्घत्वयोर्निषेधः । अश्वाघस्यादिति पुनर्दीर्घविधानाज्ज्ञापकात् । मंहिष्ठम् । महि वृद्धौ । अतिशयेन मंहिता मंहिष्ठः । तुश्छन्दसि । पा. ५-३-५९ । इति तृजन्तादिष्ठन्प्रत्ययः । तुरिष्ठेमेयःसु । पा. ६-४-१५४ । इति तृलोपः । इष्ठनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सिञ्चे । षिचिर् क्षरणे । व्यत्ययेनैकवचनम् । शे मुचादीनामिति नुमागमः ॥

> *vājayanto 'nnamicchanto vayaṃ śunaḥśepā he ṛtvigyajamānā vo yuṣmākaṃ saṃbandhinamimamindramindubhiḥ somairāsiñce | sarvataḥ siñcāmahe | tarpayāmaḥ | kīdṛśam | śatakratuṃ śatasaṃkhyākakarmopetaṃ maṃhiṣṭhamatiśayena pravṛddham | secane dṛṣṭāntaḥ | yathā yena prakāreṇa krivimavaṭaṃ jalena pūrayanti tadvat | kriviśabdo vapriḥ | kāṭurityādiṣu caturdaśasu kūpanāmasu kriviḥ kūpaḥ sūda iti paṭhitam ‖ krivim | kṛtī chedane | kṛntata iti kriviḥ | krivighṛṣvicchavisthavītyādau | u. 4-56 | kvinpratyayānto nipātitaḥ | ata eva taśabdalopaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam | yathā | yatheti pādānte | phi. 4-17 | iti sarvānudāttatvam | vājayantaḥ | vājamātmana icchantaḥ | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | na chandasyaputrasyetītvadīrghatvayorniṣedhaḥ | aśvāghasyāditi punardīrghavidhānājjñāpakāt | maṃhiṣṭham | mahi vṛddhau | atiśayena maṃhitā maṃhiṣṭhaḥ | tuśchandasi | pā. 5-3-59 | iti tṛjantādiṣṭhanpratyayaḥ | turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu | pā. 6-4-154 | iti tṛlopaḥ | iṣṭhano nittvādādyudāttatvam | siñce | ṣicir kṣaraṇe | vyatyayenaikavacanam | śe mucādīnāmiti numāgamaḥ ‖*

*Translation:* "We, the Śunaḥśepas, desiring food (*vājayantaḥ*), O priests and sacrificers, pour (*ā siñce*: 'we sprinkle on all sides, we satisfy') this Indra of yours with Soma-juices (*indubhiḥ*) — Indra who has a hundred rites (*śatakratum*) and is exceedingly grown (*maṃhiṣṭham*). The illustration for the sprinkling: as one fills a well (*krivim*) with water, so. The word *krivi* is *vapriḥ* [as printed]: among the fourteen names of a well beginning with *kāṭuḥ*, '*kriviḥ, kūpaḥ, sūdaḥ*' is read." The grammatical tail treats *krivim* (*kṛtī chedane*; *kvin*, by *nipātana* under Uṇ. 4-56, hence loss of the *t*; initial udātta as *nit*), *yathā* (all-grave at the end of a pāda, Phi. 4-17), *vājayantaḥ* (*kyac*; the *ī* and lengthening prohibited by *na chandasy aputrasya*, as the separate rule *aśvāghasyāt* shows), *maṃhiṣṭham* (*iṣṭhan* after *tṛc* by Pā. 5-3-59, loss of *tṛ* by Pā. 6-4-154) and *siñce* (singular by *vyatyaya*; *num* by *śe mucādīnām*).

**Pratipadārtha** *(pp. 459–460, rendered)* — **वाजयन्तः** we who desire food; **वः** [you], the priests and sacrificers — your; **शतक्रतुम्** him who is endowed with a hundred deeds; **मंहिष्ठम्** the exceedingly grown

### Page 460 — Sūkta 30, Rik 1 (continued)

*(Pratipadārtha continued)* **इन्द्रम्** Indra; **इन्दुभिः** with Soma-juices; **यथा क्रिविम्** as a well [is filled with water]; **आ सिञ्चे** we fill all round and satisfy.

**Bhāvārtha** *(p. 460)* — We who desire food satisfy, on every side, with Soma-juices this your Indra, who has a hundred deeds and is exceedingly great, as a well is filled with water.

**English Translation** *(as printed, p. 460)*

> We, desirous of wealth satisfy this your Indra who is the mightiest (among gods) and (is the performer or is praised) in a hundred sacrifices with drops of Soma-juice as a well (is filled with water).

**Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu** *(p. 460)* — **क्रिविम्** — *kūpaḥ kātuḥ* and so on: since the word *krivi* is read among the fourteen names of a well, *krivi* means a well. *Krivim yathā*: as a well is filled with water, so Indra's belly is filled with Soma-juice: much Soma is prepared for Indra's drinking. **शतक्रतुम्** — *kratu* is 'act' (Ni. 3-1) and 'wisdom' (Ni. 3-13); hence *śatakratu* is 'one who has done a hundred mighty deeds' or 'very wise'. The Purāṇas say 'one who did a hundred sacrifices' (Indra obtained Indra's rank so); but that sense does not fit here; the sense intended is 'one who has done a hundred [mighty] deeds'. **मंहिष्ठम्** — *mahi vṛddhau*; *atiśayena maṃhitā maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*: most grown, most excellent. **वः इन्द्रम्** — 'your Indra', the Indra whom you praise: by the word *vaḥ* the speech is understood as addressed to the priests. **सिञ्चे** — *ṣicir kṣaraṇe*: we make [him] wet, fill; with *indubhiḥ*: we satisfy Indra with Soma-juices.

### Page 461 — Sūkta 30, Rik 1: grammar

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(p. 461, noted briefly)* — *krivim*: *kṛtī chedane*, *rudhādi*; *kvin* by *nipātana* under '*krivi ghṛṣvi chavi sthavi*' (U. sū. 4-46, as printed; the bhāṣya, p. 459, prints उ. ४-५६); loss of the *t*; initial udātta by '*ñnity ādir nityam*' (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); accusative singular. *yathā*: *thāl* by '*prakāravacane thāl*' (Pā. sū. 5-3-23); *a* for the final by '*tyadādīnām aḥ*' (Pā. sū. 7-2-102); all-grave by '*yatheti pādānte*' (Phi. sū. 85, as printed; the bhāṣya prints फि. ४-१७). *vājayantaḥ*: *kyac* by '*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*' (Pā. sū. 3-1-8); *ī* etc. due by '*kyaci ca*' (Pā. sū. 7-4-33) but barred by '*na chandasy aputrasya*' (Pā. sū. 7-4-35); '*aśvāghasyāt*' (Pā. sū. 7-4-37) as *jñāpaka*; *śatṛ*, *num* (*ugit*). *maṃhiṣṭha*: *mahi vṛddhau*, *bhvādi*; *iṣṭhan* by '*tuś chandasi*' (Pā. sū. 5-3-59); loss of *tṛ* by '*turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu*' (Pā. sū. 6-4-154); initial udātta. *siñce*: *ṣicir kṣaraṇe*, *tudādi*, *laṭ* first person plural; singular by '*vyatyayo bahulam*' (Pā. sū. 3-1-85); *s* for *ṣ*; *e* by '*ṭita ātmanepa-*' (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); *num* by '*śe mucādīnām*' (Pā. sū. 7-1-59); unaccented (*tiṅ* after a non-*tiṅ*).

### Pages 462–464 — Sūkta 30, Rik 2

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(p. 462)*

*(As printed, the anudātta bar stands under* वा *after* शतं *and under* स *of* सहस्रं*, and the svarita stroke over* मा *of* समाशिरां*.)*

> श॒तं वा॒ यः शुची॑नां स॒हस्रं॑ वा॒ समा॑शिरां ।
> एदु॑ नि॒म्नं न री॑यते ॥ २ ॥

> *śatáṃ vā yáḥ śúcīnāṃ sahásraṃ vā sámāśirāṃ |*
> *édu nimnáṃ ná rīyate || 2 ||*

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> शतं । वा । यः । शुचीनां । सहस्रं । वा । संऽआशिरां ।
> आ । इत् । ऊं इति । निम्नं । न । रीयते ॥ २ ॥

> *śataṃ | vā | yaḥ | śucīnāṃ | sahasraṃ | vā | saṃ 'āśirāṃ |*
> *ā | it | ūṃ iti | nimnaṃ | na | rīyate ‖ 2 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 462)*

> य इन्द्रः शुचीनां शुद्धानां सोमानां शतं वा शतसंख्याकं समूहं वा । समाशिरां समीचीनेनाशिराख्येन श्रपणद्रव्येणोपेतानां सोमानां सहस्रं वा सहस्रसंख्याकं समूहं वा एदुरीयते । आगच्छत्येव । सोऽस्माननुगृह्णात्विति शेषः । सोमप्राप्तौ दृष्टान्तः । निम्नं न । यथा निम्नप्रदेशमाप आप्नुवन्ति तद्वत् ॥ समाशिराम् । श्रीञ् पाक इत्यस्य समाङ्पूर्वस्य क्विप्यपस्पृधेथामित्यादावाशीरादेशो निपातितः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । रीयते । रीङ् श्रवणे । दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् ॥

> *ya indraḥ śucīnāṃ śuddhānāṃ somānāṃ śataṃ vā śatasaṃkhyākaṃ samūhaṃ vā | samāśirāṃ samīcīnenāśirākhyena śrapaṇadravyeṇopetānāṃ somānāṃ sahasraṃ vā sahasrasaṃkhyākaṃ samūhaṃ vā edurīyate | āgacchatyeva | so 'smānanugṛhṇātviti śeṣaḥ | somaprāptau dṛṣṭāntaḥ | nimnaṃ na | yathā nimnapradeśamāpa āpnuvanti tadvat ‖ samāśirām | śrīñ pāka ityasya samāṅpūrvasya kvipyapaspṛdhethāmityādāvāśīrādeśo nipātitaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | rīyate | rīṅ śravaṇe | divādibhyaḥ śyan ‖*

*Translation:* "The Indra who [receives] a hundred — a group of a hundred — of pure Soma-offerings, or a thousand — a group of a thousand — of Soma-offerings joined with the *āśir*, the right cooking (mixing) substance: he comes (*ed u rīyate*) — comes indeed; [the supplied rest:] 'may he favour us'. Illustration of reaching the Soma: *nimnaṃ na* — as waters reach a low place, so." The grammatical tail treats *samāśirām* (*śrīñ pāke* with *sam* and *āṅ*; *kvip*; the substitute *āśīr* fixed by *nipātana* in the rule beginning *apaspṛdhethām*; a bahuvrīhi with the first member's own accent) and *rīyate* (*rīṅ śravaṇe*; *śyan* of the *divādi* class). No sūtra numbers are printed in the bhāṣya.

**Pratipadārtha** *(p. 462, rendered)* — **यः** which Indra; **शुचीनाम्** of pure; **शतं वा** a hundred [Soma-juices] or; **समाशिराम्** of Soma-juices mixed with purified sweet substances; **सहस्रं वा** a thousand [to receive them]; **निम्नं न** as water [flows] to a low place; **एदु रीयते** comes (naturally) [may that Indra favour us].

**Bhāvārtha** *(pp. 462–463)* — May that Indra, who accepts a hundred pure Soma-juices and a thousand mixed with sweet substances, come to us, easy and natural, like a stream of water flowing to a low place, and favour us.

### Page 463 — Sūkta 30, Rik 2 (continued)

**English Translation** *(as printed, p. 463)*

> May he who (drinks) of a hundred pure and thousand mixed libations of Soma come to this sacrifice as water runs to a low place.

**Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu** *(p. 463)* — **शतं, सहस्रम्** — though *śata* and *sahasra* mean only a hundred and a thousand, the sense is a hundred or a thousand vessels (or sacrificial offerings) of Soma-juice. **समाशिराम्** — Soma-juices joined with *āśir* substances: milk, curds, barley-meal; with milk it is *gavāśir*, with curds *dadhyāśir*, with barley *yavāśir*; the rik names none, so it is Soma mixed with some one of them. **आ इत् उ रीयते** — *āgacchaty eva, dhāvaty eva*: he does come, comes quickly. **निम्नं न** — *nimna* is a low place, a hollow; as water runs naturally to a lower place, so Indra comes to our sacrifice to drink Soma.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(pp. 463–464, noted briefly)* — *samāśirām*: *śrīñ pāke*, *kryādi*, with *sam* and *āṅ*; *kvip* by '*kvip ca*' (Pā. sū. 3-2-76); *āśīr* by *nipātana* under '*apaspṛdhethām ānṛcuḥ*' (Pā. sū. 6-1-36); genitive plural; *(p. 464)* first-member accent by '*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*' (Pā. sū. 6-2-1), initial udātta. *rīyate*: *rīṅ śravaṇe*, *divādi*, the sense changed by the preverb; *ātmanepada* (*ṅit*); *e* by '*ṭita ātmanepadānām*' (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); *śyan* by '*divādibhyaḥ śyan*' (Pā. sū. 3-1-69); unaccented by '*tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ*' (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

### Pages 464–466 — Sūkta 30, Rik 3

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(p. 464)*

> सं यन्मदा॑य शु॒ष्मिण॑ ए॒ना ह्य॑स्यो॒दरे॑ ।
> स॒मु॒द्रो न व्यचो॑ द॒धे ॥ ३ ॥

> *saṃ yanmádāya śuṣmíṇa enā́ hyasyodáre |*
> *samudró na vyáco dadhé || 3 ||*

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> सं । यत् । मदाय । शुष्मिणे । एना । हि । अस्य । उदरे ।
> समुद्रः । न । व्यचः । दधे ॥ ३ ॥

> *saṃ | yat | madāya | śuṣmiṇe | enā | hi | asya | udare |*
> *samudraḥ | na | vyacaḥ | dadhe ‖ 3 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(pp. 464–465)*

*(The bhāṣya runs over the page break after* संप्र- *(p. 464) /* सारणं *(p. 465).)*

> यत्पूर्वोक्तं शतं सहस्रं वा शुष्मिणे बलवत इन्द्रस्य मदाय मदार्थं संगतं भवति । एना ह्यनेनैव शतेन सहस्रेण चास्येन्द्रस्योदरे व्यचो व्याप्तिर्दधे । धृता भवति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । समुद्रो न समुद्र इव । यथा समुद्रमध्ये जलं व्याप्तं तद्वत् ॥ एना । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया आडादेशः । व्यचः । व्यचेः कुटादित्वमनसि । का. १-२-१-१ । इति ङिद्वद्भावस्य प्रतिषिद्धत्वाद्ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना संप्रसारणं न भवति असुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । दधे । दधातेः कर्मण्यभ्यासह्रस्वजश्त्वेषु कृतेष्वातो लोप इटि चेत्याकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । हि चेति प्रतिषेधान्निघाताभावः ॥

> *yatpūrvoktaṃ śataṃ sahasraṃ vā śuṣmiṇe balavata indrasya madāya madārthaṃ saṃgataṃ bhavati | enā hyanenaiva śatena sahasreṇa cāsyendrasyodare vyaco vyāptirdadhe | dhṛtā bhavati | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | samudro na samudra iva | yathā samudramadhye jalaṃ vyāptaṃ tadvat ‖ enā | supāṃ sulugiti tṛtīyāyā āḍādeśaḥ | vyacaḥ | vyaceḥ kuṭāditvamanasi | kā. 1-2-1-1 | iti ṅidvadbhāvasya pratiṣiddhatvādgrahijyetyādinā saṃprasāraṇaṃ na bhavati asuno nittvādādyudāttatvam | dadhe | dadhāteḥ karmaṇyabhyāsahrasvajaśtveṣu kṛteṣvāto lopa iṭi cetyākāralopaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvam | hi ceti pratiṣedhānnighātābhāvaḥ ‖*

*Translation:* "The aforesaid hundred or thousand [of Soma] is brought together for the exhilaration (*madāya*) of mighty (*śuṣmiṇe*: strong) Indra. By this very hundred and thousand (*enā hi*), in this Indra's belly, the pervasion (*vyacaḥ*) is held (*dadhe*): is held. Illustration: *samudro na* — like the sea: as water pervades the middle of the sea, so." The grammatical tail treats *enā* (*ā* for the instrumental by *supāṃ suluk*), *vyacaḥ* (the *kuṭādi* status of *vyac* is denied before *asi* (Kā. 1-2-1-1), so the *ṅit*-like treatment lapses and *grahijyā…* gives no *saṃprasāraṇa*; initial udātta as *asun* is *nit*) and *dadhe* (passive *liṭ*; after the reduplicated syllable's shortening and *jaś*, loss of *ā* by *āto lopa iṭi ca*; final udātta by the suffix accent; not made grave because of *hi ca*).

### Page 465 — Sūkta 30, Rik 3 (continued)

**Pratipadārtha** *(p. 465, rendered)* — **यत्** those (described before) hundreds and thousands of Soma-juices; **शुष्मिणे** for the strong Indra; **मदाय** for satisfaction (exhilaration); **एना हि** these [Soma-juices]; **समुद्रः न** as the sea [is filled with water]; **अस्य** this Indra's; **उदरे** in the belly; **व्यचः दधे** [they] fill.

**Bhāvārtha** *(p. 465)* — Those offerings of hundreds and thousands of Soma-juices described before, prepared for the exhilaration of the mighty Indra, together fill his belly as the sea is filled with water.

**English Translation** *(as printed, p. 465)*

> All those libations of Soma (which were mentioned above) are, for his intoxication, accumulated in the belly of powerful Indra as the water in the sea.

**Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu** *(p. 465)* — **मदाय** — for contentment, to bring about intoxication. **शुष्मिणे** — *balavate*: to the strong Indra. **समुद्रो न** — as water gathers in the sea, so the hundreds and thousands of Soma-juices we offer collect in Indra's belly and give him exhilaration. **व्यचो दधे** — *vyāptir dadhe | dhṛtā bhavati*: 'pervasion' means they are held, gathered together in the belly.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(pp. 465–466, noted briefly)* — *enā*: '*dvitīyāṭausv enaḥ*' (Pā. sū. 2-4-34): *ena* for *idam*/*etad* in *anvādeśa* before the accusative, *ṭā* and *os*; *(p. 466)* *ā* for *ṭā* by '*supāṃ suluk*' (Pā. sū. 7-1-39). *vyacaḥ*: *vyaca vyājīkaraṇe*, *tudādi*; *asun* by '*sarvadhātubhyo 'sun*' (U. sū. 4-628); '*vyaceḥ kuṭāditvam anasi*' (Kā. 1-2-1-1), so no *ṅit*-treatment under '*gāṅkuṭādi*', and no *saṃprasāraṇa* by '*grahijyāvayi*' (Pā. sū. 6-1-16); initial udātta by '*ñnity ādir nityam*' (Pā. sū. 6-1-197). *dadhe*: *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*, *juhotyādi*, passive *liṭ* third person singular; *eś* by '*liṭas tajhayor eśirec*' (Pā. sū. 3-4-81); doubling, shortening, *jaśtva*; loss of *ā* by '*āto lopa iṭi ca*' (Pā. sū. 6-4-64); final udātta; no lowering, by '*hi ca*' (Pā. sū. 8-1-34).
