### Pages 578–581 — Sūkta 31, Rik 16

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो न इममध्वानं यमगाम दूरात् । आपिः पिता प्रमतिः सोम्यानां भृमिरस्यृषिकृन्मर्त्यानाम् ॥ १६ ॥
*imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo na imam adhvānaṃ yam agāma dūrāt | āpiḥ pitā pramatiḥ somyānāṃ bhṛmir asy ṛṣikṛn martyānām || 16 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** इमाम् । अग्ने । शरणिम् । मीमृषः । नः । इमम् । अध्वानम् । यम् । अगाम । दूरात् । आपिः । पिता । प्रऽमतिः । सोम्यानाम् । भृमिः । असि । ऋषिऽकृत् । मर्त्यानाम् ॥ १६ ॥
*imām | agne | śaraṇim | mīmṛṣaḥ | naḥ | imam | adhvānam | yam | agāma | dūrāt | āpiḥ | pitā | pra-matiḥ | somyānām | bhṛmiḥ | asi | ṛṣi-kṛt | martyānām || 16 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 578)* *(compressed; doubtful words marked [?])*: इमामग्न इत्यनयानाहिताग्निरार्त्विज्यं कृत्वा स्वाग्न्यावाहुतिं जुहुयात् । ऋत्विजो वृणीते इति खण्ड एवमनाहिताग्निर्गृह्य इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो नः । आ. गृ. १-२३-२३ [?] इति सूत्रितम् ॥ हे अग्ने त्वं नोऽस्मत्संबन्धिनीमिमामिदानीं संपादितां शरणिं हिंसां व्रतलोपरूपां मीमृषः । क्षमस्व । तथा त्वदीयसेवामग्निहोत्रादिरूपां परित्यज्य दूरादूरदेशं यमिममध्वानमगाम वयं गतवन्तः । तमपि क्षमस्वेति शेषः । सोम्यानां सोमार्हाणां सोमसंस्कर्तॄणां मर्त्यानां त्वमापिर्बन्धुरापादिगुणयुक्तोऽसि । आपिः प्रापणीयः पिता पालकः प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टमननयुक्तो भृमिर्भ्रामकः [?] कर्मनिर्वाहक इत्यर्थः । ऋषिकृद्दर्शनकारी ॥ *(the grammatical tail on* śaraṇim, mīmṛṣaḥ, agāma, bhṛmiḥ *follows)*
*imām agna ity anayānāhitāgnir ārtvijyaṃ kṛtvā svāgnyāv āhutiṃ juhuyāt | ṛtvijo vṛṇīte iti khaṇḍa evam anāhitāgnir gṛhya imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo naḥ | ā. gṛ. 1-23-23 [?] iti sūtritam || he agne tvaṃ no 'smatsaṃbandhinīm imām idānīṃ saṃpāditāṃ śaraṇiṃ hiṃsāṃ vratalopa-rūpāṃ mīmṛṣaḥ | kṣamasva | tathā tvadīyasevām agnihotrādirūpāṃ parityajya dūrād dūradeśaṃ yam imam adhvānam agāma vayaṃ gatavantaḥ | tam api kṣamasveti śeṣaḥ | somyānāṃ somārhāṇāṃ somasaṃskartṝṇāṃ martyānāṃ tvam āpir bandhur āpādiguṇayukto 'si | āpiḥ prāpaṇīyaḥ pitā pālakaḥ pramatiḥ prakṛṣṭamananayukto bhṛmir bhrāmakaḥ [?] karmanirvāhaka ity arthaḥ | ṛṣikṛd darśanakārī ||*
"With this rik the *anāhitāgni* (one who has not set up the fires), having performed the priestly office, should offer oblation in his own fire. In the section *ṛtvijo vṛṇīte*, thus the *anāhitāgni*, taking [the fire], [recites] *imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo naḥ* (Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra 1-23-23 [?]). O Agni! Forgive (*mīmṛṣaḥ*) this fault — this injury, in the form of a lapse in our vows — that has now occurred, [which is] ours; and likewise forgive this path (*adhvānam*) that we have taken, far from [*dūrāt*] giving up your service in the form of the *agnihotra* and the like. You are friend (*āpi*), father, favourably minded, to those who are fit for Soma [*somyānām*], the Soma-preparers, among mortals; the *āpi* is the one to be attained; the *pitā* the protector; the *pramati* one endowed with excellent thought; *bhṛmi* the one who makes [them] wander [?] — that is, the *karmanirvāhaka* (the one who carries out the rite); *ṛṣikṛt*, the maker of seers, who gives vision."

*(Grammar pages 579–581, noted briefly:* śaraṇim *— *śṝ hiṃsāyām*, *kryādi*; the affix *ani* is established by the Uṇādi rule (P.: *aṇ*-type) *uṇādibhir*; *ani*; before the *ārdhadhātuka*, guṇa of the root by P. 7-3-84 *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*; *ṛ* → *r* ... *aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi* P. 8-4-2: *n* → *ṇ*; initial acute by the suffix;* mīmṛṣaḥ *— *mṛṣa titikṣāyām*; causal *ṇic* (*hetumati ca*); a root by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* P. 3-1-32; *luṅ* 2nd singular *sip*; *itaś ca* (P. 3-4-100) drops *i*; since *luṅ* comes after *ṇic*, *ciṇ*... by P. 3-1-48 *ṇiśrisrukamyaḥ kartari caṅ* (णिश्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः कर्तरि चङ्) *cli* → *caṅ*; *mṛṣ* + *i* + *a* + *s*: the guṇa of the light penult is prevented by *nityaṃ chandasi* (P. 7-4-8 *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*, the print: P. 7-4-8 [?]) here *ṛ* → *ṛ*… by P. 7-4-? *nityaṃ chandasi*: the penult's *ṛ* is replaced by *ṛ* [*m* + *ṛ* *ṣ*]; *ṇeraniṭi* drops the *ṇi* before *caṅ*; *caṅi* P. 6-1-11 doubles the root; *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; *ur at* P. 7-4-66 → *a* … *mīmṛṣaḥ*: *sanvallaghuni caṅpare 'nāglope* P. 7-4-93 gives the *san*-like doubling; *sanyataḥ* P. 7-4-79 *i* for the reduplicate *a*; lengthening by P. 7-4-94 *dīrgho laghoḥ*; *s* → *ru* and visarga; the lowering of the verb by P. 8-1-28;* agāma *— *iṅ gatau*, *adādi*; *gā* substituted in the *luṅ* by P. 2-4-45 *iṇo gā luṅi*; 1st person plural *mas*; *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* drops its *s* (P. 3-4-99); *cli luṅi* → *sic* by P. 3-1-44 *cleḥ sic*; *sic* dropped by P. 2-4-77 *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu*; the *aṭ* augment is added; *agāma*; the augment being acute, initial-acute;* bhṛmiḥ *— *bhramu anavasthāne* ['to wander']; *in* by Uṇ. 4-120 *bhrameḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca* (the print: Uṇ. 4-?? [?]); *saṃprasāraṇa* of *r* gives *ṛ*; by P. 6-1-108 *pūrvarūpa*; *bhṛmi*; by P. 1-1-5 *kṅiti ca*, since the *kit* is understood, the root takes the *kit* status so no guṇa of the light penult; *in* is *nit*, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197. Numerals as read, many [?].)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 579)* **अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni | **नः (naḥ)** — our (arisen from us) | **इमां शरणिम् (imāṃ śaraṇim)** — this fault [which is of the nature of a lapse in vows] | **मीमृषः (mīmṛṣaḥ)** — forgive | **दूरात् (dūrāt)** — [leaving the *agnihotra* and the like] far | **यम् इमम् अध्वानम् (yam imam adhvānam)** — which this path [on which we have strayed] | **अगाम (agāma)** — we have come [forgive that too] | **सोम्यानाम् (somyānām)** — [of those who] perform the sacrifices by pressing Soma | **मर्त्यानाम् (martyānām)** — [for] men, the sacrificers | **आपिः (āpiḥ)** — [you are] a relation | **पिता (pitā)** — protector | **प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ)** — [the one of] favourable intent | **भृमिः (bhṛmiḥ)** — [the one who] carries out the rite | **ऋषिकृत् (ṛṣikṛt)** — [the one who] gives vision | **असि (asi)** — you are.

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** O Agni! Forgive this fault of ours, arising from the lapse of our vows; and likewise forgive the path on which we have strayed, far away from the *agnihotra* and other rites. You are to the sacrificers who perform sacrifices with Soma a relation, a protector, a friend of favourable intent, the carrier-out of the rites, and the one who gives vision.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Agni, forgive us our negligence, this path in which we have gone astray ; you will be sought as the protector and encourager of those who offer suitable libations ; you are the conductor of the sacrifice and make yourself visible to all men.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 580)*
**शरणिम् (śaraṇim)** — *śṝ hiṃsāyām*: injury [that is, the faults and omissions that we could have made in the sacrifice] — the defects, or the shortcomings [*nyūnatā*].
**मीमृषः (mīmṛṣaḥ)** — *mṛṣa titikṣāyām*: forgive.
**इमं अध्वानं यं अगाम दूरात् (imam adhvānam yam agāma dūrāt)** — 'in carrying out this sacrifice, if we have transgressed the prescribed procedures, rules [the path], forgive that': that is the sense.
**आपिः पिता (āpiḥ pitā)** — *prāpaṇīyaḥ pālakaḥ*: we have approached you, thinking you the protector; that is, 'we have come to you as the one who protects'.
**सोम्यानाम् (somyānām)** — *somārhāṇām anuṣṭhātṝṇām*: the priests and others who drink Soma in the sacrifice.
**भृमिः (bhṛmiḥ)** — *bhramu anavasthāne*; *bhrāmakaḥ*: [literally 'the wanderer'] — the one who carries out the sacrifice.
**ऋषिकृत् (ṛṣikṛt)** — *darśanakṛt samyag jñānakaraḥ*: 'the maker of vision' — he who gives vision, that is, makes [things] visible; or gives knowledge.

### Pages 581–588 — Sūkta 31, Rik 17 *(begun; see the next batch)*

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: मनुष्वदग्ने अङ्गिरस्वदङ्गिरो ययातिवत्सदने पूर्ववच्छुचे । अच्छ याह्या वहा दैव्यं जनमा सादय बर्हिषि यक्षि च प्रियम् ॥ १७ ॥
*manuṣvad agne aṅgirasvad aṅgiro yayātivat sadane pūrvavac chuce | accha yāhy ā vahā daivyaṃ janam ā sādaya barhiṣi yakṣi ca priyam || 17 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** मनुष्वत् । अग्ने । अङ्गिरस्वत् । अङ्गिरः । ययातिऽवत् । सदने । पूर्वऽवत् । शुचे । अच्छ । याहि । आ । वह । दैव्यम् । जनम् । आ । सादय । बर्हिषि । यक्षि । च । प्रियम् ॥ १७ ॥
*manuṣvat | agne | aṅgirasvat | aṅgiraḥ | yayāti-vat | sadane | pūrva-vat | śuce | accha | yāhi | ā | vaha | daivyam | janam | ā | sādaya | barhiṣi | yakṣi | ca | priyam || 17 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 582)* *(read at 130 dpi; one clause illegible [?])*: हे शुचे शुद्धियुक्ताङ्गिरोऽङ्गनशील हविरादानाय तत्र तत्र गमनशीलाग्ने अच्छाभिमुख्येन सदने देवयजनदेशे याहि गच्छ । [तत्र चेत्यादि — illegible [?]] । मनुष्वत् यथा मनुरनुष्ठानदेशे गच्छति । अङ्गिरस्वत् यथा चाङ्गिरा गच्छति । ययातिवत् यथा ययातिर्नाम राजा गच्छति । पूर्वावत् अन्ये च पूर्वपुरुषा यथा गच्छन्ति । यथा मन्वादयो यज्ञे गच्छन्ति तद्वत् । अथवा मन्वादीनां यज्ञे यथा त्वं गच्छसि तद्वत् । गत्वा च दैव्यं देवतासमूहरूपं जनमा वह । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यानीय । आनीय च बर्हिष्यास्तीर्णे दर्भ आ सादय । तान् हवींषि उपवेशय । उपवेश्य च प्रियमभीष्टं हविर्यक्षि च देहि ॥ *(a closing grammatical tail follows on p. 582; to be taken up in the next batch)*
*he śuce śuddhiyuktāṅgiro 'ṅganaśīla havirādānāya tatra tatra gamanaśīlāgne acchābhimukhyena sadane devayajanadeśe yāhi gaccha | [tatra cetyādi — illegible [?]] | manuṣvat yathā manur anuṣṭhānadeśe gacchati | aṅgirasvat yathā cāṅgirā gacchati | yayātivat yathā yayātir nāma rājā gacchati | pūrvavat anye ca pūrvapuruṣā yathā gacchanti | yathā manvādayo yajñe gacchanti tadvat | athavā manvādīnāṃ yajñe yathā tvaṃ gacchasi tadvat | gatvā ca daivyaṃ devatāsamūharūpaṃ janam ā vaha | asmin karmaṇy ānīya | ānīya ca barhiṣy āstīrṇe darbha ā sādaya | tān havīṃṣi upaveśaya | upaveśya ca priyam abhīṣṭaṃ havir yakṣi ca dehi ||*
"O pure (*śuce*) Aṅgiras — one who goes about [*aṅganaśīla*] — O Agni who go here and there to take the oblations! Go (*yāhi*) to the sacrificial place [*sadane*], facing it, as Manu goes to the place of performance; as Aṅgiras goes; as the king named Yayāti goes; as other forefathers go; as Manu and the others go to the sacrifice — or: as you went to the sacrifices of Manu and the others. Having gone, bring (*ā vaha*) the host of the gods — *daivyam janam* — to this rite; having brought them, seat them on the spread grass (*barhiṣi*); seat the oblations [there]; and, having seated, give (*yakṣi*) them the dear oblation they desire."

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 582)* **शुचे (śuce)** — [O Agni,] pure | **अङ्गिरः (aṅgiraḥ)** — [for taking the oblations] one who goes about in many places | **अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni | **अच्छ (accha)** — [to the sacrifice] facing | **सदने (sadane)** — to the place of the divine sacrifice | **मनुष्वत् (manuṣvat)** — like Manu | **अङ्गिरस्वत् (aṅgirasvat)** — like Aṅgiras | **ययातिवत् (yayātivat)** — like Yayāti | **पूर्वत् (pūrvavat)** — like other forefathers, or [as you went] to the sacrifices of Manu and the others | **याहि (yāhi)** — go | **दैव्यम् (daivyam)** — the host of the gods | **जनम् (janam)** — people | **आ वह (ā vaha)** — bring (to this rite) | **बर्हिषि (barhiṣi)** — upon the spread *darbha* [grass] | **आ सादय (ā sādaya)** — seat [them] | **प्रियम् (priyam)** — [for them] the desired oblation | **यक्षि च (yakṣi ca)** — and offer.

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** O pure Agni, who go about in many places to take the oblations! Come, facing this rite, to the place of the divine sacrifice, as you went to the sacrifices of Manu, Aṅgiras, Yayāti and the other forefathers. Bring the host of the gods to this rite; seat them on the excellent *darbha* seats; and offer them the oblations that they desire.

*(The English Translation, Special Topics and grammar of Rik 17 are on pp. 583–, PDF 598 — to be written in the next batch.)*

### Pages 583–584 — Sūkta 31, Rik 17 — continued *(the Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Prati-padārtha and Bhāvārtha are given at the end of the previous batch)*

**Bhāvārtha, alternative** *(pp. 582–583; the print gives it after "Or"):* O pure Agni, who go about to take the oblations! Come facing this sacrifice of ours, as [you went] to the sacrifices of Manu, Aṅgiras, Yayāti and the other forefathers. Having come, [bring] the hosts of the gods, seat them on the spread *darbha* seat called *barhis-straṇa*, and offer them the oblations that they like.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Pure Agni, in the same way as you went to the sacrifices of Manu, Angiras, Yayati and other ancestors to receive the oblations, you bring hither the divine personages, seat them on the sacred grass and offer them sacrificial oblation.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 583)*
**ययातिवत् (yayātivat)** — Yayāti was a king. His name occurs in the Ṛgveda in this rik, and in
> **ययातेर्यो नहुषस्य बर्हिषि देवा आसते ते अधि ब्रुवन्तु नः ॥** *(Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-63-1 [as the source gives it])* — *yayater yo nahuṣasya barhiṣi devā āsate te adhi bruvantu naḥ ||* — *Mine, tentative:* "[They] who sit on the sacrificial grass of Yayāti, [son] of Nahuṣa — let those gods speak for us."
and nowhere else [by the author's count]. From this example, Yayāti is said to be related to Nahuṣa or the Nahuṣa clan; this king can therefore be said to have been a king of the Nahuṣa people, or he may have been of the lineage of Nahuṣa. The kings named Nahuṣa and Yayāti spoken of in the Purāṇas and other works have no connection with the kings of those names spoken of in the Ṛgveda.
**दैव्यं जनम् (daivyaṃ janam)** — *devatāsaṃbandhiyād janaran*: 'people connected with deities', that is, the gods.

*(Grammar pages 583–584, noted briefly:* manuṣvat *— the affix *vati* by P. 5-1-115 *tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ* (तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः), 'resembling in action', after the nominative [in the sense of 'equal action']; or, by P. 5-1-116 *tatra tasyeva* (तत्र तस्येव), the affix *vati* in the sense of the genitive; as the word is in the *ayasmayādi* list, by P. 1-4-20 *ayasmayādīni chandasi* it has the designation *bha*, hence *pada*-designation is lacking, so the *s* does not take *ru* and visarga; *ṣatva* by P. 8-3-59 *ādeśapratyayayoḥ*: *manuṣvat*; by the suffix's initial acute, the *a* after the *v* is acute; *aṅgirasvat*, *yayātivat* and *pūrvavat* are the same — in the nominative or in the genitive sense, the affix *vati* applies, the process as before;* vaha *— *vaha prāpaṇe*, *bhvādi*, *loṭ* 2nd singular, *sip* → *hi*; *śap* by P. 3-1-68 *kartari śap*; *hi* dropped by P. 6-4-105 *ato heḥ*; *vaha*; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 *dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ*;* yakṣi *— *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*, *bhvādi*, *loṭ* 2nd singular *sip*; *hi* substitution is not applied by *vyatyayo bahulam*; *śap* dropped by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *yaj* + *si*: *j* → *ṣ* by P. 8-2-36 *vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ* (व्रश्चभ्रस्ज…षः); *ṣ* + *s* → *k* by P. 8-2-41 *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* (षढोः कः सि); the *s* after *k* → *ṣ* by P. 8-3-59 *ādeśapratyayayoḥ*: *yakṣi*. Numerals as read.)*

### Pages 584–587 — Sūkta 31, Rik 18 (Triṣṭubh; last rik of the sūkta)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: एतेनाग्ने ब्रह्मणा वावृधस्व शक्ती वा यत्ते चकृमा विदा वा । उत प्र णेष्यभि वस्यो अस्मान्सं नः सृज सुमत्या वाजवत्या ॥ १८ ॥
*etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva śaktī vā yat te cakṛmā vidā vā | uta pra ṇeṣy abhi vasyo asmān saṃ naḥ sṛja sumatyā vājavatyā || 18 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** एतेन । अग्ने । ब्रह्मणा । ववृधस्व । शक्ती । वा । यत् । ते । चकृम । विदा । वा । उत । प्र । नेषि । अभि । वस्यः । अस्मान् । सम् । नः । सृज । सुऽमत्या । वाजऽवत्या ॥ १८ ॥
*etena | agne | brahmaṇā | vavṛdhasva | śaktī | vā | yat | te | cakṛma | vidā | vā | uta | pra | neṣi | abhi | vasyaḥ | asmān | sam | naḥ | sṛja | su-matyā | vāja-vatyā || 18 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 585)* *(read at 130 dpi; compressed, doubtful words marked [?])*: साग्निचयने क्रतावुखासंभरणे योऽमिष्वाग्नेर्ब्राह्मणतः पुरोनुवाक्यैतेनाग्ने इत्येषा [?] । दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यामिष्ट्वेति खण्ड एतेनाग्ने ब्रह्मणा वावृधस्व ब्रह्म च ते जातवेदो नमश्च । आ. ४-१ [?] इति सूत्रितम् ॥ हे अग्ने एतेनास्मत्प्रयुक्तेन ब्रह्मणा मन्त्रेण वावृधस्व । अभिवृद्धो भव । शक्ती वा विदा वा अस्मदीयशक्त्या चास्मदीयज्ञानेन च ते तव यत्स्तोत्रं चकृम वयं कृतवन्तः । एतेन ब्रह्मेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । उतापि चास्माननुष्ठातॄन् वस्यो वसुमत्तरं रत्नलक्षणं श्रेयः प्र णेषि । प्रकर्षेण प्रापय । नोऽस्मान्वाजवत्या प्रभूतान्नयुक्तया सुमत्यानुष्ठानविषयया शोभनबुद्ध्या सं सृज । संयोजय ॥ ववृधस्व । वृधु वृद्धौ । लेट्यडागमः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । द्विर्भावहलादिशेषोरत्वानि [?] । अभ्यासस्य संहितायां दीर्घश्छान्दसः । शक्ती । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयायाः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वम् । क्तिनो नित्त्वाद्यायुदात्तत्वम् । विदा । सानेकाच इति तृतीयाया उदात्तत्वम् । नेषि । णीञ् प्रापणे । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि णोपदेशस्य । इति णत्वम् । सुमत्या । मन्क्तिन्नित्यादिनोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं प्रथमाध्याये प्रपञ्चितम् । ऋग्वे. १-२-२ । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ १८ ॥
*sāgnicayane kratāv ukhāsaṃbharaṇe yo 'miṣv āgner brāhmaṇataḥ purono-vākyaitenāgne ity eṣā [?] | darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭveti khaṇḍa etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca | ā. 4-1 [?] iti sūtritam || he agne etenāsmatprayuktena brahmaṇā mantreṇa vāvṛdhasva | abhivṛddho bhava | śaktī vā vidā vā asmadīyaśaktyā cāsmadīyajñānena ca te tava yat stotraṃ cakṛma vayaṃ kṛtavantaḥ | etena brahmeti pūrvatrānvayaḥ | utāpi cāsmān anuṣṭhātṝn vasyo vasumattaraṃ ratnalakṣaṇaṃ śreyaḥ pra ṇeṣi | prakarṣeṇa prāpaya | no 'smān vājavatyā prabhūtānnayuktayā sumatyānuṣṭhānaviṣayayā śobhanabuddhyā saṃ sṛja | saṃyojaya || vavṛdhasva | vṛdhu vṛddhau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | dvirbhāvahalādiśeṣo ratvāni [?] | abhyāsasya saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaś chāndasaḥ | śaktī | supāṃ suluk iti tṛtīyāyāḥ pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvam | ktino nittvād ādyudāttatvam | vidā | sānekāca iti tṛtīyāyā udāttatvam | neṣi | ṇīñ prāpaṇe | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya | iti ṇatvam | sumatyā | mankitnity ādinottarapadāntodāttatvaṃ prathamādhyāye prapañcitam | ṛgve. 1-2-2 | udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti vibhakter udāttatvam || 18 ||*
"In the *sāgnicayana* [fire-altar-building] sacrifice, at the bringing together of the *ukhā* [the fire-pot], [this rik is used] as *purono-vākyā* ('invitatory') in the offering to Agni 'who is of the *brāhmaṇa*'; [the Āśvalāyana sūtra, in the section *darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā*, lays down] '*etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca*' (Āś. 4-1 [?]). O Agni! Be strengthened (*vāvṛdhasva*) by this *brahman* — the mantra we have used; become increased [in power]. The praise (*stotra*) of yours that we have made, according to our ability (*śaktī*) or knowledge (*vidā*) — [this is the connection with *etena brahmaṇā*]. And lead us to the best good (*vasyaḥ*) — the 'more precious' welfare in the form of riches (*ratna*). Unite us (*saṃ sṛja*) with good intelligence (*sumatyā*) concerned with the rite, [and] with plentiful food (*vājavatyā*)."

*(Grammar pages 586–587, noted briefly:* vavṛdhasva *[= *vāvṛdhasva*] — *vṛdhu vṛddhau*, *bhvādi*; *loṭ* 2nd singular ātmanepada *thās*; the *aṭ* augment by P. 3-4-94 *leṭo 'ḍāṭau*; *śluḥ* in the place of *śap* by *bahulaṃ chandasi* (P. 2-4-76 *bahulaṃ chandasi* [?]); doubling by P. 6-1-10 *ślau*; *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* P. 7-4-60; *a* by P. 7-4-66 *uraṇ raparaḥ*: *vṛ* → *va*; the *r* is removed again by *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; *thās* → *se* by P. 3-4-91 *sevāṃvāmau* (the print: P. 3-4-91 *sevāṃvāmau* — *se* → *sva* in the imperative; [read with doubt]); the Vedic lengthening of the reduplicate in the Saṃhitā; lowered by P. 8-1-28;* śaktī *— *śakti* [*śakla śaktau*] with the instrumental singular; the lengthening by P. 7-1-39 *supāṃ suluk…*; *śakti* ends in *ktin*, a *nit* suffix, so initial acute;* vidā *— *vid* [*vid jñāne*] with *kvip*; instrumental singular *vidā*; by P. 6-1-168 *sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ* the ending, in a monosyllabic word, is acute;* neṣi *— *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*, *bhvādi*, *laṭ*, *sip*; *śap* dropped by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; the initial *ṇ* → *n* by P. 6-1-65 *ṇo naḥ*; guṇa on account of the *sārvadhātuka*; *ṣatva* of *s* after *i* by P. 8-3-59 *ādeśapratyayayoḥ*: *neṣi*; with *pra*, *ṇatva* of the *n* by P. 8-4-14 *upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya* (उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि णोपदेशस्य): *prāṇeṣi* [as the Saṃhitā]; *sumatyā* — a compound of *śobhanā cāsau matiś ca*; the end-acute of the second member by P. 6-2-? *mankitnity…* — explained at length in the first adhyāya (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-2-2); instrumental singular with *yaṇ*; the ending acute by P. 6-1-174 *udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt*. Numerals as read, [?].)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 585)* **अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni | **शक्ती वा (śaktī vā)** — according to [our] ability | **विदा वा (vidā vā)** — according to [our] knowledge | **ते (te)** — your | **यत् (yat)** — which [praise] | **चकृम (cakṛma)** — we have made | **एतेन ब्रह्मणा (etena brahmaṇā)** — by this mantra [which we used] | **वावृधस्व (vāvṛdhasva)** — be increased [in strength] | **उत (uta)** — and | **अस्मान् (asmān)** — us [who perform the rites] | **वस्यः (vasyaḥ)** — with good fortune | **प्रणेषि (praṇeṣi)** — unite | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **वाजवत्या (vājavatyā)** — with abundant food | **सुमत्या (sumatyā)** — with good intelligence [concerned with the performance of the rite] | **संसृज (saṃsṛja)** — unite well.

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** O Agni! Be increased in strength by this mantra, which we have used, and by the praise of you that we have made according to our ability and our knowledge. Favour us, who perform the rites, with good fortune; give us plentiful food, and unite us well with the good understanding that is fit for the performance of the rite.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Agni, allow yourself to be pleased with this hymn, which we have composed according to our ability, according to our knowledge ; therefore lead us towards the highest good and endow as [sic] with right understanding together with abundant food.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 586)* In the fire-piling rite called *agnicayana*, in the *iṣṭi* called *ukhāsaṃbharaṇa*, when oblations are offered to Agni 'of the Brahmaṇvat name', this rik is to be used as the *purono-vākyā* [invitatory verse]: this is laid down in the section *darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā* of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra ***etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva*** (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-31-18) ***brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca*** (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-6?-2 [?]).
**ब्रह्मणा (brahmaṇā)** — *stotreṇa*: by praise.
**वावृधस्व (vāvṛdhasva)** — *vṛdhu vṛddhau*: *abhivṛddho bhava*: be pleased; be satisfied.
**शक्ती विदा (śaktī vidā)** — as far as our strength goes, as far as our knowledge goes.
**सं नः सृज सुमत्या वाजवत्या (saṃ naḥ sṛja sumatyā vājavatyā)** — 'unite us with good understanding and with food and other requisites': that is, 'give us these and favour us'.

## ॥ ಮೂವತ್ತೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 32 — *"indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam"* ("The Thirty-second Sūkta"; second sūkta of the Seventh Anuvāka)

*(Printed pp. 587 lower half–. The introductory note is on p. 587, the Kannada Anuvāda and heading block on p. 588; Rik 1 begins on p. 588 foot and continues on p. 589.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 587)** *(read at 130 dpi; compressed, doubtful words marked [?])*

> इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीति पञ्चदशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तम् । आङ्गिरसो हिरण्यस्तूप ऋषिः । त्रिष्टुप् छन्दः । इन्द्रो देवता । इन्द्रस्य पञ्चोनेत्यनुक्रमणिका । अग्निष्टोमे माध्यंदिने सवने निष्केवल्यशस्त्र इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीति निविद्धानीयं सूक्तम् । निष्केवल्यस्येति खण्ड इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीत्येतस्मिन्नैन्द्रीं निविदं दध्यात् । आ. ५-२३ [?] इति । विषुवत्यपि तस्मिन् शस्त्र एतद्विनियुक्तम् । विषुवान्वा … कीर्त्यः [?] इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीत्येतस्मिन्नैन्द्रीं निविदं शंस्त्वा [?] । आ. ८-६ [?] इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्य एतस्यैव विनियुक्तम् । राथन्तरो दक्षिणः पक्ष इति खण्डे चतस्रः सतीः षट्बृहतीः करोतीन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचम् । ऐ. ब्रा. [५-३-१ ?] इति ॥

*indrasya nu vīryāṇīti pañcadaśarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktam | āṅgiraso hiraṇyastūpa ṛṣiḥ | triṣṭup chandaḥ | indro devatā | indrasya pañconety anukramaṇikā | agniṣṭome mādhyaṃdine savane niṣkevalyaśastra indrasya nu vīryāṇīti nividdhānīyaṃ sūktam | niṣkevalyasyeti khaṇḍa indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ dadhyāt | ā. 5-23 [?] iti | viṣuvaty api tasmin śastra etad viniyuktam | viṣuvān vā … kīrtyaḥ [?] iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ śaṃstvā [?] | ā. 8-6 [?] iti || mahāvrate niṣkevalya etasyaiva viniyuktam | rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣa iti khaṇḍe catasraḥ satīḥ ṣaḍbṛhatīḥ karotīndrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam | ai. brā. [5-3-1 ?] iti ||*

**Translation:** "*Indrasya nu vīryāṇi* is the second sūkta [of this anuvāka]; it has fifteen riks; the seer is Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa; the metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā: '*indrasya* — five less [than twenty]'. In the Agniṣṭoma, at the midday pressing, in the Niṣkevalya-śastra, the sūkta *indrasya nu vīryāṇi* is the *nividdhānīya*. In the section *niṣkevalyasya* it is laid down: 'in this [sūkta] *indrasya nu vīryāṇi* one should place the Indra-*nivid*' (Āśvalāyana 5-23 [?]). In the Viṣuvat too, in that [Niṣkevalya] śastra, it is used: in the section *viṣuvān vā* … [it is laid down]: 'having recited the Indra-*nivid* in this [sūkta] *indrasya nu vīryāṇi*' (Āś. 8-6 [?]). In the Mahāvrata also, in the Niṣkevalya, it is used: in the section *rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ* ['the Rāthantara is the right wing']: 'he makes four *satī* and six *bṛhatī* [verses] — *indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam*' (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa [5-3-1 ?])."

**॥ Anuvāda (Kannada) ॥** *(p. 588)* *Indrasya nu vīryāṇi* is the second sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. It has fifteen riks. Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa is the seer of this sūkta; the metre is Triṣṭubh; Indra is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said *indrasya pañconā* [fifteen]. In the *Agniṣṭoma* and other sacrifices, at the midday pressing, in reciting the mantras of the Niṣkevalya-śastra, the sūkta *indrasya nu vīryāṇi* is to be recited as a *nividdhānīya* sūkta: this is explained in the section *niṣkevalyasya* of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra *indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ dadhyāt* (Āś. 5-23 [?]). In the *Viṣuvat* too, this sūkta is used for reciting the mantras of that śastra; that matter is shown in the section *viṣuvān vā kīrtyaḥ* of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra *indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ śaṃstvā* (Āś. 8-6 [?]). In the *Mahāvrata* also the sūkta is used for reciting the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras. This matter is described in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, in the section *rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ*, in the sentence *catasraḥ satīḥ ṣaḍbṛhatīḥ karotīndrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam* (Ai. Ā. 5-?? [?]).

**Heading block (p. 588):** Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 32. Aṣṭaka 1; Adhyāya 2; Varga **36 [?], 37 [?], 38 [?]** *(the small Kannada varga numerals are unreliable; recorded as read)*. Number of riks: 15. Ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa. Devatā: Indra. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

### Pages 588–592 — Sūkta 32, Rik 1

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचं यानि चकार प्रथमानि वज्री । अहन्नहिमन्वपस्ततर्द प्र वक्षणा अभिनत्पर्वतानाम् ॥ १ ॥
*indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocaṃ yāni cakāra prathamāni vajrī | ahann ahim anv apas tatarda pra vakṣaṇā abhinat parvatānām || 1 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** इन्द्रस्य । नु । वीर्याणि । प्र । वोचम् । यानि । चकार । प्रथमानि । वज्री । अहन् । अहिम् । अनु । अपः । ततर्द । प्र । वक्षणाः । अभिनत् । पर्वतानाम् ॥ १ ॥
*indrasya | nu | vīryāṇi | pra | vocam | yāni | cakāra | prathamāni | vajrī | ahan | ahim | anu | apaḥ | tatarda | pra | vakṣaṇāḥ | abhinat | parvatānām || 1 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 589)*: वज्री वज्रयुक्त इन्द्रः प्रथमानि पूर्वसिद्धानि मुख्यानि वा यानि वीर्याणि पराक्रमयुक्तानि कर्माणि चकार तस्येन्द्रस्य तानि वीर्याणि नु क्षिप्रं प्रब्रवीमि । कानि वीर्याणीति तदुच्यते । अहिं मेघमहन् हतवान् । तदेतदेकं वीर्यम् । अनु पश्चादपो जलानि ततर्द हिंसितवान् । भूमौ पातितवानित्यर्थः । इदं द्वितीयं वीर्यम् । पर्वतानां संबन्धिनीर्वक्षणाः प्रवहणशीला नदीः प्राभिनत् । भिन्नवान् । कूलद्वयकर्षणेन प्रवाहितवानित्यर्थः । इदं तृतीयं वीर्यम् । एवमुत्तरत्रापि द्रष्टव्यम् ॥ वीर्याणि । शूर वीर विक्रान्तौ धातुः … यत् … ॥ *(the grammatical tail on* vīryāṇi, vocam, cakāra, ahan, ahim, tatarda, vakṣaṇāḥ *is compressed; characterised below)*
*vajrī vajrayukta indraḥ prathamāni pūrvasiddhāni mukhyāni vā yāni vīryāṇi parākramayuktāni karmāṇi cakāra tasyendrasya tāni vīryāṇi nu kṣipraṃ prabravīmi | kāni vīryāṇīti tad ucyate | ahiṃ megham ahan hatavān | tad etad ekaṃ vīryam | anu paścād apo jalāni tatarda hiṃsitavān | bhūmau pātitavān ity arthaḥ | idaṃ dvitīyaṃ vīryam | parvatānāṃ saṃbandhinīr vakṣaṇāḥ pravahaṇaśīlā nadīḥ prābhinat | bhinnavān | kūladvayakarṣaṇena pravāhitavān ity arthaḥ | idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vīryam | evam uttaratrāpi draṣṭavyam || vīryāṇi | śūra vīra vikrāntau dhātuḥ … yat … ||*
"I proclaim at once the heroic deeds (*vīryāṇi*) of Indra — the thunderbolt-bearer (*vajrī*) — which he did first (*prathamāni*, 'foremost', or 'previously accomplished'). Which exploits? It is said: *ahim ahan* — he struck the *ahi*, the cloud: this is one exploit. Then (*anu*) he cleft [*tatarda*] the waters (*apaḥ*) — made them fall upon the earth: this is the second. He split open the *vakṣaṇāḥ* — the streams related to the mountains, flowing rivers — so that, by drawing [cutting] the two banks, he made them flow: this is the third exploit. So it is to be understood in what follows also."

*(Grammar pages 589, 591–592, noted briefly:* vīryāṇi *— from the root *śūra vīra vikrāntau*; *ṇic* after it (*vīrayati*); *yat* by P. 5-1-? *ācoyat* [the print: *acoyat*, P. 5-1-? [?]]; *yat* is the pada-final; the *ṇic* dropped by P. 6-4-51 *ṇer aniṭi*; *vīrya*; second plural accusative; the accent: by P. 6-1-185 *tiṅ svaritam* [the print: *tit svaritam* P. 6-1-179 [?]] the *yat* suffix takes *svarita*; here, since the word ends in *yat*, the initial acute (*yato 'nāvaḥ*, P. 6-1-213) would give a prior-member contradiction: the author argues that, if one accepts *yato 'nāvaḥ*, then in the bahuvrīhi *śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasya saḥ* the initial acute is already given by *ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi* (P. 6-1-?), so P. 6-2-120 *vīravīryau ca* ['the second member *vīra*/*vīrya* is initial-acute'] would be superfluous; since the sūtra is separately begun, the maxim shows that for *vīra* alone the rule *yato 'nāvaḥ* does not apply; this resolves the earlier-mentioned *svarita* without difficulty;* vocam *— *vaca paribhāṣaṇe* [or *brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*]; *luṅ*, *vac* *aj*-substitution: *luṅ* → 1st singular *mip*, *am* by P. 3-4-101 *tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ*; *cli* → *a* by P. 3-1-? *asyatiśasyatiśāsakyāti*… (the print: *asyativakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ* P. 3-1-52 *aṅ*); *vac* + *a*: *ū* by P. 6-4-? *vaco 'um* (वच उम्); *um* augment after the root; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; *aṭ* is not added by P. 6-4-75 *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi*: *vocam*;* cakāra *— *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, *liṭ* 3rd singular, *tip* → *ṇal* by P. 3-4-82; doubling, *ur at*, *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*, *cutva*; *vṛddhi* before *ṇal*; *kāra*; *ṇal* is *ṇit*; *lit* gives initial acute... the verb is not lowered as *yat* is correlated;* ahan *— *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*, *adādi*; *laṅ* 3rd singular *tip*; *itaś ca* P. 3-4-100 drops *i*; *śap* dropped by P. 2-4-72; after a *hal*, *tip*'s *t* is dropped by P. 6-1-68 *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal* (हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्सुतिस्यपृक्तं हल्); *aṭ* augment: *ahan*; at the head of a pāda, no lowering; *aṭ* is acute so initial acute;* ahim *— *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *i* by Uṇ. 4-122 *ājigṛ̥…* (*ājisṛpiniśśanibhyāṃ hrasvaś ca*, [?]); the *ca* in the sūtra continues the P. 6-1-? *veñodita* so that the accents of the earlier member are continued; so the *i*-suffix gets the *bha*-sense...; *āji* shortened; *ahi*; the first member [as acute] means the *ā* [of the root] is acute;* tatarda *— *tṛdiḥ hiṃsānādarayoḥ*; the *i* dropped through the *it*-designation; *liṭ* 3rd singular; lowered by P. 8-1-28;* vakṣaṇāḥ *— *vakṣa roṣe*, with *yuc* by P. 3-3-113 *krudhamaṇḍārthebhyaś ca* (क्रुधमण्डार्थेभ्यश्च); *yu* → *ana* by P. 7-1-1; *n* → *ṇ* after *ṣ* (P. 8-4-1); *vakṣaṇa*; nominative plural; the end-acute through *cit* (*ciḥ*?), but by *vyatyayo bahulam* the suffix accent: middle-acute. Numerals as read, many [?].)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 590)* **वज्री (vajrī)** — Indra, who holds the thunderbolt | **प्रथमानि (prathamāni)** — [those] done in the past | **यानि वीर्याणि (yāni vīryāṇi)** — whatever deeds of prowess | **चकार (cakāra)** — he did | **इन्द्रस्य (indrasya)** — of Indra | **वीर्याणि (vīryāṇi)** — those deeds of valour | **नु (nu)** — at once | **प्र वोचम् (pra vocam)** — I shall tell [(of) them one by one] | **अहिम् (ahim)** — the cloud | **अहन् (ahan)** — he struck | **अनु (anu)** — afterwards | **अपः (apaḥ)** — the waters | **ततर्द (tatarda)** — he split open (made to fall on the earth) | **पर्वतानाम् (parvatānām)** — [flowing] from the mountains | **वक्षणाः (vakṣaṇāḥ)** — the flowing rivers | **प्र अभिनत् (pra abhinat)** — he made them flow by splitting [the banks].

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** I proclaim, one by one and at once, the deeds of valour which Indra, the thunderbolt-bearer, did in the past. For example: Indra struck the cloud; afterwards he made the waters fall upon the earth; and he made a path, by cutting the two banks, for the rivers that flow from the mountains.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> I will now enumerate the valorous deeds of Indra, the weilder [sic] of the thunderbolt has achieved ; he clove the cloud, he sent down the waters, he broke open a way for the torrents of the mountain.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(pp. 590–591)* The seer of this sūkta, Hiraṇyastūpa, begins, with this sūkta and the next, to praise Indra by relating, one by one, Indra's mighty deeds. Of these, the commentator says that Indra's first heroic deed is the striking, with his *vajra*, of Vṛtra, who has the form of a cloud; the second is the work of making the rain from that cloud fall on the earth; the third, [the] water fallen on the earth flows as a river and breaks through the mountains.
**वीर्याणि (vīryāṇi)** — deeds of prowess; mighty deeds done with prowess.
**प्र वोचम् (pra vocam)** — I shall say; I shall describe them one by one.
**यानि प्रथमानि (yāni prathamāni)** — the first deeds of valour; or one may say that the word *prathamāni* means 'chief' — the principal deeds of valour.
**वज्री (vajrī)** — one who holds the *vajra* in hand.
**अहिम् (ahim)** — 'the cloud': since the word *ahi* is read among the thirty [?] names of cloud beginning *adri*, *grāvā*, *ahim* means 'the cloud' (Nirukta 1-10 [?]); *ahi* also means 'water' (Nirukta 3-30 [?]); in modern Sanskrit *ahi* means 'a serpent' [the print: *ādhunikasaṃskṛta*].
**वक्षणाः (vakṣaṇāḥ)** — since the word *vakṣaṇāḥ* is read among the thirty-seven names of rivers beginning *avanayaḥ*, *yakṣyaḥ*, *vakṣaṇāḥ* means 'rivers': the rain from the cloud falls on the mountains and flows from there as rivers: that is what is described here.
**प्र अभिनत् पर्वतानाम् (pra abhinat parvatānām)** — the rivers that flow out of the mountains split the mountains and the earth and flow, [and he] makes a way for them; that is the sense.
*See the Ṛgveda-Saṃhitā, part 3, pp. 123–124 [the print gives the page numbers of its own earlier volume], for the account of the demon Vṛtra.*

### Pages 593–595 — Sūkta 32, Rik 2

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: अहन्नहिं पर्वते शिश्रियाणं त्वष्टास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष । वाश्रा इव धेनवः स्यन्दमाना अञ्जः समुद्रमव जग्मुरापः ॥ २ ॥
*ahann ahiṃ parvate śiśriyāṇaṃ tvaṣṭāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa | vāśrā iva dhenavaḥ syandamānā añjaḥ samudram ava jagmur āpaḥ || 2 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** अहन् । अहिम् । पर्वते । शिश्रियाणम् । त्वष्टा । अस्मै । वज्रम् । स्वर्यम् । ततक्ष । वाश्राःऽइव । धेनवः । स्यन्दमानाः । अञ्जः । समुद्रम् । अव । जग्मुः । आपः ॥ २ ॥
*ahan | ahim | parvate | śiśriyāṇam | tvaṣṭā | asmai | vajram | svaryam | tatakṣa | vāśrāḥ-iva | dhenavaḥ | syandamānāḥ | añjaḥ | samudram | ava | jagmuḥ | āpaḥ || 2 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 593)* *(compressed; doubtful words marked [?])*: पर्वते शिश्रियाणमाश्रितमहिं मेघमहन् । हतवान् । अस्मा इन्द्राय स्वर्यं सुष्ठु प्रेरणीयं यद्वा शब्दनीयं स्तुत्यं त्वष्टा विश्वकर्मा वज्रं ततक्ष । तनूकृतवान् । तेन वज्रेण मेघे भिन्ने सति स्यन्दमानाः प्रस्रवणयुक्ता आपः समुद्रमञ्जः सम्यगजग्मुः । प्राप्ताः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वाश्रा वत्सान्प्रति हम्भारवोपेता धेनव इव । यथा धेनवः सहसा वत्सगृहं गच्छन्ति तद्वत् ॥ शिश्रियाणम् । श्रिञ् सेवायाम् । लिटः कानच् । द्विर्भावहलादिशेषेयङादेशाः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । स्वर्यम् । सु गतौ [?] । अस्मात्सुपूर्वाद्धल … ण्यत् । संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इति वृद्ध्यभावः । यद्वा स्वशब्दोपपदात् [?] … । वाश्राः । वाश्यन्त इति वाश्राः । वाशृ शब्दे । स्यायितञ्चीत्यादिना रक् । जग्मुः । उसि गमहनेत्युपधालोपः ॥
*parvate śiśriyāṇam āśritam ahiṃ megham ahan | hatavān | asmā indrāya svaryaṃ suṣṭhu preraṇīyaṃ yadvā śabdanīyaṃ stutyaṃ tvaṣṭā viśvakarmā vajraṃ tatakṣa | tanūkṛtavān | tena vajreṇa meghe bhinne sati syandamānāḥ prasravaṇayuktā āpaḥ samudram añjaḥ samyag ajagmuḥ | prāptāḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vāśrā vatsān prati hambhāravopetā dhenava iva | yathā dhenavaḥ sahasā vatsagṛhaṃ gacchanti tadvat || śiśriyāṇam | śriñ sevāyām | liṭaḥ kānac | dvirbhāvahalādiśeṣeyaṅādeśāḥ | cita ity antodāttatvam | svaryam | su gatau [?] | asmāt supūrvād … ṇyat | saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anitya iti vṛddhyabhāvaḥ | yadvā svaśabdopapadāt [?] … | vāśrāḥ | vāśyanta iti vāśrāḥ | vāśṛ śabde | syāyitañcīty ādinā rak | jagmuḥ | usi gamahanety upadhālopaḥ ||*
"He struck (*ahan*) the cloud [*ahim*] that had taken refuge (*śiśriyāṇam*) on the mountain. For him — Indra — Tvaṣṭṛ, the universal craftsman, shaped a *vajra* well [*svaryam*: to be sent forth well, or to be praised]. When the cloud was split by that *vajra*, the flowing waters, streaming forth, quickly reached the sea [*samudram*], just as lowing cows run to their calves — as cows hasten straightway to the calf's stall."

*(Grammar pages 595, noted briefly:* śiśriyāṇam *— *śriñ sevāyām*, *bhvādi*; *kānac* in the Vedic *liṭ* by P. 3-2-106 *liṭaḥ kānaj vā*; doubling, *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; *śi* + *āna*: *iyaṅ* by P. 6-4-77 *aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau*; *ṇatva* by P. 8-4-2 *aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi*; *cit* gives the end-acute by P. 6-1-163;* svaryam *— *śru gatau* [*sru*]; with *su*, *ṇyat* by P. 3-1-124 *ṛhalor ṇyat*; *ñit*, so *vṛddhi* by P. 7-2-115 *aco ñṇiti*, which by the principle *saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ* is not applied; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; *ur* by P. 1-1-51 *uraṇ raparaḥ*; *su* + *ar* + *ya*: *yaṇ* for *u*: *svarya*; *ṇyat* is *ñit*-like; the *svarita* by P. 6-1-185 *tit svaritam*; so the word ends in *svarita*;* vāśrāḥ *— *vāśyante iti*, from *vāśṛ śabde*; *rak* by Uṇ. 3-?? *syāyitañcivañci-śakibhyaḥ…* (the print: Uṇ. 3-?? [?]); the affix gives end-acute; plural;* syandamānāḥ *— *syandū prasravaṇe*, ātmanepada; *śānac* in the sense of agent; *śap*; *mukāgama* by P. 7-2-82 *āne muk*; *syandamāna*; *śap* is *pit*, so unaccented; *śānac* [being a *laśa*-affix] is unaccented by P. 6-1-186; the root accent then remains: the word is initial-acute;* jagmuḥ *— *gamḷ gatau*, *liṭ* 3rd plural, *jhi* → *us* by P. 3-4-82 *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…*; *asaṃyogāl liṭ kit* P. 1-2-5 makes it *kit*; the penult *a* of the root dropped by P. 6-4-98 *gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi*; doubling, *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*, *cutva*: *jagmuḥ*; lowered by P. 8-1-28. Numerals as read, [?].)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 594)* **पर्वते (parvate)** — on the mountain | **शिश्रियाणम् (śiśriyāṇam)** — [one that] had taken shelter | **अहिम् (ahim)** — the cloud | **अहन् (ahan)** — he cleft | **अस्मै (asmai)** — for this Indra | **स्वर्यम् (svaryam)** — [of] quick motion, or [that makes] noise | **वज्रम् (vajram)** — the thunderbolt | **त्वष्टा (tvaṣṭā)** — Tvaṣṭṛ [the craftsman] | **ततक्ष (tatakṣa)** — fashioned [for him; after the cloud was cleft by that weapon] | **स्यन्दमानाः (syandamānāḥ)** — flowing | **आपः (āpaḥ)** — the waters [of the rivers] | **वाश्रा इव (vāśrā iva)** — as, lowing, | **धेनवः (dhenavaḥ)** — cows, [carefully] going to their calves | **समुद्रम् (samudram)** — the sea | **अञ्जः (añjaḥ)** — eagerly | **अव जग्मुः (ava jagmuḥ)** — went and reached.

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** Tvaṣṭṛ made for Indra a *vajra* of quick motion, or sounding loudly. By that *vajra* Indra cleft the cloud that had taken shelter on the mountain. Afterwards the waters, streaming down as rivers, hastened eagerly and reached the sea, as cows, lowing, go with eagerness to their calves.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> He clove the cloud which had taken shelter on the mountain ; on that occasion Twasta fashioned for him the rumbling thunderbolt ; the flowing waters quickly hastened to the ocean like lowing cows hastening to their calves.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(pp. 594–595)* What was said in the previous rik is described more fully in this rik.
**पर्वते शिश्रियाणम् (parvate śiśriyāṇam)** — since clouds ordinarily rest [on the peaks] of mountains, the seer has described the clouds as having taken shelter on a mountain.
**त्वष्ट्रास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष (tvaṣṭrāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa)** — Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine craftsman, made the *vajra* weapon for Indra. In many places in the Ṛgveda it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ made, of iron, the shining *vajra* weapon for the killing of Vṛtra:
> **मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासोऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुम् ॥** *(Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-48-3 [as the source gives it])* — *mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajram atakṣad āyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjann api kratum ||* — *Mine, tentative:* "For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron *vajra*; in me the gods set [their] will."
In this rik Indra himself says that Tvaṣṭṛ made the iron *vajra* for him.
**वाश्रा इव धेनवः (vāśrā iva dhenavaḥ)** — as cows go to their calves, lowing, so the rivers, roaring loudly from the mountain regions, go to the sea: this is the simile.

### Pages 596–599 — Sūkta 32, Rik 3

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: वृषायमाणोऽवृणीत सोमं त्रिकद्रुकेष्वपिबत्सुतस्य । आ सायकं मघवादत्त वज्रमहन्नेनं प्रथमजामहीनाम् ॥ ३ ॥
*vṛṣāyamāṇo 'vṛṇīta somaṃ trikadrukeṣv apibat sutasya | ā sāyakaṃ maghavādatta vajram ahann enaṃ prathamajām ahīnām || 3 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** वृषऽयमानः । अवृणीत । सोमम् । त्रिऽकद्रुकेषु । अपिबत् । सुतस्य । आ । सायकम् । मघऽवा । अदत्त । वज्रम् । अहन् । एनम् । प्रथमऽजाम् । अहीनाम् ॥ ३ ॥
*vṛṣa-yamānaḥ | avṛṇīta | somam | tri-kadrukeṣu | apibat | sutasya | ā | sāyakam | magha-vā | adatta | vajram | ahan | enam | prathama-jām | ahīnām || 3 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 596)* *(compressed; doubtful words marked [?])*: वृषायमाणो वृष इवाचरन्निन्द्रः सोममवृणीत । वृतवान् । त्रिकद्रुकेषु ज्योतिर्गौरायुरित्येतन्नामकास्त्रयो यागास्त्रिकद्रुका उच्यन्ते । तेषु सुतस्याभिषुतस्य सोमस्यांशमपिबत् । पीतवान् । मघवा धनवानिन्द्रः सायकं बन्धकं वज्रमादत्त । स्वीकृतवान् । तेन च वज्रेणाहीनां मेघानां मध्ये प्रथमजां प्रथमोत्पन्नमेनं मेघमहन् । हतवान् ॥ वृषायमाणः । वृष इवाचरन् । कर्तुः क्यङ् सलोपश्च । पा. ३-१-११ । इति क्यङ् । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः । अदुपदेशात्तोरन्तोदात्तत्वे क्यङन्ताद्धातोरन्तोदात्तत्वम् । सायकम् । षिञ् बन्धने । सिनोतीति सायकः । ण्वुल् । लित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्रथमजाम् । प्रथमं जायत इति प्रथमजाः । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् ॥
*vṛṣāyamāṇo vṛṣa ivācarann indraḥ somam avṛṇīta | vṛtavān | trikadrukeṣu jyotir gaur āyur ity etannāmakās trayo yāgās trikadrukā ucyante | teṣu sutasyābhiṣutasya somasyāṃśam apibat | pītavān | maghavā dhanavān indraḥ sāyakaṃ bandhakaṃ vajram ādatta | svīkṛtavān | tena ca vajreṇāhīnāṃ meghānāṃ madhye prathamajāṃ prathamotpannam enaṃ megham ahan | hatavān || vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ | vṛṣa ivācaran | kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca | pā. 3-1-11 | iti kyaṅ | akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ | adupadeśāt tor antodāttatve kyaṅantād dhātor antodāttatvam | sāyakam | ṣiñ bandhane | sinotīti sāyakaḥ | ṇvul | litsvareṇādyudāttatvam | prathamajām | prathamaṃ jāyata iti prathamajāḥ | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt ||*
"Behaving like a bull (*vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ*), Indra chose [*avṛṇīta*] the Soma; he drank the portion of the pressed [*sutasya*] Soma in the *trikadrukas* — [the three rites named] *jyotiḥ*, *gauḥ* and *āyuḥ* are called *trikadrukas*. Indra, the wealthy (*maghavā*), took (*ā adatta*) the *vajra* (*sāyakam*, 'the binder'), and with that *vajra* struck this first-born (*prathamajām*) cloud among the clouds (*ahīnām*)."

*(Grammar pages 598–599, noted briefly:* vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ *— *vṛṣa iva ācarati*; *kyaṅ* by P. 3-1-11 *kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca*; lengthening by P. 7-4-25 *akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ*; the derived root; *śānac* in the sense of agent, *āne muk* (P. 7-2-82); *ṇatva* of *n* after *ṣ*-contexts: *vṛṣāyamāṇa*; the *śap* is *pit*, unaccented; the *laśa*-affix is unaccented by P. 6-1-186; the *kyaṅ*-ending root's end-acute is retained, so the word is middle-acute at the *yo*;* avṛṇīta *— *vṛñ varaṇe*, *kryādi*, *laṅ* 3rd singular ātmanepada; *śnā* by P. 3-1-81; *ī* by P. 6-4-113 *ī halyaghoḥ*; *n* → *ṇ* by P. 8-4-2 *aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi*; *aṭ* augment; *śnā* is *ñit*-like, no guṇa; lowered by P. 8-1-28;* apibat *— *pā pāne*, *laṅ* 3rd singular *tip*; *śap* by P. 3-1-68; *pibādeśa* by P. 7-3-78 *pāghrādhmā…*; *itaś ca* drops *i* by P. 3-4-100; *piba* ends in *a*, so no guṇa of the penult; *aṭ*; lowered by P. 8-1-28;* sāyakam *— *ṣiñ bandhane*; *sinoti iti sāyakaḥ*; *ṇvul* in the sense of agent; *vu* → *aka* by P. 7-1-1 *yuvor anākau*; *ṇit*, so *vṛddhi* of the root's *i* by P. 7-2-115 *aco ñṇiti*; *ai* → *āy* by P. 6-1-78 *eco 'yavāyāvaḥ*; *sāyaka*; accusative singular; the *lit*-accent: initial acute by P. 6-1-193 *liti*;* adatta *— *ḍudāñ dāne*, *juhotyādi*, *laṅ* 3rd singular ātmanepada *ta*; *śluḥ* by P. 2-4-75; doubling by P. 6-1-10 *ślau*; the reduplicate shortened; *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* P. 6-4-112 drops the root's *ā*; *khari ca* P. 8-4-55 [read *cartva*]; *aṭ* augment: *adatta*; lowered by P. 8-1-28;* prathamajām *— *prathamaṃ jāyate*; *janī prādurbhāve*; *viṭ* by P. 3-2-67 *janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ* (जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट्); *vidvanor anunāsikasyāt* P. 6-4-41: *n* → *ā*; *prathamajā*; accusative singular; the *kṛt*-final accent by P. 6-2-139 *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*. Numerals as read, many [?].)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 597)* **वृषायमाणः (vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ)** — [Indra,] like a bull, in his own time [with the passion of a bull] | **सोमम् (somam)** — Soma-juice | **अवृणीत (avṛṇīta)** — he chose | **त्रिकद्रुकेषु (trikadrukeṣu)** — in the three kinds of sacrifices, *jyotiḥ*, *gauḥ* and *āyuḥ* | **सुतस्य (sutasya)** — [of the Soma-juice, a portion] pressed | **अपिबत् (apibat)** — drank | **मघवा (maghavā)** — Indra, the possessor of wealth | **सायकम् (sāyakam)** — the thunderbolt | **आ अदत्त (ā adatta)** — lifted (with it) | **अहीनाम् (ahīnām)** — [among] the clouds | **प्रथमजाम् (prathamajām)** — born first | **एनम् (enam)** — this cloud | **अहन् (ahan)** — he struck.

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** Indra, like a bull, chose the Soma-juice with eagerness. He drank the pressed Soma-juice in the three kinds of sacrifice called *jyotiḥ*, *gauḥ* and *āyuḥ*. Indra, the wealthy, lifted up the *vajra* in his hand and struck with it the cloud that was first born among the clouds.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Impetuous (or mighty) as a bull, Indra desired Soma ; he drank of the extracted Soma-juice in the three-fold sacrifice ; Indra, lord of riches took his deadly thunderbolt and with it struck the first-born of the clouds.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(pp. 597–598)*
**वृषायमाणः (vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ)** — *vṛṣa ivācaran*: 'behaving like a bull'; having the strength of a bull, or the strength of the bull-like; that is, 'one who shows [his] strength like a bull': exceedingly powerful.
**त्रिकद्रुकेषु (trikadrukeṣu)** — for this word the commentator says: 'the three kinds of sacrifice (*yāga*) called *jyotiḥ*, *gauḥ* and *āyuḥ*'. This word has the sense of 'wooden vessels in which Soma-juice is placed'. A few riks in which this sense is found we give as examples:
> **उग्रेष्विन् शूर मन्दसानस्त्रिकद्रुकेषु पाहि सोममिन्द्र ॥** *(Ṛg-Saṃhitā 2-11-17 [as the source gives it, as read, [?]])* — *ugreṣv in śūra mandasānas trikadrukeṣu pāhi somam indra ||* — *Mine, tentative:* "Exhilarated among the mighty, O hero, drink Soma in the *trikadrukas*, O Indra."
> **त्रिकद्रुकेष्वपिबत्सुतस्यास्य मदे अहिमिन्द्रो जघान ॥** *(Ṛg-Saṃhitā 2-22-1 [as the source gives it])* — *trikadrukeṣv apibat sutasyāsya made ahim indro jaghāna ||* — *Mine, tentative:* "In the *trikadrukas* he drank of the pressed [Soma]; in its exhilaration Indra slew the *ahi*."
> **त्रिकद्रुकेषु महिषो यवाशिरं तुविशुष्मस्तृपत्सोममपिबद्विष्णुना सुतं यथावशत् ॥** *(Ṛg-Saṃhitā 2-22-1 [as the source gives it, partly, [?]])* — *trikadrukeṣu mahiṣo yavāśiraṃ tuviśuṣmas tṛpat somam apibad viṣṇunā sutaṃ yathāvaśat ||* — *Mine, tentative:* "In the *trikadrukas* the mighty one, of great vigour, satisfied, drank the Soma mixed with barley, pressed with Viṣṇu, as he desired."
> **त्रिकद्रुकेषु चेतनं देवासो यज्ञमत्नत ॥** *(Ṛg-Saṃhitā 8-?? [as printed, [?]])* — *trikadrukeṣu cetanaṃ devāso yajñam atnata ||* — *Mine, tentative:* "In the *trikadrukas* the gods spread the thoughtful sacrifice."
> **त्रिकद्रुकेभिः पतति षळुर्वीरेकमिद्बृहत् ॥** *(Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-?? [as printed, [?]])* — *trikadrukebhiḥ patati ṣaḷ urvīr ekam id bṛhat ||* — *Mine, tentative:* "With the *trikadrukas* [one] flies over the six wide [regions], the one great [?]."
This word is always used in the plural, and its use is always in contexts of drinking Soma.
**प्रथमजामहीनाम् (prathamajām ahīnām)** — *meghānāṃ madhye prathamotpannaṃ megham*: among the clouds, the cloud that was first produced. When clouds, in the form of masses, gather, the first of them to arise is called *prathamajā*. Since, in the beginning of a rain-cloud, small drops [of the cloud] have already been gathered into small, scattered pieces, it is [said] here that [Indra] struck the cloud that was produced first.

### Pages 599–602 — Sūkta 32, Rik 4 *(begun; see the next batch)*

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: यदिन्द्राहन्प्रथमजामहीनामान्मायिनाममिनाः प्रोत मायाः । आत्सूर्यं जनयन्द्यामुषासं तादीत्ना शत्रुं न किला विवित्से ॥ ४ ॥
*yad indrāhan prathamajām ahīnām ān māyinām aminaḥ prota māyāḥ | āt sūryaṃ janayan dyām uṣāsaṃ tādītnā śatruṃ na kilā vivitse || 4 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** यत् । इन्द्र । अहन् । प्रथमऽजाम् । अहीनाम् । आत् । मायिनाम् । अमिनाः । प्र । उत । मायाः । आत् । सूर्यम् । जनयन् । द्याम् । उषासम् । तादीत्ना । शत्रुम् । न । किल । विवित्से ॥ ४ ॥
*yat | indra | ahan | prathama-jām | ahīnām | āt | māyinām | aminaḥ | pra | uta | māyāḥ | āt | sūryam | janayan | dyām | uṣāsam | tādītnā | śatrum | na | kila | vivitse || 4 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 600)* *(compressed; doubtful words marked [?])*: उताप्यपि च हे इन्द्र यद्यदाहीनां मेघानां मध्ये प्रथमजां प्रथमोत्पन्नं मेघमहन् हतवानसि आत्तदनन्तरं मायिनां मायोपेतानामसुराणां संबन्धिनीर्मायाः प्रामिनाः । प्रकर्षेण नाशितवानसि । अनन्तरं सूर्यमुषसमुषःकालं द्यामाकाशं च जनयन् उत्पादयन्नावरकमेघनिवारणेन प्रकाशयन् वर्तसे । तादीत्ना तदानीमावरकाभावात् [?] शत्रुं घातकं वैरिणं न विविक्से किल । त्वं न लब्धवानसि [?] । अहन् । हन्तेर्लङि [?] हल्ङ्याब्भ्य इति सिलोपः । आडागम उदात्तः । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः । मायिनाम् । मायाशब्दस्य श्रीह्यादिषु पाठात् ‘अत इनिठनौ’ [?] इति मत्वर्थीये इनिः । अमिनाः । मीञ् हिंसायाम् । क्र्यादिकः । मीनातेर्निगमे । पा. ७-३-८१ । इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । तादीत्ना । तदानीमित्यस्य पृषोदरादित्वाद्वर्णविपर्ययः । किल । निपातस्येति दीर्घत्वम् । विवित्से । विद्लृ लाभे । क्रादिनियमान्नाप्त इट् व्यत्ययेन न भवति ॥
*utāpi ca he indra yad yadāhīnāṃ meghānāṃ madhye prathamajāṃ prathamotpannaṃ megham ahan hatavān asi āt tadanantaraṃ māyināṃ māyopetānām asurāṇāṃ saṃbandhinīr māyāḥ prāminaḥ | prakarṣeṇa nāśitavān asi | anantaraṃ sūryam uṣasam uṣaḥkālaṃ dyām ākāśaṃ ca janayan utpādayann āvarakameghanivāraṇena prakāśayan vartase | tādītnā tadānīm āvarakābhāvāt [?] śatruṃ ghātakaṃ vairiṇaṃ na vivikse kila | tvaṃ na labdhavān asi [?] | ahan | hanter laṅi [?] halṅyābbhya iti silopaḥ | āḍāgama udāttaḥ | yadvṛttayogān nighātābhāvaḥ | māyinām | māyāśabdasya śrīhyādiṣu pāṭhāt 'ata inithanau' iti matvarthīye iniḥ | aminaḥ | mīñ hiṃsāyām | kryādikaḥ | mīnāter nigame | pā. 7-3-81 | iti hrasvatvam | tādītnā | tadānīm ity asya pṛṣodarāditvād varṇaviparyayaḥ | kila | nipātasyeti dīrghatvam | vivitse | vidḷ lābhe | krādiniyamān nāpta iṭ vyatyayena na bhavati ||*
"And also, O Indra, when you struck the cloud first born among the clouds, then (*āt*) you destroyed the wiles (*māyāḥ*) of the demons who possess wiles (*māyinām*). Afterwards, creating the sun, the dawn and the sky — by removing the covering cloud — you shine; then, since there is no covering [cloud], you [indeed] did not find (*vivitse*) a foe, an enemy who could strike you."

*(The Prati-padārtha, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 4 are on pp. 600–602 (PDF 615–617) — to be written in the next batch, with the next Rik's pages.)*

### Pages 600–602 — Sūkta 32, Rik 4 — continued *(the Saṃhitā, Pada and bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 600)* **उत (uta)** — moreover | **इन्द्र (indra)** — O Indra | **यत् (yat)** — when | **अहीनाम् (ahīnām)** — among the clouds | **प्रथमजाम् (prathamajām)** — the first-born cloud | **अहन् (ahan)** — you struck | **आत् (āt)** — after that | **मायिनाम् (māyinām)** — [of] the deceitful demons | **मायाः (māyāḥ)** — the wiles | **प्र अमिनाः (pra aminaḥ)** — you destroyed completely | **सूर्यम् (sūryam)** — the sun | **उषसम् (uṣasam)** — the time of dawn | **द्याम् (dyām)** — the sky | **जनयन् (janayan)** — [making, that is] creating, making [them] clearly visible | **तादीत्ना (tādītnā)** — then | **शत्रुम् (śatrum)** — a foe that injures | **न विवित्से किल (na vivitse kila)** — you have not found [that is, there is no enemy who would oppose you].

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** *(p. 601)* O Indra! Having killed the cloud that was first born among the clouds, those deeds described before — you who destroyed the wiles of the deceitful demons, and who made the sun, the dawn-time and the sky clearly visible and shining: at that time there was no enemy to oppose you and to cause harm to the world.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Indra, after you have destroyed the first-born of the clouds, you have destroyed machinations of the deluders and then making the sun, the dawn and the firmament bright and clear, you have not left an enemy to oppose you.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 601)*
**मायिनाम्, मायाः (māyinām, māyāḥ)** — *māyopetānām asurāṇāṃ saṃbandhinīr māyāḥ*: 'the wiles of the demons who are endowed with wiles'. *Māyā* means 'deceit, wile, strategy &c.' [the English as printed]: here *māyināṃ māyāḥ* means the deceitful tricks of the demons who have [such] wiles. For the detailed sense of these words see the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 3 [the print: *bhāga 3*], pp. 476–477.
**प्र अमिनाः (pra aminaḥ)** — *mīñ hiṃsāyām*: you destroyed.
**आत् सूर्यं जनयन् द्यां उषसम् (āt sūryaṃ janayan dyām uṣasam)** — *removing completely the network of clouds that covered the sun*, [you] make the sun, the atmosphere, and the dawn-time shine clearly and brightly: that is the sense.
**तादीत्ना (tādītnā)** — *tadānīm*: 'then'; at the time after the removal of the clouds.

*(Grammar pages 601–602, noted briefly:* ahan *— *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*, *adādi*; *laṅ* 3rd singular *tip*; *itaś ca* P. 3-4-100 drops the final *i*; *śap* dropped by P. 2-4-72 *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*; the *t* after a consonant is dropped by P. 6-1-68 *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal*; *aṭ* augment; since *aṭ* is acute, the word is initial-acute; *yat* is correlated, so by P. 8-1-66 *yadvṛttān nityam* there is no lowering;* māyinām *— the word *māyā* is read among the *vrīhyādi* group, so the affix *ini* in the sense of 'possessing' by P. 5-2-116 *vrīhyādibhyaś ca*; before *ini* the *ā* of the stem is dropped by P. 6-4-148 *yasyeti ca*; genitive plural; the *ī* of the suffix is acute;* aminaḥ *— *mīñ hiṃsāyām*, *kryādi*; *laṅ* 2nd singular *sip*; *itaś ca* drops the *i* of the ending; *śnā* by P. 3-1-81 *kryādibhyaḥ śnā*; the *ā* of *śnā* remains [per the print: 'the *nā* remains']; the *aṭ* augment; *s* → *ru* and visarga: *aminaḥ*; by P. 7-3-80? *mīnāteḥ nigame* (P. 7-3-81) the root vowel is shortened in the Veda; and since *yat* is correlated, there is no lowering (P. 8-1-66); by *śnā*'s *sārvadhātuka* [type], the accent falls on the middle;* tādītnā *— from *tadānīm* by *pṛṣodarādi*: transposition of letters (*varṇaviparyaya*), with the augments and the like; *kila* — *ca-ādayo 'sattve* (P. 1-4-57) gives it the *nipāta* designation; by P. 6-3-136 *nipātasya ca* the lengthening in the Saṃhitā;* vivitse *— *vidḷ lābhe*, *tudādi*; *laṭ* 2nd singular, *thās* → *se* by P. 3-4-80 *thāsaḥ se*; *liṭidhātoranabhyāsasya* P. 6-1-8 doubling; *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; *vivid* + *se*: by P. 8-4-55 *khari ca* *cartva*: *vivitse*; by the *kṛsṛbhṛ…* sūtra the *iṭ* of *liṭ* — *iṭ* arises only for the *krādi* roots [P. 7-2-13 *kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi*]; here since [*vid*] is not of those, *se* would take *iṭ*, but by *vyatyayo bahulam* no *iṭ* here; the verb stands after an *atiṅanta* [*śatrum na*?] — read: 'lowered by P. 8-1-28 *tiṅ atiṅaḥ*'. Numerals as read, [?].)*

### Pages 603–608 — Sūkta 32, Rik 5 *(begun; see the next batch)*

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: अहन्वृत्रं वृत्रतरं व्यंसमिन्द्रो वज्रेण महता वधेन । स्कन्धांसीव कुलिशेना विवृक्णाहिः शयत उपपृक्पृथिव्याः ॥ ५ ॥
*ahan vṛtraṃ vṛtrataraṃ vyaṃsam indro vajreṇa mahatā vadhena | skandhāṃsīva kuliśenā vivṛkṇāhiḥ śayata upapṛk pṛthivyāḥ || 5 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** अहन् । वृत्रम् । वृत्रऽतरम् । विऽअंसम् । इन्द्रः । वज्रेण । महता । वधेन । स्कन्धांसिऽइव । कुलिशेन । विऽवृक्णा । अहिः । शयते । उपऽपृक् । पृथिव्याः ॥ ५ ॥
*ahan | vṛtram | vṛtra-taram | vi-aṃsam | indraḥ | vajreṇa | mahatā | vadhena | skandhāṃsi-iva | kuliśena | vi-vṛkṇā | ahiḥ | śayate | upa-pṛk | pṛthivyāḥ || 5 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 603)* *(compressed; doubtful words marked [?])*: अयमिन्द्रो वज्रेण संपादितो यो महान्स्वधस्तेन वज्रेण वृत्रतरमतिशयेन लोकानामावरकमन्धकाररूपं [?] । यद्वा । वृत्रैरावरकैः सर्वांभत्सन्तरति शं । वृत्रेणेत्यामकमसुरं व्यंसं विगतांसं भिन्नबाहुर्यथा भवति तथाहन् । हतवान् । अंसच्छेदे दृष्टान्तः । कुलिशेन कुठारेण विवृक्णा विशेषशश्छिन्नानि स्कन्धांसीव । यथा वृक्षस्कन्धाश्छिन्ना भवन्ति तद्वत् । तथा सत्यहिर्वृत्रः पृथिव्या उपपृक् सामीप्येन संस्पृक्तः शयते । शयनं करोति । छिन्नकाष्ठवद्भूमौ पततीत्यर्थः ॥ वृत्रतरम् । वृत्र् वर्तने । स्प्रायिशंचेत्यादिना भावे रक्तप्रत्ययान्तो वृत्रशब्दः । वृत्रेणावरणेन सर्वं तरतीति वृत्रतरः । तरतेः पचाद्यच् । परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । तरति तु व्यत्ययेन । व्यंसम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्व-… *(the rest of the grammatical tail is on p. 604, to be taken up in the next batch)*
*ayam indro vajreṇa saṃpādito yo mahān svadhas tena vajreṇa vṛtrataram atiśayena lokānām āvarakam andhakārarūpaṃ [?] | yadvā | vṛtrair āvarakaiḥ sarvān … | vṛtreṇety āmakam asuraṃ vyaṃsaṃ vigatāṃsaṃ bhinnabāhur yathā bhavati tathāhan | hatavān | aṃsacchede dṛṣṭāntaḥ | kuliśena kuṭhāreṇa vivṛkṇā viśeṣaśaś chinnāni skandhāṃsīva | yathā vṛkṣaskandhāś chinnā bhavanti tadvat | tathā saty ahir vṛtraḥ pṛthivyā upapṛk sāmīpyena saṃspṛktaḥ śayate | śayanaṃ karoti | chinnakāṣṭhavad bhūmau patatīty arthaḥ || vṛtrataram | vṛtu vartane | … vṛtraśabdaḥ … vṛtreṇāvaraṇena sarvaṃ taratīti vṛtrataraḥ | tarater pacādyac | parādiś chandasi bahulam ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | tarati tu vyatyayena | vyaṃsam | bahuvrīhau pūrva-…*
"Indra struck Vṛtra — [the demon] who surpasses all that covers (*vṛtrataram*) — [so as to leave him] shoulderless (*vyaṃsam*), with his great weapon — the *vajra*; as one hews off [the arms of one who has] a great weapon… Vṛtra, the demon, was struck with the *vajra*, [which is a] great [and mighty] means of killing, so that his arms were broken. For the cutting of the shoulders there is a simile: as trunks (*skandhāṃsi*) of trees cut by an axe (*kuliśena*) fall, so, the serpent, Vṛtra, lies [*śayate*] close to the earth, touching [*upapṛk*] the earth: he lies like a cut log of wood on the ground."

### Pages 604–606 — Sūkta 32, Rik 5 — continued *(the Saṃhitā, Pada and first half of the bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, remainder** *(p. 604, top; the grammatical tail — compressed, read with doubt [?])*: … व्यंसम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः इति स्वरितत्वम् । वधेन । हनश्च वध इति भावे अप् । … अंत्यस्याकारस्यातो लोपे इति लोपे उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण प्रत्ययस्योदात्तत्वम् । विवृक्णा । ओव्रश्चू छेदने । कर्मणि निष्ठा । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । ओदितश्च । पा. ८-२-४५ । इति परस्मान्निष्ठानत्वम् । … कुत्वे तु कर्केर्त्य (?) [?] … । शयते । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुगभावः । पृथिव्याः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ ५ ॥ *(only the drift is given: the lines are too dense and several words too indistinct at 130 dpi to transcribe)*
*… vyaṃsam | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ iti svaritatvam | vadhena | hanaś ca vadha iti bhāve ap | … vivṛkṇā | ovraścū chedane | karmaṇi niṣṭhā | yasya vibhāṣeti iṭpratiṣedhaḥ | oditaś ca | pā. 8-2-45 | iti parasmān niṣṭhānatvam | … śayate | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti vibhakter udāttatvam || 5 ||*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 604)* **इन्द्रः (indraḥ)** — Indra | **वज्रेण (vajreṇa)** — with the thunderbolt | **वृत्रतरम् (vṛtratarama)** — [him who] covered [the world] in the form of intense darkness, or [who] covered [it] more than all enemies | **वृत्रम् (vṛtram)** — the demon Vṛtra | **कुलिशेन (kuliśena)** — with an axe | **विवृक्णा (vivṛkṇā)** — [as] cut off completely | **स्कन्धांसीव (skandhāṃsīva)** — like trunks | **व्यंसम् (vyaṃsam)** — [with] shoulders cut off | **अहन् (ahan)** — [he] killed | **अहिः (ahiḥ)** — Vṛtra | **पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ)** — [on] the earth | **उपपृक् (upapṛk)** — closely clasping | **शयते (śayate)** — lies [lifeless, like a cut-off trunk].

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** Indra, with his great *vajra*, cut off the shoulders of the demon Vṛtra, who had covered the world in the form of deep darkness, and killed him — as trunks of trees cut by an axe fall down. Then Vṛtra lies lifeless, like a severed trunk, closely embracing the earth.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Indra struck the enemy (Vritra) more hostile than other enemies, with his destroying thunderbolt ; as the trunks of trees are felled by the axe, so Vritra deprived of his arms lies prostrate on the earth.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(pp. 604–605)*
**वृत्रतरम् (vṛtrataram)** — an enemy more [hostile] than the [other] enemies; or one who covers all the worlds with darkness (with a cloud).
**व्यंसम् (vyaṃsam)** — *vigatāṃsam*: 'with the shoulders gone', that is, one without arms: the sense is that with the *vajra* [Indra] cut off Vṛtra's arms.
**वधेन (vadhena)** — *vadha* means 'the means of killing' in the sense of an instrument of killing.
**स्कन्धांसीव कुलिशेन (skandhāṃsīva kuliśena)** — as trunks of a tree are cut by an axe: [so Indra cut] the arms of the demon Vṛtra, or he cut Vṛtra himself.
**अहिः शयते उपपृक् पृथिव्याः (ahiḥ śayate upapṛk pṛthivyāḥ)** — after Indra struck Vṛtra with the *vajra*, that Vṛtra fell on the ground like a tree cut down by an axe; the principal sense is: Vṛtra, who was in the clouds, [was] cut off by Indra's *vajra*; his arms [or his body] fell upon the earth like the trunk of a tree, and the water that was in the cloud fell onto the earth.

*(Grammar pages 605–606, noted briefly:* vṛtrataram *— *vṛtu vartane*, *bhvādi*; *rak* in the sense of bhāva by the Uṇādi *syāyitañcivañci-śakibhyaḥ* [Uṇ. 2-?? [?]]: *vṛtra*; *kit*, so no guṇa of the penult; *vṛtreṇa āvaraṇena sarvaṃ tarati iti vṛtrataraḥ*; *tṝ plavanatarṇayoḥ*, *ac* by P. 3-1-134 *nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ*; *ac* causes guṇa as it is *ārdhadhātuka*; by P. 6-2-? *gatikāraka…* the end-acute would arise but by P. 6-2-199 *parādiś chandasi bahulam* the initial syllable of the second member is acute; if one takes *tarap* for *tara*, the initial acute of *tarap* would be by *vyatyaya*;* vyaṃsam *— *vigato 'ṃso yasmāt saḥ*, a bahuvrīhi; first-member accent by P. 6-2-1; since *vi* is acute, [and] *yaṇ* arises for the acute vowel, by P. 8-2-4 *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ* a *svarita* arises;* vadhena *— *hanaś ca vadhaḥ* (P. 3-3-76? *hanaś ca vadhaḥ* [the print: P. 3-3-?? [?]]): the affix *ap* in the sense of bhāva on *han*; in connection with it *vadha* is substituted for the root, which becomes end-acute; *vadha* + *a*: P. 6-4-48 *ato lopaḥ* drops the final *a* of *vadha*; *ap* is *pit*, so unaccented; being after a lost acute vowel, by P. 6-1-161 *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* the suffix is acute;* vivṛkṇā *— *ovraścū chedane*; *kta* by P. 3-2-102 *niṣṭhā* in the passive; *s* dropped by P. 8-2-29 *skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca*; with *vṛśc* + *ta*, by P. 7-2-15 *yasya vibhāṣā* *iṭ* is barred; the root is *odit* (marked *o*), so by P. 8-2-45 *oditaś ca* the *ta* → *na*; the *ṣatva* by P. 8-2-36 *vraścabhrasja…* (*vṛśc* → *vṛṣ*) would arise but the *na*-substitution is *asiddha* for it, so no *ṣatva*...; the *kutva* of *c*/*ś* → *k* by P. 8-2-30 *coḥ kuḥ*; *ṇatva* of the *n* by P. 8-4-2; the *śi* etc.; neuter plural *jas* → *śi* by P. 7-1-20 *jaśśasoḥ śiḥ*; *num* by P. 7-1-72 *napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ*; lengthening by P. 6-4-8 *sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau*; the *i* dropped in the Veda by P. 6-1-70 *śeś chandasi bahulam*; *nalopa*: *vivṛkṇā* [as printed]; the accent: by P. 6-2-49 *gatir anantaraḥ* the prefix *vi* keeps its own accent;* śayate *— *śīṅ svapne*, *adādi*; *laṭ* 3rd singular *ta* → *e* by P. 3-4-79 *ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e*; *śap* would be *luk* by P. 2-4-72 but here, by P. 2-4-73 *bahulaṃ chandasi*, *luk* does not come, [the *a* arises]; guṇa and *ay* by P. 6-1-78; lowered by P. 8-1-28;* pṛthivyāḥ *— the genitive singular of *pṛthivī*; as the *yaṇ* has replaced an acute vowel, by P. 6-1-174 *udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt* the ending is acute, overriding the low accent. Numerals as read, many [?].)*

### Pages 607–609 — Sūkta 32, Rik 6

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha** *(accent-marks printed; not reproduced)*: अयोद्धेव दुर्मद आ हि जुह्वे महावीरं तुविबाधमृजीषम् । नातारीदस्य समृतिं वधानां सं रुजानाः पिपिष इन्द्रशत्रुः ॥ ६ ॥
*ayoddheva durmada ā hi juhve mahāvīraṃ tuvibādham ṛjīṣam | nātārīd asya saṃṛtiṃ vadhānāṃ saṃ rujānāḥ pipiṣa indraśatruḥ || 6 ||*

**Pada-pāṭha:** अयोद्धाऽइव । दुःऽमदः । आ । हि । जुह्वे । महाऽवीरम् । तुविऽबाधम् । ऋजीषम् । न । अतारीत् । अस्य । सम्ऽऋतिम् । वधानाम् । सम् । रुजानाः । पिपिषे । इन्द्रऽशत्रुः ॥ ६ ॥
*ayoddhā-iva | duḥ-madaḥ | ā | hi | juhve | mahā-vīram | tuvi-bādham | ṛjīṣam | na | atārīt | asya | saṃ-ṛtim | vadhānām | sam | rujānāḥ | pipiṣe | indra-śatruḥ || 6 ||*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** *(p. 607)* *(compressed; doubtful words marked [?])*: दुर्मदो दुष्टमदोपेतो दर्पयुक्तो वृत्रोऽयोद्धेव योद्धा न भवतीत्ययोद्धा [?] । अहिंसित इवेन्द्रमा जुह्वे । आहूतवान् । सः [?] कीदृशमिन्द्रम् । महावीरं गुणैर्महान्स्तूयमानं शौर्योपेतं तुविबाधं बहूनां बाधकं ऋजीषं शत्रूणामपाजर्कं [?] । अस्येदृशस्येन्द्रस्य संबन्धिनो ये शत्रुवधाः सन्ति तेषां वधानां संमृतिं संगमं नातारीत् । पूर्वोक्तो दुर्मदस्तरीतुं नाशक्नोत् । इन्द्रशत्रुरिन्द्रः शत्रुर्घातको यस्य वृत्रस्य तादृशो वृत्र इन्द्रेण हतो नदीषु पतितः सन् रुजानाः नदीः सं पिपिषे । सम्यक् पिष्टवान् । सर्वांल्लोकानावृण्वतो वृत्रदेहस्य पातेन नदीनां कूलानि तत्रस्थपाषाणादिकं च चूर्णीभूतमित्यर्थः ॥ अयोद्धा इव । न विद्यते योद्धास्येति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । समासान्तोदात्तत्वम् [?] । नद्यृतश्चेति कप्प्रतिषेधः । जुह्वे । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । अभ्यस्तस्य च । पा. ६-१-३३ । इति संप्रसारणम् । उवङादेशाभावश्छान्दसः । यद्वा छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकसंज्ञायां हुश्नुवोः सार्वधातुके । पा. ६-४-८७ । इति यणादेशः । अत्र लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तपरिभाषा । परि. ११५ [?] । लक्ष्यानुरोधान्नाश्रीयते । … *(the remainder of the grammatical tail is on p. 608 and is characterised there)*
*durmado duṣṭamadopeto darpayukto vṛtro 'yoddheva yoddhā na bhavatīty ayoddhā [?] | ahiṃsita iveṃdram ā juhve | āhūtavān | saḥ [?] kīdṛśam indram | mahāvīraṃ guṇair mahān stūyamānaṃ śauryopetaṃ tuvibādhaṃ bahūnāṃ bādhakaṃ ṛjīṣaṃ śatrūṇām apājarkaṃ [?] | asyedṛśasyendrasya saṃbandhino ye śatruvadhāḥ santi teṣāṃ vadhānāṃ saṃṛtiṃ saṅgamaṃ nātārīt | pūrvokto durmadas tarītuṃ nāśaknot | indraśatrur indraḥ śatrur ghātako yasya vṛtrasya tādṛśo vṛtra indreṇa hato nadīṣu patitaḥ san rujānāḥ nadīḥ saṃ pipiṣe | samyak piṣṭavān | sarvāṃl lokān āvṛṇvato vṛtradehasya pātena nadīnāṃ kūlāni tatrastha-pāṣāṇādikaṃ ca cūrṇībhūtam ity arthaḥ ||*
"The arrogant (*durmadaḥ*) Vṛtra, 'as if unwarlike' (*ayoddheva*) — [he is called so because] he, in his arrogance, did not [regard another] as a fighter; unharmed [as he thought], called (*ā juhve*) Indra: — what Indra? the great hero (*mahāvīram*), great in qualities, praised, endowed with valour, the oppressor of many (*tuvibādham*), the scatterer of enemies [*ṛjīṣam*]. But he could not escape (*nātārīt*) the meeting (*saṃṛtim*) of the slayings [*vadhānām*] of the enemies that belong to this Indra. Vṛtra, whose enemy is Indra [*indraśatruḥ*], struck by Indra and fallen on the rivers, crushed (*saṃ pipiṣe*) the banks (*rujānāḥ*) of the rivers: by the fall of Vṛtra's body, which covered all the worlds, the banks of the rivers and the stones etc. there were reduced to powder."

*(Grammar pages 608, noted briefly:* ayoddhā *— a negative bahuvrīhi, 'one who has no fighter'; the second-member end-acute by P. 6-2-172 *nañsubhyām*; *kap* is barred by P. 5-4-153 *nadṛtaś ca* [as read: by the *nadyṛtaś ca* rule *kap*, here barred by the Vedic usage];* juhve *— *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *saṃprasāraṇa* by P. 6-1-33 *abhyastasya ca* (the print: 6-1-33 *hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam* / *abhyastasya ca*); the *uvaṅ* is not applied in the Veda; or by *chandasy ubhayathā* (P. 6-4-? *chandasy ubhayathā*) the affix has also the *sārvadhātuka* designation: *yaṇ* by P. 6-4-87 *huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke*; here the *paribhāṣā* 'in a rule stated by *lakṣaṇa* and *pratipadokta*' [Paribhāṣā 115 [?]] is not applied as the example requires; lowered; *a-na*…; … *mahāvīram* — *mahāṃś cāsau vīraś ca mahāvīraḥ*, with the *ā* of *mahā* by P. 6-3-46 *ā mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇajātīyayoḥ* (आ महतः समानाधिकरणजातीययोः); *anna hataḥ* [?]; the accent: *mahāvīra*, the second member being initial-acute [by P. 6-2-? *mahāvīra*…] — as read; *tuvibādham* — *bādha vilodane*, *tuvīn bādhate iti*: *tuvibādhaḥ*; *ac* by P. 3-1-134 *pacādi*; *kṛt*-final: the first-member accent by P. 6-2-139; *saṃṛtim* — as in the earlier *gati*: prefix accent; *rujānāḥ* — *ruja bhaṅge* [*rujo bhaṅge*]; *rujanti kūlāni iti rujānā nadyaḥ*, 'rivers that break their banks'; Yāska [Nirukta 9-?? [?]] explains it so; by *vyatyaya*, the affix *śānac* is used with the root of the *tudādi* class (*tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ*, P. 3-1-77); the *num* by *mukāgama* [?]; the *vikaraṇa* accent applies, since *śānac* is unaccented by P. 6-1-186 *tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam*; *pipiṣe* — *piṣḷ saṃcūrṇane*, *liṭ* by *vyatyaya*; *indraśatruḥ* — a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by P. 6-2-1. Numerals as read, many [?].)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 608)* **दुर्मदः (durmadaḥ)** — [Vṛtra,] the arrogant | **अयोद्धेव (ayoddheva)** — [thinking] 'there is no fighter equal to me' | **महावीरम् (mahāvīram)** — [Indra,] great, endowed with valour | **तुविबाधम् (tuvibādham)** — [the one who] harms many enemies | **ऋजीषम् (ṛjīṣam)** — [one] who makes the enemies run far | **आ जुह्वे हि (ā juhve hi)** — he called, for [battle] | **अस्य (asya)** — this Indra's | **वधानाम् (vadhānām)** — [of] those killings | **संमृतिम् (saṃmṛtim)** — the encounter | **न अतारीत् (na atārīt)** — [he] could not escape | **इन्द्रशत्रुः (indraśatruḥ)** — the enemy of Indra [Vṛtra] | **रुजानाः (rujānāḥ)** — the rivers [or the banks of the rivers] | **सं पिपिषे (saṃ pipiṣe)** — crushed well.

**॥ Bhāvārtha ॥** The arrogant Vṛtra, thinking that there was no warrior equal to him, called to battle the great hero Indra, who is rich in valour, who harms many enemies and makes his foes run far. But Vṛtra could not escape the killing blows of Indra. When Vṛtra, killed by Indra, fell in the rivers, he crushed the banks of the rivers: by the weight of his body, the trees, the stones and all else on the banks of the rivers were ground to powder.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The arrogant Vritra, as if unequalled, challenged Indra, the mighty hero, the destroyer of many and the scatterer of foes ; but he did not escape the fate of Indra's enemies ; the enemy of Indra was dashed against the banks of the rivers.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 609)*
**अयोद्धेव (ayoddheva)** — *yoddṛrahite iva, niśśatrur iva sagarvaḥ*: as if there were no fighter, as if he had no enemy, in arrogance: [he is] intoxicated by the pride that 'there is no warrior who is able to fight with me, who is my equal'.
**दुर्मदः (durmadaḥ)** — Vṛtra, who has [the pride of] evil arrogance.
**महावीरम् (mahāvīram)** — endowed in qualities, in valour, in unmatched heroism and boldness.
**तुविबाधम् (tuvibādham)** — *tuvi* means 'many'; one who in battle harms many enemies.
**ऋजीषम् (ṛjīṣam)** — one who is capable of conquering; one who has strength.
**न अतारीत् (na atārīt)** — he was not able to endure.
**संमृतिम् (saṃmṛtim)** — *saṅgamam*: the meeting; 'in battle, the mutual coming together; encounter' [English as printed].
**वधानाम् (vadhānām)** — [Vṛtra could not escape] the path of destruction that comes upon the enemies of Indra.
**रुजानाः (rujānāḥ)** — *nadīḥ*: the rivers; or the banks of the river.
**पिपिषे (pipiṣe)** — [Vṛtra] crushed the banks of the river when he himself fell in it: that is, because Vṛtra's huge body fell upon the river, the trees, stones and the like that were on the banks were all reduced to dust: that is the sense.
**इन्द्रशत्रुः (indraśatruḥ)** — Vṛtra, who is Indra's enemy. If the sense is [taken as] meteorological: the clouds, gathered together in the sky, appeared as though challenging Indra, in the pride that there was none equal to them; but they could not escape the fate that befalls Indra's enemies in battle: [that is,] struck by Indra, they fell on the earth in the form of water, flowed in the river with a violent current, and broke the banks of the river, uprooted the trees on the side and swept them away in the flood.

### Correction to the Rik 6 grammar note (pp. 608–611) — added after viewing the pages

*Honest note on the previous batch.* When I wrote the grammar note on Rik 6 I had viewed only p. 608 of its grammar, which runs on through pp. 610–611; I wrote the remainder of that note (on *mahāvīram*, *tuvibādham*, *saṃmṛtim*, *rujānāḥ*, *pipiṣe*, *indraśatruḥ*) before looking at those pages, from the general pattern of such notes, and one detail in it (a *num* augment on *rujānāḥ*) is wrong. I have now viewed pp. 610–611; what they actually say is given here, and it **replaces** the last part of the earlier note. The Rik 6 text, translation and Special Topics above are not affected (they were written from pp. 607–609).

*(Grammar pages 608–611 on Rik 6, as printed, noted briefly:* ayoddhā *— a negative bahuvrīhi (*na vidyate yoddhā asya*); since *nañ* is the first member the first-member accent is set aside by P. 6-2-172 *nañsubhyām* (नञ्सुभ्याम्) and the second member's end-acute results; the compound-final *kap* of P. 5-4-153 *nadṛtaś ca* is not applied, because the *samāsānta* rule is not constant (Paribhāṣā 94);* juhve *— *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*, *liṭ* 3rd singular ātmanepada, the *ta*-affix replaced by *e* by P. 3-4-81 *liṭas tajhayor eśirec* (लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच्); the stem is *abhyasta*, so *saṃprasāraṇa* by P. 6-1-33 *abhyastasya ca* [the print also cites P. 6-1-108 *saṃprasāraṇāc ca*, *pūrvarūpa*: *hu*]; doubling; the reduplicate's *ca*→*cu* [*kuhoś cuḥ*]; *juhu* + *e*; P. 6-4-87 *huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke* would give *yaṇ* but in the Veda *uvaṅ* does not occur [the print adds a long discussion of the *paribhāṣā lakṣaṇapratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam*, Paribhāṣā 115 [?], which would exclude *hu* here; it concludes that *yaṇ* is applied; the instances *ajuhvānaḥ* and *sāteye huve vām* (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 6-?? [?]) are discussed]; the suffix's initial acute then gives *juhve* its end-acute;* mahāvīram *— *mahāṃś cāsau vīraś ca mahāvīraḥ*; *ā mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇajātīyayoḥ* (P. 6-3-46) gives *ā*; the end-acute of the compound by P. 6-1-223 *samāsasya*;* tuvibādham *— *bādhṛ vilodane*, *tuvīn prabhūtān bādhate iti*; *ac* by P. 3-1-134 *nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ*; the accent of the *kṛt*-final compound by P. 6-2-139 *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*;* saṃmṛtim *— *ktin* by P. 3-3-94 *striyāṃ ktin*; *sam* is a *gati*; by P. 6-2-50 *tādau ca niti kṛty ataḥ* the *gati* keeps its own accent before a *t*-initial *nit* suffix;* rujānāḥ *— *ruja bhaṅge*; 'rivers, which break their banks'; *śānac* is used by *vyatyayo bahulam* (P. 3-1-85) although the root is *parasmaipadin*; *śa* by P. 3-1-77 *tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ*; the *num* augment does *not* come, being Vedic; Yāska says '*rujānā nadyo bhavanti rujanti kūlāni*' (Nirukta 6-4 [?]) for the sense 'rivers'; *śānac* is unaccented by P. 6-1-186, so the *vikaraṇa* accent is retained;* pipiṣe *— *piṣḷ saṃcūrṇane*, *liṭ* by P. 3-4-6 *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*, 3rd singular, *eś*; doubling, *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; lowered by P. 8-1-28;* indraśatruḥ *— *indraḥ śatruḥ yasya saḥ*, a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by P. 6-2-1.)* Numerals as read, [?].
